Loading gene effect data...
— extended version —

Changelog (development)

v.89.18 (2026-08-31)

  • Reference Data: the citation note no longer credits DepMap with all cell-line data; the screening, sequencing and molecular data are DepMap's, the annotation layers have their own sources.

v.89.17 (2026-08-31)

  • The gene effect / mRNA choice returns to being extended-version only, reversing the previous entry. Correlate V1 instead states what it runs on, where the choice would sit: "Correlates on: gene effect (CRISPR knockout, DepMap 26Q1)".

v.89.16 (2026-08-31)

  • Reference Data reads as a page for outsiders. Every source is now a link (COSMIC, OncoKB, NCCN, the WHO tumour classification, both Lehmann papers, CCLE); the retroelement entry explains where the sequencing comes from and how the signal was computed in two sentences; the closing paragraph says plainly what to cite for what instead of asserting that databases "have their own attribution requirements"; and "Curated annotations (in this app)" now says what it means: layers assembled by analysis while building Correlate, not taken ready-made from a database.
  • The gene effect / mRNA choice ships in Correlate V1 as well (it was an extended-version exclusive; the expression data was already there).

v.89.15 (2026-08-31)

  • The "Correlate on" choice says what its options are. "Gene effect" and "mRNA" assumed the reader knew the assays behind them; they now read Gene effect (CRISPR) and mRNA (bulk RNA-seq), and the heading names the release (DepMap 26Q1).

v.89.14 (2026-08-31)

  • Searching the mutation table finds every tested gene. The search only looked through the rows already drawn, which are the ones passing the p filter, so a gene that was tested but not significant came back as nothing, and no row read as "not tested" when the true answer was "tested, not significant". Two or more typed letters now search the full result list, a footnote says the filters are being looked past, and each row still shows its own p. On desktop and phone alike.
  • Phone: the mutation toolbar is three controls. The export row and the column filters are desktop tools, so they are gone from the phone; the search takes its own row and Enrichr and Heatmap split the row below it evenly.
  • "Open in heatmap" is now "Heatmap", matching the network's button.
  • Phone: the logo sits closer to the middle. The nudge that centres the wordmark read as the whole image hanging right on a narrow screen; half the nudge splits the difference.

v.89.13 (2026-08-31)

  • "hide * genes" says when it has nothing to do. The box hides genes marked with *, the ones measured in fewer cell lines than the rest of the cohort. In a small cohort where every gene has full data no row is starred, so the box did nothing and read as broken. It now disables itself with an explanation in that case. The * and the box also measured against different references, so a p-filtered table could be hidden from without a single visible star; both use the same bar now.

v.89.12 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone and tablet: running a mutation analysis scrolls to its table. The results sit below a tall column of controls, so pressing Run looked like nothing had happened. Only a fresh run moves the page; re-sorting a column or changing a filter redraws the same table and leaves the page where you left it.
  • Phone: the mutation table is about half as wide. Its fourteen column headers name the gene and the copy-number level, and every column was sized to fit its title on one line, which made the table around four screen-widths across. The headings wrap over several lines now and the numbers underneath stay on one, so roughly twice as many columns fit on screen at once. Desktop is unchanged.

v.89.11 (2026-08-30)

  • A Tissue split can now mix levels: Melanoma together with the whole of Bowel. Tissue, subtype and disease are one nested choice with a single lineage at the top, so a selection spanning two lineages where one is sliced finer had nowhere to go. It was applied as the tissue alone and the finer tick was dropped without a word, while the popup's footer counted both. Such a selection now travels as the list of branches it actually is, and everything reads it: the cohort, the results, the chip beside Run, the analysis it is saved into, its inspect and compare views, and the AI export.
  • Fix: the disease menu did not follow the tissue chosen in a Tissue split. Picking Bowel there left the menu offering melanomas and glioblastomas, because the split set the lineage without announcing it and the menus only rescope when told. All three levels scale to each other now however the choice was made, including across the branches of a mixed selection.
  • Reopening a Tissue split shows what is filtering. Only the lineage row was ever ticked again, so a subtype or disease pick came back as an empty table. The branches now come back ticked, with their rows opened.

v.89.10 (2026-08-30)

  • Tissue split: a tissue and one of its own subtypes can no longer both be ticked. The finer level replaces the coarser one when the filter is applied, so ticking Skin and Melanoma together filtered on Melanoma and the Skin tick did nothing, while the footer counted both. Ticking one level now clears the others in that branch: tick Melanoma and Skin lets go, tick Skin again and its subtypes let go. Separate branches are untouched, so several tissues, or several subtypes of one tissue, still combine as before. Both Tissue split popups behave the same way.

v.89.9 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone: the tree in the logo was cut off at the right edge. The logo image is wider than its lettering, so it is nudged right to bring "Correlate" over the middle of the app. On a phone the image already filled the width, leaving nothing for that nudge to move into, so it pushed the tree off the screen. The image is a little smaller there now and the whole logo fits.

v.89.8 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone: the cell lines you label on a scatter are now a list you can act on. Tapping a point labels it, but a phone has no hover, so nothing the app knows about that cell line was reachable from the plot. The labelled lines appear as chips directly under it: tap a name for its summary card, its wiki, or to open it in the Cell Line Browser, and tap the × to take the label off. Before anything is labelled the row says what to do, which was the other half of the problem. The row keeps its height either way, so it never appears and pushes the plot around. Desktop and tablet are unchanged, hover already reaches all of this there.

v.89.7 (2026-08-30)

  • Fix: alteration picks made in the Cell Line Browser silently narrowed charts opened elsewhere. Picking rows in the browser's mutation grid is meant to filter the browser's list and nothing else, which is what it already does for analyses. The gene-effect and expression popouts applied them anyway, so opening a gene from a cell line's wiki drew it over whatever the browser happened to be filtered to and still called the chart every lineage: a gene shown across 112 cell lines with no hint of why. Those picks now stop at the browser's list. Picks made inside the popout itself still apply there, as before.
  • Fix: the disease filter in the gene-effect popout did nothing on its own. It was nested inside the alteration-grid branch by mistake, so choosing a disease only had an effect when a grid filter happened to be active too.
  • Phone: the comparison selector now sits above the chart it describes. "All lineages / this lineage by primary disease / this lineage by disease" was placed after the chart, behind an export row a phone doesn't show, so it was below the fold and the chart looked like it offered no choice.

v.89.6 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone: a finger on a chart now scrolls the page. Charts were meant to stop claiming the touch for their own pan, but the setting was written to the wrong object (it belongs to the chart's layout, not its config) so it never took effect, and a swipe that started over any plot went nowhere. Scrolling is the same everywhere now, over text or over a chart; a tap still reaches a point.
  • The male and female symbols sat below the name beside them. The app's own font has no glyph for them, so each device substituted a different font and iOS picked one that draws them low. They are drawn as small shapes now, so they line up on every device. Italic still means the sex was read off expression rather than annotation.
  • Wiki: the WGD panel's bar labels ran into its axis title. "No WGD" and "WGD-positive" are too long for a panel that narrow, so they were tilted and collided with "WGD status" underneath. They read WGD− / WGD+ and sit flat.
  • Wiki: the genes under "Pathway dependencies unique to this line" are clickable. They were plain text while the same genes a line above, under the druggable list, opened their gene-effect view. Both behave the same way now.
  • Phone: the UpSet plot was cut off on the right. It opened at a fixed inset from the left edge sized for a desktop window, which on a phone pushed its right side past the screen and took the last combination with it. The inset scales with the screen.

v.89.5 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone: everything in "1. Set Parameters" sat flush against the card's left edge. A collapsed section on a phone is meant to shrink to a line of text, so the box it lives in drops its padding. "Lineage and disease" and "Genetic alterations" share that box with the rest of the card, though, so collapsing them (they start collapsed) stripped the padding from Analysis Mode, Correlate on and every label above them too. The box only sheds its padding now when it holds nothing but the collapsed section.

v.89.4 (2026-08-30)

  • The heatmap legends wrapped at the grid's width, not the screen's. The grid is thousands of pixels wide behind its sideways scroller, so the lineage and annotation legends were laid out to match and ran off the right edge of a phone. They wrap to the width actually on screen now, so a 29-lineage legend reads as a block instead of a line to chase sideways. Desktop is unchanged.
  • Phone: the heatmap is view-only. Tapping a gene name silenced it and tapping a lineage chip hid that group, but a fingertip covers several rows and several chips at once, so it fired by accident more than on purpose and the way back needed screen room a phone doesn't have. Both are off below 640px, and the cursor and hover text no longer offer them. Tablets and desktop keep them.

v.89.3 (2026-08-30)

  • Network → Heatmap counted the wrong genes. "Genes I entered" was counting the entered genes that ended up drawn as nodes, not the genes actually entered: a gene whose strongest correlation falls below the cutoff never becomes a node, so a run of 18 genes that drew 8 offered a heatmap of 8 and called them the ones entered. It now offers all 18, and says on hover how many of them the network left out and why. "All network genes" and "Correlating genes only" still describe the network itself and are unchanged.

v.89.2 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone and tablet: the heatmap now opens on the heatmap. It used to open on its settings stack, which is tall enough to fill a phone screen on its own, so the picture sat below the fold and the first thing you saw after asking for a heatmap was a column of dropdowns. On a touch screen the grid, its legends and the scroll hint move to the top and the settings follow underneath. The scatter has behaved this way for a while; this is the same idea. Opening one on a touch screen also scrolls it into view.
  • Phone: the annotation rows ran off the right edge. Each row is a line of dropdowns sized for a desktop window, so on a 390px screen it was more than twice as wide as the app and pushed the whole popout sideways. The controls wrap onto as many lines as they need now. The colour legends, which are drawn at a fixed width, pan sideways on their own instead of stretching the page.

v.89.1 (2026-08-30)

  • Phone audit: sliders and their step buttons were still mouse-sized. Everything else on a phone was deliberately enlarged some releases ago, but the four network appearance sliders kept a 6px track and their − / + buttons an 18px box, which is a hard target for a finger on the one device where the pointer is a finger. The track is 30px now, the thumb 24px and the step buttons 34px square. Desktop is untouched.
  • Phone: the gate percentage box no longer takes a row to itself. A rule giving every text box in the Cell Line Browser the full width outranked the narrow one meant for a two-digit number, so "25" occupied 205px of a 390px screen.

v.89.0 (2026-08-30)

  • The Enrichr gene column is narrower, which makes the whole table shorter. It was wide enough to lay each row's genes out on one or two lines while the term beside them wrapped onto four, so the genes were using a fraction of the height the row already had. Narrowing it hands the width back to the term, which then wraps less: the same results now take eleven rows on screen where they took eight, and the genes fill the height that was there anyway.
  • Version numbering restarts at 89.0 after 134 releases in the 88 series.

v.88.134 (2026-08-30)

  • Dialogs can be sized as well as moved. Grips on the left, right and bottom edges of every popout set its width and height, alongside the dragging by the title bar that was already there. Dragging the left edge keeps the right one still, so a panel does not walk across the screen while being narrowed.
  • Enrichr opens on the left and its Full window button is gone. The network is drawn on the right of the page, so a panel on the right covered the thing the results are about; on the left it covers the parameter boxes, which is what you can afford to lose while reading. The toggle went with it: with the panel movable and resizable there is nothing the full-window state was doing.

v.88.133 (2026-08-30)

  • Cell lines highlighted on the correlation plot can be opened in the Cell Line Browser. Encircling points with the lasso, clicking them or typing them in gathers a set worth working with, and until now the only way out of it was copying the names and pasting them back. Open in browser beside the Copy button ticks exactly those lines in the browser, ready for its filters, sorts, gates and exports; the plot stays open underneath and closing the browser returns to it.

v.88.132 (2026-08-30)

  • Color by tissue is one click in the correlation popout. It is the colouring worth reaching for most often and it sat three clicks down a select, below the highlight box. A button above that select turns it on and off and shows which state it is in; by subtype and by disease answer narrower questions and stay in the select.

v.88.131 (2026-08-30)

  • Where to paste a block is now part of the reading steps, not just the reference section. An assistant handed over a view block with no destination even though the file explained where it goes, because that explanation sat in a section it had no reason to open. The step that asks for a figure now also asks, in the same sentence, for the menu path to be named beside any block it writes.

v.88.130 (2026-08-30)

  • One export for several questions, not one each. Every export round costs a dialog, a download and an upload, and that cost is yours rather than the assistant's. The instructions now say to gather what the open questions need between them, the union of the genes, the widest cohort and the union of the layers, and ask once; the only accepted reason to split is when the first answer would change what the second should ask for, and it has to say so.
  • The question line asks for a hypothesis. The file usually goes straight back to the same assistant, so restating the question tells it nothing it did not already know. What the field is worth is committing to a test before the numbers arrive: not "does X explain Y", which invites finding the pattern that fits, but "X explains Y, which predicts A and would be refuted by B".

v.88.129 (2026-08-30)

  • A block an assistant writes now says where to paste it. One of the two assistants tested named the menu path and the other handed over a bare block with no destination, which leaves you holding something with nowhere to put it. Every block and every worked example now carries # paste into Options › Other › ... as its second line, so the address travels with the thing even if the assistant forgets to mention it, and both sets of instructions now ask outright for that line to appear beside the code fence.

v.88.128 (2026-08-30)

  • Fix: a gene card outlived the popout it came from. Hovering a gene name inside the correlation popout could leave its card pinned over the front page after the popout closed, with nothing on screen to say where it had come from. A card belongs to the view it was raised from, so it now goes whenever a dialog closes, not only when one opens.
  • The Enrichr panel can be made wider or narrower by dragging its left edge, and it remembers the width for the session. The Fill the window button is now Full window, and its opposite is Beside the network: each says where it takes you rather than describing a layout.
  • The mark style and colour for highlighted genes sit in the Enrichr panel too, beside the line about clicking a row. They are the same setting as Mark in the network's Settings panel, not a copy: changing it in one place moves the control in the other and redraws the network once.

v.88.127 (2026-08-30)

  • Fix: a floating panel could be dragged sideways but not up or down. Its position is pinned by a CSS rule that uses !important, and the drag wrote a plain inline style, which loses to it. Every draggable dialog now writes its position at the same priority, so the Enrichr panel moves in both directions.
  • Enrichr beside the network is wider, so the gene and count columns are on screen instead of cut off at the right edge. Phones and narrow tablets keep the condensed layout.
  • A row's gene list is cut at a comma, and later than before. It was cut at 60 characters wherever that landed, so a row ended "TP5…"; with the wider panel most rows now show every gene without expanding.
  • The genes in each row read down two or three columns rather than one per line, which was making every row tall enough to hide the next, and they are in alphabetical order now: a row's genes are a set, and alphabetical is the order that lets you find one.

v.88.126 (2026-08-30)

  • "Open a view from AI", shorter than what it was called yesterday, and the trailing dots are gone from it, from Custom export for AI and from Open saved figure. They meant "this opens a dialog", which is a convention worth less than the clutter.

v.88.125 (2026-08-29)

  • An assistant can now open a view on your screen instead of describing one. Reading an export, it can write a CORRELATE-VIEW block naming a plot and its settings; paste that into Options › Other › Open a view from AI and the app builds it. Three views to begin with: a scatter of two genes on any measure, a gene-effect view across tissues, and the cell line list sorted by a measure, each with optional tissue and disease filters. Its "why" line is shown when the view opens, so what to look for arrives with the picture. The two block types are no longer a trap either: paste an export request into the view box, or a view into the export box, and each hands it to the other.
  • The numbered reading steps arrive in order. They are assembled by filtering a longer list and then appending one at the end, so a file could carry Step 3b before Step 3a and Step 3 last. They are sorted by their own number now.
  • Assistants are asked to argue with figures. The reading instructions now say that a claim resting on a shape in the data deserves a drawing, that one figure carrying the argument beats three decorating it, and that where the app can draw the same thing it should supply the view block too, so you can open it and click around rather than only look at a static picture.

v.88.124 (2026-08-29)

  • The export says how much of the release its matrices carry. They are variance-filtered, often to a fifth of the genes, and the file never gave a denominator, so a reading assistant took "this gene is not in the file" for "this gene is not a partner" and reported it as a negative result. A new matrixCoverage block states carried versus in-release for both matrices, and each matrix's own description now says outright that an absent gene was filtered, never measured as flat, and can be asked for by name.
  • A new assay note on what a pooled screen cannot show. Every knockout grows beside thousands of others, so anything secreted and shared is invisible: interferon, and everything upstream of it, scores near zero while the receptor and below score strongly. That boundary is the assay, not the biology, and two assistants spent a round each on it. The note gives the interferon case as the worked example.
  • Fix: a custom export of a closed plot described its axes as "?". It now reads the axis controls, and where even those are empty it says the axes were not recorded and points at the companion image, instead of writing a gene called "?" into the description.

v.88.123 (2026-08-29)

  • The instructions an assistant reads before writing a request block are clearer about what it cannot know. The block it writes chooses values on your behalf without seeing your screen, and cohort: view is the line that goes wrong. That is now said at the top of the section, not only in the key's own entry, and a second worked example shows the safe shape: a named gene panel across the whole release, which needs nothing open. The genes entry also states that superseded symbols are swapped for the current ones and the swap reported, so an assistant writes the symbol it knows rather than leaving a gene out.

v.88.122 (2026-08-29)

  • A pasted request asking for "cohort: view" says so straight away when nothing is open. That line means "whatever the app is showing", which an assistant writing the block cannot see. The dialog used to report it as understood and then refuse at Export, which read as the whole block being rejected. It is now flagged on Apply, with the fix named: open the view first, or ask for all or a named group. The syntax handed to assistants leads with those instead, and warns about this.
  • Renamed gene symbols in a pasted list are resolved. An assistant writes the symbol it learned, and HGNC keeps renaming: DDX58 is RIGI in this release. The synonym table the gene box already uses is now consulted here too, and the dialog reports what it renamed rather than calling a live gene missing.

v.88.121 (2026-08-29)

  • Slow jobs now say they are running. A full Export for AI takes tens of seconds, and the button gave no sign it had been pressed, so the natural response was to press it again. Export, Find correlates, Inspect selected vs rest and Inspect A vs B now put a spinner on the button, stop accepting clicks while they work, and count the seconds beside them. The export finishes with the time it took.
  • Clearer wording on the export format. The note claimed chat assistants cannot open a compressed file. The truth is narrower: a .gz has to be unpacked first, which needs a code or data-analysis tool switched on, so plain is the safer upload rather than the only one that works.

v.88.120 (2026-08-29)

  • Fix: a pinned gene card could not be dismissed once you had clicked it. The click-outside-to-close listener was set to fire once, so any click on the card itself, a link in it or just its text, used the listener up and nothing outside it closed the card afterwards. On a phone that is the only exit the card offers, so one tap left it stuck over whatever was underneath. A card also now closes when Export for AI opens, the same as when a popout opens: it belongs to the view behind the dialog, and it draws above every dialog.
  • The export dialog says why plain .json is the default. Most chat assistants cannot open a compressed attachment, so plain is offered first and anything over 8 MB switches to .gz on its own. The rule now appears under the two choices, since the exact sizes cannot be known until the file has been built.

v.88.119 (2026-08-29)

  • Fill both gates from the two ends of a sorted list. Sort the Cell Line Browser by drug response, expression, copy number, interferon or retroelement signal, then Top / bottom puts the strongest share into gate A and the weakest into gate B, 25 % each by default and adjustable. Only cell lines that actually carry a value for that sort are eligible, so the unmeasured tail every value sort collects at its end can never become a gate.
  • Fix: an alteration measured in one cell line headed the comparison table. Copy-number rows rest only on the lines with whole-genome sequencing, so a gate of four could contribute a single line, and "100 % (1/1) against 0 % (0/3)" scored a perfect 100-point gap and sorted above every row resting on real numbers. Rows that could not be tested now sort below the ones that could, and a ⚠ marks any side standing on fewer than three cell lines.

v.88.118 (2026-08-28)

  • The AI export says how the cell line list was ordered. A group taken off the top or the bottom of a sorted list is defined by whatever the list was sorted by, and the file never said. Browser gates now record the ordering in force at the moment each gate was filled, not at export time, so changing the sort afterwards cannot misdescribe them; when both gates came from the same ordering the file states outright that the split is one-dimensional on that measure.

v.88.117 (2026-08-28)

  • Export for AI carries the retroelement signal and the interferon score per cell line. Both are measures a group can be built on, since the Cell Line Browser sorts by either, but neither was in the file: a reader asked to explain a LINE-1-high versus LINE-1-low split could not see the axis that produced the split, and said so. Each line now carries its LINE-1, HERV-K, SVA and total CPM with the top-decile flag, and its interferon score. Absence is stated rather than left to inference: only 669 of the 1,208 lines have an alignment to measure retroelements from, and a line without the field was never measured, which is not a zero.

v.88.116 (2026-08-28)

  • The Cell Line Browser gates work on a phone. They are filled by ticking rather than by dragging, so unlike the heatmap's gates there is nothing about them a touch screen cannot do. Each Set Gate button now stays joined to its own count when the toolbar wraps, and the count and its clear link are sized for a finger.

v.88.115 (2026-08-28)

  • Two gates in the Cell Line Browser, compared against each other. Until now a selection could only be measured against the rest of the panel. Tick some cell lines and press Set Gate A, tick others and press Set Gate B, then Inspect A vs B compares the two directly, gene by gene, with the same tables, volcano and statistics the heatmap gates produce. Sort by drug response first and the two ends of the list become the two gates. Setting a gate clears the ticks so the other one can be picked, members are tagged in the list, and the gates survive a saved view.

v.88.114 (2026-08-28)

  • Fix: the compound list scrolled over its own heading. In the Cell Line Browser's drug-response sort, the explanation pinned at the top of the compound list was painted over by the compounds themselves, leaving two lines of text on top of each other. The rows are dimmed to mark broadly-cytotoxic compounds, and that dimming was enough to let them cover the heading. The gene and copy-number pickers had the same weakness and were fixed with it.

v.88.113 (2026-08-26)

  • Fix: the arrow naming a cell line pointed at nothing. Row labels are shortened to fit (hard on a phone, to 9 characters), but the arrow still asked for the full name, which matches no row, so it was dropped in open space between the boxes. It now anchors to the label the row actually carries. The arrow also no longer tries to land on rows the p-value filter has removed from the chart.
  • The comparison picker reaches the phone. "All lineages / this lineage, by primary disease / by disease", and the two sides when a gene was opened from a comparison, sat in the export row, which phones hide in full. It now sits on its own above that row, full width and tappable, so the chart's comparison can be changed there as on a desktop.

v.88.112 (2026-08-25)

  • The interferon and retroelement sorts start at the top. Both opened lowest-first, which put the unremarkable lines on screen and buried the answer. "Which lines are interferon-high" is the question those sorts exist for, so they now run highest to lowest, like the expression and copy-number sorts. The direction button reverses them as before.

v.88.111 (2026-08-24)

  • Fix: the expression correlates in Find correlates were computed on misaligned data. The expression matrix covers more cell lines than the CRISPR screen and holds them in a different order, but the list was reading it with the screen's row positions, so every value belonged to some other cell line. The top expression correlates of TP53 gene effect were noise; they are now EDA2R, PTCHD4, ZMAT3, RPS27L and CDKN1A, and the r in the list matches the r on the plot you land on.
  • Fix: picking an expression correlate said the gene does not exist. Expression covers thousands of genes the screen never targets, and an Expr axis was still being checked against the gene-effect list, so a gene the panel had just offered was rejected. The Expr axis is now checked against the expression data, and the "Open in Gene Effect" button beside it appears for those genes too.
  • Test Genes steps back once there are genes in the box. It is an invitation for an empty box; with a list in place it is only a way to wipe what was typed, so it drops its green.

v.88.110 (2026-08-21)

  • The comparison tissue picker is a proper popout. "Pick tissues / diseases" in the selection inspect now opens a draggable, searchable panel instead of a cramped sidebar box. Each row carries a level tag (tissue / subtype / disease), because a subtype can share its name with one of its diseases: Melanoma the subtype also holds Acral and Cutaneous Melanoma, so "melanoma" at the two levels means two different sets of cell lines.

v.88.109 (2026-08-21)

  • Low-coverage genes can be filtered out, not just flagged. Some genes are only measured in a subset of cell lines, so their rows rest on less data. The selection inspect gains a "Hide ⚠ genes with data in fewer lines" tick (searching still finds them), the mutation analysis table gains "hide * genes", and the heatmap gains a Gene min n control that hides gene rows measured in fewer than n of the shown lines, naming what it hid in the summary.

v.88.108 (2026-08-21)

  • Lined-up genes keep their spacing. Changing the font or node size, or adding gene effect to the labels, now re-spaces the lined up below/right block, so labels no longer overlap after the controls change.
  • "Correlating genes only" always means what it says. The network's Heatmap menu now classifies genes by how each node was drawn (input vs surfaced by correlation) instead of re-reading the input box, which could be empty after a restore and made the choice behave like "All network genes".
  • Annotation row order matches the heatmap. Turning Sort on for a row that sits below unsorted rows moves it to Row 1, because that is where the heatmap draws it (the block strip is always on top). The list and the picture can no longer disagree.

v.88.107 (2026-08-21)

  • Code comment cleanup. Source comments rewritten for clarity: shorter, no version history or dates in the code itself (that lives in this changelog and git). No behavior changes.

v.88.106 (2026-08-20)

  • The clusters row has no off state. A Cell-line clusters row with Sort off did nothing at all (no colours, no order), which read as a broken control. The row now clusters for as long as it exists; remove it with its x to stop clustering. Rows from older saved views switch on when reopened.

v.88.105 (2026-08-20)

  • Subtype is pickable on its own. The subtype dropdowns (main parameters, gene effect popout, scatter) used to sit empty until a lineage or disease was chosen; they now list every subtype with counts from the start, the same way the disease dropdown always worked, and rescope when a lineage or disease narrows them.

v.88.104 (2026-08-20)

  • The alteration table sorts by clicking its headers. In the inspect's Genetic alterations panel, click a column to sort by it (Alteration A to Z, the two percentages, Δ%, or p with untested rows kept at the bottom), click again to reverse, and a third time to return to the default ranking. And the column words are real words now: "% selected" and "% others" instead of "% sel" and "% rest" (gate views say "% gate A" / "% gate B").

v.88.103 (2026-08-20)

  • Colour by GE / expression, simplified and scalable. The unintuitive "GE / Absolute" sub-choice is gone: gene effect always colours on its signed orange-to-purple scale. In its place, one choice that works for both measures: scale the colours to the genes on screen (default) or to the whole input set, so a gene keeps its colour when others are hidden. The export legends follow the same choice. In mRNA mode nothing gene-effect-specific shows any more.

v.88.102 (2026-08-20)

  • Network polish, three pieces. Floating input genes now settle on a ring around the connected network instead of freezing wherever the solver left them, sometimes right among the connected nodes. The coarse pan arrows and - / + buttons are gone (drag and scroll do the same job smoothly); the fit button stays. And the Enrichr menu states each choice's gene count for the current run: "All input genes (n=18)", "Correlated genes (the clusters) (n=11)", "Everything in the network (n=18)".

v.88.101 (2026-08-20)

  • Gene-value annotation rows use the full colour range. The expression / gene effect bands were coloured on the whole-panel z scale, so a small cohort whose values sit close together drew as one washed-out shade. The band now stretches its colours across the range of the shown lines, edge to edge; the legend states the numeric range and says "coloured across this range", so the picture stays honest.

v.88.100 (2026-08-20)

  • Min n stays with the grouping it was set for. A threshold chosen for lineage blocks used to keep applying after the blocking moved elsewhere: drilling into a lineage could land on an empty grid, and blocking by a hotspot could silently swallow the mutated groups (an Eye cohort with Min n 9 drew one wild-type block and hid both CDKN2A-mutated groups). Now the threshold resets to 1 whenever the blocking row changes or a drill starts, and going back from a drill restores it. Within the same grouping it keeps whatever you set.

v.88.99 (2026-08-20)

  • The sort "score" says what it is. The options on lineage / subtype / disease rows now read "Median gene score, high first / low first", and the control's hover text spells it out: each cell line's score is its mean of the shown genes, and the groups are ordered by their median of that. The selects widened to fit.

v.88.98 (2026-08-20)

  • No two Sort options that do the same thing. On hotspot, fusion, copy-number and gates rows the "Score high/low" choices were withdrawn: with only two or three fixed categories they almost always reproduced the level order (wild-type first / altered first), so the list offered two names for one picture. Lineage, subtype and disease rows keep their score ordering, where ranking many blocks by median score is a genuinely different view.

v.88.97 (2026-08-20)

  • Heatmap toolbar text no longer runs under its arrows. The "then by" select ("Score (mean of shown genes)") and the cohort select ("The cell lines the browser is filtered to") were narrower than their own labels, so the dropdown arrow sat on top of the text. Both widened to fit; a sweep of every other select in the toolbar found no further clipping.

v.88.96 (2026-08-20)

  • Lined-up gene labels no longer touch. The parked block's spacing is now taken from the real measured width of the widest label instead of a per-character estimate, which had swung from too airy to overlapping. Compact, with a clear gap between neighbours, at any font size.

v.88.95 (2026-08-20)

  • The lined-up genes pack tightly. The parked block's spacing was measured on the label text INCLUDING its italic markup, so a 6-letter gene was spaced as if it were 13 characters wide and the block sprawled across twice the room it needed. Measured on the visible text now, plus tighter padding: the below variant reads as one neat footnote row, the right variant as a compact column beside the network, and the network itself draws larger since less of the canvas is wasted. The network's Heatmap button also drops its down-arrow.

v.88.94 (2026-08-20)

  • Exports print at the width you asked for. PNG and TIFF used to be stamped with the pre-trim resolution, so after the automatic whitespace trim a 12 cm request printed at about 11 cm and some exports lost up to a quarter of their width. The density is now derived from the pixels actually in the file, matching how PDF and PowerPoint already honoured the chosen size.

v.88.93 (2026-08-20)

  • Export housekeeping from the audit's leftovers. Four CSVs now carry their scope in the filename (network correlations and clusters get the lineage/subtype, the scatter gets its tissue filter, the Cell Line Browser list its active filters, the mutation grid its filter label), and the correlations CSV gains the same # provenance block its clusters sibling always had. The mutation analysis CSV in functional loss / amplification / deletion mode names its columns as the screen does (Intact / Lost, WT / Amp) and drops the copy-number columns that never applied there, including a p-value of 1 for a test that was never run. The long-dead full-screen Compare modal (unreachable since v.84.33) is deleted outright.

v.88.92 (2026-08-20)

  • Network polish. "Show all input genes" is no longer on by default (Floating stays the default arrangement once it is switched on), and the "Lined up right" block is now properly centred on the network's vertical middle instead of sitting pressed toward the top.

v.88.91 (2026-08-20)

  • The heatmap's exported text is editable. Settings gains "Text on the exported figure": the title and the caption line each have a box (empty keeps the automatic wording, shown grayed) and an on/off tick to leave the line out of image exports and Copy. Custom text rides Save view. The .csv, Methods and AI exports keep the automatic text, so the record of how the figure was made stays intact.

v.88.90 (2026-08-20)

  • The heatmap's annotation rows are the hierarchy, plainly. Row order now IS the sort order: the first row with Sort on splits the columns into blocks, rows below it sort within each block, and rows with Sort off just paint colours. The ▦ blocks button and the arrow toggles are gone; each row carries one Sort select with choices that fit it: largest or smallest group first, A to Z, score high or low (blocks ordered by their median score), and for alteration rows wild-type first (0, 1, 2) or altered first (2, 1, 0).
  • Clustering is just a row now. The Cluster cell lines checkbox and its toolbar selects are gone; add a Cell-line clusters row instead. First in the list it orders the whole cohort by the dendrogram; below a sorted row it clusters within each of that row's blocks. Its one setting: No split (tree only, the default, no coloured band) or Auto / 2-8 coloured clusters. Cell-line tree drawing detail moved into Settings.
  • Better default. The heatmap opens blocked by Lineage with blocks ordered by median score (by Disease when the cohort is already one lineage), TP53 hotspot as a colour row below. Old saved views reopen unchanged: the old blocks flag is translated into the new row order.

v.88.89 (2026-08-20)

  • All input genes show in the network by default, floating. "Show all input genes" starts on, and genes without a surviving correlation drift freely around the network instead of parking in a row. The lined-up option now comes in two placements: below the network (as before) or in a column to its right. The Methods text names whichever arrangement is in force.

v.88.88 (2026-08-20)

  • Export for AI always offers a picture of the view. The dialog has a new "Also save an image of the view" choice, on by default, and the companion PNG now also covers the views that never produced one: the selection / gate inspect (volcanoes, tables and panels as on screen), the Cell Line Browser list and the cell line wiki. Charts inside those panels are rendered by Plotly itself before the screenshot, so they come out crisp and in place.
  • Alignment. The "Where the cell lines come from" panel's three tables (tissue / subtype / disease) now share one column layout, so % in A, % in B and Direction line up down the whole panel instead of drifting per table.

v.88.87 (2026-08-20)

  • The condensed Methods paragraph now reads like a Materials and Methods section. Every view's short paragraph was rewritten in paper register: data source, cohort, method with its thresholds and tests, software. Result numbers (r values, pair and cluster counts, rows listed), on-screen display state (tick boxes, list caps reached) and reader instructions moved out; they stay in the long section and on screen, where they always were. The date and the DepMap acknowledgment also live in the long section's header rather than in the paragraph meant for pasting into a manuscript.

v.88.86 (2026-08-20)

  • Two full export audits, fifteen fixes. Every image export and every data export was driven through the real UI, in plain and worked states, and everything found broken is fixed. Data side: the gate-mode inspect CSV names gate A / gate B in its columns; the heatmap CSV corner cell now tells the truth about hidden groups, silenced genes, min-n and hidden no-data lines, and the annotation bands ship as rows; the AI export from a scatter now carries the gates it always promised and no longer claims to have no precomputed lists while shipping three; the AI export from a mutation analysis applies the additional hotspot / fusion filters to its cohort, so its counts match the table on screen; the custom AI export no longer attaches a screenshot of a view it just disclaimed, and no longer silently loses a cell line whose display name could not be resolved back; three CSVs (oncoprint, both correlation-analysis exports) now pass the formula-injection guard like every other CSV.
  • Image side. The gene-effect chart keeps its title and filter line after a filter or cell-line search (a highlight redraw was deleting the title annotation); the network SVG draws the highlight rings, honours the chosen print width and carries each node's real border; the network raster export never stretches into ellipses when the dialog remembers another view's height; PCA/UMAP transparent background is actually transparent; "the whole panel" screenshots no longer paint a second, giant copy of the chart and now print at the width you asked for; and the regression line is clipped to the plot again in every scatter export (the legend un-clipping was un-clipping the data layer too).

v.88.85 (2026-08-19)

  • The gate export passed a blind-reader audit, after fixes. A reading assistant given yesterday's gate file with no other knowledge found the gate membership filed where the file's own index called it absent, a leftover sentence claiming the comparison side was not included, and the only statistically significant genes hidden outside the exported lists. All fixed: the two gates are a properly indexed top-level section, the composition of BOTH gates is tallied, every differential list now ships a significance-first companion (top 50 by q) plus a one-glance summary of how many genes survive correction, the selection-vs-gate-A column mapping is stated in words, and the not-included section no longer describes things the file actually carries.

v.88.84 (2026-08-19)

  • Export for AI understands gates. Exporting the inspect while it compares two gates now ships BOTH gates' cell lines in full, states which line belongs to which gate, and carries the gates' provenance: where they were drawn (the named scatter axes or the heatmap), each rectangle's bounds, a warning when two gates really amount to a one-dimensional split, and a note when the two groups are very unequal. A reader can now re-split or recompute the contrast from the file alone; before, only gate A's lines were included.

v.88.83 (2026-08-19)

  • Methods knows which build it is in. The Methods texts now name the app from the page itself and cite the address they are generated at, so the standard and CoExpress builds write their own name and URL instead of this one's, and a build without a version badge simply leaves the version out.

v.88.82 (2026-08-19)

  • One comparison view everywhere. Compare on the scatter's gates now opens the same comparison the Cell Line Browser and the heatmap gates open, instead of the small tabbed panel that used to appear under the plot. That means the volcano, both ranked gene tables (gene effect and expression, with q-values), the collapsible "where the cell lines come from" panel and the full alteration panel with its chips, all reading gate A against gate B.
  • The comparison opens on top of the scatter and closes back to it with both gates, their chips and the plot untouched, so Compare can be pressed again after moving a gate. Apply gate as filter, Clear and the gate drawing itself are unchanged.
  • The retired panel's own Methods, image export and AI export are gone with it; the comparison view carries its own Methods, exports and Enrichr, and its Methods now names the plot each gate was drawn on.

v.88.81 (2026-08-19)

  • The comparison panels are in every inspect, not just the gates. Inspect selected vs rest now carries the same two collapsible panels the heatmap gates got: where the cell lines come from (tissue, subtype, disease) and how their genetic alterations differ, always comparing your selection against whatever comparison group is in force, whether that is the rest of the panel, the same lineage, a picked group or a pasted list. Both start closed, and their headers name the two sides the same way the gene tables do.
  • The alteration panel covers everything, ranked by the size of the difference. Hotspot mutations, damaging mutations, fusion calls, focal amplifications and deep deletions are all one ranked table now, ordered by the gap in percent altered rather than by p. Chips across the top narrow it to a single type, a type with nothing to show stays in place greyed out, and the table opens at the top 25 with a Show all button so a long comparison does not lock the panel.
  • Every row says what it rests on. Each side carries its carriers over its group size, copy-number rows count only the cell lines with whole-genome sequencing rather than treating unsequenced lines as event-free, and a side with fewer than three cell lines carrying a call is listed but marked not tested.
  • The Methods text for the selection inspect and for the scatter's gate comparison now describe their alteration tables from the same source the tables are drawn from, so each states its own coverage.

v.88.80 (2026-08-19)

  • Blocks and sorting are now two separate choices. Every annotation row has its own ▦ blocks toggle beside its sort arrows. One row at a time can be the blocks, wherever it sits in the list, and the colour strip, its labels, the legend, Min n and the drill all follow that row; its arrows then set the order of the blocks. Every other row's arrows sort inside the blocks, top row first. Before this, the topmost row with its arrows on quietly became the blocks, which meant sorting by a row and blocking by it could not be asked for separately.
  • The gates are an annotation row. The thin gates band is gone; as soon as a gate holds a cell line, a Gates row joins the list, with its own label, legend, tooltip, sort arrows and blocks toggle, so the columns can be blocked or sorted by gate A, gate B, both or none. Its × clears both gates, and the row leaves with them. Painting the gates is unchanged: arm Gate A or Gate B and drag across the grid.
  • Double-click a lineage, subtype or disease band to open the Cell Line Browser holding exactly that category's cell lines from the heatmap. The heatmap stays open behind it. Double-clicking anywhere else on a column still opens that cell line's wiki.
  • Cluster cell lines no longer adds a lineage row you did not ask for. It adds the Cell-line clusters row and nothing else.
  • Older saved views still open. A view saved under any earlier heatmap version reproduces its old drawing: its grouping becomes the blocks row (reusing an existing row of that kind rather than adding a duplicate) and its sort becomes the sort arrows.
  • The help texts caught up. The Cell Line Browser help now describes the annotation-row ordering, all six sorts, the four Inspect comparison groups and Send to another view; How Correlate Works introduces the Methods button; Reference Data lists the full gene-level copy-number matrix with its hybrid provenance, the retroelement signal source and the interferon score definition.

v.88.79 (2026-08-19)

  • No more saying it twice. When a row's sort arrows make it the block strip, that row no longer also draws its own colour band and second legend entry beneath the grid: the strip and its legend carry it alone. The same applies to the clusters row while the cluster groups are the strip.
  • The gene tree's colours are a choice. A new select beside Cluster genes (Tree order only / Auto / 2-12 groups) controls whether the gene tree's branches are coloured by subtree, and a fresh heatmap opens with the tree plain, matching how the cell-line side works.

v.88.78 (2026-08-19)

  • Every view can explain itself. A new Methods button sits beside the export buttons of the scatter, the gene effect view, expression correlates, correlation by group, the mutation analysis, the network and its two tables, the heatmap, the Cell Line Browser, selection inspect, gate comparison and the UMAP / PCA plot. It writes out how what is on screen was made, in two forms: one paragraph in materials-and-methods voice, ready to paste into a manuscript, and a longer plain-language walk-through of the cohort, the settings, the statistics and what the numbers do and do not say. Both are read from the view as it stands right now, so changing a filter and asking again gives different text; each has its own Copy, and Download .txt saves both.

v.88.77 (2026-08-19)

  • The gene tree shows its groups. The dendrogram beside the gene labels is now coloured by subtree: the tree is cut where its own structure suggests, and each group of co-behaving genes gets one colour, with the branches above the cut staying gray. Display only, the row order is unchanged.

v.88.76 (2026-08-19)

  • One ordering hierarchy. The heatmap's separate Sort row is gone: the annotation rows now carry the whole column order. Toggle a row's arrows and it blocks the columns; the next toggled row sorts within those blocks, with score as the final tie-break. Cell-line clustering now appears as its own annotation row when enabled, so clustering can be placed under a lineage row to cluster within each lineage. A fresh heatmap opens sorted by plain score. Min n, Show median and Redraw live on the Cell lines row.

v.88.75 (2026-08-19)

  • Scrolling beside a narrow heatmap. When the heatmap is narrower than its panel, the empty space to its right still belongs to the grid's sideways scroller and was swallowing vertical scrolls; scrolling now works across the whole panel regardless of how wide the drawn grid is.

v.88.74 (2026-08-19)

  • Send to the heatmap. The Cell Line Browser's "Send to another view" now includes the heatmap: Highlight marks the sent cell lines as gate A above the columns, ready for gate inspect; Only these draws the heatmap on just them, with a note saying where the cohort came from. Clear all of these covers both.

v.88.73 (2026-08-19)

  • Gates grew up. With both heatmap gates filled, Inspect A vs B opens the browser's inspect comparing the two gates directly, volcano first, with collapsible panels comparing where the gates come from (lineage, subtype, disease) and their genetic alteration percentages, the same statistics the scatter's gate comparison uses. The inspect's own gene lists gained Open in heatmap with the top-N menu, and gate controls are hidden on phones where dragging cannot work.

v.88.72 (2026-08-19)

  • Sort direction on annotation rows. The sort button on each annotation row now cycles: sort, reversed, off, with the arrow showing the direction, so wild-type-first or smallest-groups-first views are one click away.

v.88.71 (2026-08-19)

  • Scrolling works beside the heatmap too. The empty space to the right of the grid belongs to the grid's sideways scroller, which was swallowing vertical scrolls; a mostly-vertical wheel over any sideways-only scroller now scrolls the page or dialog like everywhere else.

v.88.70 (2026-08-18)

  • The annotation rows are now the sort. Every annotation row has a sort toggle: toggled rows order the columns top-down, Row 1 outermost, alterations altered-first and categories biggest-first, with a then-by choice (score or name) inside the innermost blocks. The old sort dropdown is gone; saved views and handoffs translate automatically.

v.88.69 (2026-08-18)

  • Heatmap default view, take two. A fresh heatmap now opens grouped by lineage with the columns score-sorted inside each block, or grouped by disease when the view is already narrowed to a single lineage, with a TP53 hotspot annotation row ready and medians shown by default. Copy-number annotation rows now draw (the gene picker's decorated values were never stripped, so the rows were silently dropped). The annotation-row legends under the grid now state each category's n, and its median score when Show median is on. Clustering is one click away as before, with the suggested cluster count intact, and turning it on still brings the lineage colours along as a row.

v.88.68 (2026-08-18)

  • CRISPR and mRNA no longer share colours. Gene-effect views now run orange (negative, dependency) to purple (dispensable), a colourblind-safe pair, while mRNA keeps the universal blue-to-red with red high. The same two colours meant opposite numeric directions across the two data types, which read as a bug; now a glance says which data type a heatmap shows. Legends and captions state the mapping as before.

v.88.67 (2026-08-18)

  • Open in heatmap, from the mutation analysis and the browser. The mutation analysis results table and the Cell Line Browser's gene lists gain Open in heatmap: pick the top 10 to 100 genes or type any number, and the heatmap opens on exactly the cell lines and filters the source view was using, with the analysed mutation carried as an annotation row and the columns blocked mutated-first where it applies.

v.88.66 (2026-08-18)

  • Colouring the network by expression now looks like expression. mRNA values were being pushed through the signed gene-effect colour ramp centred at zero, so every node landed on one half, flat colours under a wide-looking legend still labelled gene effect. Expression mode now uses the same white-to-green scale as the heatmap's raw expression, fitted to the shown values, the legend says mRNA expression (log2 TPM+1) with real bounds, node labels read Expr instead of GE, and the signed/absolute choice greys out where it has no meaning. Gene-effect colouring is unchanged.

v.88.65 (2026-08-18)

  • Network cleanup, AI files any assistant can open, and the phone heatmap button. Running a new network clears the previous run's removed-genes banner. Export for AI offers a plain .json (chat assistants often cannot open .json.gz), picking the best default by size, with a copyable instruction line for the assistant. On phones the network's Heatmap button now sits above the graph instead of hidden inside the collapsed View controls panel, and its menu no longer flashes closed on a tap; real-device check still pending.

v.88.64 (2026-08-18)

  • The heatmap became hands-on. Double-click a column to open that cell line's wiki. Click a gene name to silence it, removing it from the drawing and the score, with one click to restore. And two gates, A and B: arm a gate, drag across columns to collect cell lines, then copy them, clear them, or open the browser's inspect on exactly that set; gates survive re-sorting because they hold the lines, not the positions.

v.88.63 (2026-08-18)

  • Clustered by default, with a suggested cluster count. The heatmap opens with the cell lines clustered and coloured into an automatically suggested number of clusters (pick your own under Clustering), lineage colours underneath, and the colours scaled against all cell lines by default so a filtered view still says where the lines sit among all cancers. The tree-detail selects say they only change the drawing, and a ? beside Scaling explains exactly how the colours are computed, per gene, never across the gene set, with the legend stating the scale in use.

v.88.62 (2026-08-18)

  • Heatmap fixes. The clustering controls sit together on their own toolbar row. Show median works whenever there are groups to label, including coloured clusters, instead of being tied to the Group by choice. Clicking outside the heatmap no longer closes it. And adding an annotation row now opens the gene picker and says the row draws once a gene is picked, instead of silently showing nothing.

v.88.61 (2026-08-16)

  • Dendrograms fit their content. Trees with fewer than a handful of leaves are not drawn at all (a two-gene bracket says nothing), the tree band above the grid never grows taller than the grid itself, and the coarseness setting self-limits on small trees so Very coarse and Minimal never reduce a small group to bare stems.

v.88.60 (2026-08-16)

  • Gene-effect heatmaps colour dependency red. On gene-effect views red now marks negative values, the dependencies, and blue the dispensable genes, matching the DepMap convention and putting the heat on the biology; expression keeps red = high. The legend, captions and AI export state the mapping for each data type.

v.88.59 (2026-08-16)

  • The alteration-grouping gene box got real. Picking the gene for Group by: Genetic alteration now works like the other filter boxes: a searchable list showing each gene's mutation count in the currently filtered cell lines, most mutated first, including the genes scored by damaging mutations.

v.88.58 (2026-08-16)

  • Network filters follow into the heatmap. Opening the heatmap from the network now uses exactly the cell lines the analysis was run on, stated in the summary line; change the Cell lines box to leave that cohort.

v.88.57 (2026-08-16)

  • Sorting on annotation rows, made obvious, and clustering means everything. Checking Cluster cell lines now clusters the whole cohort into one tree, switching grouping off and keeping lineage visible as a colour row, since that is what the question usually is; pick a grouping afterwards for within-group trees. Annotation rows can be reordered with arrows, and row order is sort order: the annotation-rows sort blocks the columns by Row 1, then Row 2 within, and so on. The sort options say what they do, and the summary line points out when annotation rows are shown but not sorted on. The network's Enrichr menu also states its choices plainly: all input genes, or everything in the network.

v.88.56 (2026-08-16)

  • Subtype and disease annotation rows. The heatmap's annotation rows can now show subtype and Oncotree disease alongside lineage, mutations, fusions and copy number, with the same colours, legends and altered-first sorting.

v.88.55 (2026-08-16)

  • Tree detail moves next to the clustering toggles. Two selects in the top row now control how much branch detail the gene tree (left) and the cell-line tree (top) draw, from Full down to two new coarser levels, Very coarse and Minimal. The setting is out of the Settings panel and beside the toggles it belongs to, still remembered and still carried into saved views and exports.

v.88.54 (2026-08-16)

  • The heatmap says when it is working. A draw that takes longer than about two seconds, typically the first open on a large cohort, now shows the same working spinner the analysis run uses, instead of looking frozen. Quick draws finish before the spinner would appear, so nothing flickers.

v.88.53 (2026-08-16)

  • Cluster the whole panel. Cell-line clustering now handles every line at once (the limit rises from 400 to 1,300) thanks to a faster exact algorithm producing the same trees. And turning clustering on adds a lineage colour row automatically when none is set, so whether the cell lines cluster by lineage or by something else is visible at a glance in the colours under the grid.

v.88.52 (2026-08-16)

  • Fix: the grid no longer slips 60px below its gene labels. Leaving a state that had drawn the cell-line dendrogram (for example turning off grouping on a cohort too large to cluster) left an invisible box where the tree had been, shifting every row below its label. The box is now fully removed with the tree.

v.88.51 (2026-08-16)

  • Clustering, tidied. Cluster genes and Cluster cell lines now sit together in the top row. A Tree detail setting (Settings) draws the cell-line dendrograms at full, medium or coarse resolution, collapsing the finest branches when they are just visual noise. And within every cluster the columns now run high score to low instead of arbitrary order, so a clustered heatmap reads left to right like the score sort does.

v.88.50 (2026-08-16)

  • Dendrograms everywhere clustering runs, and honest empty columns. With a grouping active, Cluster cell lines now draws a small tree above each group instead of silently skipping the dendrogram; the single-tree view is unchanged. Cell lines with no data for the shown genes draw as hatched columns when shown, so hiding or showing them visibly means something, and their tooltip says why they are empty.

v.88.49 (2026-08-16)

  • The heatmap connects outward. The network gains a Heatmap button that draws its genes as a gene set heatmap: your input genes, every network gene, or only the correlating ones. And after drilling into a heatmap group or cluster, one click ticks exactly those cell lines in the Cell Line Browser, ready for its filters, sorts and exports.

v.88.48 (2026-08-16)

  • Heatmap settings, and views you can save. A Settings button adjusts the heatmap's font sizes and cell dimensions, for the screen and every export, same panel as the network's. And Save view downloads the whole configuration, gene set, cohort, filters, annotation rows, clustering, hidden groups and settings, as a small .json file: drop it on the app later and the exact heatmap reopens, including a snapshot of the cell lines it was drawn on.

v.88.47 (2026-08-16)

  • Cluster the cell lines, see the tree, ask why. A Cluster cell lines toggle orders the columns by similarity and draws a dendrogram above the grid, matching the gene tree on the left. A cluster-count setting cuts the tree into 2 to 12 clusters, coloured in the tree, the strip and the legend, with the usual click-to-hide and drill-down. The AI export then carries each cluster's composition, its lineages, subtypes and scores, so an assistant can answer what actually distinguishes the clusters. With a grouping active, clustering runs within each group as before.

v.88.46 (2026-08-16)

  • Annotation rows. The heatmap's second row grows into up to four annotation rows, each showing a lineage, a hotspot mutation, a fusion or copy number for a gene of your choice, picked from a searchable box that lists the most common genes first, scaled to the filters applied. A new sort, annotation rows (altered first), blocks the columns by those rows in order, all BRAF-mutated to the left, NRAS blocks within, expression-sorted inside every block, so the heatmap reads like an oncoprint.

v.88.45 (2026-08-16)

  • Heatmap polish. The toolbar boxes align into columns across the rows, and the genetic alteration filters sit together on their own line. Group labels under the colour strip stay inside the picture instead of getting cut mid-word, prefer one flat line of text, and only stagger with connector lines where it is genuinely crowded. The group legend says what clicking does: click hides or shows a group, double-click keeps only it. And a Copy genes button copies the shown genes in drawn order.

v.88.44 (2026-08-16)

  • Z-score basis, and mutation-dose grouping. The heatmap's z-score can now be computed against all cell lines instead of only the shown ones: a melanoma-only view of a MAPK signature looks flat scored within melanoma, and strong scored against the whole panel, and both readings are now available under Scaling. Grouping by a genetic alteration splits into wild-type, one copy and both copies, in that order, matching the second-row colours, so mutation dose reads directly off the blocks.

v.88.43 (2026-08-16)

  • The heatmap's controls now follow the browser's design. Same toolbar rows, same box sizes, with lineage and the genetic alteration filters side by side as in the Cell Line Browser, and every change applies immediately, no Redraw needed. Cell lines with no data for the shown genes are hidden by default, with a toggle and an honest count either way. Group labels under the grid use up to three staggered rows and standard abbreviations (DLBCL, CLL/SLL, AML), so most groups are named instead of only the widest two; very small groups keep their colour and legend entry but skip the text.

v.88.42 (2026-08-16)

  • Retroelement quick filters per family, and calmer scrolling. Beside retroelement-high there are now LINE-1-high, HERV-K-high and SVA-high quick filters, each the top tenth of the measured lines for that family, with the reasoning explained in the quick-filter info. This also fixes the filters not showing at all: quick filters added since v.81.74 needed a registration step that interferon-high, interferon-low and retroelement-high never got, so they existed but were invisible. All six appear now. Hover cards no longer chase the pointer while a list is scrolling; they stay away until the scroll settles, which makes the cell line browser noticeably easier to scroll.

v.88.41 (2026-08-16)

  • Wiki: retroelement histograms, plainer explanations. The retroelement section now shows where the line sits among the 669 measured lines, with a histogram for the total signal, each family and the active-element count, matching the genome section's panels. Its text sticks to what the score is and how it was measured. WGD, ploidy, aneuploidy and CIN in Genome signatures are explained in plain language, and the CIN tier text now matches the computed tier. The retroelement sort gains a chooser for which measurement to sort by: total, LINE-1, HERV-K, SVA or active elements.

v.88.40 (2026-08-15)

  • Heatmap filters now rescope each other. Picking a lineage immediately narrows the subtype and disease lists (and the map), instead of waiting for Redraw, and the genetic alteration filters narrow the counts those lists show. The colour rows under the grid now carry a title saying what they show, on screen and in exports. And the page scrolls normally with the pointer over the heatmap or any other drawn image; only the network keeps the wheel for zooming.

v.88.39 (2026-08-15)

  • Retroelement signal. Cell lines now carry a measured retroelement score: RNA-seq reads over 750 full-length LINE-1, HERV-K and SVA elements outside genes, computed from the public CCLE sequencing files for 669 lines. Sort the browser by it, filter with the new retroelement-high quick filter, and read it on each line's card and wiki, where high lines are highlighted. Lines with more element transcription depend measurably more on ADAR1, beyond what the interferon score predicts.

v.88.38 (2026-08-15)

  • The heatmap opens grouped by lineage, and can be narrowed much further. Subtype and disease filters sit beside the lineage box and scale to each other, a Min n control drops groups smaller than you care about, and double-clicking a lineage in the legend shows only that lineage split into its diseases, with a link back. A second annotation row under the group band can show lineage, a hotspot mutation or an amplification / deletion.
  • Fix: the exported heatmap had grey panels behind the labels and the colour scale. One was a background fill meant for the screen, the other a transparent hole punched through the export. Both are gone, so a saved figure is clean.
  • The exported heatmap says what it is. A caption names the gene set and the measure, then the cohort and where it came from, including the Cell Line Browser filters that produced it, the grouping and the scaling.
  • The heatmap resets when reopened, so a previous session's filters and drill-downs are not inherited.

v.88.37 (2026-08-15)

  • The heatmap splits cell lines by genetic alteration. Group by a gene and the lines separate into mutated and wild-type, so a pathway set can be read straight against the driver: MAPK output across BRAF-mutant lines sits at a median of 0.71 against 0.01 for wild-type. Hotspot, fusion and copy-number filters are available too, with the same levels and chips as the rest of the app.
  • Genes cluster by default, with a dendrogram. Genes that behave alike sit together every time, and the tree beside them shows how they group. A new gene set holds the 25 most often hotspot-mutated genes in the panel.
  • Groups can be ordered by score, highest first from the left, and their labels read n=42 with an optional median. Clicking a group in the legend hides it and clicking again brings it back.
  • Export for AI from the heatmap, with the picture saved beside the data. The .csv now states in its first cell what it holds: the measure, the scaling, the cohort and the grouping.

v.88.36 (2026-08-15)

  • Fix: switching the statistical test in the selection inspect froze the tab. The rank test had to build and sort a list of values for each of 18,531 genes, which locked the browser for minutes. The choice is gone and everything uses Welch's t, which is what it defaulted to. Where the groups are small the panel now says so, rather than offering a test that could not finish.
  • Searching a gene adds it to the volcano instead of emptying it. The table still narrows to what you searched for, but the plot keeps the genes it was showing and marks the searched ones in amber, larger and always labelled, so you can see where a gene sits relative to everything else.
  • Export for AI describes the view it was taken from, everywhere. Every export now carries a sentence describing what the picture actually shows, and the state that changes it travels with the file: the scatter's colouring, its clicked labels and an applied gate, the network's highlighted gene set, the browser's filters, and which statistical test was used. Charts save a matching .png beside the data.

v.88.35 (2026-08-15)

  • Fix: Export for AI described the wrong view when two groups were being compared. A chart comparing chosen cell lines against a lineage was exported as "gene effect across all cell lines", so a reader answered about the gene in general instead of about the contrast on screen. The file now names both groups with their sizes, means and the difference between them, and states what the plot looks like.
  • Export for AI saves the picture beside the data. A .png of the chart is written under the same name as the .json.gz, so the pair stays together and can be uploaded together, and the data file names the image so a reader knows to look for it.

v.88.34 (2026-08-15)

  • The heatmap covers fourteen gene sets, and can be split by group. Beyond the interferon signature there are now sets for TP53, NF-kB and MAPK output, MYC targets, cell cycle, EMT, hypoxia, senescence, apoptosis, antigen presentation, nucleic acid sensing, interferon gamma and retroelement silencing, each with a line saying what it reads out and what it cannot tell you. A lineage box narrows the heatmap to one tissue, and Group by arranges the cell lines by lineage, subtype or disease with a coloured band and labels under the plot, plus a legend with counts. Sorting and clustering then run inside each group. Grouping travels into the exported image and the .csv.

v.88.33 (2026-08-15)

  • The interferon score now explains itself. It appears on each cell line's own card with a "?" describing what it measures and what counts as high or low, the sort states what the numbers mean under the list, and the browser's help covers both the score and where to find the heatmap. Exported and copied lists label the column properly.

v.88.32 (2026-08-15)

  • Interferon score, and a gene set heatmap. Cell lines now carry a type I interferon score, the mean z-score across 34 interferon-stimulated genes, with quick filters for interferon-high and interferon-low and a matching sort in the browser. The new Gene set heatmap (Options, Other) draws any gene set against the cell lines a filter leaves showing: pick a preset or paste your own genes, choose mRNA or gene effect, and sort by score, lineage, name or by clustering similar profiles together. Exports as an image, to the clipboard or as a .csv.

v.88.31 (2026-08-15)

  • Fix: an exported network kept the highlight rings but lost the sentence explaining them. Marking genes from Enrichr writes a caption above the network saying which term they came from and its adjusted p-value, and that caption was on screen only, so a saved or copied figure showed rings whose meaning was gone. The caption now travels with the picture, in both the image and the vector export, wrapping to the figure width.

v.88.30 (2026-08-14)

  • The edge tap-for-r now works on the phone too, without overlapping boxes. The first tap on an edge shows the pair and its r; the second opens the correlation, on phones as on tablets. Showing the button now clears vis-network's own edge tooltip and any pinned gene card, which used to sit across it.
  • Fix: the gene info card could not be closed on an iPad. The card was pinned (interactive, with a close button and tap-anywhere-to-close) only on phones; a tablet got the hover version, which has no close and nothing to un-hover with a finger, so it sat over the chart for good. Any touch screen now gets the pinned card, and opening a popout from the network always clears it.

v.88.29 (2026-08-14)

  • iPad: tapping a network edge shows its r, and a second tap opens the correlation. An edge is a hard double-tap target on glass, and there is no hover to say what it holds. The first tap now answers with the pair and its r as a small button by your finger; tapping that opens the correlation popout, scrolled so the scatter plot is what you land on. Opening an edge by double-tap scrolls to the plot the same way. Desktop with a mouse is unchanged.

v.88.28 (2026-08-14)

  • iPad: Run and Update bring the result into view. The one-shot scroll the phone already had now also covers tablets, where the results likewise stack below the controls. Only a press moves the page; a chart redrawn for any other reason leaves it alone.

v.88.27 (2026-08-14)

  • iPad: a slightly shorter gene box, and no "Rank by" under Run. The paste box comes down three rows, and the Rank by / best-lineage picker that appears under the Run button after a run is hidden at tablet size, as it already is on a phone. The desktop keeps both as they were.

v.88.26 (2026-08-14)

  • iPad: the gene set analysis sidebar opens on a tap. "Lineage and disease" and "Genetic alterations" start as single lines that open when tapped, the same as on a phone, so the Run button sits right under the parameters. The gene paste box is taller in both input modes, standard and With Stats.

v.88.25 (2026-08-14)

  • New tab keeps every layer of the view. A gene opened from the browser's inspect and sent to a new tab used to arrive as the bare gene-effect chart; the comparison it was opened with (the selected lines vs the compared group), the red-marked selection, the measure, the scope and any pasted cell-line list now all travel along. The scatter's New tab likewise carries a gate-applied cohort, which lives outside the text box the other filters are read from.

v.88.24 (2026-08-14)

  • Filter boxes in the popouts scale to each other. In the gene-effect popout the subtype and disease counts were quoted from the whole panel while the tissue counts came from the lines actually measured for the gene on screen, so Lung could read n=123 in one box and n=126 in the next. All three now count over the same cohort, and applying a hotspot, fusion or copy-number filter rescales every other box, in the gene-effect, correlation and scatter popouts alike. The Cell Line Browser already worked this way.
  • Gene suggestions list the whole family. Typing "usp" and analyzing used to suggest USP1, USP10 and USP11, three arbitrary names; it now lists every gene starting with what was typed, in order, USP18 included, scrolling when the family is long.
  • iPad layout. On a tablet held upright the start page stacks: parameters and gene input side by side, then Results with the full width, so the network settings are no longer clipped off the right edge. The network toolbar now follows the width of the panel it sits in at every size, and on any touch screen the controls keep a fingertip's size.

v.88.23 (2026-08-14)

  • Network highlights default to black, not purple. The ring on highlighted genes, the caption bar over the network and the Enrichr marking note now start black; the colour is still yours to change in the network settings. Gate colours are unchanged.

v.88.22 (2026-08-14)

  • Copy data in the selection inspect now mirrors one volcano at a time. It asks which measure, like the image export, and copies every gene that plot draws with its difference and FDR, under a first line saying what was compared, so the chart can be redrawn in whatever software the numbers are pasted into.

v.88.21 (2026-08-14)

  • The Cell Line Browser has a banner. The title of the browser is now an illustrated banner, a row of cell types in the app's green, in place of the plain text heading.

v.88.20 (2026-08-14)

  • The inspect volcanoes sit level and gained the standard chart tools. The CRISPR and mRNA columns now share one grid, so the two charts sit at the same height and size whatever their notes do. A Settings button in the footer opens the same text panel the other charts have, for either volcano. Copy data puts the whole gene table on the clipboard, tab separated for Excel or GraphPad. And each volcano now carries a heading naming the two groups compared, so an exported image says what it shows; the heading is editable in Settings.

v.88.19 (2026-08-14)

  • Fix: building a network from an inspect gene list did nothing. The run is restricted to the selected cell lines, and "Min Cell Lines" is a floor on how many a gene needs data in. Left at its default of 25 it rejected any selection smaller than that, so the panel closed, the genes landed in the box and the analysis stopped on the home screen with a message about too few cell lines. The floor now comes down to the size of the selection.

v.88.18 (2026-08-14)
