  • The inspect header says what each side of the comparison is. Under the title, a line gives the size of the selection, where it came from and the browser filters it was drawn from, then the size of the comparison group and the rule that produced it.
  • Fix: the counts in the tissue / disease picker were cut off. The tree was wider than the box holding it, so the numbers on the right had to be scrolled to.
  • The cell line count above the browser list is a quarter larger.

v.88.17 (2026-08-14)

  • Enrichr sits beside the network instead of over it. Opened from the network it now floats to one side with the picture still live underneath, so clicking a term marks its genes while you watch. "Fill the window" in its header goes back to the full-size panel.
  • It looks like the rest of the app. It was the one dark panel, black with grey text, which is most of why it read as something else.
  • Fix: a long list of highlighted genes broke the layout above the network. Highlighting 25 genes took the control column from 278px to 833px and pushed the buttons beside it off the panel. The list wraps and scrolls now, and the same applies to the selected and removed lists.
  • Fix: highlights survived a new Run. Genes from a previous network were still listed under View controls after running a different gene set, naming genes that were no longer drawn anywhere.

v.88.16 (2026-08-14)

  • The network says why its genes are marked. Highlighting from an Enrichr result writes the term above the picture, with how many genes it covers and its adjusted p, so an exported figure carries what the marks mean.
  • That line is yours to edit, in the settings popout beside the filter banner: its wording, size and colour.
  • Four ways to mark a highlight: a dashed ring, a solid ring, a filled node, or fading everything else, in a colour of your choosing. One setting, used by both the Enrichr highlight and the Highlight button, since they are the same mark meaning the same thing.
  • An Enrichr result now says the network is behind the window, and offers to close it and show you.

v.88.15 (2026-08-14)

  • Fix: the counts beside each gene in the alteration filters ignored the disease you had chosen. With Colon Adenocarcinoma selected, 48 cell lines, the hotspot list offered KRAS n=34 and TP53 n=43. Those are the figures for the whole of Bowel, 63 lines. The grid, which filters properly, said 24 and 30, and it was right. The cohort those lists are counted over was built from tissue, subtype, sex and every alteration filter, but not from the disease level. The fusion and copy-number lists were counted the same way and were wrong in the same way.

v.88.14 (2026-08-14)

  • An Enrichr result highlights its genes in the network. Click a row and the genes behind it light up, with a line above the table naming the term, how many of the genes sent it covers and its adjusted p.
  • The three gene sets offered are clearer: all genes, the correlated ones (the clusters, without the unconnected genes parked to the side), or everything in the image. Whether a gene was typed in or found by the search is no longer one of the choices: once it is drawn and correlated it is part of the same answer.

v.88.13 (2026-08-14)

  • Fix: a finger on a chart would not scroll the page, in some places. Five charts had been named individually, so any other chart still swallowed the drag. Every chart scrolls the page now.
  • Enrichr from the network. A button under View controls asks which genes to send: everything you typed in, everything actually drawn, or only the correlated genes the search added. The network is usually a smaller set than the input, and which of the two you mean is the question.
  • Volcano labels no longer print on top of each other. Two genes at nearly the same place had their names overlap, since the labels were only alternated above and below their dot. They are now moved apart as far as they need, each with a thin line back to the dot it belongs to.
  • Phone: the gene box with statistics is the same size as the one without.

v.88.12 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: inspect selection puts its settings first. "Compare with" decides what the whole panel says, so it is what you land on, with the two cutoff boxes under it as headings that open on a tap.
  • Fix: it was wider than the screen. The results table has six columns and was pushing the panel out past the edge; it scrolls inside its own box now.
  • The volcano no longer takes a screen of its own, so the chart and the table it belongs to read as two halves of one answer.
  • Building a network from the listed genes is not offered on a phone.

v.88.11 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the correlation plot is sized as one piece. Only its y axis had been scaled down, so the heading, the statistics line and the whole x axis stayed at their desktop sizes beside a shrunken y axis. Everything scales together now.
  • Fix: the plot heading ran off the right edge. Whether it fitted was measured against the width control rather than the width the plot actually has on a phone, and a pair on one measure had no line break available to take.
  • Phone: the plot no longer fills the window exactly, which made the gene boxes, filters and Update below it look absent rather than further down. The top of the controls now shows under the chart.
  • The Cell Line Browser suggests names as you type. Typing the first letters of a cell line is how it is usually opened, and a name spelled the other way came back empty with no hint that the line is there.

v.88.10 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: Analyze put the gene effect chart back after you asked for expression. Switching the measure to Expression redrew the gene correctly, and then pressing Analyze, or Enter in the gene box, quietly returned to gene effect. Both now run the gene in whichever measure is selected. Everywhere, not only on a phone.

v.88.09 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: an edge opens its correlation on a single tap, and the tap does not have to land on the line. An edge is a few pixels wide, which a mouse can be placed on and a finger cannot, so a tap that misses now looks around itself for one. The double tap it was bound to also competes with the browser's own double-tap-to-zoom.
  • Phone: gene effect offers the by-tissue view only. The hotspot scan and the stratify-by-mutation view are each a second chart to read against the first, and with one view left there is nothing to label.

v.88.08 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: a gene card could be left stranded over the view it opened. Tapping a gene name in the wiki both opens the gene and, a moment later, shows the card describing it, which landed on top of the chart that had just opened. On a phone that card could not be closed at all, and its links could not be tapped, though it invited both. It is dismissed when a view opens, and where it does appear it now behaves as it says it does.
  • Fix: a collapsed heading sat against the edge of the screen. A closed section drops its padding to keep it to one line, which left its heading further left than everything around it, and a right-aligned label like "Selection" ended up at the far left of its row. Headings carry their own inset now, so closed and open line up.

v.88.07 (2026-08-13)

  • The line under the inspect selection title saying what is being measured is back on a phone; only the test selector was meant to go.

v.88.06 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: inspect selection is one column. It kept a fixed sidebar of control cards beside the results, which pushed the volcano and its table off the right edge of a phone. Everything is stacked now, results first and the controls under them, so the panel opens on the answer.
  • The choice of statistical test is not offered on a phone; it runs Welch's t, as it does unless changed.

v.88.05 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the alteration grid could be opened and not shut on a phone. Its title was set never to wrap, which made the header wider than the popup and pushed the close button off the right edge with nothing to scroll it back. The header wraps now and the close is thumb-sized.
  • The row of buttons under that grid wraps rather than running off the edge, and its export and copy buttons are hidden on a phone like the rest.
  • Selection in the Cell Line Browser opens on a tap, like the other sections. It is a row of things to do with a selection, and the selection is made in the list below it.
  • The "Export CSV" heading in that row no longer appears on a phone with nothing under it: the buttons were already hidden, the heading was not.

v.88.04 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the alteration grid was zoomed in too far. It was given a fixed cell size to make it pressable, which put only a handful of cell lines on screen and left the rest behind a long sideways scroll. It now uses the same sizing as the desktop, scaled up about a quarter, so a cell is still a reasonable target and a large panel still reads as a panel.

v.88.03 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: pressing Run or Update brings the result into view. The chart it makes usually sits below the controls that made it, so on a small screen it appeared off the bottom of the page and the press read as though nothing had happened. Only a press does this; a chart redrawn for any other reason leaves the page where it is.
  • Fix: "View" in the gene effect took the gene with it. Its heading shares a row with the gene box, the gene effect / expression selector and Analyze, so collapsing it hid the gene being looked at. That row no longer collapses: which gene, and whether it is gene effect or expression, stays on screen.
  • Phone: what a selection is for is back in the Cell Line Browser. "Inspect selected vs rest" and "Send to another view", with Select Visible and Show only selected, were hidden with the rest of that row, so cell lines could be ticked and then nothing could be done with them. Pasting a custom list and Copy Names stay hidden.
  • The gene set box with statistics is the same height as the one without.

v.88.02 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the cohort selectors were cutting their own text in half. Tissue, subtype, sex and sort each showed the bottom half of their value on a phone. The toolbar gives every control one fixed height, and the phone rules then put larger text and padding inside that same box, leaving less room for the text than the text needed.
  • Fix: the Wiki button on a cell line card was cut off. The card stopped at the height of the summary above it and could not be scrolled, so the deep dive, the first thing to reach for, was off the bottom.
  • Close on that card is a normal button again rather than the width of the card: it carries a word, so it was caught by the rule that enlarges the bare × glyphs.
  • The thin dividers between the toolbar groups are gone on a phone, where the toolbar wraps into a column and they read as stray marks.

v.88.01 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the Gene Effect filters open on a tap too. View, Lineage and disease (all three selectors together) and Genetic alterations start closed, so the chart is what you see when the popout opens rather than three rows of filters above it.

v.88.0 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the correlation view opens on the plot. It opened on a screenful of controls with the plot somewhere below them, which is backwards, and the collapsed filter headings were still being laid out two across so they read as a scattered list rather than a stack of things to open. Plot first, one control per row, and the gene and its measure sit together instead of each taking a line of its own.
  • Fix: "Rank by" no longer appears under the Run button on a phone. It is a way of hunting for the lineage with the strongest correlations, and it read as a stray filter turning up after a run.

v.87.99 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: network nodes and edges are drawn bigger, so a node or edge can be tapped to open the next level. A node at 25px and an edge at 3px are a fine mouse target and a poor finger one, and the network library offers no way to widen the hit area without widening the drawing.
  • Fix: a finger on the correlation plot moved the plot instead of the page. Letting the touch through in the stylesheet was not enough, because the chart library still claimed the gesture for its own panning. With zoom already locked on a phone there is nothing a drag should do, so it no longer takes one. Tapping a point still works.
  • Fix: the popout from a node sat partly off the screen. It was kept inside the right and bottom edges but not the left, so on a narrow screen it was pushed off the left instead. It is kept inside all four now, and no wider than the screen. It also no longer suggests holding Shift or pressing Escape, neither of which a phone has.

v.87.98 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the "With Stats" gene input drops its manual-entry / upload-file choice. Nobody uploads a file from a phone, so the choice was not a choice; it opens on manual entry, which is where it already started.

v.87.97 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: "Lineage and disease" left Subtype and Disease behind. The heading sits inside its own group while those two selectors are siblings of that group, so collapsing the heading hid only the lineage selector. All three go together now.
  • Phone: a finger on a chart scrolls the page. The chart swallowed the touch to pan itself, and since a chart is most of a phone screen there was often nowhere else to put your finger. Zoom and drag are already off there, so a vertical swipe now passes through. Tapping a point still works.
  • Phone: the gene box is bigger, and "Export" no longer appears under View controls.

v.87.96 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the browser's boxes cut off their own text on a phone. They carry fixed pixel widths written for a desktop row, and the phone rules then put bigger text and more padding inside that same fixed width, so the value no longer fitted. They size to the row now.
  • Pressing a cell line shows it straight away. The detail stacked under the whole list, so reaching a cell line's wiki meant scrolling past every other cell line. It sits above the list on a phone.
  • Fix: Gene pairs and Clusters were cropped at the right edge. Both tables are wider than a phone and nothing was allowed to scroll; they scroll sideways now.
  • The correlation popout's boxes are the same height. Each sized itself around its own contents, so the Hotspot filter towered over its neighbours and Fusion overlay was much taller than Hotspot overlay. Their dropdowns are also bounded, so a long list no longer stretches the box holding it.

v.87.95 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: a collapsed panel would not stay collapsed. The open/closed state lived only in the page, so every rebuild of a panel lost it, and a second rebuild nested one wrapper inside another so the toggle moved an element the panel no longer used. The state is now remembered per panel and re-applied whenever the panel is rebuilt, and a panel is only ever wrapped once.
  • Phone: a collapsed panel is a line of text, not an empty box. It kept its border, padding and background while collapsed, so three of them stacked looked like three empty cards taking the room of the controls they were hiding.
  • Phone: Lineage and disease, and Genetic alterations, start collapsed too, so the Run button is reachable without scrolling past two blocks of selectors.

v.87.94 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the alteration grid can be pressed. Its cells were between 3 and 8 pixels wide and 14 tall, which is a reasonable mouse target and an impossible finger one. On a phone they are 15 by 30. The grid already scrolls sideways, so the only cost is more scrolling.

v.87.93 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the "Other" button on the start page. The four Options buttons were forced into four equal columns, about 85px each on a small phone, so "Other ▾" overflowed its own button and sat off-centre. They now sit two per row.
  • An opened panel looks exactly as it did before. Collapsing a panel wrapped its controls in a container, and that container, not the controls, was picking up the box's own layout rules, so an opened panel came back looking different. The wrapper is now transparent to layout.

v.87.92 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the × that closes a popout is now big enough to press. It is the most-used control on a phone and was the smallest on the screen, a bare glyph with no padding around it. Every close button is now a 44px target with a larger glyph.

v.87.91 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the network showed through behind a popout on a phone. Popouts are fullscreen there, but the backdrop behind them was still half-transparent, so the network appeared along the bottom of the screen and read as part of the popout. The backdrop is solid now.
  • Phone: the remaining export and copy buttons are gone, in the mutation analysis, the results tabs, the Cell Line Browser, the wiki and the selection inspect. A file downloaded on a phone has nowhere useful to go.

v.87.90 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the link row ran off the right of a phone screen. The row was set never to wrap and the version badge was positioned to hang past its right edge, so everything after "Green Listed" was off-screen. It wraps and centres now, and the badge sits in the row.
  • Phone: the network control panels open on a tap. Appearance, Labels and color, and View controls start closed and open when you press the heading, instead of filling the screen above the network. Export is hidden entirely, since a downloaded file has nowhere to go on a phone.
  • Phone: lasso highlight is hidden, since it needs a drag on a plot that does not take drags there.

v.87.89 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the five threshold controls are gone and the defaults run. Correlation cutoff, minimum slope, minimum cell lines, the gene-coverage floor and the p-value threshold took about half the sidebar and are the settings a phone session is least likely to want to change. They run at 0.50, 0.10, 25, 100 and p < 0.001, which is where a desktop session usually leaves them. Still fully adjustable on desktop.

v.87.88 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the Cell Line Browser still would not scroll on a phone. The previous attempt freed the list but left the card split into a fixed toolbar and a scrolling remainder, and on a phone the stacked filter toolbar takes most of the height, so the part that scrolls was a sliver. The whole card now scrolls as one page, toolbar included.
  • Phone: the long explanatory blocks are out of the way. The selection-bias note, the paragraph explaining Welch's t-test, and Exclude Tissues took most of a screen before any result appeared. All still on desktop.

v.87.87 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the Cell Line Browser stopped scrolling part-way down on a phone. The list has its own scrollbar inside a clipped row, which works on desktop but becomes a trap once the layout stacks: the inner list ran out at a fixed height and everything under it was clipped, so the remaining cell lines and the detail panel could not be reached. The browser now has one scroller on a phone instead of three.
  • Phone: the cancer-type names are shorter again. Cut to 13 characters they still took about 40% of the screen once the count was added; the longest label is now 16 characters instead of 32, so the boxes have the majority of the frame.

v.87.86 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the controls that survive are now finger-sized. They were being made SMALLER than on desktop, 11px text and 3px padding, giving targets around 22px on the one device where a finger is the pointer. Boxes, dropdowns and buttons are now at least 40px tall with 15px text, and checkboxes and radios are twice the size. Fewer controls reach a phone, so the ones that do can afford the room.
  • Phone: more of what a phone cannot use is out of the way. Export for AI, "New tab", Enrichr, the network's Select and Remove modes, and the "Compare all ..." tables are hidden, on top of the image and CSV exports already hidden. What is left is the five things a phone is good for: finding a cell line by its mutations, reading its wiki, a gene's effect, a pair on the scatter, a mutation analysis, and a network from the Test Genes set. Nothing is removed from the desktop app.

v.87.85 (2026-08-13)

  • Phone: the cancer-type names no longer squeeze the gene effect plot. A row label like "Peripheral Nervous System (n=47)" is 32 characters and took close to half a phone screen, leaving the boxes too narrow to compare, which is the only thing that chart is for. Names are cut much shorter on a phone; the full name is still on the point.
  • Phone: tapping a cell line says which one it is. These plots relied on hover to name a dot, which a phone does not have, so the only way to find out was a tap that threw you into the Cell Line Browser. A tap now names the dot, and tapping a named dot opens it. The on-screen hint no longer tells phone users to Shift-click, which they cannot do.

v.87.84 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: a gene effect chart narrowed by a pasted cell-line list did not say so. Every other filter leaves a mark on a control, but a custom list leaves none: the lineage box still read "All lineages" over a chart down to two cell lines, which reads as the app having inherited a filter from somewhere else. The list is now named above the chart, first, since it is usually the strongest filter in the popout.
  • Fix: the same line credited the chart with filters it had ignored. Genes picked from an alteration grid in the Cell Line Browser are deliberately not applied to this chart, but were listed above it as though they were.

v.87.83 (2026-08-13)

  • Find correlates and Open in Gene Effect share a row. Both take the plot apart into a single gene, so they belong together rather than on separate lines.
  • Hovering a gene beside Open in Gene Effect describes it, the same as hovering a gene in the network or a results table.

v.87.82 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the disease menu's counts did not match the list. With the browser narrowed to 13 EBV-transformed B-cell lines, the disease menu still offered "Plasma Cell Myeloma (n=19)" and its numbers added up to four times the list below it. The counts were computed before the quick filters were applied. They now count what is actually on screen, so they sum to the list.

v.87.81 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: Growth Rate as a plot axis drew nothing. It was offered in both axis pickers, passed the check that its data had loaded, and then produced an empty plot reading "n=0", because the code behind the axis was retired at some point and the option was left in the menu. The option is gone. The data itself is untouched and still describes each cell line in the export and the wiki.
  • Growth rate is no longer called a gene effect. A plot against it was titled "Growth Rate (gene effect)", which is wrong: it is a proliferation rate, not a knockout effect. Gene-set scores were mislabelled the same way.

v.87.80 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the mRNA column's counts did not match the heading. The panel said 50 selected cell lines and the gene effect column agreed, while the mRNA column quietly rested on 49, because expression covers a different set of cell lines and one of the selected lines has none. The mRNA column now says how many lines it actually rests on whenever that differs, the same way the gene effect side has since it was reported claiming "48 vs 12" for a comparison it ran on 27 vs 3.

v.87.79 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the two cell line inspect CSVs would not open properly. A line describing the file was added above the column names in v.87.76; that made the description the header row as far as Excel and any scripting language are concerned, so the real column names were read as data and the numbers stopped lining up. The column names are back on the first line, where every other CSV in the app has them. What the file covers is still said when you export it, and is in the filename.

v.87.78 (2026-08-13)

  • An expression axis says what its numbers are. The Gene Effect view's axis read only "DUSP4 Expression", leaving the scale to be guessed, while the Correlation plot beside it has always said log2 TPM+1. Both now agree, along with the by-tissue detail plots; one chart also said "log TPM+1" where every other said "log2".
  • Each axis of the Correlation plot can be opened on its own. Two buttons under the gene boxes, naming the gene and the measure they will open, so a point on the plot can be followed into the Gene Effect view without retyping the gene. Hidden for growth rate and gene-set scores, which are not a single gene.
  • The gene names in the plot heading describe themselves on hover, the same as gene names everywhere else in the app.

v.87.77 (2026-08-13)

  • Three things called almost the same thing now have their own names. A gene pair plotted across every cell line was Correlation, the same pair split by tissue or mutation was Correlation Analysis, and the table of every pair in your set was Correlations. The plot keeps the name Correlation; the split-by-group view is now Correlation by group; the results tab is now Gene pairs.

v.87.76 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: a saved figure came back in the wrong colour. The settings file records the dot colour, and reopening it set the picker correctly, but the plot itself stayed the default blue: the colour is the one setting applied straight to the chart rather than read while drawing, and a restore sets the control without triggering that. The reopened figure now matches the file it came from. Checked across all five formats, and against the gene-effect and network files, which restore correctly.
  • Images now export at Medium by default rather than Small. A 5 cm figure is a thumbnail; the first export nearly always had to be redone larger. Whatever size you last chose still wins.
  • The volcano plots are square, and export through the usual dialog, so format, print size, resolution and background are all available rather than a flat screenshot.
  • Fix: comparing a whole lineage against itself produced a blank panel. Selecting every skin line and comparing against "same lineage only" leaves nothing on the other side, so every gene failed its minimum and the tables came out empty under a title claiming "(0 screened)", which was not true of the selection. It now says there is no comparison group, why, and what to change.
  • Sending a selection now opens the view it was sent to. Highlighting cell lines on a chart you cannot see was a setting with nothing to show for it. Mutation analysis and gene set analysis are separate rows, each opening its own mode with the cohort already applied.
  • The row that sends cell lines to the two-gene plot calls it Correlation, which is what the rest of the app calls it.
  • Six dead button handlers removed, left over from features whose buttons were taken out.

v.87.75 (2026-08-13)

  • Inspect selection looks like the rest of the app. It was the only analysis view with its own title bar, its own heading size and its actions crowded into the header, which is most of why it read as a different program. It now uses the same furniture as every other panel: a column of control cards down the left, the results on the right, and the exports in a footer bar. The comparison buttons, the test and the gene search moved into the sidebar, and the paragraph of method that filled the title bar is behind a "How to read this" link.
  • Both measures now get a volcano plot. This was the only analysis view with no chart at all, so whether a comparison was a handful of strong hits or a broad shift could only be guessed at from a ranked list. The strongest genes are labelled, points follow the cutoffs in the sidebar so the plot and the table always agree, and clicking a point opens that gene. Export image and Copy in the footer.
  • Fix: Save wrote a file nothing could open. The button that reads these files back was removed some time ago and Save was left behind, so it produced a saved analysis, said it had worked, and there was no way in to it. Save is gone. The unreachable correlation-inspect code behind it went too, some 460 lines that no button had opened since it was retired.
  • The two CSV exports say what they cover. They were called ".csv" and ".csv per cell line" and sounded like the same data in two shapes; one is every gene tested and the other only the genes on screen, capped at 300. The labels now say which is which and each file opens with a line describing its own scope.
  • Send selected cell lines to another view. A new button in the Cell Line Browser carries a selection over: highlight it on the scatter or on the gene-effect charts, or narrow those views, the mutation analysis or a gene set or network run to it. Getting a selection into another view previously meant copying names out and pasting them into whichever panel had a box for it.
  • Fix: the mutation analysis ignored the cell-line subset the other analyses honour. The same removable chip narrowed a gene set run and did nothing to a mutation run. It now applies to both, and it is shown beside the Run Mutation Analysis button, since the panel that used to list it is hidden in that mode. A subset sent over from the browser also survives the switch into the mode that uses it, rather than being cleared on the way.
  • Inspect selection has a Reset, like every other analysis view.

v.87.74 (2026-08-13)

  • Export for AI, audited again by handing files to assistants who had never seen the app. Twelve exports from nine views went out with a researcher's question attached, and the changes below are what those readers got stuck on or got wrong.
  • Fix: the co-essentiality note described the sign backwards. It said a positive correlation between two genes meant one buffering the other, and a negative one meant a shared pathway. Gene effect is negative for a dependency, so two genes needed by the same cell lines move down together and correlate positively: BRAF against MEK1, MEK2 and ERK2 all sit near +0.6 to +0.8. An assistant following the old wording would have reported the mechanism inside out.
  • Fix: a custom export could carry the previous view's results. Asking for lung cell lines while a melanoma comparison was open produced a file of lung lines whose top differences were BRAF, DUSP4 and SOX10, none of them in the file, under a description of fifty cell lines that were not there. Results computed over a different cohort are now dropped, and the file says what went and why. Narrowing the genes while keeping the cohort still keeps the analysis, which is the case the dialog exists for.
  • Every precomputed list now says whether it is complete or cut, and by what rule. Readers could not tell a genome-wide table from a top-200 one and hedged answers that needed no hedging, or read a gene's absence as a result when it had merely fallen outside a cut.
  • A gene set now carries every pairing among its genes. Asking whether DUSP4 sits with the MAPK genes or the lineage genes, a reader was handed three of that gene's nine pairings, the six missing ones being the weak lineage ones that would have settled it. All nine are now there, each with its p, marked for whether the network drew it.
  • A network says what it correlated and over which cell lines, in words. Typing in melanoma genes does not restrict the cohort to melanoma, and a reader assumed it had. The cluster count was also the number of genes rather than the number of clusters, so ten genes in one cluster reported ten clusters; and the leftover pile of genes that clustered with nothing was annotated with pathway names as though it were a module.
  • A gated comparison says that the lines between the gates are not in the file at all, that the gates were dragged by hand rather than computed, and, when both gates span the same range on one axis, that the split is really on the other axis alone.
  • A mutation analysis names the evidence that split the lines. A functional-loss analysis is an integrated copy-number, mutation and expression call, so MTAP put 243 lines in the altered group with no damaging point mutation anywhere in the release; the file said only that the damaging sub-type was on.
  • The file answers "do you have MSI status" directly, along with the other per-line attributes, instead of leaving a reader to search the prose and hit the genes MSI1 and MSI2 first. Where a single gene is in focus, the MSI comparison is now precomputed alongside the driver-gene ones.
  • The self-check no longer reads as a guarantee it never made. It compares gene names only, yet three readers tried to reconcile the counts in the caption beside it against the file and could not, because the caption describes the view and the file describes the export.
  • Scales for the numbers that had none: ploidy, instability, loss of heterozygosity, the MSI score, aneuploidy and proliferation rate. The donor's age and sex and the line's Cellosaurus ID are now carried, because the written cell-line summary already stated them and nothing in the file could confirm it.
  • The eight tumour suppressors behind the functional-loss calls are named rather than counted, and absence of a call is stated to mean "not called" rather than "called negative".
  • The request block tolerates how an assistant actually writes. Bullets, numbered lines, bold keys and code fences were rejected outright, losing every instruction in the block; a bare group name, and the obvious alternative key names, now resolve. Asking for something impossible says what the legal values are, and asking for a comparison group explains that an export carries one cohort.

v.87.73 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the UpSet bars did not line up with the dots below them. The invisible click target is a second bar on the same axis, and bars on one axis are drawn side by side by default, so each got half the slot and the visible bar sat off-centre. Both now share the slot, which also puts each count back over its own bar.
  • Fix: a gene selected in the grid but not applied came back as an applied filter. Exporting with KRAS merely selected, so its bar is green and the KRAS-negative bars still stand, and reopening the settings file gave a cohort filtered to KRAS with those bars gone. The file now records whether the picks were applied.
  • The UpSet header names what the cohort was filtered by. Raised from the Cell Line Browser it read only the parameter panel's filters, so a plot built over the lung lines said nothing about lung.
  • Exporting an UpSet starts at Medium rather than the 5 cm default, which was too small to read.

v.87.72 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: the settings file saved beside an UpSet or grid image did not carry the Cell Line Browser's own filters. It saved the parameter panel's filters, which are different controls, so a plot built over 50 skin BRAF-mutant lines reopened over all 1,208 and looked nothing like the image it came from. The browser's tissue, subtype, disease, sex, alteration, quick-filter, pasted-list and tick state now travel with the file and are restored before the grid is rebuilt.
  • Fix: an UpSet saved without picking genes by hand reopened as a grid with no UpSet at all, because only an explicit pick was recorded. The genes actually plotted are saved now, however they were chosen. Counts, percentages and the top-N cut travel too.

v.87.71 (2026-08-13)

  • UpSet: the count and the percentage now sit one above the other. Side by side, "32 · 42.7%" is about fifty pixels over a bar with under thirty to itself, so labels ran into their neighbours and each one looked shifted off its own bar. Stacked, each label sits over the bar it belongs to.
  • Removed the option to print the combination name inside the bar. On a bar a few pixels wide it was unreadable, and on a short one it did not fit at all. The name is still on hover and in the matrix of dots underneath.

v.87.70 (2026-08-13)

  • The rows in the comparison picker now add up. Melanoma held 67 while the two disease rows under it held 8 and 4, because 55 melanoma lines carry no finer label and so appeared in no row at all. Those lines now have a row of their own, so 4 + 3 + 10 makes the 17 above them and 8 + 4 + 55 makes the 67.
  • The note above the tree says how many of the cell lines are your selection and that each count reads "how many are left to compare against, of how many the group holds".

v.87.69 (2026-08-13)

  • Fix: title and subtitle sizes were applied to each other. On a chart whose heading is one block, the title carries no size of its own and takes the annotation's, but the code assumed the first size it found belonged to the title, which was the subtitle's. Setting the title to 19 put 19 on the subtitle and shrank the title to 9. Both now go where they are meant to.
  • Cell line names clicked onto a chart can be resized, under a new "Cell line names" control that appears once there are any. They were the only text on the plot with no setting.
  • Cell line dots start at 7 rather than 5, which is easier to hit and easier to see in an exported figure.
  • The box colour schemes explain themselves. Each says what it does on hover, and a line above them says they all read the same thing, the group's mean, and differ only in how they show it. "Essential" is red where the group needs the gene, green where losing it helps.
  • Closing a plot now closes its settings box. The box sits outside the window it belongs to, so it can be dragged clear, which is why it used to be left hovering over an empty page pointed at a chart that had gone. This applies wherever such a box is used.

v.87.68 (2026-08-13)

  • The tissue / disease picker can be closed, with an × or by pressing the button that opened it. It had no way out, so once open it stayed open.
  • The counts in that picker now say what will actually be compared against. Picking Melanoma to compare 45 BRAF-mutant melanoma lines against leaves 22, not the 67 the list showed, because a cell line cannot be on both sides. Groups you selected from now read "22 of 67", with the rest explained on hover.
  • When no genes pass the cutoffs, the reason now appears in the table itself, under the headings, where the rows would have been. As grey text above the table it read as a caption and went unread, so an empty table looked like an answer rather than a cutoff to loosen.

v.87.67 (2026-08-12)

  • Every export for AI now carries everything needed to ask for more data. The file describes each key of the request language, what each optional layer would add, the tissue names that actually resolve, where to find disease and subtype names, and which layers this file already has, so an assistant writes a working request instead of describing what it would like. Verified by feeding the file's own example, and a request built only from what it declares legal, back through the parser that has to accept them.
  • The layer vocabulary now has one definition that both the parser and the exported documentation read, so the two cannot drift apart as the request language grows.

v.87.66 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: a custom export could fail silently. Asking for "what the current view shows" with nothing open produced no file and no message, because the explanation was written into the standard export dialog, which is not on screen at that point. The custom dialog now says what went wrong in its own words, stays open so the settings can be corrected, and the cell-line option carries its own count so an empty view is visible before pressing Export.
  • A request can now name a chromosome region. genes: 16q takes all 384 genes on that arm, 16q22 just that band. Asking whether one gene's copy number stands out against the rest of its arm needs the rest of the arm, and no one is going to type 384 symbols.

v.87.65 (2026-08-12)

  • Find a gene in the cell line inspect. A box beside the test selector shows the genes you name in both tables. It ignores the cutoffs while you search, since a lookup that came back empty because the gene sits under a threshold would be no use, and it says so.
  • Full view is a toggle now. It expanded the popout and then hid itself, so the chart-only view could not be got back without closing and reopening. It now reads "Chart only" once expanded, wherever a compact view makes sense.

v.87.64 (2026-08-12)

  • The per-gene profile CSV no longer carries columns that are empty for every row. Asking for a gene that is not on the curated copy-number panel produced a CancerCN column blank on all 11 lines, which reads as missing data rather than as a column that does not apply. Anything dropped is named in the header instead.
  • The provenance lines above the table are all marked as comments now. Only the first one was, so the rest opened in a spreadsheet as if they were data, two columns wide, above a table that is twelve.

v.87.63 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: the chart disagreed with the table it was opened from. Clicking a gene in the cell line inspect opens the two groups being compared, but a genetic-alteration filter left over from the Cell Line Browser was still being applied on top of them. It left the selected lines untouched (they all carry the alteration, that is what selected them) and quietly cut the group they were compared against, so the same gene showed one average in the table and another in the plot. The two groups are now the whole cohort of that chart, with nothing applied on top, and the subtitle no longer names filters it is not using.

v.87.62 (2026-08-12)

  • The per-cell-line CSV is now one row per cell line, with a column per gene for each measure (BRAF_GE, BRAF_expr, and so on) instead of the same numbers repeated down 3,000 rows. Genes are ordered by the size of the difference they showed, so the columns worth looking at come first, and capped at 300 since each gene adds two columns to every row.
  • A gene nothing in the cohort has an expression value for no longer gets an empty column on every row.

v.87.61 (2026-08-12)

  • The group names down the axis can now be renamed in Text settings, under "Row labels". They were the one piece of text on a chart with no way to edit it, so a comparison exported for a figure was stuck with "4 selected (n=4)" and "My list (n=4)".
  • Fix: "Export CSV:" could end up on the line above its own buttons when the footer wrapped. Each label now wraps together with the buttons it names.
  • Fix: "By Cell Line" produced an empty file. The chart's own renderer replaces its statistics with a stripped copy for the table below it, dropping the cell lines behind each group, and the export was reading that copy. It now reads the version that still carries them: 8 rows for a two-group comparison, 1,208 for the whole panel.
  • An empty inspect table now says which cutoff emptied it. Instead of a blank table it reads "515 genes are big enough, but none reach q ≤ 0.05, the best being 0.98. Set q to 1 to see the strongest differences, and read them as exploratory", or names the largest difference present when the size cutoff is the one blocking.

v.87.60 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: A549_CRAF_KD was described as a drug-treated line. It is a RAF1 (CRAF) knockdown, not a drug exposure. Drugs and genes had been kept in one list when reading the names, so a gene in a name came out phrased as something the cells were grown in. The two are now separate kinds, and the card, the wiki, the quick filters and the exported file each say which one they are looking at.

v.87.59 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: the drug-treated quick filters were built but never showed up. A separate list decides which of the curated filters reach the panel, and the two new ones were not on it. "Drug-selected line with its parent" and "Drug-selected derivative only" now appear under Matched pairs.
  • Rewrote the matched-pair note on the card and in the wiki. It said the same thing three ways and repeated the cell line name back at you; it now reads "Grown from A375 under dabrafenib until it survived the drug."
  • Hover boxes wait longer before appearing. The delay had been set separately in six places and drifted from 150 ms to 450 ms, so the network fired almost on contact. All of them now wait the same, longer moment, so sweeping the pointer across a dense chart no longer throws popups.

v.87.58 (2026-08-12)

  • Custom export for AI: cell lines can now be chosen as a group (tissue:Skin, disease:Melanoma) rather than only by name, in the dialog and in a pasted request. Asking for skin lines needed all 75 typed out before.
  • Drug sensitivity can be narrowed to the compounds, targets or mechanisms you care about instead of always carrying the whole 89-compound panel.
  • Wording fixes an assistant reading the file got caught by: what "settled" means on an identity record, that the treated lines were never put through the drug screen, that a narrow gene matrix is narrow by request rather than truncated, and that the three grouping levels are separate passes rather than a nesting.

v.87.57 (2026-08-12)

  • New: Custom export for AI (Options › Other). Choose the cell lines, the genes, how many genes and how big the correlation scans are, and add layers the standard export leaves out: drug sensitivity, copy number for every gene, virus status, disputed identities, and treated/parental line pairs.
  • The assistant can write the settings for you. Every standard export now carries the request syntax and where to paste it, so an assistant that finds the file short of something replies with a small block; paste it into the dialog and every control is set at once. It says what it understood and what it could not use.
  • Naming the genes you care about is what makes room for everything else: a file about twelve genes can carry every cell line and every extra layer at once.

v.87.56 (2026-08-12)

  • Treated lines and their parents are now paired up. The panel carries nine matched pairs, a cell line and a version of it carried in a drug until it grew in that drug. The card says which is which and links to the other, and there are two new quick filters: the pairs together, or the treated lines on their own.
  • New in the cell line wiki: History and provenance. What a line is a version of, whether its identity is disputed, whether it was established by a virus, and links to the primary records. It only appears when there is something to say.
  • Fixed a name that lost a character upstream: RVH421_DAB_R was showing as RVH42DABR, which reads as a cell line that does not exist. Names are now derived from the catalogue name where the shortened form disagrees with it by more than punctuation.

v.87.55 (2026-08-12)

  • Cell line names placed on the gene effect chart can be dragged apart. Two names on nearby dots simply overlapped and there was no way to separate them, which the scatter has always allowed.
  • Axis labels can now actually be typed in. An axis with no label starts with its switch off, so typing one wrote the text into a hidden label and nothing appeared. Typing a label now turns it on, and switching it back on restores what you typed rather than what was there before.
  • The per-cell-line CSV follows the chart. It exported every cell line with a fixed tissue column whatever the view was set to, so changing the grouping to disease, or to the two sides of a comparison, changed the picture and not the file. It now exports what is drawn, with a column naming the group each line is in.
  • New in the cell line inspect: a per-cell-line CSV. One row per gene per cell line, for the genes the tables are showing, so an outlier carrying a group mean is visible instead of hidden behind it.

v.87.54 (2026-08-12)

  • Choose the test in the cell line inspect. Welch's t compares the means and is punished by ordinary spread, which bites hardest on small groups. A rank test, which asks only whether one group sits above the other, is now offered beside it. On eight melanoma lines against the rest, SOX10 goes from a p that does not survive correction to one that does.
  • The strongest result your group sizes allow is now stated. A rank test on three lines against three can never produce a p below 0.1, so a stricter cutoff empties the table for a reason that has nothing to do with the biology. The header says what that floor is, next to the group sizes actually behind the comparison.
  • Clicking a gene in the cell line inspect now opens on the comparison the table was built from, rather than the by-tissue chart, which answers a different question. The two groups keep the table's order instead of being sorted by their means, so they no longer swap places when the direction of the difference flips.

v.87.53 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: a cleared filter still reading as applied. Searchable dropdowns kept showing the old choice after Reset had genuinely cleared them, most visibly the disease filter in the Cell Line Browser. The box now follows the filter itself rather than only user clicks, everywhere such a dropdown is used.
  • Fix: highlighting cell lines in the scatter matched far too much. Typing a short name pulled in every line that merely contained those letters, so CI brought NCIH1650 and 94 others with it. Punctuation and spacing are still ignored, so MEC-1 finds MEC1, but a short name now has to be the name or start it. Commas and semicolons separate names as well as line breaks.

v.87.52 (2026-08-12)

  • Export for AI: the analysis steps and method notes in each file are now filtered to what that file actually contains, so a view with no single gene at its centre no longer opens with four steps naming things that are not there.
  • Smaller fixes from the same review: the steps read in order, near-miss correlation pairs carry their slope, the file says plainly when an absent annotation means "not called" rather than "called negative", and counts that only matter when they differ are shown only then.

v.87.50 (2026-08-12)

  • Export for AI, rebuilt around what an assistant reading it actually got stuck on. Five files from five different views were handed to assistants with no knowledge of the app, and their complaints drove the changes: each file now opens with a list of the sections it does and does not contain, and only documents what is in it, instead of describing a dozen sections belonging to other views.
  • Every precomputed correlation now carries its own p-value, so "is this real" can be answered without recomputing. The three similarly named correlation lists say in one place how they differ and what a positive value means in each.
  • Scatter exports carry the correlation for the axes actually plotted, plus the same two genes on the other pairings, so a flat plot is no longer read as "no relationship" when the two genes track each other strongly a different way.
  • Copy number now gets the same driver-by-driver test that mutations already had, so an amplified driver can be ruled out as the explanation without a hand scan.
  • Correlation exports include the strongest pairs just below the cutoff, flag any gene the file cannot verify, and always carry the genes you typed in. The screen-quality check per cell line is now in every export, not only single-gene ones, and the variance check says it passed rather than leaving it to be guessed from silence.

v.87.48 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: Export for AI failed from the cell line inspect. That view had no description of itself to put in the file, and the export stopped with an error instead of producing anything. It now describes what it is, carries the top differences between the selected lines and what they were compared with, and states how many of each group actually have a screen. Any view without a description of its own gets a plain one rather than failing.
  • Settings files: opening one for an expression correlate that is missing its partner gene now says what it holds instead of appearing to do nothing.

v.87.46 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: the settings file saved next to an UpSet plot did not reopen it. Two things were wrong. The grid it is built on draws its cell lines from the Cell Line Browser, which the restore never opened, so the grid came back with nothing behind it; and the genes named in the file were looked for only among the grid's current most-altered genes, which are different ones once the saved picks narrow the cohort. The browser is now opened first, and a gene named in the file is rebuilt from the data if it is not in that list.
  • Opening a settings file for a picture the app cannot rebuild, such as a screenshot of a whole panel, now says so by name instead of listing it as unknown.

v.87.45 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: arrow keys moved the network instead of the text cursor. Typing in a box such as the cell line search and pressing left or right slid the network about behind the dialog while the caret stayed put. The network listens for those keys on the whole window, which is what lets it pan without clicking the canvas first, and the guard meant to hold them back was attached where it could never get in front. The keys now reach the text field alone whenever the caret is in one, and the network still pans as before otherwise.

v.87.44 (2026-08-12)

  • Fix: opening a gene from the browser's inspect wiped the browser's filters. Clicking a gene there opens the Gene Effect view, whose reset was clearing the set of alteration picks it shares with the Cell Line Browser, so they were gone on the way back. That reset now leaves picks made in the browser alone, which is why it only happened after clicking a gene.
  • Export for AI in the Cell Line Browser, beside Export image. It sends whichever cell lines are listed, or just the ticked ones if any are ticked, with the filters that produced them stated in the file.

v.87.43 (2026-08-12)

  • The Export for AI dialog can be dragged by its title bar, like every other dialog. It opens over whichever view raised it, so being able to slide it aside and read what is underneath matters here as much as anywhere.

v.87.42 (2026-08-12)

  • Clicking a bar in the UpSet plot now selects in the grid rather than filtering straight away. It was applying immediately, which narrowed the cohort under the grid, so the grid redrew with far fewer genes and the choice was gone before it could be looked at. The combination is now ticked into the grid exactly as if its squares had been clicked, and Apply there is what carries it to the list.
  • The warning on a flagged cell line says what is actually on record. It read as a verdict on the vial in your freezer, which nobody here is in a position to give. It now says the line has been reported as incorrectly labelled or cross-contaminated, and points to the full record.

v.87.40 (2026-08-11)

  • Alteration grids, the UpSet plot and the filter chips now behave the same wherever they appear. The copy-count choice had reached some of them and not others: the scatter's own grid chips still offered only altered or wild-type, several chips printed a bare "Mut" whatever had been chosen, and the count shown inside the grid while picking used a different rule from the filter it was previewing, so it could disagree with the result. All of them read the same state and use the same test now.

v.87.39 (2026-08-11)

  • Fix: an UpSet plot opened from the scatter filtered the wrong thing. The scatter deliberately keeps its own set of grid picks, so that choices made there do not reach into the analysis cohort, and clicking a bar was writing to the shared set instead: the scatter did not change, and the gene set analysis quietly did. Clicking a bar now applies to whichever grid the plot was opened from, and the plot in front of you updates.

v.87.38 (2026-08-11)

  • Filters are listed in one place again. Picks made from an alteration grid were still being written into the parameters box, twice over, as a line of green text and as a row of chips, while everything else had moved to Active filters beside Run. All of them now appear in that one box, each removable, and the two older lists are gone.

v.87.37 (2026-08-11)

  • Clicking a bar in the UpSet plot no longer rearranges it. Applying a combination redrew the whole chart, and the redraw chooses which genes to show from the filters in force, so the plot restructured under the click. The chosen bar simply turns green now and every other bar stays where it was.

v.87.36 (2026-08-11)

  • Choosing a gate shape is now asked plainly. Rectangle or lasso used to be two lines of small text under the button, easy to miss and easy to dismiss by accident. It is a proper dialog in the middle of the screen, each option saying what it does, in the colour of the gate being drawn.
  • The Cell Line Browser keeps an Active filters box on screen, with its own Reset beside it, the way the scatter does. It reads "none" when nothing is applied, so the row never appears and shifts everything below it.

v.87.35 (2026-08-11)

  • Find correlates asks for a share of the cohort, not a fixed count. With 315 cell lines showing, the top correlates of ATM were genes measured in about 20 of them, roughly 6 % of the data, because a correlation on a handful of points is large by accident. A gene must now be measured in 75 % of the cell lines in view, adjustable, and 0 shows everything. On the full panel the top of that same list becomes TP53, TP53BP1, CHEK2, MDM2 and CDKN1A, which is the pathway ATM actually sits in.
  • Small bars in the UpSet plot can be clicked. A combination with two cell lines drew a sliver next to one with hundreds and there was nothing to hit; every column now has the same click target whatever its count, and the plot says so.
  • A combination picked in the UpSet plot shows up in the grid behind it, so it can be adjusted there before it reaches the list.
  • Mutation filter chips in the Cell Line Browser offer the copy count. The menu on a pick made from the alteration grid still had only altered and wild-type; it now offers either copy, one copy, both copies or wild-type.
  • The gate comparison goes into PowerPoint as two pictures, so the two plots can be moved and resized independently on the slide instead of arriving as one flattened image.

v.87.33 (2026-08-11)

  • Clicking a bar in the UpSet plot filters on that combination. A bar is already a filter, exactly the genes with a filled dot altered and the rest not, so clicking one applies it to the grid behind the plot, where it sits with the other picks and can be changed or removed once the plot is closed. Clicking the same bar again takes it off.
  • Grid picks can name the copy count. A pick made from the alteration grid offered only altered or wild-type; it now offers either copy, one copy, both copies or wild-type, matching the filter boxes. The chip says which.
  • Every dialog can be dragged by its title bar. The larger ones were left out before on the grounds that there is nowhere to move them to, which is backwards: on a small screen that is exactly when it matters.
  • Fix: the gate comparison export crowded its heading against the plot. The top margin is inherited from the chart on screen, where the heading block is shorter relative to the plot; at export size its last line landed on the plot edge. The margin now grows to fit the block, and the second panel follows it so the two plots stay level.

v.87.31 (2026-08-11)

  • Fix: the new cell-line count warned on every row. A small selection tripped a "fewer lines than expected" mark on all of them, which said nothing. The mark now appears only where a row really does rest on fewer lines than the groups you picked, and the mRNA column is measured against the mRNA cohort rather than the smaller CRISPR one.
  • Fix: Reset in the Cell Line Browser left the disease filter set. Disease is the third level of the tissue choice and was added after that button was written. The same gap is closed where removing a tissue or subtype filter in the Gene Effect view left the disease behind, and where the scatter cleared its subtype but not its disease.
  • Mutation filter chips offer all four choices everywhere. The Gene Effect view only understood mutated or wild-type; it now offers either copy, one copy, both copies or wild-type, as the Cell Line Browser already did.
  • Wide panels open centred rather than pushed back from whichever screen edge they hit, which put the quick filters off to the right on smaller screens.

v.87.30 (2026-08-11)

  • Comparisons say how many cell lines they actually rest on. Not every line has a CRISPR screen, so a comparison of 48 lines against 12 could quietly come down to 27 against 3 for a given gene while still being labelled 48 against 12. Each row now carries the two counts behind it, marked when they fall well short of the groups you picked, and the heading says so too.
  • Genes measured in very few cell lines can be left out. The latest release added genes screened in only a handful of lines; 600 of the 18,531 are measured in fewer than 100. Their statistics rest on almost nothing yet they crowd the top of every ranking. A new setting beside Min Cell Lines drops them, at 100 by default. Set it to 0 to include everything, and genes you type in are never dropped.
  • A warning when a gene's score follows its own copy number. In an amplified region every cut is lethal whatever the gene does, so a gene can look essential simply for sitting in an amplification. 771 genes show this pattern, among them ERBB2 and its amplicon neighbours, MYCN and FGFR2. The gene effect view now says so, with the strength of the pattern, and leaves the judgement to you.
  • Growth rate is available again, as an axis in the scatter. It covers every cell line, and proliferation is the usual alternative explanation for a modest dependency, so it is worth being able to plot against directly.
  • Fix: the measure switch did nothing when a gene was opened from the network. Switching between gene effect and expression re-opened the view in a way that reset the choice on the way, so the control appeared dead.
  • Exports for AI are written for you, not for the file. The assistant was opening with the file's internal field names at a reader who has never seen it. It now begins by saying what you were looking at, how much data came with it and what you asked, answers the question in plain language before any numbers, and stops to ask when no question was attached.
  • Fix: the gate comparison export ignored the font settings and drew its headings on top of each other. The heading and statistics lines are positioned for the size the plot is on screen, and the export renders at another size without moving them; the font fields were also being applied to a heading the scatter does not use. Both are fixed, and the gate panel now follows the current text settings instead of the ones in force when the gate was drawn.
  • Fix: applying any text setting dropped the scatter legend's fixed-width font, so its columns stopped lining up.

v.87.28 (2026-08-11)

  • Fix: the scatter legend could still be cut off at the edge on a narrow plot. Its width was estimated before the entries existed, and the entries were then sized back from that estimate, so on a small plot with long disease names the text ran past the box. The width is now worked out from the columns that will actually be drawn, including the "not selected" entry, and the text shrinks and the names narrow until everything fits.

v.87.27 (2026-08-11)

  • A gene opened from the comparison table can now be charted as the comparison itself. The choice above the chart, which offered all lineages or this lineage broken up two ways, gains a fourth: your selection against whatever you chose to compare it with, whether that was all other cell lines, the same lineage, tissues and diseases you ticked, or a list you pasted. The chart then holds those two groups and nothing else, which is the question the table was asking in the first place.
  • In that view the selected lines are one of the two groups, so they are no longer separately marked as highlighted on top of it.

v.87.26 (2026-08-11)

  • Fix: the disease level of the comparison picker could not be opened. The rows were built with a separator character that browsers strip out of the markup, so clicking a subtype did nothing. Diseases now open and can be ticked like the levels above them.
  • Fix: opening the picker left the tick on the wrong choice. "All other cell lines" stayed marked as selected until something had been ticked, so the picker looked inactive while it was open. The mark now follows what was chosen; the comparison itself still falls back to all other cell lines until a pick is made.

v.87.25 (2026-08-11)

  • Tissue, subtype and disease are one filter chip, not three. They are a single nested choice, so listing them separately suggested a middle level could be removed on its own. The chip names the most specific level and spells out the full path on hover.
  • Fix: removing a filter could leave part of it behind. Clearing a disease picked through the Tissues button left a green note beside the lineage box still naming it, so the filter looked applied when it was not. Clearing now goes through the same path the app uses everywhere else and takes the note with it.
  • Remove all beside the Active filters heading clears every one of them at once.
  • The dividing rule moved below the filters, where it separates them from what follows instead of doubling up with the rule above.

v.87.24 (2026-08-11)

  • Gene set analysis and mutation analysis keep their own filters. The two share one box of cohort settings, so a tissue, an alteration or a gate set for one quietly narrowed the other as well. Each now remembers its own: switching modes puts the current settings aside and brings back whatever that mode had, or a clean slate the first time. Gates in particular no longer follow you from one analysis into the other.

v.87.23 (2026-08-11)

  • The network font slider now means what it says. Labels are drawn in the network's own coordinates, so zooming out to fit the whole picture shrank the text with it: at a typical fit a "20" label reached the screen at about 16. Labels are now scaled back up by the same amount, so 20 on the slider is 20 on screen whatever the network's size.
  • The scatter legend is laid out in columns, with a quiet header saying what those columns are. Names, counts and values now line up down the list instead of landing wherever the name happened to end. Group size is shown as "n=" and is what the legend states by default; correlation, average and median are the alternatives.
  • Active filters are listed at the end of the gene set, each removable. They narrow the gene set and mutation analyses and carry into a scatter or gene effect opened from the network; the Cell Line Browser has its own filters. The earlier line in the Options box has been removed: it was in the wrong place, and it claimed to describe the whole app, which was not true.
  • Fix: a filter could look as though it had done nothing. The line describing the cohort was reporting the size of the previous run, so picking a tissue left the count unchanged until the next Run.
  • The comparison picker in the cell line browser now matches the rest of the app, using the same table, checkboxes and expanding rows as the tissue breakdown elsewhere. Opening Inspect starts from the default view again rather than remembering the last comparison chosen, and the pasted list takes any number of names.
  • HeLa is no longer named as an example anywhere. It was removed from the app some time ago and should not be suggested.

v.87.22 (2026-08-11)

  • You choose what the legend states for each coloured group. When colouring by tissue, subtype or disease, a new selector under the colour picker offers the correlation, the average of each axis, the median of each axis, or the count on its own. Correlation answers whether the relationship holds inside a group; the average or median answers where the group sits, which is the more useful reading when groups separate by level rather than by trend. The median is there because one extreme cell line moves a small group's average a long way.

v.87.21 (2026-08-11)

  • Two more ways to choose what a cell line selection is compared with. Alongside "all other cell lines" and "same lineage", you can now tick tissues, subtypes and diseases in a tree, at any level and as many as you like, or paste your own list of cell lines. The count of what you are comparing against is shown as you go, and names that are not in the panel are named rather than silently dropped.
  • Hovering a gene in that table now says what the gene is, together with the numbers from the row you are pointing at, so you no longer have to open the gene to find out whether it is worth opening.
  • Fix: network labels were smaller than they should have been. Gene names are drawn in italics, and italic text was being rendered at a fixed size that ignored the size slider entirely. The slider now governs plain, bold and italic labels alike.
  • Fix: clearing a filter in the scatter no longer undoes itself. A filter carried in from the network came back every time the axes were changed and Update was pressed. A filter you clear now stays cleared for as long as you are in that plot, while arriving fresh from the network still brings its filters with it.
  • The cell line subset in force now sits at the end of the gene set, next to Run and under a dividing rule, instead of further up where it was easy to miss.
  • The "all genes found" line uses the app's green, having been styled with the amber reserved for warnings.

v.87.20 (2026-08-10)

  • The outside libraries the app loads are now pinned by content. Each one carries a checksum, so a browser refuses to run it if what arrives is not byte-for-byte the reviewed file. One library was worse than unpinned: it asked for "latest", meaning the app would silently pick up any new release, breaking or otherwise. It now names an exact version.
  • Outbound links no longer hand the app's page over to the site they open. Every external link now opens fully detached.

v.87.19 (2026-08-10)

  • The cohort you are working on is now stated in one fixed place. Filters set in one part of the app stay in force in the others, which is intended but was invisible: a cohort narrowed in the browser quietly narrowed the next analysis, results looked wrong, and reloading the page appeared to be the cure. A line under the Options buttons now always names the current cohort, and offers a reset when one is applied.
  • Fix: Reset in the Gene Effect popout broke the mutation analysis behind it. It cleared that analysis's results as well as its own, after which every Inspect button in the results table did nothing at all, with no message. Reset now leaves the analysis alone, and Inspect says what it needs if the results really are gone.
  • Fix: popouts could be scrolled off into empty space. Scrolling past the end of a dialog slid the whole card away, leaving a large blank patch. The card now moves only as far as something is genuinely out of reach, whether that is below the window edge or below the screen edge.
  • Fix: overlapping column titles in the mutation analysis image export. The vector table used a fixed column width, so any header longer than about ten characters ran into its neighbour. Columns are now measured from their contents, and a long title wraps onto a second line.
  • Exports for AI answer subgroup questions properly. A question naming a disease now resolves to actual cell lines at export time, because the disease field is coarser than most questions: chronic lymphocytic leukemia is not a value it takes, and its lines sit inside a bucket that also holds several other diseases. Groups are now also broken out at the finer Oncotree level, small groups are flagged rather than dropped, and each group carries the focal gene's rank against every other gene for the same contrast, which settles a question that a group mean cannot.
  • Alongside that: a calibration for how large a group difference has to be at each group size, the two standard controls for a weak dependency per cell line (the line's own mean gene effect, and the focal gene against that line's own distribution), proliferation rate per cell line, and a plain statement that the genome-wide correlation scans are cohort-wide, so absence from them is not evidence of absence in a subgroup.

v.87.18 (2026-08-10)

  • Cell lines now show which virus transformed them. Cellosaurus records the transforming agent for 53 lines in the panel, most often EBV, HPV16/18 or HBV. A small virus appears beside the name in the browser list, the summary at the top of the card says so, and the wiki gives the full record with a note on what it means.
  • Why it matters: viral oncoproteins override the pathways an experiment is usually aimed at. HPV E6 and E7 degrade p53 and inactivate RB, so an HPV-transformed line behaves as p53- and RB-deficient whatever its TP53 and RB1 sequence says, and an EBV-immortalised lymphoblastoid line is not a tumour line at all.
  • Four new quick filters under Viral transformation: confirmed transformed by any agent, or specifically by EBV, HPV or HBV. They are named “confirmed” deliberately: a line without a record has simply never had one made, which is not the same as being free of the virus, and no filter in the app implies otherwise.
  • The AI export now names viral transformation among the layers it does not carry, so an assistant reading the file can ask for it rather than assume its absence means anything.

v.87.17 (2026-08-10)

  • Fix: p-values in exported CSVs were text, not numbers. They were written the way they are displayed ("3.8 × 10⁻⁵⁷", with superscript digits), which a spreadsheet imports as words: the column could not be sorted or calculated with. Files now carry plain values (3.800e-57); the app still shows the readable form on screen.
  • Fix: bold and italic gene names exported as raw markup. The network's SVG export wrote the styling tags into the label text instead of applying them, so a bold or italic network came out with the tags printed beside every gene. Both SVG exporters now set real font weight and style.
  • Fix: the caption under a gated export crowded the bottom edge. It sat under the left panel only, which made that half look taller, and the whitespace trim then cropped it flush to the edge. It is now centred under both panels, and a composed figure is no longer trimmed.

v.87.16 (2026-08-10)

  • Find correlates has a minimum cell-line count. The 26Q1 release added genes screened in only a handful of lines, which flooded the list with correlations computed on almost no data. The panel now asks for at least 10 cell lines with both genes measured, adjustable beside the two |r| cutoffs (0 shows everything).
  • The colour legend under the scatter no longer runs off the edges. Entries are held to the width of the row, the legend text shrinks when that would help, and names too long for any readable size (several Oncotree diseases run past 100 characters) are shortened with an ellipsis, keeping the count and r that the entry is read for. The full name stays on the chip above the plot.

v.87.15 (2026-08-10)

  • The gated export's two plot areas now line up exactly. Borrowing the chart's margins was not enough: each panel was still free to grow its own margins to fit its tick labels, and since the two carry different ranges they ended at different heights. That is now switched off for the gating plot, so both panels share one plot area, one type size and one baseline.

v.87.14 (2026-08-10)

  • The two panels of a gated export now match exactly. The gating plot was a picture taken from the screen while the chart beside it was redrawn at export size, so it came out a different size, with different lettering and the on-screen gray panel against the chart's white. The gating plot is now redrawn for the export at the chart's own width, height, margins and background, so plot areas, type and panel colour are identical and the two line up.
  • Export for AI says what it leaves out. The file now carries a notIncluded section naming the data the app holds but the export does not (drug response, growth rate, the genome-wide copy-number matrix, genes below the tier's variance filter, cell lines outside the cohort, raw fusion calls, identity warnings) and how to fetch each, plus what the app has no data for at all. The instructions tell the assistant to name such a gap and ask for it rather than treat the absence as a result.

v.87.13 (2026-08-10)

  • The gate is named above the plot, in the same line that lists the tissue and alteration filters, so a gated plot says so where you read the rest of its cohort.
  • Exports read in the order of the analysis: the gating plot first, then the plot of the population it selected, both the same size. PowerPoint places the two independent pictures the same way round.

v.87.12 (2026-08-10)

  • A gated figure exports as two panels side by side, at the same size. The gating plot used to be stacked underneath, which made a tall narrow figure; it now sits to the right of the chart, both panels exactly the same size, with the caption under the gate. The gating plot is also captured at the same dimensions the export renders at, so the two always match.
  • PowerPoint gets them as two separate pictures. Instead of one composed image, the slide carries the figure and the gating plot as independent objects, side by side and equally sized, so either can be moved, resized or deleted on the slide.

v.87.11 (2026-08-10)

  • The gene-check panel matches the rest of the app. It sat inside the same box the short status lines use, so it inherited their typewriter font and heavy brown headings, which made it the loudest thing on the page. It now uses the app's own typeface and weights at the size of the controls around it, keeping only the warm tint that marks it as something needing attention.

v.87.10 (2026-08-10)

  • A gate used as a filter now behaves like every other filter. It appears in Active filters as "Gate A (363)", stacks with the tissue and alteration filters, and is removed by clicking the chip. Changing the genes or axes no longer drops it: erasing the drawn shapes and removing the filter made from them are separate things now, so the main plot stays fully editable underneath the gate.
  • The gating plot is the same size as the plot above it and stays put while you change genes or filters, since those describe the plot above, not the gate that produced the cohort.

v.87.9 (2026-08-10)

  • Fix: a best-filter pick now shows in Lineage and disease. Choosing a tissue from the best-filter list applied it to the analysis but left the Lineage box reading "All lineages", so there was no sign of it and nothing to reset. The pick now goes through the Lineage control itself: the box shows the tissue, the subtype list and counts follow, and clearing it there clears the filter.
  • Fix: "Pick diseases to color" did nothing. The picker still only opened for tissue and subtype; it now opens for disease as well, listing the diseases grouped under their tissue.

v.87.8 (2026-08-10)

  • Both sex readings now cover every cell line. Sex has two independent axes: the annotation from DepMap's Model table, and the call computed from Y-chromosome markers and XIST. The annotation moved to 26Q1 with the rest of the data, but the expression-based call had only been carried over for the lines that existed before, leaving the 22 new ones blank. It is now recomputed across all 1,208 (302 female, 400 male, 506 unknown, where unknown covers Y-loss males and XIST-silenced females as before). None of the existing calls changed.

v.87.7 (2026-08-10)

  • A gate can now be used as a filter, the way a FACS gate is. Draw one or two gates and Apply gate as filter appears next to Compare; with both drawn it asks which one.
