The cell lines inside that gate become the cohort, every other filter still applies on top, and the plot the gate was drawn on is kept underneath so the figure still shows where the population came from. Exporting the image brings that gating plot with it, stacked under the chart with a one-line caption.
  • Comparison results announce themselves. On a short screen the comparison appeared below the fold with nothing to say so; a small green cue now points down and scrolls there when clicked, and gets out of the way on its own.
  • The correlation cutoff can go past 0.8. The slider still ends at 0.8, where it is most useful, but the + button keeps going to 1.0 for the very strongest correlations only, and the track returns to normal on the way back down. Min slope works the same way.
  • Fix: the compound list was still cut off on a wide screen. It was being clipped by the browser panel rather than the window edge; the pickers now measure against whichever boundary comes first.
  • The best-filter ranking controls no longer break mid-phrase in a narrow column, and export wording says "a spreadsheet" rather than naming one program.

v.87.6 (2026-08-10)

  • Export or copy the cell-line list as it stands. Two buttons in the Cell Line Browser take the visible list in its current sort order, with tissue, subtype, disease, sex and whichever value the list is sorted by (expression, drug-response AUC, copy number, mutation counts): one saves a CSV, the other copies tab-separated text straight into Excel.
  • Best filters can rank by correlation strength. The list still ranks tissues by how many genes stay connected; a second choice ranks by the average |r| of the pairs that survive there, which is the way to see where the relationships are tightest rather than most numerous. Lineages resting on fewer than three pairs are held below the others, since an average over one pair is not evidence.
  • Changing genes or the measure in the scatter keeps your filters. Editing the Genes (X/Y) box, switching GE / Expr / CN, or pressing the swap-axes button reset the tissue filter, colouring and axis measures; they now stay as you set them. Arriving at a different pair from the network still starts fresh.
  • Color by disease shows its group picker, as tissue and subtype already did.
  • Fix: patient sex was missing since the 26Q1 update. The field was dropped when the cell-line metadata was rebuilt, so the sex filter and symbols had nothing to read. Restored for all 1,208 lines.
  • The mRNA cutoff default is back to 0.50, matching gene effect, and the gene effect / mRNA choice is a quieter inline pair again.

v.87.5 (2026-08-10)

  • Gate comparison reaches the disease level. Comparing two gates showed where their cell lines come from by tissue and by subtype; it now adds the exact Oncotree disease as a third table, which is often where the real difference shows (CNS/Brain as a tissue becomes Glioblastoma IDH-Wildtype as a disease). The three tables are built by one shared routine instead of a copy each.
  • Color by disease in the scatter. The Color by picker offers tissue, subtype and now disease, with the same pick-your-groups list and per-group correlation in the legend.
  • mRNA runs start at a 0.60 cutoff. Expression correlates sit higher than gene effect across the board, so 0.50 returned a great deal more on that basis. Switching to mRNA expression moves the cutoff to 0.60 (and back to 0.50 for gene effect), leaving any value you set yourself untouched.
  • Fix: the compound list was cut off at the screen edge. The drug, gene and copy-number pickers in the Cell Line Browser hung from the left of an input near the right edge, so the explanation ran off the window. They now align to the input's right edge and stay inside the window.

v.87.4 (2026-08-10)

  • Fix: the network was drawn far too small. After the automatic arrangement the view zoomed out much further than the picture needed, leaving a small cluster in a mostly empty panel. The layout engine sizes the view from each label's last drawn position, and moving nodes into place does not refresh that: the labels were still recorded at their old coordinates, so the content looked hundreds of pixels wider than it was. The view now refreshes before it fits, which on a typical network is about a quarter larger than before.
  • The cancer type is underlined in the cell-line hover card, so it stands out from the rest of the sentence.

v.87.3 (2026-08-10)

  • The gene effect / mRNA choice is easier to find. It was plain text with small radio buttons, easy to miss under the analysis-mode block; the two options now sit in the same boxed, highlight-the-active-one style as the choice above them, headed Correlate on, each with a one-line description of the question it answers.

v.87.2 (2026-08-09)

  • The network can run on mRNA expression. A new Correlate using choice in Set Parameters switches the whole gene-set analysis between gene effect (CRISPR, the default) and expression (log₂ TPM+1), on the same cell lines, so the two networks are directly comparable. Everything follows the choice: the network, Correlations, Clusters (columns relabel to Expr mean / SD), the below-cutoff rows, node tooltips, and double-clicking a node or edge opens the matching expression view. The choice is saved with exports and restored with them; changing it marks Run as changed like any other parameter.

v.87.1 (2026-08-09)

  • Groundwork for the simpler builds. The PCA/UMAP wiring now checks that its section exists before attaching, so the V1 build (which removes the section) no longer loses every Cell Line Browser control registered after it. No change to how V2 behaves.

v.87.0 (2026-08-09)

  • Data files now update reliably. The big binary matrices (gene effect, expression, copy number) and a few side files were fetched without the version token, so a returning browser could pair fresh indices with a stale cached matrix and silently misread values after an update. Every data file now carries the same cache token as the app itself.
  • Data updated to DepMap 26Q1. Gene effect and expression, hotspot and damaging mutations, fusions (raw, validated and clinical tiers), functional loss, inferred subtypes, genome signatures, growth rate and the Model metadata all move from 25Q3 to the 26Q1 release. The CRISPR cohort grows from 1,186 to 1,208 cell lines (22 added, none removed, many of them pediatric bone and soft-tissue models) and from 18,435 to 18,531 genes; expression covers 1,719 lines. The copy-number layers deliberately stay on their previous releases (the merged gene-level CN matrix is 24Q4, the clinical WGS calls 25Q3), as DepMap has not updated the merged file and the WGS-only 26Q1 file would halve CN coverage. Saved figures re-run against the new data, so values can shift slightly; that is the point of the update. Sex-by-expression and STR annotations are carried over for existing lines (the 22 new lines show the annotated sex from the Model table).

v.86.41 (2026-08-09)

  • Grid filters stay where they were made. Gene picks from the Cell Line Browser's filter grids now affect only the browser list: they no longer filter any analysis, mark Run as changed, or appear in the parameters box. Picks made while Mutation analysis is the active mode belong to it alone, and picks made in Gene set mode belong to the network run alone, so switching modes no longer silently carries one cohort's filters into the other.

v.86.40 (2026-08-09)

  • Popouts stay usable when part of the browser window is off screen. A page cannot tell that the window's lower edge sits behind another app or past the screen border, so a popout's footer could end up unreachable there. Two ways out now: keep scrolling past the end and the whole popout slides up, bringing the footer into view (scrolling back first slides it home); or drag it by the title bar, which may now go above the window top.

v.86.39 (2026-08-09)

  • White background is back, and it works. A tick box in the scatter footer switches the plot panel between the default light gray and plain white, live on screen. The old pair of boxes it replaces was never wired to anything. The choice travels with exports and New tab.
  • A dragged popout comes back centered. Moving a popout by its title bar pinned it to that spot for the rest of the session; reopened on a smaller window it could sit with its footer beyond the screen edge and no way to scroll to it. Reopening any dialog now clears the old position. The title bar and footer also can no longer be squeezed out of a cramped dialog.

v.86.38 (2026-08-09)

  • No Plotly toolbar over the scatter. Arming a gate put Plotly's zoom/draw buttons in the plot's top corner; the chart now never shows that toolbar. Gates are drawn exactly as before, straight on the plot.
  • The dead White bg / Transparent tick boxes are gone from the scatter footer. They were wired to nothing; the background choice lives in the Export image dialog, where it now works.
  • Cell Line Browser cannot outgrow the window. The browser card could be pushed wider than the screen by its own toolbars (a flex quirk: a min-width of auto beats the max-width), cutting off the third list column. It now always fits, and the three columns share the visible width.

v.86.37 (2026-08-09)

  • Fix: White / Transparent now reaches the chart panel. Chart exports kept the light-gray plot area whichever background was picked, so the two options looked identical and Transparent did not appear to work. White now gives a solid white figure throughout; Transparent removes every background, plot panel included. Both options also explain themselves on hover.
  • Cell Line Browser: Export image. A new button in its header captures the whole browser as a picture (PNG / TIFF / PDF / PowerPoint), with the usual size and resolution choices.

v.86.36 (2026-08-09)

  • Export image works before any analysis. With no network drawn the button used to do nothing; it now opens the export dialog with one choice, The whole page, so a clean shot of the app itself can go straight into a presentation. Format, size and resolution are chosen as usual.

v.86.35 (2026-08-09)

  • The left-leaning network is fixed at its root. The layout's centre of gravity sits at a fixed point, but after the automatic arrangement (satellites moved aside, rows parked) the network's centre no longer did: the released picture slowly slid sideways toward it, then jumped to the middle at the next re-fit. The network is now centred on that point as the last assembly step of every Run and Shuffle, so there is nothing left to slide; no extra correction layers involved, and the earlier partial fix is folded into this one.
  • Gates: rectangle or lasso. Pressing Set Gate A/B now asks which shape to draw; the lasso is a free-hand loop for groups a box cannot isolate. Both can be dragged and reshaped afterwards, and Compare works the same.
  • Gene statistics label controls match the rest. The None/LFC/FDR row is now a Show statistics in label tick box that reveals the LFC/FDR choice, like the other label and color settings.
  • Clusters shows only correlated genes by default. The input genes without correlations moved behind the below cutoff tick, together with the near-miss flags; the Correlation column appears only then. Ticking Show all input genes in network now also ticks below cutoff in the Correlations and Clusters tabs, and unticking clears them.
  • Fix: PDF export garbled small p-values. The standard PDF fonts lack most superscript digits, so 10⁻²²² came out as "10{" plus broken spacing that pushed the stats line off the page. Exponents the font cannot show now export as 10^-222.
  • Fix: exported scatter figures forgot clicked labels. Cell lines marked by clicking a dot (and where their labels were dragged) were missing from the export file, so reopening it lost them. They are saved and restored now.

v.86.34 (2026-08-09)

  • The synonym panel is redone. Suggestions now sit in two white cards, Suggested replacements and No match found, with the names lined up in columns, green links like the rest of the app, and a hover ? on each heading explaining what the section does and what clicking a name changes. The buttons are now Use all and Keep my names.
  • Dropping a gene onto a parked one nudges it clear. A node dragged onto a gray parked gene used to sit exactly on top of it. It now slides just off on release; hand placement is untouched everywhere else, and no rule was added to the layout itself.
  • Edge slider numbers line up with the handle. The tick labels were evenly spaced but their values were not, so the handle at 5 did not sit over the 5.
  • * now marks the added genes. In the Correlations and Clusters tables the asterisk flags genes brought in by expanding a set, not your own list: the added genes are the few worth spotting.
  • Clusters: the Corr column is now labeled Correlation.

v.86.33 (2026-08-09)

  • Clusters: below cutoff tick box, same as the Correlations tab. Ticking it flips the Corr cell to Below cutoff for genes whose only correlations just missed the cutoff, and lists any such gene not already in the table, grayed at the bottom.
  • Correlations: * marks genes from your own list when expanding a set, matching the Clusters tab.
  • Consistent cursor over gene names. The Correlations and Clusters tables showed a question-mark cursor on hover; they now use the standard cursor like the rest of the app. The info popout on hover is unchanged.
  • Lined up / Floating only shows when relevant: the sub-choice now appears once Show all input genes is ticked, like the other sub-options.
  • Fix: parked genes turned green. Switching a node coloring off repainted every node input-green, including the genes without correlations; they now go back to gray.
  • Fix: the network could drift into the parked row. After a large run the network settles away from the layout's centre of gravity and then slides slowly back, straight through the lined-up genes. The network is now re-centred when the row is parked, and with a long gene list the parked genes no longer take part in the settling at all. The gap between network and row is also a little wider, keeping labels clear of the parked nodes.

v.86.32 (2026-08-09)

  • Show all input genes: choose Lined up or Floating. A small sub-choice under the checkbox now switches the genes without correlations between the tidy parked row (Lined up) and drifting freely around the network (Floating), as they did before the row existed.
  • The lined-up row sits much closer and tighter. The parked genes still nudged the network away from themselves through the layout physics, opening a wide gap that shrank the whole picture. They are now fully out of the simulation, spaced by what a node and its label actually need, and centred right under the network.
  • A quiet pointer on very large networks. When a network has so many genes that labels shrink to specks, a small dismissible note suggests the Correlation and Clusters tabs for the overview, and exporting the image at a larger size for a full-page figure.

v.86.31 (2026-08-09)

  • Reset all starts quiet. On a fresh page it now looks like its Options neighbours (outline, nothing to shout about) and only turns solid green once there is actually something to reset: an analysis has produced results, or a filter has been changed.

v.86.30 (2026-08-08)

  • One synonym flow instead of two. The Find Synonyms button and the separate "did you mean" line are folded into a single automatic panel: unknown genes are checked against the synonym and mouse-ortholog tables as you type, matches appear as "Trp53 → TP53" suggestions with Use all synonyms and Don't use suggested names as the resolutions (each name is also clickable on its own), and whatever has no synonym falls through to the nearest-match alternatives, with an optional online search (MyGene.info) as the last resort.
  • Network font size can go beyond the slider. The slider still draws 10-40, but the + button keeps going past 40 when a poster needs bigger labels; stepping back down returns to the normal range. Reopened figures saved with a larger font get it back too.

v.86.29 (2026-08-08)

  • Reopening an exported network now recreates its look, not just its graph. The saved settings (font, node and edge size, Color by GE / stats, labels, node border) were written into the controls on open and then silently wiped by the "new run" reset before the network drew. The reset now steps aside during a restore. The export also carries more of the picture: Spread, the Aa text settings (font family, label/node color, legend and banner size/color, custom banner text, bold/italic), and highlighted nodes, all of which are reapplied on open. Older export files still open, they just fall back to defaults for the fields they predate.

v.86.28 (2026-08-08)

  • Scatter: the tissue/subtype legend now shows each group's own correlation. With Color by tissue or subtype active, every legend entry reads like "Lung (125, r=-0.81)", including the gray "Not selected" bucket, so group-specific relationships are visible at a glance. Groups with fewer than 3 cell lines show no r.

v.86.27 (2026-08-08)

  • The network no longer settles off to the left. The in-frame guard used to act only when a node left the panel; satellites drifting back toward the cluster could empty one side without tripping it, and the picture sat off-centre. The guard now also re-centres when the network's middle wanders from the panel's.
  • The Run button announces stale results. Changing the correlation cutoff, min slope or min cell lines after an analysis, or picking a tissue from the Best filters dropdown, turns the button into "Run ▶ (filters changed)" so it is clear the picture no longer matches the settings. Tissue, subtype and disease pickers already did this.
  • Show all input genes: the extra genes now line up. The input genes without correlations used to scatter and drift, since no edge holds them. They now park in a tidy alphabetical grid below the network's lower right corner, pinned in place; drag one and it stays where you drop it.

v.86.26 (2026-08-08)

  • Found and fixed the real Expand my set freeze. After every run, the "Best filters" search silently re-ran the full 18,000-gene scan once per tissue, ~30 scans in one uninterruptible block. In Expand mode that froze the page for 30-60 seconds: the network's settle animation starved into jumps, and the guard that keeps the picture in frame expired before it could act, leaving the network off-centre. The search now ranks tissues using the genes the run actually produced (hundreds of times cheaper), works through tissues one at a time so the page keeps painting, and a new Run cancels a search still in progress instead of queuing behind it.
  • The network stays in frame as long as it floats. The off-screen rescue used to stop watching 4 seconds after a run; the floating layout could drift out of view right after. It now watches until you take hold of the view yourself (any drag or zoom stops it).

v.86.25 (2026-08-08)

  • Expand my set no longer freezes the page. Two seconds-long stalls hit expanded networks: an untangling pass whose cost explodes with network size (it now runs only on networks small enough to benefit, under a hard time limit), and a slow initial-layout computation that big networks skip entirely, they start from random positions like Shuffle does.
  • Big networks settle before they are shown, and stay in frame. Networks past 150 genes get twice the hidden settling time, so the visible jumping after load is mostly gone, and the guard that re-frames the view when nodes drift off-screen now watches large networks for 12 seconds instead of 4.

v.86.24 (2026-08-08)

  • The Spread meter always tells the truth. Shuffle keeps all your settings (font, node, edge, Spread) but the meter used to jump back to 100 while the layout kept the old spacing; it now stays at the value the layout was settled with. The Reset button, which left Spread untouched, now returns it to 100 and actually widens the layout.
  • "How it works" refocused on the two main tools. Gene set analysis and the Cell Line Browser carry the intro and the tool cards; Mutation analysis is a one-line pointer under Options → Other.

v.86.23 (2026-08-08)

  • The network floats unless you lock it. All the automatic locking is gone: big networks no longer open locked, separated clusters are no longer pinned in place, and the Spread control no longer freezes the layout. Nodes belong to the physics engine at all times unless you press Lock.
  • Spread now changes the physics itself. Lowering it shortens the springs and softens the repulsion, so the cluster visibly floats into a tighter arrangement and settles at a real equilibrium with even spacing, exactly like the layouts the solver produces on its own. Raising it back re-expands the same way. The camera never moves. If you have locked the layout, the slider instead scales the frozen picture in place, as before.
  • Trade-off, made deliberately: without pinning, a disconnected small cluster can slowly drift toward the main network and settle beside it. Node-on-node overlap is still prevented by the repulsion, and everything stays draggable. The guarantee that Run and Shuffle never leave nodes or labels outside the visible area is unchanged.
  • Wiki: the p53 panel is now called "p53 (damage response)".

v.86.22 (2026-08-08)

  • The Spread buttons no longer throw the network sideways. The spacing change re-centered the camera on the average node position, which sits away from the middle whenever a separate small cluster is parked to one side, so one press shifted the whole picture. Spacing now changes around the point you are looking at and the camera stays put.
  • Separated clusters can be dragged again. Their nodes are pinned so the physics engine cannot pull them back across the main network, but pinning also blocked hand-dragging. Grabbing a pinned node now unpins it for the drag and re-pins it where you drop it.
  • The scatter's alteration grids now actually filter the scatter, and only the scatter. Picks made from the grid buttons in the scatter apply to that plot immediately and never touch the analysis: no "filters changed" marker on the network's Run button, and the scatter's Reset clears only its own picks. The grid also shows the cells currently in the plot. Grid picks from the analysis side still carry into an open scatter as before, and a separate bug is fixed where those picks never refreshed an open scatter at all.
  • Dot color joins the scatter settings. The cell-line dot color can now be changed both in the Plot size box and in the Aa settings dialog (the two stay in step), the settings section is called "Cell line dots" instead of "Markers", and Scale All sits directly above Font Sizes & Visibility.
  • Gene Effect: a subtype pick divides the chart into diseases, the same way a tissue pick divides it into subtypes. Applies to the tissue view and the inline compare tables.
  • Wiki: the p53 panel no longer calls the brake lost when only 9p21 is deleted. CDKN2A and CDKN2B are lost together in one 9p21 deletion but were listed as two independent hits; they now merge into one CDKN2A/B entry. CDKN2B (p15, a CDK4/6 inhibitor with no p53 role) moved to the cell-cycle panel, where the deletion correctly reads "Brake lost". When the p53 panel's only loss is CDKN2A, the verdict reads "Regulation lost, TP53 intact": the p14ARF arm of that locus restrains MDM2, so p53 is deregulated upstream while TP53 itself is unaltered, which matches the CRISPR readout in such lines (TP53 knockout helps, MDM2 knockout hurts).

v.86.21 (2026-08-08)

  • Options focused on the app's two pillars. The row now reads Gene set analysis, Cell Line Browser, Other, Reset all. Mutation analysis moved into the Other menu; while it is the active mode the Other button itself turns green and reads "Mutation analysis", so the current mode stays visible and the way back is the same menu. Reset all moved up from the results tab row into the freed slot.

v.86.20 (2026-08-08)

  • One tooltip per gene chip. Copy-number gene chips and the wiki's pathway chips showed two overlapping popups on hover: the browser's own tooltip and the gene info card. The chip's context (relative copy number, why the pathway flags it) now appears inside the single gene card instead.

v.86.19 (2026-08-08)

  • Saved views restore the full cohort, not just the picture. A field-by-field audit of every export/restore path found many settings the app used but never saved, or saved but never re-applied. Network exports now carry the disease-level pick, hotspot/fusion/CN parameter filters, tissue exclusions and the cell-line subset, and re-apply them on restore. Mutation Inspect exports carry the additional analysis filters, tissue exclusions, group minimum and the GE/expression metric. Scatter restores keep the disease filter, overlay view modes, highlighted cells and the custom cell-line list; the gene-effect and pair-correlation popouts keep their disease and level filters. Alteration-grid exports remember whether they were a hotspot, fusion or CN grid. An expression-correlate scatter now restores as itself, mutation analysis and all, instead of as a bare scatter, and a by-tissue chart reopens as the by-tissue view. Opening a saved file in a working tab also resets all of this state first, so the current session's filters no longer bleed into the restored view.

v.86.18 (2026-08-08)

  • Saved grid picks are applied again on restore. Two restore paths stored the oncoprint grid's include/exclude picks but never applied them: a Mutation Inspect reopened in a new tab re-ran on the unfiltered cohort, and a restored grid showed the checkboxes ticked while every downstream view ignored them. Both now reproduce the saved cohort exactly.

v.86.17 (2026-08-08)

  • Exact p-values at every cohort size. A numerical audit against SciPy found two defects in the t-distribution p-value used by the mutation analysis, the pair correlations and the expression correlates: above 100 degrees of freedom it switched to a normal approximation that overstates significance enormously in the far tail (KRAS vs KRAS reported p = 3.6e-112 where the correct value is 2.0e-54), and the exact formula it fell back on stopped converging for large cohorts. Both fixed; p-values now agree with SciPy to full precision across the tested range (t up to 40, df up to 1145, p down to 1e-219). Gene rankings were essentially unaffected, but borderline genes near p = 0.05 were slightly over-called before and no longer are.

v.86.16 (2026-08-08)

  • Cohort descriptions name the disease level. The network filter banner and the Gene Effect popout's filter description now list an applied disease filter alongside tissue and subtype, so what was run is fully stated.

v.86.15 (2026-08-08)

  • Copy sweep across the whole app. Typos fixed ("analyses", a garbled sentence in the Cell Line Browser help), stale text updated (the first-run hint now names "2. Input Gene Set", the Synonyms tab explains Find Synonyms, the Summary tab uses the current mode names), "cells" is now "cell lines" wherever the unit is cell lines, spelling standardized to American English (color, tumor, ortholog, leukemia…), the same feature now has one name everywhere (Custom cell lines, By hotspot mutation, Min Cell Lines, Gene 1/Gene 2), and legend/heading capitalization is consistent.

v.86.14 (2026-08-08)

  • Copy-number analyses no longer restore as Functional Loss. Opening a CN amplification / deep-deletion inspect in a new tab, or restoring one from an exported image, silently re-ran it as a functional-loss analysis with different groups and p-values; the sub-type is now carried and restored exactly. Expression correlates and the AI export also re-align their call matrix to the results on display, so flipping the sub-type radio without re-running can no longer swap in the wrong data.
  • Every mutation-analysis view now speaks the words of its sub-type. A sweep found many places that said "mutated vs WT" for fusion / functional-loss / copy-number results: the statistics line, the p<0.05 filter label, the results header, the empty-result explanation, the inspect legend, the expression-correlate scatter and subgroup choices, the comparison tables and their tooltips, the UpSet plot, and every CSV header. They now say fused vs no fusion, lost vs intact, amplified vs neutral, and so on. CSV columns on an mRNA run now say Expr instead of GE, and the AI export groups cell lines under type-correct names instead of calling neutral lines "WT".

v.86.13 (2026-08-08)

  • The disease filter now reaches everywhere the tissue and subtype filters do. A deep audit found the newest filter level silently dropped in several places; all now respect it: the inspect scatter opened from an analysis or from the network (the disease pick carries over with the tissue), the Gene Effect popout opened with first-page or Cell Line Browser filters, the "compare all" mutation/fusion/copy-number tables in the inspect scatter (they are computed over exactly the plotted cell lines), the popout comparison tables (By tissue and the Δ tables), Find correlates run before the plot is built (also gained the copy-number filter), Expression correlates (also now honours the popout's subtype pick), and the option counts in filter dropdowns.
  • Versions after v.85.99 renumbered to v.86.0-12: the counter rolls over at .99.

v.86.12 (2026-08-07)

  • The Spread slider scales the network you are looking at. It used to scale a stored snapshot of the layout taken before the solver's final adjustments, so grabbing the slider could snap the network to an older shape. It now takes the current on-screen layout as its reference the moment you move it, so the arrangement stays the same and only the distances change.

v.86.11 (2026-08-07)

  • Shuffle no longer leaves the network secretly locked. The shuffle stopped the solver to separate sub-networks but never handed the nodes back, so the network behaved locked under an unlocked button, and the layout kept its strained, compressed look instead of relaxing to even spacing. The solver now gets the nodes back after every shuffle (when unlocked), with a re-fit once it settles.

v.86.10 (2026-08-07)

  • Shuffle keeps Spread at 100. Rolling a random Spread with each shuffle made the layout look compressed more often than good, so a shuffle now only re-rolls the arrangement at full spacing; the Spread slider stays yours to adjust afterwards.

v.86.9 (2026-08-07)

  • An empty result says why. When Run returns nothing, both analyses now state the specific reason: too few cell lines under the current filters for the Min Cell Lines setting (with the numbers), or genes tested but none passing the cutoff, each with the fix to try.
  • Mutation analysis defaults to Min Cell Lines 3 (was 5).
  • The Shuffle's rolled Spread now visibly takes effect. The roll was being cancelled twice over: the final re-fit zoomed to the compacted content and the released solver re-expanded it to its spring spacing. The shuffle now frames the settled layout first, compacts it by the rolled Spread at that zoom, and ends Locked so the layout keeps its density; Unlock restores the full spacing as always.
  • The "nodes outside the view" warning clears itself. It used to stay up after the view had already been rescued; it now keeps re-checking while shown and disappears the moment everything is back inside. The automatic rescue also uses the same fit test as the warning, so the two can no longer disagree.

v.86.8 (2026-08-07)

  • The network can no longer end up outside the view after Run or Shuffle. Event-based re-fitting proved unreliable against the solver's last micro-adjustments; for a few seconds after every Run and Shuffle a guard now watches the frame and re-fits the moment anything strays, stopping as soon as you take hold of the view.
  • Every AI export now verifies itself against the visible title. The correlation, gene-effect, gates, mutation and expression-correlate exports record a check of their focal gene(s) against the title on screen, and warn before download if the two disagree, so a stale-state mismatch like the one just fixed cannot pass silently anywhere.

v.86.7 (2026-08-07)

  • Fix: the AI export could name the wrong gene. Exporting from a mutation-inspect view read the gene from the normal gene-effect view's state, which can hold a stale gene from an earlier analysis, so the file (its label, its precomputed summaries and its filename) described a different gene than the plot. The export now reads the plotted gene, and also records the disease filter and whether the view showed gene effect or mRNA expression.

v.86.6 (2026-08-07)

  • Run re-frames after the solver's final settle, the same guard Shuffle got: the released solver could still nudge the cluster after the fit, leaving a node half outside the view.

v.86.5 (2026-08-07)

  • Run leaves the network unlocked again, safely. Instead of locking everything, only the separated side-components are pinned individually (they can still be dragged by hand); the main cluster stays live as before, and unlocking no longer reforms the picture out of view.
  • Shuffle rolls look right again. The rolled Spread is now applied before the components are packed; scaling the packed arrangement squeezed side-components back over the main cluster, which is what made some rolls look strange.

v.86.4 (2026-08-07)

  • Shuffle also rolls the spacing. Each click draws a new Spread between 60 and 100 alongside the new layout, so consecutive shuffles offer different densities; the slider follows the drawn value and can be tuned from there.

v.86.3 (2026-08-07)

  • Run and Shuffle always leave the whole network in view. After the components were separated, the solver was handed the nodes back and drifted them out of the fitted frame, clipping nodes and labels at the edges. A hand-arranged multi-component layout now stays locked (unlock to release it), many small components wrap into rows instead of one wide strip, and the view is re-fitted as the very last step.

v.86.2 (2026-08-07)

  • Pathway figure cleaned up. The complex label overflowed its box; the TSC card now holds the two subunits with a small caption underneath, everything inside its border.

v.86.1 (2026-08-07)

  • Disconnected sub-networks are laid out apart. A separate pair or cluster could settle across another component's edges (a TSC1–TSC2 pair lying over the TP53 cluster). After the layout settles, and after every Shuffle, components are now moved side by side with clear space between them.

v.86.0 (2026-08-07)

  • The network's arrow buttons move the network the way they point. They used to pan the camera, so pressing left slid the picture right. Each arrow now shows, and does, the direction the network itself moves.
  • Gene set analysis marks its Run button too. Changing a filter after a run turns Run amber reading "filters changed", the same signal the mutation analysis got.

v.85.99 (2026-08-07)

  • "Not further specified" diseases are marked. Some lines are typed only to the subtype level, so their disease entry repeats the subtype name ("Melanoma" beside "Cutaneous Melanoma"), which read as a separate entity. Disease menus now say "Melanoma, no finer subtype recorded (n=…)" (as the Cell Line Browser already did), and the Tissue split popups mark such rows with a * and a footnote.

v.85.98 (2026-08-07)

  • Mutation-inspect chips and header show the tissue and disease. The chip strip was drawn before the filters were filled in, so it missed them; it now redraws after, and the plot's header line names the disease level alongside lineage and subtype.
  • Run marks itself stale on any filter change. Changing lineage, subtype, disease, excluded tissues, a Tissue split or any genetic-alteration filter after a run turns the Run button amber ("filters changed"), same as grid picks.

v.85.97 (2026-08-07)

  • Title and subtitle switch independently everywhere. On plots where the two share one annotation (gene-effect tissue view, UMAP), the Title box used to hide both; each part now has its own switch that leaves the other alone.
  • Highlighted genes are listed under View controls, like Select Mode's selection: click a name to remove that highlight, or Clear to remove them all.

v.85.96 (2026-08-07)

  • Grid picks no longer run the analysis by themselves. Applying a grid filter silently re-ran the mutation analysis, which made pressing Run afterwards look dead. The table now stays as it is, the Run button turns amber reading "filters changed", and you run when ready.
  • Highlight ring: longer dashes, same gaps.
  • Several diseases from a Tissue split show up everywhere. Inspect opened from such an analysis used to state only the lineage (e.g. Skin) while filtering correctly underneath; its disease selector now carries the whole set as one entry ("Melanoma + Acral Melanoma (from analysis)"), shown in the chips too. The set also scopes the front page's tissue and subtype lists, travels with "Open in new tab" and image exports, and is restored with them; the AI export names it as well.

v.85.95 (2026-08-07)

  • The disease filter reaches everywhere. Inspect opened from a mutation analysis now shows the run's disease in its filter row and applies it; several diseases ticked in a Tissue split (e.g. melanoma + cutaneous melanoma) now filter the run as a set, are shown in the header and chips, and clear together; the filter-menu counts in the popouts also respect the disease pick.
  • Popups can be moved. The Tissue split and general tissue popups drag by their header, so nothing is stuck half off-screen on a small laptop.
  • Highlight ring restyled. A thick dashed ring in the node's own colours instead of the purple one.
  • Text settings: every element on the plot can be switched off. X and Y tick labels gained on/off boxes like the title, labels and legend.
  • The mutation table names its measure. Columns and the statistics note read Δ Expr / mean Expr when the analysis ranks mRNA expression, instead of always saying GE.
  • Scatter polish. The Active filters box is always present (no layout jump) with Reset on its header row; the alteration filter menus respect the disease pick.
  • "How it works" polish. Tighter wording, a redrawn pathway figure (now including RHEB), numbered figures, and the platform described as multi-omics analysis of human cancer cell lines built around CRISPR screens.

v.85.94 (2026-08-07)

  • The Tissue split's finer levels now reach the analysis. Selecting a subtype or exact disease in the split popup set the filters, but Run only honoured the lineage, so the WT / mutated counts disagreed with the popup. The disease level is now applied in the analysis, its inspect views and compares, and shown in the results header.
  • Grid picks no longer lock the alteration filters. Applying e.g. TP53 Mut from a grid grayed out the hotspot filter widget; it stays usable, so a picked gene and further grid picks combine.
  • Highlight is click-to-highlight. The network's Highlight button now works like Select Mode: click it, then click genes to give them the purple ring (kept in exports); no typing needed. The two button rows share one height, and the Appearance box stretches to match its neighbours.
  • Mutation-inspect compares match the scatter. The compare row reads Compare: Tissue / Hotspot / Amp/Del / Fusion, and the table now replaces the plot with a Back to Graph button instead of appearing below it. Clicking a row applies the filter and returns to the graph.
  • Scatter: filters separated from Compare, and Reset resets. Filter chips live in their own "Active filters" box with the Reset button, which now also clears the disease filter and grid picks (it previously left both).
  • Mutation analysis toolbar on one row. Search, Enrichr and the exports share a row; Compare by Tissue is removed (the Tissue split in box 1 covers the per-tissue view). The two p-value controls explain their different jobs on hover.
  • AI export upgraded. Exports now carry the focal genes' own mutation and copy-number status, a note that gene effect is Chronos-processed and already copy-number-corrected, and a calibration guide for judging correlation sizes; the reply instructions ask for a brief write-up that leads with the biological answer instead of narrating every check.

v.85.93 (2026-08-07)

  • "How it works" rewritten around the three tools. Correlate is presented as a multi-omics platform centred on CRISPR screen data: Gene set analysis (connections within a set, extended networks), Mutation analysis (mutation-specific vulnerabilities) and the Cell Line Browser (finding cell lines with the features a project needs), with the correlation explainer framed as the machinery behind Gene set analysis.

v.85.92 (2026-08-07)

  • Hover cards wait longer and stop lingering. Cell-line cards now appear after 450 ms instead of 180 ms, and opening any popout closes leftover hover cards and the network's Settings panel, which used to stay on top of the new view.
  • Filter widgets no longer look locked. Clicking a filter box that already holds a pick (e.g. TP53) used to search for that text and offer nothing else; it now shows the full list so the pick can be changed. In the mutation-inspect view the same boxes suggested nothing at all; they now fall back to the whole panel's genes.
  • Reset clears the disease filter everywhere. The gene-effect popout's reset also kept the subtype select hidden and grid picks alive; all cleared now.
  • Network highlight: purple, and its own button. The ring is purple instead of orange, and a Highlight button sits in View controls (two rows of four) with a small popup, no need to dig into Settings.
  • Mutation analysis polish. Genes measured in fewer cell lines get a * on their N columns with a footnote (e.g. INTS4); Enrichr sits on the same row as Compare by Tissue; the compare window is titled by what it splits (e.g. "MTAP lost vs intact") instead of always saying "Hotspot Mutational Analysis"; opening Inspect from an mRNA table now sets the GE/Expression selector to Expression.
  • Mutation-inspect filters reorganized. Two labelled rows, "Lineage and disease" and "Genetic alterations" (the same group names the front page and the Cell Line Browser use), with compact boxes instead of full-width ones.

v.85.91 (2026-08-07)

  • The header centres over the app. The logo image is shifted so its visible text sits on the page's centre line; the tagline and links centre beneath it, and the distance from the page edge to "How it works" now equals the distance to "YouTube". The version badge floats just after YouTube without taking part in the centring.
  • Network gene names are italic, as gene symbols conventionally are, with Bold / Italic toggles in Settings. Settings also gains the gene-name size (the same control as the Font slider above the network; the two stay in step) and a Highlight genes box: type one or more genes and they get an orange ring that carries into Export image and Copy network.
  • Appearance slider polish. The tick numbers now sit under the ends of the green track instead of under the − / + buttons, and the track runs light-to-dark green so it hints which way the value grows.
  • Exported networks centre over their legend. The legend centres on the image, but the nodes sat wherever they were last panned, visibly off-centre with wider legends (e.g. with a node colour scale). The network is now shifted so its content centres over the legend.
  • The correlation popout always shows all three tissue filters. A reset hid the subtype select, so the box sometimes showed two levels and sometimes three.
  • Grid picks now redraw the open popout. Ticking include / exclude in an alteration grid opened from the correlation, gene-effect or correlation-analysis panel applied the filter but nothing refreshed, so it looked like the grid did nothing. The grid is also how several hotspot genes are combined: pick one in the filter box and add more from the grid.
  • Scatter Reset clears every filter. The disease pick, the copy-number filter and grid picks survived a reset; now nothing does.
  • Hotspot filters say "hotspot". Chips and filter summaries read e.g. "TP53 hotspot-mutated" / "TP53: hotspot mut (1+2)" instead of the ambiguous "TP53: 1+2 mut".

v.85.90 (2026-08-07)

  • Compare-by-Hotspot numbers match what clicking shows. The correlation popout's hotspot comparison computed its groups from 2-copy mutants only, while clicking a row filtered the scatter to 1+2-copy mutants, so n and r changed on the way. The table now uses the same 1+2 split as the click.
  • Find correlates: separate cutoffs for GE and Expression. Expression-vs-GE correlations run weaker, so one shared 0.3 cutoff left the expression panel almost always empty. The expression list now defaults to |r| ≥ 0.1, adjustable on its own.
  • A disease can be chosen first. Picking e.g. Ewing sarcoma with no tissue set now narrows the tissue and subtype lists to where it belongs, in the parameters, correlation, gene-effect, correlation-analysis and cell-line-browser panels. All three selectors scale to each other in both directions.
  • Mutation analysis cleanup. Its own Run button (box 2 is hidden in this mode and took the Run button with it); the boxes now read 1 and 2; the Network / Correlations / Clusters tabs leave with the mode; the per-alteration tissue button is renamed "Tissue split" so it cannot be confused with the general Tissues selector; the Disease dropdown looks and opens like Lineage and Subtype.

v.85.89 (2026-08-07)

  • The mutation-inspect y-axis title stays on the canvas. It could disappear in two ways: the plot's width is unknown while the popout is still opening, which mis-placed the rotated label (sometimes fully off the canvas), and long group labels pushed it past the reserved margin. It is now placed in pixels from the plot edge and clamped inside the margin. A dragged label position also no longer carries over to a different gene or stratifier.

v.85.88 (2026-08-07)

  • Subtype and disease selectors scale to each other, everywhere. The disease list was already narrowed by the chosen subtype; picking a disease now narrows the subtype list in return, in the parameters, correlation, gene-effect, correlation-analysis and cell-line-browser panels. Every subtype list is ranked by count with the count shown, and a still-valid choice is kept when the list rescopes.
  • The correlation-analysis subtype filter works. The control was in the panel but never filled, so it always read "All subtypes" whatever the tissue.

v.85.87 (2026-08-07)

  • Shuffle button for the network layout. Next to Reset in View controls: each click re-rolls the layout from new random starting positions and lets it settle, so you can keep clicking until the arrangement looks right. The Lock state is left as it was.
  • Node border moved into Settings. The checkbox now sits with the other appearance controls in the network's Settings popout instead of crowding the toolbar.

v.85.86 (2026-08-07)

  • The three-panel view's headings have their own settings row. Text settings now shows a Panels row under Font Sizes & Visibility: one checkbox switches all three panel headings on or off (like the title's), and one size control resizes them together, medians line included.

v.85.85 (2026-08-07)

  • The Tissues popouts drill down three levels. In mutation analysis (and the general tissue selector), expanding a tissue shows its subtypes as before, and expanding a subtype now shows the exact Oncotree diseases beneath it, with the same counts, bars and checkboxes. Ticking one disease and pressing Apply sets tissue, subtype and disease filters in one go.

v.85.84 (2026-08-07)

  • The header lines up on the logo. The tree makes the logo image wider than its text, so "extended version" and the links below centred on the page but sat visibly right of the wordmark. Both now centre under the visible text, with "Green Listed" pinned to the exact middle of the row; the version badge stays on the right, outside the centring.
  • Copy beside every image export. The Gene Effect chart, the expression-correlate scatter, the correlation analysis chart, the UMAP / PCA plot, the mutation grid and the UpSet plot now have the same Copy button the correlation scatter and network already had: one click puts the picture on the clipboard, ready to paste into an email or slide. The grid copies in full, not just the part scrolled into view.

v.85.83 (2026-08-07)

  • Fusion counts agree everywhere. The fusion grid and the filter menus counted only the fusion caller's output, while selecting a fusion also included cell lines whose fusion is documented in the literature but that the caller could not read (most Ewing sarcoma lines, for example: the grid said 14 EWSR1-FLI1 lines, selecting it gave 23). All counts now include the published calls; in the grid they are drawn as high-confidence.

v.85.82 (2026-08-07)

  • Wiki gene plots mark the Wiki's own cell line again. Opening a Wiki by shift-clicking a point in a correlation plot and then clicking a gene showed the gene-effect or expression plot without the arrow marking that cell line. The plot was told to mark the cell line inspected in the Cell Line Browser, which is empty or a different line when the Wiki comes from a plot.
  • The sparse-data warning no longer runs off the plot. The orange note about a gene measured in few lines was one long line, cut off at both ends on narrower plots. It now wraps to the plot width.
  • The subtitle can be switched off in the correlation plot's text settings. The Subtitle row under Font Sizes & Visibility now has an on/off box like the title, axis labels and legend.

v.85.81 (2026-08-07)

  • A wrapped title is no longer cut off at the top. The space reserved above the plot covered the gap to the heading but not the heading's own height, so the first line of a two-line title sat outside the visible area. Both blocks are now measured from the top of the plot and the reserve covers the whole stack.

v.85.80 (2026-08-07)

  • Title and subtitle no longer collide, or run into the plot. Splitting them in the previous version left the statistics lines positioned off a control that does not always exist, so they landed on the heading and over the chart. Both blocks are now placed from the real plot height, with the space above reserved to match.
  • The grid button sits beside its gene box. The box gives up the width the button needs; previously the button had exactly its own width to fit in and was pushed onto the next line by the four pixels of its margin.
  • Removing an alteration filter from its chip no longer reopens the grid. The grid's own clear button still redraws it, which is what that button is for.
  • Test Genes cycles through five sets. Press it again for a different one: the p53 axis with TSC1/TSC2 alongside, homologous recombination, RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and chromatin remodelling. Each is a coherent piece of biology, so the network has something to show rather than being a grab-bag.

v.85.79 (2026-08-07)

  • Click a cell line's label on the correlation plot to take it off. The same gesture the gene effect popout uses, with a “click to remove” hint on hover. Until now labels could only be removed from the chip row under the plot, which meant hunting for the name you had just clicked onto the chart.
  • Title and subtitle no longer stretch apart on the expression view. They are drawn as two separate blocks, so the heading keeps its size and the statistics lines under it keep their tight spacing. Previously they shared one block and therefore one line height: tight enough for the statistics made the heading collide, loose enough for the heading pushed the statistics far apart.
  • The grid button no longer sits on top of the gene box. It was covering the start of the placeholder text.

v.85.78 (2026-08-07)

  • The title keeps its size when an axis switches to expression. A longer label made the heading shrink from 25px to 17px to stay on one line. It now keeps the size it is set to and wraps instead, with the two lines spaced so they cannot collide.
  • Unlocking the network brings everything back into view. Releasing hand-placed nodes could leave one, or its label, over the edge; the view is now refitted once the layout stops moving.
  • Three tissue levels everywhere, all the same shape. Tissue, subtype and disease now sit together in the correlation scatter and the gene effect popout, all the same width and size. The disease selector was stretching right across the plot, and subtype was missing altogether in the scatter.
  • Subtype no longer appears and disappears as a tissue is picked, in the scatter and the gene effect popout as well as the analysis panel, so nothing jumps.
  • The grid buttons share a row with their gene box rather than taking a line of their own.

v.85.77 (2026-08-07)

  • The header sits straight. The version badge was part of the centred row, so the five links were pushed left of the logo. It is now placed on the right independently and the links centre on the logo exactly. “Extended version” has been tucked up under the tagline, clear of the links below.
  • One heading style above the network. Two of the four blocks of controls had a heading and two had none, and the ones that did set their own size and weight. All four now read the same: Appearance, Labels and colour, View controls, Export.
  • One chip everywhere. Filter chips had their own size, weight and radius in each place they were built. Size, shape and border now come from one rule, so a chip looks the same in the browser, the analysis panel and every popout. The row of them sits in its own panel labelled Active, rather than reading as another line of small text.
  • Subtype and disease are always on screen in the analysis panel instead of appearing once a lineage is picked, so choosing a tissue no longer makes the panel jump. The new disease selectors also match their neighbours instead of standing out white.

v.85.76 (2026-08-07)

  • Lineage, subtype and disease everywhere. Only the Cell Line Browser offered all three levels; the analysis panel and the gene effect popout stopped at subtype and the correlation analysis panel had tissue alone. All four now have a Disease selector using the same Oncotree entities, and the correlation analysis panel gains a subtype selector too. Each disease list follows the tissue and subtype already chosen in that panel, so it never offers a disease that would empty the view, and the choice appears as a chip like every other filter.

v.85.75 (2026-08-07)

  • The network never opens with anything cut off. Running an analysis could still leave a node or its label over the edge. The fit was being applied before the layout engine got the nodes back, and it then nudged one out again. It now runs after the layout has settled, and recentres before zooming out.
  • Spread starts at 100 again, and the sliders are back to their original stacked look with their scales, at about 70% of the old size. The single-line version was too cramped.
  • No more wild-type / mutated dropdown beside the alteration filters. Picking a gene assumes altered, as in the Cell Line Browser; click the chip that appears to switch it to wild-type or a specific copy count, or use the grid button. Applies to the analysis panel, the correlation scatter, the gene effect popout and the correlation analysis panel.
  • A grid button beside every alteration filter, everywhere. The correlation scatter and correlation analysis panels also honour genes picked from a grid now, which they previously ignored.
  • Dragging a node no longer gets undone by the Spread slider. Spread scales from a stored copy of the settled layout, which did not include nodes you had moved by hand, so they snapped back. Moved nodes are now folded into that copy.

v.85.74 (2026-08-06)

  • A suggested spelling goes into the box you typed in. When a gene is not found the “Did you mean” suggestions used to copy to the clipboard, leaving you to find the box and paste it, which is the work the suggestion was there to save. Clicking one now replaces the misspelling where it was typed, whichever gene box that was, and re-runs whatever depended on it. If nothing on screen still holds the typo it falls back to copying.

v.85.73 (2026-08-06)

  • Correlation titles no longer overlap themselves. When the gene pair was too long for one line the second line landed on top of the first. The plotting library spaces the lines of a heading by the heading's own font size rather than the size each line is drawn at, so a title drawn large inside a block spaced for small text collided. The pair label now shrinks until it fits on one line, and in the rare case it still has to wrap the block is spaced for the title instead.

v.85.72 (2026-08-06)

  • The headings on a split plot can be edited. When a correlation is shown as three panels (wild-type / one mutation / two mutations, or the fusion equivalent) each panel has its own heading, but the text settings only offered the overall title, so those three were fixed. They now appear as Panel 1, 2 and 3 alongside the title and axis labels. A panel you do not edit keeps exactly the heading it was drawn with.

v.85.71 (2026-08-06)

  • The Wiki histograms have been redrawn. All of them, receptor status, drug response and the genome panels, now share one look: solid bars in a single muted colour instead of a pale fill ringed by a bright outline, which was what made them look sketched; a real gap between bars; and no gridlines or tick labels on the small panels, where the shape is the whole message and the rest was furniture. This cell line is still marked by a red line with its value above it, the one number on the panel. The bar colour was checked for contrast against the panel and for separation from that red marker, including for colour-blind readers.

v.85.70 (2026-08-06)

  • Switching between gene effect and expression keeps you in Mutation Inspect. Flipping the measure dropped the whole mutation-inspect layout and returned you to the standalone by-tissue view, throwing away the split you had set up for what was only a change of y-axis. It now redraws in place, and only By Tissue or By Hotspot leaves that view, as you would expect.
  • The gene effect popout no longer inherits the last measure. Opening a gene from a gene-effect list after looking at an expression gene left the toggle on expression, so the heading and the toggle disagreed about what was on screen. Where the link does not say which measure it wants, the popout opens on gene effect; links that do say, including restored exports, are honoured.

v.85.69 (2026-08-06)

  • Mutation analysis has its own view. Choosing it now hides the gene box entirely, since mutation analysis never reads it: it ranks the whole screen by itself. The right-hand side switches to the Mutation Analysis table, empty until you press Run, instead of leaving the previous network on display. Both made it look as though the genes listed were about to be used.
  • “Export for AI” no longer suggests a question about gates everywhere. The suggested question was shared by every panel and mentioned gates, which only exist in the correlation scatter.

v.85.68 (2026-08-06)

  • Exported networks keep the right edge thickness. In the SVG, PDF and PowerPoint exports the node sizes and edge widths were scaled by the current zoom but the gene labels were not, so at any zoom below 1 the text stayed full size while everything around it shrank, and an edge came out looking far thinner than the same edge on screen. Labels now scale with the rest.
  • The colour scale follows the network as genes are removed. With Scale: network only, removing a gene in Remove Mode left the colours keyed to a range that included the gene that had just gone; you had to re-pick the scale to refresh it. Removing or restoring a gene now recolours straight away.
  • “Nodes outside the view” now counts nodes and labels, not centres. The warning only looked at the middle of each node, so a node sitting half over the edge, or one whose gene name hung off the side, counted as visible. Running an analysis also zooms out if anything would be cut off, so a network is never handed back already clipped.

v.85.67 (2026-08-06)

  • Correlation scatter hover text corrected. It said Shift-click opens the Cell Line Browser; it opens the cell line's Wiki, which is what it already did.
  • “Reset all” uses the standard green. It had a green of its own plus a heavy black border, which made it shout louder than it needed to.

v.85.66 (2026-08-06)

  • The gene effect popout uses the shared chips too. All five places you can filter cell lines, the Cell Line Browser, the analysis panel, the correlation scatter, the correlation analysis panel and the gene effect popout, now draw their filter chips from one piece of code, so the same filter reads the same everywhere: mutated (either copy), one copy mutated, both copies mutated, wild-type, fused / not fused, event present / no event.

v.85.65 (2026-08-06)

  • The same filter chips in the correlation scatter and the correlation analysis panel. Both now show active filters as chips under their controls, with the same wording and the same click-to-change menus as the Cell Line Browser and the analysis panel. Four of the five places you can filter cell lines now behave identically; the gene effect popout already had chips and keeps them.

v.85.64 (2026-08-06)

  • The analysis filters now work like the Cell Line Browser's. Active filters appear as small chips under the controls. Click one to switch which cell lines it keeps, mutated against wild-type, fused against not fused, event present against absent, or to remove it. Same chips, same wording and same menus as the browser.
  • A grid button on each of the three alteration filters. The single “Oncoprint” button named the chart rather than what it does and only ever opened the mutation grid. There is now one small grid button beside the hotspot, copy-number and fusion filters, matching the browser. Genes picked from a grid appear as chips alongside the rest, which is how more than one gene of the same kind can be filtered on at once.
  • Lineage and disease sit together. The tissue and disease selectors are under one Lineage and disease heading rather than being separated.

v.85.63 (2026-08-06)

  • Network sliders sit one per row again, each on a single line. Name, value and track share a row, so they are still readable at full width but take a quarter of the height the stacked version did.
  • A new network opens unlocked. Placing nodes requires the layout engine to be stopped, which was leaving Lock pressed on every new network. The spacing is applied and the nodes handed straight back, so Lock starts off unpressed.
  • Copying the network no longer disturbs it at all. The high-resolution copy is drawn in a second, off-screen network rather than by resizing the one on the page, so nothing on screen moves.
  • Receptor status wording corrected. The help said clinical status is defined by IHC and FISH “on protein”, which is wrong about FISH. ER and PR are scored by immunohistochemistry on protein; HER2 by immunohistochemistry, with in-situ hybridisation (FISH) counting ERBB2 gene copies where the staining is equivocal. The transcript and copy-number readings in this app are approximations of those tests, and the text now says so.

v.85.62 (2026-08-06)

  • The controls above the network take up much less room. The four sliders sit two to a row with the label and value on one line, so the network itself starts higher up the page. Compact is gone: it did the same job as the Spread slider. Networks now open at Spread 65 rather than 100, which is a tighter default.
  • Unlock puts the layout back. Compacting to 60 and then pressing Unlock used to leave the packed picture on screen while the setting still read 60, and the next compaction measured from that, so 60 behaved like the previous 100. Unlock now restores the full-width layout and returns the setting to 100, so the number always describes what you are looking at.
  • Quick filter descriptions rewritten. They describe what each filter selects and what it approximates, rather than how the definition came about. The breast receptor filters in particular.
  • “Export for AI” in the quick filters panel. Downloads every filter currently offered with its definition and how many cell lines it holds, so the groupings can be discussed with a language model without reading them one hover at a time.
  • Copying the network no longer makes it jump. The high-resolution copy briefly resizes the drawing canvas; a still of the network is now held over the top while that happens.

v.85.61 (2026-08-06)

  • Spread and Compact actually move the nodes now. They only worked if you had pressed Lock first. While the layout engine is running it owns the node positions and redraws its own arrangement over anything placed by hand, so the setting changed the stored coordinates, reported them back correctly, and left the picture on screen alone. Spread and Compact now freeze the layout themselves before moving anything, and the Lock button flips to Unlock so it is clear what happened and how to undo it.

v.85.60 (2026-08-06)

  • The 9p21 locus is reported once everywhere, not just where both genes happened to be called. 34 cell lines reported a focal deletion of CDKN2B on its own, with CDKN2A not mentioned at all. Checked against the full copy-number matrix, 33 of those 34 have CDKN2A at effectively the same copy number as CDKN2B (0.33 against 0.33, 0.40 against 0.40): it is one deletion, and CDKN2A simply missed the curated call list. Naming CDKN2B alone pointed at the gene that is rarely the point while leaving out the one that is. All of these now read CDKN2A/B, and MTAP folds into the same locus. Across all 1,186 cell lines no summary now names CDKN2A or CDKN2B on its own.

v.85.59 (2026-08-06)

  • Spread works, and there is a Compact button. Dragging it down pulls the nodes closer together at exactly the same node, font and edge size, and the whole network stays in the panel. Compact does the same in one click, each click packing them tighter; Fit puts them back.
  • Why it only goes one way now. Spread used to run up to 220, and above 100 it pushed nodes off the edge of the panel, which read as the setting doing nothing. Once the whole network is in view, how far apart the nodes look is no longer something that can be dialled independently of node size: scaling the layout up and re-fitting is cancelled exactly by the zoom, and re-running the layout engine with a longer spring is cancelled the same way. Measured on an 18-node network, a twelvefold change in spring length moved the layout from 139 to 3410 units across while the picture on screen stayed the same size. So the top of the slider is now “as far apart as they can sit with everything still visible”, and the range below it is real.

v.85.58 (2026-08-06)

  • HER2+ now comes from copy number, not transcript level. Clinical HER2+ means amplification, which is what FISH tests, and the focal copy-number panel already carried ERBB2. The 11 lines called HER2+ all sit at CN 5.6 or above. Two lines the transcript rule had called HER2+ turn out to carry no amplification at all: MDA-MB-453, the standard AR+ / LAR model, and UACC-3133, which reads ER+ and moves to HR+.
  • Published annotation and measured call are separate axes, and the published one leads. A Lehmann TNBC classification used to be quietly folded into the measured triple-negative set, so a line could be labelled TNBC with nothing to indicate its own data said otherwise. The quick filters now offer Breast, receptor subtype (published annotation) and Breast, receptor subtype (measured) as separate groups, the way annotated sex and sex by expression are already separate, plus a filter for the lines where the two disagree. Where a published call exists it is the one shown, with the measured reading stated next to it when they differ. One line disagrees: KPL-1, called TNBC (LAR) by Lehmann but reading HR+ from its own ER transcript, which sits at the 88th percentile of breast lines. It is also a documented MCF-7 derivative.

v.85.57 (2026-08-06)

  • The cell line summary says “candidate drivers”, not “driven by”. These alterations are the ones most likely to be driving the line on the evidence in the data layers, but none of it has been tested in the cell, and an alteration being recurrent in a cancer type is not proof it drives this particular model. The wording now says what the evidence supports.
  • CDKN2A and CDKN2B are reported as one event. The two genes sit side by side at 9p21 and are removed by the same deletion, so reading “functional loss of CDKN2A” and then “focal deletion of CDKN2B” made a single lesion look like two. They now collapse to CDKN2A/B.

v.85.56 (2026-08-06)

  • Breast receptor status is called against fixed expression levels. The split was the breast-line median for ER and PR and the top fifth for HER2, which decides in advance that half the panel is hormone-receptor positive: 25 of 50 lines came out HR+ where about 8 are. Receptor expression across these lines is not centred, it is two separate groups, so the cutoffs now sit in the gap between them (ERBB2 ≥ 8.0, else ESR1 ≥ 3.0 or PGR ≥ 1.0, on log₂-TPM). HR+ is now the eight recognised luminal models, and HER2+ picks up JIMT-1, which the old top-fifth cut left out.
  • Where the Lehmann panel disagrees, both calls are shown. A published Lehmann TNBC subtype used to silently win, so KPL-1 was labelled triple-negative with no hint that its ER transcript sits at the 88th percentile of breast lines. The cell line summary and the Wiki now give the transcript call and state that Lehmann says otherwise, leaving the judgement to the reader. Two lines are affected, KPL-1 and MDA-MB-453.

v.85.55 (2026-08-06)

  • The cell line summary leads with the likely driver, and says when one does not fit. Alterations were listed in the order the data layers happened to be read, so a focal amplification could open the sentence ahead of the fusion that defines the line. They are now ranked: driver fusion, then a named oncogene hotspot, then an unnamed one, then focal amplification, and within each of those the alteration canonical for that cancer type comes first. Anything not expected for the cancer type is marked atypical, which is how MDA-MB-231 now reads as KRAS-driven, atypical for breast. Only fusions and oncogene hotspots are judged this way; TP53 or CDKN2A loss turns up almost everywhere and says nothing about lineage. Roughly 1 in 60 lines carries a flag.
  • Curated cancer-type knowledge base corrected. KMT2A rearrangements and RAS mutations were missing from acute myeloid leukaemia, CTNNB1 from colon adenocarcinoma and the PI3K genes from glioblastoma, and acute promyelocytic leukaemia lines were being matched to the general AML entry because the two vocabularies word the disease differently. All four affected the Wiki's “typical alteration pattern” block as well.

v.85.54 (2026-08-06)

  • “Copy network” copies what you would have exported. The button used to screenshot the plot area alone, so the legend and the filter banner were missing from anything pasted into a slide. Copy and Export image now build the same picture, banner on top, legend underneath, and the button is named and styled like the other export buttons instead of sitting there as a small outlined “Copy”.

v.85.53 (2026-08-06)

  • “Export for AI” in the help popouts. Rather than reading the help end to end, download it and ask an LLM. The file carries the help text as shown, the version, the sizes of the CRISPR and expression cohorts and the note that they are different sets of cell lines, where each layer's data comes from, and what the panel was filtered to at the time, so questions like “why does my list show 27 cell lines” can actually be answered. Available in the Cell Line Browser help and the quick-filter criteria.

v.85.52 (2026-08-06)

  • Names clicked onto the correlation plot can be removed. They now appear as a row of chips under the cell line box, each reading “click to remove this label”, with a Copy names button, exactly as in the gene-effect popout. The row only ever wrote into the gene-effect panel before, so labels on the scatter had no visible way off. The double-click attempt is removed.
  • Known limitation: the network Spread slider does not change the distance between nodes. The layout engine fixes the spacing once it has settled and will not re-run, so the control cannot do what it promises; it is left in place but should not be relied on.

v.85.51 (2026-08-06)

  • Spread now visibly condenses the network. Scaling the layout and then refitting the view cancelled itself out, which is why the nodes never appeared to move. The zoom is now held steady, so the nodes really do close up: the network spans 336 pixels at the default, 135 at the tightest setting and 740 at the widest.
  • Double-clicking a labelled point removes its name, on the correlation scatter and the gene-effect plots. A double-click used to toggle twice and leave the label where it was.
  • Lasso highlight. A button beside the cell line box turns on lasso mode; encircle points and they join the highlighted set. Separate from the gates: it marks cell lines and nothing else.
  • The Cell Line Browser “?” sits next to Reset.

v.85.50 (2026-08-06)

  • Spread actually spreads the network now. It was writing the spacing to a physics solver the network does not use, and even with that corrected the layout does not re-simulate once settled, so no physics value could move a node. Spread now scales the settled layout out from its centre: at 40% the network spans 150 units where it spanned 375, at 220% it spans 825, and returning to 100% restores it exactly.
  • Copy the names of highlighted or coloured cell lines. The highlight row gains “Copy 2 names”, counting what is highlighted, and the colour-by legend gains “Copy names”, which copies the cell lines in the groups currently shown and respects any group you have hidden.

v.85.46 (2026-08-06)

  • The correlation popout starts fresh on a new gene pair. Axis measures and filters were read from whatever the controls happened to say, so after setting one plot to gene effect against expression, clicking the next edge in the network opened as gene effect against expression too, without being asked. A new pair now resets the axis measures, the axis ranges, the tissue, mutation, fusion and copy-number filters, colour-by, highlights and custom cell lines, and closing the popout resets them as well.
  • Returning to the same pair, from a gene popout for instance, keeps its setup, so the reset only fires when the pair actually changes.

v.85.45 (2026-08-05)

  • Internal: the gate feature is marked as belonging to the extended build only, in all four places it appears, and the set of features the simpler build leaves out is written down in one file rather than living in scattered comments. No change to how anything works.

v.85.44 (2026-08-05)

  • A selection that is only partly on the chart says so. The heading reported how many selected cell lines were highlighted without saying how many were selected, so a gene screened in few lines quietly dropped most of them. Selecting all 126 lung lines and opening a gene measured in 332 of the 1,186 now reads “41 of 126 selected cell lines shown, the other 85 have no value for this gene”.

v.85.43 (2026-08-05)

  • Exported images are no longer squashed. Placing the legend below the plot changes the figure's proportions after the export dialog has collected a width and height, and it was then stretched into the old box: round markers became ellipses and every label was condensed. The image now keeps the proportions of what it actually contains.
  • A gene opened from the browser now appears in front of it. It was being given a z-index below the browser, so clicking a gene looked like it did nothing but return to the list.
  • One control for the comparison, replacing two buttons that had to be read together: all lineages, this lineage by primary disease, or this lineage by disease.
  • Fix: the comparison control could offer a lineage left over from a previous popout, showing Skin over a Bowel analysis. The mutation analysis fixes its own lineage, so the control stays out of the way there.

v.85.40 (2026-08-05)

  • The receptor call says where it came from. A published Lehmann subtype overrides the transcript rule, and without saying so the label could contradict the histograms beside it: HCC70 sits above both the ER and PR medians yet is a textbook triple-negative line. It now reads “from the published Lehmann subtype (BL2), which takes precedence over the transcript rule”.
  • Reset clears the quick filters along with everything else.

v.85.39 (2026-08-05)

  • A lineage can be split by disease. Charts broke a lineage up by DepMap's primary disease, which is coarse: every one of the 98 non-small-cell lung lines sat in a single box. Switching to the Oncotree disease separates them into lung adenocarcinoma (53), small cell (24), squamous, large cell and the rest, which is usually the more useful comparison.
  • The choice is a button beside the lineage switch and applies to every chart that splits a lineage: the gene-effect and expression views, and the mutation inspect.

v.85.38 (2026-08-05)

  • Clicking a gene in the wiki now follows the list it came from, the same as in the browser's Inspect. A gene ranked against the whole panel opens across every lineage; one ranked against the cell line's own lineage opens on that lineage, split by subtype. Both carry the switch between the two views. One shared function does this now, so the two places cannot drift apart again.
  • The wiki's expression profile gained “uniquely low”, against the whole cohort and against the same lineage. Only high expression was listed, although a gene the cohort expresses and this line does not is just as informative, whether a lost lineage marker, a deleted tumour suppressor or an immune-evasion loss. The CRISPR section already covered both directions.

v.85.37 (2026-08-05)

  • The y axis names the alteration, not just the gene. Groups labelled 0 / 1 / 2 say nothing on their own, and the axis read only “KRAS Mutations”. It now reads KRAS hotspot mutations, BCR-ABL1 fusion, TP53 functional loss, MYC amplification or CDKN2A deep deletion, so the split is readable from the chart alone.

v.85.36 (2026-08-05)

  • A gene measured in few cell lines says so. A small n looked like a filter was still on when it was really the data: RPL13A carries a CRISPR score in 332 of the 1,186 cell lines, against 1,147 for TP53. The chart heading now adds “measured in 332 of 1,186 cell lines” whenever a gene covers less than 95% of the panel, and stays quiet otherwise.

v.85.35 (2026-08-05)

  • A button to switch between one lineage and all of them. Opening a gene from Inspect gave no way back out of the lineage it opened on, because the condensed popout has no filter row. There is now a button beside Settings that names both states: “Showing Bone only, show all lineages” and back. It starts on whichever comparison Inspect was making.
  • The plot ignores the browser's filters. A gene opened from Inspect inherited every filter the browser had on, so a chart billed as all cell lines was really only those that survived the tissue, subtype, sex and mutation filters.
