With the browser narrowed to 14 cell lines, the same click now plots 1,147 across 31 lineages. Only the comparison Inspect was making shapes the plot.

v.85.33 (2026-08-05)

  • A gene opened from Inspect follows the comparison Inspect was making. It was inheriting the browser's own tissue and subtype filters instead, so with the browser narrowed to Ewing sarcoma the gene always opened on Ewing sarcoma alone, whichever comparison was on screen. Comparing against all cell lines now opens across every lineage; comparing within the same lineage opens on that lineage split by subtype, so Bone shows Ewing sarcoma, osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma side by side. The tissue chip removes it to see everything.

v.85.32 (2026-08-05)

  • Inspect works without ticking anything. Having filtered the list down to a group is itself a selection, so with nothing ticked it compares the cell lines currently showing. The title and the note say which set was used, so a filtered run is never mistaken for a ticked one. If no filter is active there is nothing to compare against, and it says so rather than comparing the panel with itself.

v.85.31 (2026-08-05)

  • The grids' live count was wrong for fusions and copy number. It read the hotspot mutation table whatever the grid was showing, so ticking EWSR1-FLI1 or MYC amp previewed as 0 of 1,186 before you even pressed Apply. All three places that test a grid row now use the same per-layer check.
  • Reset clears the selection. Ticked cell lines survived a reset, so Inspect and Export went on acting on a selection that no longer matched anything on screen.
  • The Inspect cutoffs have − and + buttons. The size cutoff steps by its own increment; q walks the values people actually use, 0.001 to 1, rather than adding a fixed amount.
  • A gene opened from a lineage-scoped Inspect opens on that lineage, split by subtype. The tissue chip in the popout removes it to see every lineage.

v.85.28 (2026-08-05)

  • A correction is no longer called a dispute. Sixteen of the twenty cancer-type flags record a reclassification the current label already reflects, so calling them disputed suggested a disagreement that does not exist. SK-N-MC read as neuroblastoma, Askin tumour and Ewing sarcoma at once; it is an Ewing-family tumour, and the other two are its history. These now appear as quiet background with no marker in the list. The four genuinely unresolved ones keep the warning.
  • The alteration boxes line up with the row above. Each box plus its grid button now matches the width of the control above it: hotspot with search, fusion with tissue, amp/del with subtype.

v.85.27 (2026-08-05)

  • Fusion and copy-number filters from the grids work. Including EWSR1-FLI1 reported 0 of 1,186 because the row was recorded without its layer and then looked up among hotspot mutations, where a fusion name does not exist, so every cell line failed the test. It now returns the 23 lines carrying it.
  • The list redraws the moment a grid filter is applied. It kept showing every cell line while the filter was already in force, so Select Visible picked up all 1,186 and the list then collapsed, which looked as though selecting had emptied it. Inspect then reported no cell lines.
  • The grid agrees with the rest of the app about who carries a fusion: published calls count here too, so EWSR1-FLI1 gives 23 rather than 14.

v.85.25 (2026-08-05)

  • Inspect works on a single cell line. It asked for three, which was the requirement of the significance test rather than of the comparison. One line against the rest is a reasonable question, so the difference is shown; below three lines there is no spread to test, so the q column and its filter step aside and the panel says why.
  • The sort arrow sits directly after the sort box and reverses any sort, names included. For a gene or compound sort it waits until you have entered one. No wording, just the arrow.
  • An empty gene list explains itself. Two cutoffs can each pass plenty while nothing passes both, which used to read as a broken panel; it now says how many pass each.

v.85.22 (2026-08-05)

  • The three alteration boxes line up with the row above. Each box plus its grid button now spans exactly the width of the search box, so the Cohort and Genetic alterations rows share the same column edges.
  • The sort arrow is greyed out until a sort basis is chosen, and again if the gene or compound is cleared. Hovering it says why, or which way the list is running. It stays in place rather than appearing and disappearing, so nothing shifts.

v.85.19 (2026-08-05)

  • Cell line warnings are written in plain terms. They were showing Cellosaurus's record verbatim, which meant tooltips carrying reference numbers and phrases like “personal communication of…”. Each warning now states what the flag means in one sentence, quotes Cellosaurus only where its wording adds something, marks the quote as theirs, and links to the full record.
  • The sort arrow is back to ▲ / ▼, now always visible and working. Hovering says which way the list is running.
  • Data files follow the app version. They were fetched without one, so after an update a browser could keep serving the previous day's data to new code, which is how a warning could appear with no text in it.

v.85.17 (2026-08-05)

  • Sorting runs both ways. The direction control was invisible in every sort mode, so there was no way to reverse the list, and the Name sort ignored direction even when it was triggered. The button is now always there and says what it will do: A → Z / Z → A for names, Low → high / High → low for gene effect, expression and drug response.

v.85.15 (2026-08-05)

  • The help no longer offers sorts that do not exist. It listed ten, including Tissue + Subtype, Hotspot muts, Damaging muts, Fusions, Ploidy / Aneuploidy / CIN and Copy number, most of which were removed as excessive. There are four: Name, GE for gene(s), Expression of gene(s) and Drug response.
  • It also still described a single Oncoprint button. That became three alteration grids, one each for hotspot mutations, curated fusions and copy number, and the help now says so.
  • A disease that repeats its own group is explained. Filtering to Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer lists NSCLC again among its own subtypes; those are the six cell lines Oncotree never typed any further, and they now read “no finer subtype recorded”. The nine entries sum to the 98 lines in the group.
  • Toolbar boxes match on a phone. iOS draws a native dropdown on grey while the searchable disease box is white, so one control looked unlike its neighbours. All are pinned to white.

v.85.14 (2026-08-05)

  • The three toolbar rows line up. Cohort and Selection started at the same edge but Genetic alterations did not, because its longer label was held on one line and pushed its controls to the right. The label now wraps to two lines inside a fixed column, so Search cell lines, Hotspot gene and Custom cell lines all begin at the same place.

v.85.13 (2026-08-05)

  • The UMAP / PCA lasso is explained properly. It is real lasso selection, but the plot already starts in lasso mode, so the Lasso select button changed nothing when pressed and looked broken. The instruction now leads with “drag on the plot to lasso a cluster, no button needed”, and the button is renamed Back to lasso: it exists to return after using the plot toolbar to zoom, pan or box-select. Pressing it now confirms the mode instead of doing nothing.

v.85.12 (2026-08-05)

  • Dimensionality reduction is collapsed until you ask for it. The browser now opens on the cell-line list, with PCA / UMAP behind a button at the bottom. Everything it needs sits inside one block, so it can be left out of a simpler build.
  • The “?” moved out of the title bar to sit after Sort, beside the controls it explains.
  • Help rewritten for what the browser now does: the ⚠ warning marks and what identity-disputed and cancer-type-disputed mean, how fusion calls treat a cell line that was never RNA-sequenced, where the published calls come from, the two-column Inspect with q-values and the choice of comparison group, and the searchable disease filter. Data sources now name Cellosaurus alongside DepMap and COSMIC.

v.85.11 (2026-08-05)

  • The disease dropdown's open list matches the others. Its current choice was a solid block of brand green and the search box took the browser's blue focus ring, so it stood out from every neighbouring dropdown. The selection is now marked with a tick and bold text on a neutral background.
  • Warnings say where they come from. Each problematic cell line notice now carries a link to its Cellosaurus entry rather than naming it in plain text.
  • Cellosaurus is credited in Data sources for the published fusion calls and the problematic-line flags, with its citation. COSMIC was already credited for the curated fusion and subtype panels.

v.85.10 (2026-08-05)

  • Correlate and Green Listed now share one palette. Green Listed's green ramp was built as the midpoint between the two apps' wordmarks, keeping Correlate's lightness steps and shifting only the hue, so Correlate has adopted it. The greys and the earth accents were already identical.
  • Stray greens folded into the ramp. Around 300 hard-coded colours, including a separate green used for headings and links that belonged to neither app, now sit on the shared scale. Text contrast improves everywhere it changed.
  • Shared radius tokens for cards, inputs and buttons, matching Green Listed.
  • Fix: the cell line warning repeated its first word, showing "Misclassified. Misclassified. Originally thought to be...", because the category was printed in front of a note that already began with it.

v.85.9 (2026-08-05)

  • Gene names that Excel turned into dates are recognised and offered back. Paste a list containing 9-Sep, 1-Mar or 1-Dec and the app names the gene each one came from, one click to restore it. It reads the usual shapes: 9-Sep, Sep-9, 09-Sep-25 and 2025-09-09.
  • Ambiguous ones are never guessed. Ten of the thirty-eight date cells could be two different genes, because both once shared the old name: 1-Mar is MARCHF1 or RTL1, 2-Sep is SEPTIN2 or SEPTIN6. Both are offered and the choice is yours.
  • Exports avoid the problem at source. Anything shaped like a date, and clone identifiers such as 2310009E13 that Excel reads as scientific notation, are written so Excel keeps them as text. Real numbers, including negative gene effects and values like 1e5, stay numeric.
  • The gene symbols in this dataset already use the current HGNC names (SEPTIN9, not SEPT9), so exports were not affected; the guard covers anything you type and any future data release.

v.85.8 (2026-08-04)

  • Exported .csv files can no longer carry a formula. Excel and Sheets run a cell whose text starts with =, +, - or @, and these files get shared onward. Every field in every export is now checked and made literal where needed. Plain numbers are exempt, so negative gene effects stay numeric rather than turning into text.
  • Analytics honours Do Not Track and no longer records campaign parameters, matching the settings used on Green Listed.

v.85.7 (2026-08-04)

  • 56 cell lines are flagged as problematic. The panel-wide Cellosaurus check found 36 whose identity is disputed (contaminated, misidentified, or a derivative of another line) and 20 whose recorded cancer type is disputed. MKN28 is a MKN74 derivative; KE-97 is filed as gastric but is a B-lymphoblastoid line; SK-HEP-1, filed under liver, most likely arose from endothelium.
  • Where you see it: a warning at the top of the cell line summary, in the card and the wiki alike, carrying Cellosaurus's own wording and reference; a ⚠ beside the name in the browser list; and two quick filters, Identity disputed and Cancer type disputed, to include or exclude them.
  • Flagged lines are never hidden. A contaminated line can still be a good experimental model; what it cannot be is evidence about the tumour type on its label. Calls Cellosaurus states as possible rather than settled say so.

v.85.6 (2026-08-04)

  • Curation extended to the whole panel. Every one of the 1,167 cell lines with an RRID was checked against Cellosaurus. 26 recurrent driver fusions that the caller did not report are now available to filter on, among them EML4-ALK in NCI-H3122, TPM3-NTRK1 in KM12, KMT2A-AFF1 in RS4;11, FUS-DDIT3 in DL-221, MYB-NFIB in UM-HACC-2A, CRTC1-MAML2 in H3118, four MYC-IGH Burkitt lines and the FGFR2 fusions in the cholangiocarcinoma lines.
  • Only recurrent drivers were added. Private one-off fusions and ordinary immunoglobulin V-J rearrangements, which every B cell carries, are left out on purpose: including them would put back the noise the curated fusion axis exists to avoid.
  • Of the cell lines the caller could not read, only one outside Ewing sarcoma has a published fusion. Fusion-driven sarcomas are characterised because the fusion defines the disease; most carcinomas simply have none to find.
  • A comparison group that carries a different fusion of the same gene is now named without being judged, so what counts as a control stays your call.

v.85.5 (2026-08-04)

  • Published fusion calls fill in the cell lines the caller could not read. Rather than holding out every line without RNA-seq, their fusion status is taken from Cellosaurus where it is documented. For Ewing sarcoma this brings 9 cell lines back: EW-22, SCCH-196, MC-IXC, ES4, EW-7, EW-1, TC-32, EW-16 and ES8 all carry EWSR1-FLI1. The EWSR1-FLI1 group goes from 13 to 22.
  • The comparison group says what it actually carries. All four EWSR1-FLI1-negative Ewing lines carry a different fusion of the same gene: EWSR1-ERG in CADO-ES1, TC-106 and COG-E-352, EWSR1-FEV in TC-205. They are not fusion-free, and the results header now says so. Cellosaurus also records that CADO-ES1 was reported as EWSR1-FLI1 in error in one publication.
  • ES5 has no documented fusion anywhere, so it stays held out rather than being guessed at.
  • Switching between CRISPR and mRNA states its own group sizes. The two panels cover different cell lines, so the same comparison is 22 vs 4 on CRISPR and 13 vs 4 on mRNA. Each mode now names its own numbers and what the other would give, instead of the count changing with no explanation.
  • Filtering on a fusion with no data no longer matches every cell line. An unrecognised pair fell through to "passes", so the whole panel looked positive.

v.85.4 (2026-08-04)

  • Cell lines that were never RNA-sequenced are no longer counted as fusion-negative. A fusion call needs RNA-seq, so a line without it is unknown, not negative. For EWSR1-FLI1 in Ewing sarcoma that meant 14 "not fused" cell lines of which only 4 could ever have been called. Those 10 are now held out of both groups and reported separately, in the analysis, the results header and the tissue breakdown.
  • This is also why gene effect and mRNA disagreed, 13 vs 14 against 13 vs 4: the uncallable lines have no expression data either, so they dropped out of one view but not the other. Both now read 13 vs 4.
  • Inspect follows the measure you are looking at. Opening it from the mRNA table plotted knockout effect, so the numbers had nothing to do with the row clicked. Title, axis and data now all follow the choice.
  • "Stratify Y by" offers the same four alteration types as the analysis panel, in the same order. Functional loss used to appear only if the analysis had started there, so what you could stratify by depended on how you arrived.
  • Editing text no longer crops the title. Any change in Text Settings replaced the wrapped heading with a single long line, which the plot cut off at both ends. Edited text is re-wrapped to the plot width, and the subtitle box keeps one stats line per row instead of running them together.

v.85.3 (2026-08-04)

  • The cell line summary leads with what drives the cancer. The card and hover popout were reading only the inferred-subtype layer, so a KRAS hotspot recorded in the mutation matrix but never called as a specific variant, or a focal MDM2 amplification, went unmentioned and ploidy was left as the headline. Order is now driver fusion, oncogene hotspot, tumour-suppressor loss, focal amplification and deletion, then genome-wide state.
  • Ploidy is no longer reported as notable. Near-diploid says nothing on its own. Whole-genome doubling, MSI-high, a high mutation burden and lost Class-I presentation are still reported, and ploidy appears only when extreme.
  • The card and the wiki now say the same thing, from one generator instead of two that had drifted apart. When no driver is found, both say so and note it is a statement about the data layers rather than proof of absence.
  • The tissue breakdown popup stays on screen. With the button near the top of a short window it could be given a negative height, which browsers ignore, so the list ran past the bottom of the screen and Apply Filter could not be reached.

v.85.2 (2026-08-04)

  • Inspect reports significance. Every gene gets Welch's t-test between your selection and the cell lines it is compared with, adjusted across all genes tested with Benjamini-Hochberg. The q column is sortable and each side has a q ≤ box, starting at 0.05. Set it to 1 to show everything regardless.
  • Choose what the selection is compared with. All other cell lines as before, or same lineage only, which keeps just the cell lines sharing a tissue of origin with your selection. The second answers what is special about these lines for their tissue, rather than how that tissue differs from every other one.
  • The .csv carries p and q for both measures.
  • The disease filter follows the other filters. Choosing Skin leaves only skin diseases to pick from, with counts matching what the list shows. A disease already chosen stays selectable and says when the other filters leave none of it.
  • The disease box matches its neighbours. It was drawn in the app font while the plain dropdowns beside it used the browser's, and it alone turned green when pressed. The whole toolbar now shares one font, and the green focus ring is gone.

v.85.1 (2026-08-04)

  • Network from Inspect now really uses your selected cell lines. It said "Selection (27 cell lines)" in the banner but the correlations were computed across the whole panel, because the filter it set was the one belonging to the scatter plot and the analysis never read it. Corrected: the selection is a genuine subset of the analysis.
  • The subset is visible and removable. A Cell line subset chip appears above the lineage filter with an × to drop it. Any lineage or alteration filter narrows within the subset rather than replacing it, which is now stated where the chip is. If a combination leaves too few cell lines, the message names the subset as one of the causes.
  • Enrichr in Inspect asks which genes to send, like the one in mutation analysis: top 25 / 50 / 100 / 250 by size of difference, everything shown, or one direction on its own. Sending genes that go up and down together dilutes the enrichment, so the directions can go separately. The menu carries the link to Enrichr at the Ma'ayan Lab.

v.85.0 (2026-08-04)

  • Decimals use a dot everywhere. Boxes where you type a decimal (the Inspect cutoffs, the correlation-inspect cutoffs, the mutation threshold, export width and height) were drawn by the browser in its own language, so a cutoff typed as 0.3 could read back as "0,3" while the text beside it said 0.30. They now always show a dot, matching every number the app prints. Typing a comma still works and is read as a decimal point.

v.84.99 (2026-08-04)

  • Inspect now shows CRISPR on the left and mRNA expression on the right, at the same time. Before, the two tables held the same measure asked two different ways, which never made clear why both were there. Each column now answers one question: which genes differ most between your selection and every other cell line, in that measure.
  • Both columns rank by the size of the difference, largest first, so genes that are higher and lower in your selection sit together at the top. Cutoffs start at 0.3 for gene effect and 1.0 for expression, a two-fold change, instead of showing everything down to 0.1.
  • Export as .csv or for AI. The .csv carries both measures per gene in one file. Export, Save and close sit on one row with the title.
  • Closing a gene returns you to Inspect rather than dropping you back on the browser list with your comparison gone. Clicking a gene in the expression column opens it on expression.
  • "Show only selected" says what it will do. It carries the number of ticked lines, and is greyed out until you have some, rather than looking like a button that does nothing.

v.84.98 (2026-08-04)

  • The disease filter matches the other dropdowns. It is a searchable list rather than a plain menu, and was picking up different styling, at one point collapsing to just its arrow. It now takes the same height, border and width as the tissue and sex filters beside it.
  • Renamed to "All diseases", in line with All tissues, All subtypes and All sexes.
  • Long disease names are readable. The list was 220px wide and cut names off; it is now at least 380px and wraps rather than truncating.
  • Abbreviations work. Type CLL, CML, AML, GBM, DLBCL, SCLC, PDAC and so on. Initials are derived from each name, with a few added by hand where the usual abbreviation is not the initials.

v.84.97 (2026-08-04)

  • The Inspect tables say what they are. "Most depleted in selection" and "Most different from rest" are replaced by "Strongest dependencies in your selection" and "Biggest dependency difference vs the other cell lines", each with a line explaining what it answers. In expression mode they become "Highest expressed in your selection" and "Biggest expression difference", with no talk of depletion.
  • Sensible starting cutoffs. The difference table opened at 0.1, which is inside the noise, so nearly every gene was listed. It now starts at 0.3 for gene effect and 1.0 for expression, a two-fold change. Selecting the 27 Ewing sarcoma lines gives 96 genes rather than thousands.
  • Ranked by the size of the difference, either direction, so genes the selection needs more and less both surface. For Ewing sarcoma the list now opens with FLI1 and EWSR1, the two partners of the fusion that defines it.
  • Export as .csv or for AI, and the measure toggle, Save and close now share one row instead of being split across the panel.

v.84.96 (2026-08-04)

  • Expression correlates retired. The same question is better answered by the gates or by Export for AI, both of which work from the whole dataset rather than one precomputed list. The panel no longer appears after a mutation analysis.

v.84.95 (2026-08-04)

  • Cell Line Browser can filter by exact disease. The tissue and subtype fields are coarse, so entities such as chronic lymphocytic leukemia could not be picked at all, being filed under mature B-cell neoplasms. A new picker lists all 165 Oncotree entities with their counts; CLL selects its 4 cell lines.
  • The gate comparison uses the standard export dialog rather than separate PNG and SVG buttons, matching every other chart.
  • Gates have their own Export for AI, which opens with the question the export is for: what distinguishes the cell lines in gate A from those in gate B, using the mutation, copy-number, fusion, expression and dependency data rather than only the two genes plotted.

v.84.94 (2026-08-04)

  • The executive summary now reports a hotspot the inferred list missed. PGA1 carries a KRAS hotspot in the mutation matrix but has no entry in DepMap's inferred variant list, and the summary was built only from the latter, so the most relevant finding on the page went unmentioned. It now falls back to the mutation matrix for any canonical oncogene.
  • Network image exports honour the resolution you ask for. The network was copied from the on-screen canvas and stretched, so 1200 dpi carried no more detail than 600; only the legend, drawn directly at full size, actually improved. The network is now redrawn at the export size first, about nine times the pixels at 3x, with the view restored afterwards.

v.84.93 (2026-08-03)

  • Mutational analysis can compare mRNA expression as well as knockout effect. A Measure toggle beside the result count switches between the two: gene effect answers "what do BRAF-mutant lines depend on", expression answers "what is expressed differently in BRAF-mutant versus wild-type lines". Cell lines without expression data are left out of both groups rather than counted as zero.

v.84.92 (2026-08-03)

  • Correlation controls regrouped. The fusion filter sits below the hotspot filter and beside the amp/deletion filter, so the four cohort filters read as one block. Compare is a single row with its buttons together. Thin lines separate the groups: genes, then plot size and axis ranges, then the filters, then compare.

v.84.91 (2026-08-03)

  • Cell lines you label by clicking are now listed under the Gene Effect plot, with a Copy names button, so the names can be taken out rather than only read off the chart. Clicking a name in the list removes its label from the plot.

v.84.90 (2026-08-03)

  • The hotspot and fusion overlay read-out no longer runs off the plot. Three groups each with n and r made a line too long to fit, and it was cut at the edge. It now breaks across lines to match the plot width.
  • Overlay and title text are editable in the settings panel. A title that wrapped, or an overlay line, was treated as subtitle from the first line break onwards, so parts of it could not be reached.
  • Fixed a Copy button showing on the scatter footer when the tissue chart it belongs to was hidden.

v.84.89 (2026-08-03)

  • Gene Effect filter chips work like the Cell Line Browser's. Click a chip to switch which cell lines are kept, mutated to wild-type, fused to not fused, event present to absent, or to remove the filter. Tissue and subtype chips can be removed the same way.

v.84.88 (2026-08-03)

  • A very long subtype name no longer squeezes the gene-effect chart. One subtype runs to 99 characters, and the axis gave it whatever room it asked for, leaving a sliver for the data. Row labels are shortened to 34 characters with the full name on hover.
  • The whole title is editable in the text settings, not just its first line. A title long enough to wrap was split at the wrap, and everything after the first line was treated as subtitle.

v.84.87 (2026-08-03)

  • A scan hit can now be checked against chance. With a dozen cell lines per group a genome-wide scan throws up striking-looking results from noise alone, and the rank on its own gives no sense of that. A button on the gene-effect scan shuffles the group labels and reports how many genes separate that strongly by chance, so you can see what fraction of hits at that level are noise. Offered only for cohorts of 200 cell lines or fewer, which is where the question arises; with hundreds per group the ordinary p-value is already dependable.

v.84.86 (2026-08-03)

  • The gene-effect scan warns when a hit's pathway partners do not move with it. A gene that separates strongly on a split while its known complex or pathway partners stay flat is usually screen noise: a complex cannot work without its subunits, so a real dependency difference should shift them too. The check runs on the strongest hit and says nothing when the partners do move.

v.84.85 (2026-08-03)

  • Copy button on the network, scatter, tissue chart and mutation table. Copies the chart as an image straight to the clipboard, ready to paste into an email or a slide without saving a file first.
  • Network Spread slider. Node spacing was tied to the node and font size, so the only way to make a network more compact was to shrink the labels. Spread scales the spacing on its own, from tight to wide, and refits the view afterwards.

v.84.84 (2026-08-03)

  • A mistyped gene now suggests the right one. Every "gene not found" message across the app was a bare browser alert; it is now a popout listing the closest symbols, each clickable to copy. IL4RA offers IL4R, CDNK2A offers CDKN2A, ABL offers ABL1 / ABL2 / ABLIM1, and a mouse symbol such as Trp53 offers its human ortholog TP53.
  • Gene tooltips lead with what the gene does. RefSeq summaries often open with transcript-variant housekeeping, so the first line of a short tooltip said nothing useful: CDKN2A began "This gene generates several transcript variants which differ in their first exons" and now begins with the sentence describing it as an inhibitor of CDK4 kinase.

v.84.83 (2026-08-03)

  • Filtered network exports no longer carry wide white margins. The filter banner drew a separator line right across the canvas, and being the only non-white thing at the edges it stopped the whitespace trim from cropping the sides. The line is now only as wide as the banner text. On a test composition the export crops from 1200px to 530px wide.
  • The network warns when nodes are outside the view, with a Fit button in the corner. Enlarging the font or nodes could push part of the network off-screen with nothing to indicate anything was missing.

v.84.82 (2026-08-03)

  • Export for AI now names what it will send. It said "plus source-specific extras"; it now spells out what the current view contributes, states that the filters and settings in force are included, and that nothing outside the current cohort is.
  • Scatter CSV columns carry the gene names, so "TP53_Effect_xAxis" rather than "Gene1_Effect". When filters are narrowing the plot, a ShownOnPlot column marks which rows are the ones you can see.

v.84.81 (2026-08-03)

  • The network filter banner now describes the network you are looking at. It read the filter dropdowns live, so changing a filter without pressing Run relabelled an unchanged network, and a subtype from a previous run could appear against results that never used it. The banner is captured when the analysis runs.
  • Changing to a tissue with no subtypes now clears the subtype filter. The control was hidden but kept its value, and every filter chain still read it, so a subtype from the tissue you just left kept narrowing results invisibly.

v.84.80 (2026-08-03)

  • Enrichr A and B on the gates work again. They asked for a p-value cutoff through a native browser prompt, which blocks the page and is refused outright by some browsers, so the button did nothing at all. They now use the panel's own p-value box, defaulting to 0.05, and the result names the cutoff used. If there is no comparison to send, it says so rather than doing nothing.
  • The three remaining native prompts are gone too, replaced by a small in-page dialog: the two build-network cutoffs and the gene list for the Cell Line Browser gene export.

v.84.79 (2026-08-03)

  • Switching analysis mode now clears the previous results. A network and its correlation and cluster tables stayed on screen after switching to mutational analysis, which made them look like part of the new analysis. The gene list is kept.
  • Fixed the comparison p-values at small group sizes. Eight places computed a Fisher z-test straight from the correlation, which is infinite at r = ±1, and r is exactly 1 whenever a group has only three cell lines. Those comparisons could return NaN or a meaningless p-value.

v.84.78 (2026-08-03)

  • The hotspot and fusion overlay lists now count against what is actually plotted. They followed the tissue and subtype filters but ignored the mutation, fusion and copy-number ones, and they were refreshed before the plot rather than after, so the numbers were a step behind. With no filter KRAS reads 174 mutated of 1,147 cell lines; with a TP53-mutated filter applied it now correctly reads 100 of 574.

v.84.77 (2026-08-03)

  • Color by gene effect now rescales when you remove nodes. The node colors already followed the genes on screen, but all four legends still measured every analyzed gene, so the numbers stopped matching the colors after using Remove mode.
  • Shift-clicking a cell line opens its wiki everywhere. In the correlation scatter it opened the Cell Line Browser instead, while the gene-effect view opened the wiki.
  • Long axis labels no longer get clipped. "MDM2 Expression (log2 TPM+1)" was taller than a 400px plot and lost characters at both ends; labels break before the unit when they will not fit.

v.84.76 (2026-08-03)

  • The correlation title now names the measurement, so "TP53 vs MDM2 (gene effect)" rather than just the gene pair, and both are named when the axes differ.
  • Export for AI no longer steers you to one assistant. It says the instructions were written and tested against Claude, and that the file is plain JSON that works elsewhere.
  • Reworded the fusion explanation in the wiki: a fusion joins parts of two genes into one, usually after a rearrangement such as a translocation.
  • Reset all is now solid green with a dark border.

v.84.75 (2026-08-03)

  • American English throughout, color rather than colour, tumor, behavior, center, gray, labeled, analyze, signaling. 425 changes across the app.
  • Alteration grids no longer look squashed when there is little to show. A grid with two rows shrank the whole panel to about 300px wide and crushed the toolbar; it now keeps enough width for the controls.
  • A grid with nothing to show now says so instead of the button appearing to do nothing.

v.84.74 (2026-08-03)

  • "No fusion data" is now separate from "not fused". A fusion call needs RNA-seq, and 74 cell lines have none, so the caller could never report one for them. They were being counted as fusion-negative. In a small cohort that is enough to invent a result: for YRDC across 27 Ewing sarcoma lines, 9 of the 13 apparent negatives had simply never been sequenced, and the difference disappears once they are set aside. Fusion filters now offer three states, and the counts beside them say how many lines fall in each.
  • Cell Line Browser: sort moved to the end of the Cohort row, and the second row is now labeled Genetic alterations.

v.84.73 (2026-08-03)

  • Fixed: the fusion and copy-number grids selected no cell lines. Their include / exclude choices were being checked against the hotspot mutation table, where a fusion name or an "amp / del" row does not exist, so every cell line failed the test. Each row is now checked against the layer it came from. Verified: BCR-ABL1 gives 12 cell lines, CDKN2B del gives 295, both matching the counts in the grid.
  • Fixed: the Quick filters button and the three gene pickers did not open. They take their hidden state from a stylesheet rule now, and the code that opened them was still clearing an inline style, which no longer had any effect.
  • Fixed overlapping text in the fusion and copy-number grids. The row-label pane was a fixed width sized for gene symbols; it now measures the longest label being drawn.
  • The grid's Apply button is now the obvious next step, larger and in solid green.

v.84.72 (2026-08-03)

  • Fixed overlapping text in the Cell Line Browser. When a row wrapped, the second line started at the far left, underneath the row label. Controls now sit in their own column so a wrapped line stays clear of it.
  • The mutated / wild-type dropdowns are gone again. Picking a gene now simply keeps the cell lines carrying that alteration, which is what it is for. Wild-type, single-copy and both-copies stay available on the colored chip the filter produces. The gene pickers keep their full ranked list.
  • Custom cell lines moved onto the Selection row, at its start.
  • Inspect explains what it compares. It is now titled "N selected cell lines vs the other M" and states that each gene is averaged across the selection and compared with the average across every other cell line, with Δ = selection − rest.
  • Inspect can switch between CRISPR gene effect and mRNA expression, with the column headers and cohort size following the choice.
  • Fixed Δ appearing as literal "&Delta;" in the Inspect header.

v.84.71 (2026-08-03)

  • The status dropdowns are back beside each alteration filter. The chip menu still works as a second way to the same setting.
  • Sort moved up after Quick filters, with a separator, and Custom cell lines now sits at the end of that row, just before the Selection row.
  • The fusion grid uses curated driver fusions, not the raw fusion-caller output. Most lines in this panel carry more than 30 raw partners, the great majority of which are passenger or artefactual calls in rearranged genomes, so a grid ranked on them showed noise rather than drivers.
  • Grids can show rows outside the top 25. The add box searches everything with at least one cell line, and remembers what you added separately for the mutation, fusion and copy-number grids.
  • The UpSet plot names which layer it is built from, hotspot mutations, curated fusions or copy-number events.
  • The sex filter now shows as a chip like the others. It was being applied without appearing in the filter strip, so the strip did not describe the list it sat above.
  • Every filter chip is clickable: tissue, sex, hotspot, fusion, copy number, quick filters and the grid-derived gene filters. Click one to change which side is kept, or to remove it.

v.84.70 (2026-08-03)

  • Cell Line Browser toolbar reorganized. Reset and ? moved up beside the dialog title. Row 1 is the cohort (search, tissue, subtype, sex), row 2 is alterations (hotspot, fusion, amp/deletion, then quick filters and custom cell lines), row 3 is sort.
  • Each alteration filter has its own grid button, opening a mutation, fusion or copy-number grid for the cell lines currently shown. The standalone Oncoprint button is gone, and the grids are now titled by what they show, with "oncoprint" kept in brackets as the field's term for it.
  • The wild-type / mutated dropdowns are gone from the toolbar. That choice now lives on the filter's own chip: click it to switch side (including one copy vs both copies mutated) or to remove the filter.
  • Wiki pathways are framed as hypotheses, "pathways that may have contributed to transformation", and both labels are defined: driver activated = an activating hotspot, focal amplification or curated fusion in a growth-promoting gene; brake lost = a damaging mutation, functional loss or focal deletion in a tumor suppressor. The section also states what was and was not checked, including that activating hotspots come from a 49-gene panel.
  • Expression signatures renamed to "gene programs expressed above / below average", stating that the score is mean mRNA z-score across the expression table and is not a measurement of pathway activity.

v.84.69 (2026-08-03)

  • The pinned wiki header no longer has text sliding above it. The dialog's top padding scrolled away with the content while the header anchored below it, leaving a 20px strip where body text showed through. The spacing moved onto the card so the header sits at the true top, with a soft shadow so content clearly passes behind it.
  • CRISPR dependencies renamed to "which genes this cell line needs, and which ones hold it back". The section also lists knockouts that speed growth up, which the old wording left out.

v.84.68 (2026-08-03)

  • The color-by group picker now lists only the tissues or subtypes actually on the plot. It was built from the full dataset, so with a filter applied it offered groups that had already been filtered out, and picking one changed nothing. "Suggest" is scored on the plotted points for the same reason.

v.84.67 (2026-08-03)

  • Drug rows no longer print the compound's clinical indication. A drug approved for colorectal cancer, listed beside a pancreatic line's own screen result, read as though the line were colorectal. The indication describes the drug and says nothing about the cell line, so it now lives only in the CSV export.
  • Removed the leftover therapy-matching code that paired a line's alterations with drug classes. It had already been taken off the page as over-interpretation; the code that produced it is now gone too.
  • Cohort wording in the expression and drug sections simplified to state plainly which cell lines each comparison uses.

v.84.66 (2026-08-03)

  • The wiki now scrolls as one ordinary long page. It used a card capped at the window height with a separate scrolling area inside it, which meant scrolling only worked if a script routed each wheel movement to the right one of several scrollers. That arrangement is gone: the dialog itself scrolls, the title bar stays pinned at the top, and no script is involved in scrolling it.

v.84.65 (2026-08-03)

  • Pathways are now one ranked list instead of two blocks. All 25 pathways are checked against every layer, hotspot and damaging mutations, functional loss, focal copy number and curated fusions, and each says whether a driver is active, a brake is lost, or nothing was found. The four with a CRISPR read-out carry it underneath. Pathways with nothing found collapse to a single line. The 25-panel scan previously existed but was never actually shown on the page, which is why the pathway coverage looked thin.
  • A hotspot in a tumor suppressor is no longer called "activating".
  • Gene names are readable chips rather than tiny comma-separated text, colored by whether the gene is a suppressor or an oncogene, and the wiki now uses three font sizes instead of six.
  • PDF: page numbers as "3 / 12", centered at the bottom of every page.
  • PDF: pages no longer cut through text. A break was only allowed on a row that was white right across, which never happens inside a block with a colored left border, so dense sections were sliced mid-line. Breaks now land in the gap between lines.
  • Corrected: expression comparisons are against the expression table, not the CRISPR panel. The text claimed "~1,100 cell lines"; the expression z-scores are actually computed over 1,698. Both sections now name their own number and note that the two sets differ.
  • Removed the XIST row, which said the same thing for every cell line: XIST is a non-coding RNA and is not in the protein-coding expression table at all.
  • Wheel handling over charts now walks out to the nearest scrollable ancestor before falling back to the dialog's main scroller.

v.84.64 (2026-08-03)

  • The wiki scrolls again. With the wiki open on top of the Cell Line Browser, the scroll handler picked the browser underneath rather than the wiki, so every wheel over one of the wiki's charts was handed to the wrong panel and nothing moved. It now follows what is actually on top.
  • Cancer pathways expanded from 14 to 25, about 200 genes: TGF-beta/SMAD, Hippo/YAP, NRF2 oxidative stress, hypoxia/VHL-HIF, apoptosis (BCL2 family), Hedgehog, spliceosome, cohesin, antigen presentation, ubiquitin/protein turnover, and nucleotide-excision/crosslink repair. Each says what the pathway does and why its loss matters.
  • The pathway scan says what it does not cover. It reads point mutations only, so a clean scan is not the same as an unaltered pathway.

v.84.63 (2026-08-03)

  • The oncoprint's include / exclude boxes now actually filter the Cell Line Browser. Clicking one recorded the filter but nothing ever applied it, and Clear reopened the grid against the whole panel instead of the lines you were looking at.
  • Cell Line Browser toolbar rebuilt into three fixed rows, filter, sort, then what to do with the result. The order no longer changes with window width, every box and button shares one height so they line up, and thin separators mark the groups.
  • Oncoprint moved out from between the hotspot box and its status dropdown and now sits with Inspect Gene Effects, where the other things you can do with the visible cell lines live.
  • Custom cell lines is a popout instead of a text box in the toolbar, and explains what it accepts: the cell line name as shown in the list, or the DepMap ACH-000000 identifier.
  • Show Selected says what it needs when nothing is ticked, instead of looking like a dead button.
  • One of the two "showing N of 1186" counts is gone. The list header keeps it; the filter strip now just shows the filters.
  • Quick filters sit after Sort, and the repeated "Quick filters:" label before the button is gone.

v.84.62 (2026-08-03)

  • The wiki no longer states things it has not measured. A cell line with no mutation calls at all used to show three confident zeros; it now says the calls are missing. "No fusions" and "none called" are distinguished, and the fusion row explains that the table lists calls only. Copy-number wording is split by depth: a single-copy loss is called that rather than a "focal deletion", and a band is a "loss" rather than a "deep loss".
  • "Canonical drivers not altered here" now checks the damaging-mutation table, which it never did. A gene with a frameshift or nonsense mutation was listed as unaltered, and the suggestion to re-authenticate the line was made without looking at the largest mutation layer the app carries.
  • Fusion confidence tiers are explained honestly. The green box said every call was confirmed on three independent signals; a low-tier call actually has none, and the caption now says what each tier means. The drug-context section no longer treats any raw ALK, ROS1, BCR or ABL1 partner as a driver fusion.
  • Executive summary fixes: ages printed as "69.0-year-old", the literal word "unknown" appeared as a tumor stage, and a donor age of 0 was dropped entirely.
  • Corrected figures and wording: the whole-genome-doubling share (73% of lines that have a ploidy call, not 58% of everything), "very high fusion count" on a threshold most lines exceed, MSI-high asserting mismatch-repair deficiency as certain, and "hypermutated" meaning three different things in three places.
  • Sources are no longer all labeled 25Q3. The copy-number regions come from 24Q4 and the drug screen from 25Q2, and both now say so, since the two copy-number blocks can disagree.
  • Breast receptor status explains the rule it actually applies, and a line with no expression data is no longer called triple-negative by default.
  • Drug rows: the z-score and the "of N tested" count use different cohorts, which is now stated, and compounds with no variation across the panel are dropped instead of being scored exactly average.
  • Security and robustness: a saved figure can only set the controls the app itself saves, text from external gene databases is escaped, and a malformed PNG no longer throws while being opened.
  • Removed three unused page sections that were built and never displayed, one of which claimed a cell line had "retained the canonical tumor-suppressor functions" based on an eight-gene panel.

v.84.61 (2026-08-02)

  • Cell line wiki corrections. The pathway panels only looked at the mutation tables, so a line could read "CDKN2A functional loss" in one section and "No mutation in RB1 / CDKN2A / CCND1" in the next; they now use the same functional-loss layer as the rest of the page. "BCR-ABL fusion detected" fired whenever BCR or ABL1 turned up anywhere in the raw fusion-caller output, which was wrong for 17 of the 29 lines it flagged, and now uses the validated BCR-ABL1 call. Copy numbers in the amplified-region list assumed every cell line was diploid, but most are genome-doubled, so they are now scaled by each line's own ploidy. A missing measurement is no longer reported as a finding: a line with no copy-number data says so instead of "nothing detected", and an annotated-male line with no expression data no longer reads as "almost certainly loss of the Y chromosome". The XIST row explains that XIST is absent from the protein-coding expression table rather than silently disappearing, and the p53 summary no longer claims an MDM2 dependency that the bullet above it contradicts.
  • The expression-correlate scatter was broken since v.83.11, it threw before drawing. Clicking a row in the expression-correlates table now opens the plot.
  • Reset network settings now resets the font, node and edge-width sliders too. Two methods shared a name and the one that reset the sliders never ran.
  • Saved figures restore the cell-line search box again, and no longer abandon the rest of the restore halfway through when a search term is present.
  • Text from a saved figure, a share link or an uploaded gene table is escaped before display, so it cannot inject markup into the page.
  • No more NaN or Infinity in plot titles, legends and axis boxes for groups too small or too uniform to give a correlation, or for genes with no copy-number or expression record. A very large expanded network no longer fails at the end with "Analysis failed".
  • Escape works again after using the UpSet plot, and the Cell Line Browser no longer runs Split once per time it has been opened.

v.84.60 (2026-08-02)

  • The Cell Line Browser stops moving under the cursor. Choosing a tissue used to make the subtype dropdown appear from nothing and shove the rest of the toolbar along, and the filter summary line did the same to the row beneath it. The subtype dropdown is now always there, grayed until a tissue is chosen, the tissue and sex boxes keep a fixed width instead of resizing with their text, and the summary line keeps its place whether or not anything is in it. Verified: nothing on the toolbar moves when filters are applied or cleared.
  • Quick filters moved up beside Select Visible, removing a row that was mostly empty.
  • ? Filters is now ? Help, since it covers the whole browser rather than the filter boxes alone.

v.84.59 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: the cell line Wiki could not be scrolled. Its text area could not shrink inside the panel, so it never became a scrolling area and everything past the first screen was unreachable.
  • The Wiki has an Export for AI button, so a single cell line can be discussed. The file states plainly that the Wiki's written summary is the app's own reading of the same numbers, and asks that claims in it be checked against the underlying values rather than taken as given.
  • Cell Line Browser filter row tidied. The status dropdowns sat underneath their filter boxes; they now sit beside them. The copy-number filter uses the same wording as the rest of the app, and the two bare ? buttons say what they explain.
  • Exported files carry the date and time. Two exports made minutes apart from different settings no longer share a name, and the settings file matches its image.
  • More buttons explain themselves on hover, including every popout's close button and the CSV downloads.

v.84.58 (2026-08-02)

  • The data exports look like the image export. Export for AI and All Data (ZIP) were blue and drew the eye first; all three now share the same neutral button.
  • The network's AI export includes the weaker pairs. Correlations below the cutoff travel with the file, with a note that the cutoff is a drawing threshold rather than a verdict, so questions can be asked about relationships the picture leaves out.
  • Cell Line Browser tags now match the filters. They claimed "mutated" and "fused" whatever the selector said, and copy number had no tag at all. All three now name the side in view and turn gray on the wild-type side.
  • Legends move out of the way on two more plots, the correlation-analysis detail view and the expression-correlate scatter, which both pinned theirs to the top-left over the data.
  • Blank margins are trimmed from the UMAP / PCA and mutation-table images too.
  • p-values read the same everywhere. The correlation-analysis, Gene Effect and pathway-enrichment tables formatted theirs separately and showed things like 1.2e-15.
  • No settings file is written for views that cannot be reopened, rather than leaving one in your downloads that does nothing. The gate report is one; the export dialog says so for the others.

v.84.57 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: the Active filter tag said "mut" when wild-type was selected. The chart caption had it right but the tag above it always claimed the mutated side, so the two contradicted each other. The tags for the hotspot, fusion and copy-number filters now follow the selector and go gray when showing the wild-type side.
  • The bias warning beside those filters no longer talks only about mutations: filtering to wild-type is just as much a selection, and can skew the comparison by cancer type the same way.

v.84.56 (2026-08-02)

  • See the pairs that just missed the cutoff. A below cutoff tick box above the Correlations table lists them under a divider, grayed, so a borderline result is not simply invisible. They are context only: not in the network, no cluster.
  • Fix: reopening a saved figure lost some network settings. Color by GE was recorded but never re-applied after the analysis re-ran, and Show all input genes was not recorded at all. Both now come back, along with the GE label, its SD, the statistics label and the node border.
  • Fix: the tip above the Correlations table named a button that does not exist. It said to click Scatter; the button is Correlation.
  • The AI exports are all called Export for AI, instead of .json.gz, and the network has one now too.
  • Cluster columns say what they measure. Mean (All) and SD (All) are now GE mean and GE SD, with the caption explaining that gene effect is how much the cell lines depend on that gene.
  • Chart exports are trimmed like the network ones. Charts reserve space above for the title, which left a blank band across the top of the picture.
  • The group picker's buttons no longer crowd Apply into the corner.

v.84.55 (2026-08-02)

  • Gene names no longer land on top of other nodes. The layout spaced nodes by a fixed distance that took no account of the label, which is drawn below the circle, so a name could sit squarely over its neighbour. Spacing is now worked out from the node and font sizes, so it keeps working when either slider is moved, and each node is treated as an area to keep clear rather than a point. The same applies to the other layouts under Settings.

v.84.54 (2026-08-02)

  • The export dialog is titled "Export image". It read Export chart / PNG, which named a format you had not chosen yet and were about to pick two lines below, and called everything a chart when the same dialog exports networks and oncoprints.
  • Dropped the "vector" claim from the export choice. It said the chart on its own (vector, best for figures) even when PNG was selected, which is not vector. The options now simply say what they capture, with a line underneath explaining where the format is actually limited: the chart alone can be SVG or PDF if you want to edit it, a whole-panel capture is a picture in every format.

v.84.53 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: group tags lingered after the coloring was switched off. Turning Color by back to nothing left the tags and the picker button sitting there naming groups that were not on the plot, which read as though a filter were still in force. Both now clear whenever nothing is colored.
  • The two shortcuts now say what they select. Top 8 is now 8 largest, since it picks the groups holding the most cell lines, nothing to do with correlation. Suggest is now Strongest r and does what that says: the 5 groups with the strongest correlation of their own, counting only groups of at least 10 cell lines so a value from a handful of points cannot crowd out a real one.
  • More groups than colors no longer means repeated colors. With 74 subtypes against a 40-color palette, two groups used to share a color with nothing to tell them apart. The marker shape now changes on each pass through the palette, so every group is distinct, and the shape shows in both the plot legend and the group tags.

v.84.52 (2026-08-02)

  • Gene Effect filters gained a with-event / only-WT choice. The hotspot, fusion and copy-number filters there always kept the carriers, unlike the same filters everywhere else in the app. Each now has its own selector, appearing once a gene is chosen, and the figure caption says which side you are looking at.
  • Five missing quick filters added: SMARCB1, SETD2, FAT1, FBXW7 and TET2 deletions. They are on the curated panel and filterable everywhere else, but had no entry in the Cell Line Browser's quick filters.
  • The genotype legend places itself out of the way. It was pinned to the top left, which is exactly where the mutated lines gather on a gene-effect pair, so it sat on top of the points it described. It now goes to whichever corner has the fewest cell lines under it, preferring the top.
  • Exported network images are trimmed. The picture was drawn at the size of the on-screen panel, so a graph that did not fill it came out framed in white. The blank margin is cropped to a thin border and the print height adjusted so the proportions stay right.

v.84.51 (2026-08-02)

  • Color by tissue shows every tissue again, which is the quick way to see whether a pattern is there at all, busy as it is. You can still narrow to chosen tissues.
  • Color by subtype starts empty and waits for you to pick, rather than choosing subtypes for you.
  • New Suggest button in the group picker: it ticks the groups of at least 10 cell lines whose own correlation departs most from the cohort as a whole, using the same statistic as Compare by tissue, so the ones worth labeling are one click away.
  • Fix: three Cell Line Browser quick filters could never match anything. CDKN2A deletion, RB1 deletion and PTEN deletion were built from genes the curated deletion panel deliberately leaves out, because functional loss already covers them. Removed, and the "Any focal deletion" description corrected: it listed CDKN2A as being in the panel when it is not.
  • Fix: copy-number filters said "deep deletion" but did not mean it. They match the curated deletion panel, which includes single-copy loss as well as homozygous. They now say deletion and spell out what is included. Only the mutation-analysis sub-type used the strict ≤0.3 definition, and it still does.
  • Fix: Mutation Inspect still offered "Deep deletion" as something to stratify by, months after it was removed as an analysis sub-type. Gone, along with the same claim in the "How it works" panel.
  • Fix: the wiki copy-number caption stated the wrong thresholds for what counts as an amplified or deleted region.
  • The Gene Effect scan button now reads By hotspot mutation, which is what it does. The copy-number filter on the main page now uses the same wording as everywhere else.

v.84.50 (2026-08-02)

  • The extra file that downloads with an image is now explained. The export dialog states plainly that a small settings file (.correlate.json) is saved beside the picture, what it holds, and exactly how to use it: Options → Other → Open saved figure returns the app to that view so you can change something and export again. There is a tick box if you would rather not have it.
  • Oncoprint and UpSet now save one too. Neither did before, so a figure from either was a dead end. Both record the cohort, filters and any genes you added, and reopen exactly as they were, with the UpSet restoring its chosen genes on top of the oncoprint.
  • Where a view genuinely cannot be reopened, the dialog says so instead of quietly not saving the file. This applies to the mutation results table.

v.84.49 (2026-08-02)

  • Highlighted cell lines are now listed. Clicking a point in the plot used to leave no trace in the Highlight / Color box, so there was no way to see what was highlighted or to take one off. Every highlight, typed or clicked, now appears as a small tag with an × to remove it.
  • Subtypes are shown under their tissue. The group picker lists each lineage with its subtypes indented beneath, so it is clear where a subtype comes from. Ticking a lineage takes all of its subtypes; the box shows a dash when only some are selected.
  • Chosen groups are easy to drop. They appear as tags under the picker, each removable with one click, and the picker has None alongside Top 8 and Color all.
  • By genetic change now scans hotspot mutations only. Fusions and amplification / deep-deletion added far more rows than could be read and mixed change types that are not really comparable. The chart, table and captions all say so.

v.84.48 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: popouts could not be scrolled. A chart fills most of a panel, and Plotly takes the scroll wheel for its own zoom and stops it there, so the panel underneath never moved. Scrolling over a chart now scrolls the panel it sits in (or the page, on the main view). This affected the Correlation and Gene Effect popouts and the Cell Line Browser.
  • Fix: “Hold Shift for full text” on network genes. The box disappears as soon as the pointer drifts off the node, taking its own key handler with it, so Shift usually arrived too late. Shift is now handled centrally, the box lingers briefly after you move away, and holding Shift before hovering works too.
  • Correlation statistics now include a p-value. The single plot shows n, r, p, slope; each panel of the hotspot three-panel view shows n, r, p with the median x and y underneath.
  • All screenshot buttons are gone, folded into Export image. The dialog now asks what to export: the chart on its own, or the whole panel as a screenshot. The whole-page screenshot lives in the network's Export image as “the whole page”. Format and resolution are chosen in the one place.
  • Run explains itself correctly in each mode. In mutation analysis it no longer claims to use the gene list in box 2, which it ignores.
  • View Controls explain themselves on hover: Fit, Select Mode, Remove Mode, Lock, Settings and Node border.
  • Removed a duplicate, shadowed p-value formatter that reported an underflow as the fabricated value 1.0e-300.

v.84.47 (2026-08-02)

  • More links when you hover a gene. Alongside NCBI and HGNC there are now Human Protein Atlas, GeneCards, UniProt and DepMap. They resolve on the gene symbol, so they work even when the lookup service is slow or unavailable.
  • Buttons explain themselves. Hovering a button for half a second shows a readable explanation instead of the browser's small, slow tooltip. All Data (ZIP), Run, Test Genes and others gained descriptions where they had none.
  • The whole-page screenshot has moved out of the network Export row and into Options → Other → Screenshot the page. It is for explaining the app rather than making a figure, so it no longer sits beside the figure exports, and it now goes through the usual export dialog where you choose format and resolution rather than always producing a PNG.
  • Fix: page screenshots had a tall white band above the content. The capture always started at the top of the document while the page was scrolled somewhere else, so the offset appeared as empty space. Roughly a third of the image was blank; it is now about one percent, and your scroll position is put back afterwards.

v.84.46 (2026-08-02)

  • Color by tissue or subtype now starts with the 8 largest groups and grays the rest as Not selected, instead of giving 30 tissues (or 70 subtypes) a color each and leaving the plot unreadable. The Pick groups button opens pre-ticked with those 8, so you can see what you are changing; Top 8 and Color all are one click each, and the plot only grays anything when there are more than 8 groups to begin with.
  • The gray bucket is called Not selected rather than Other, because Other is a real lineage in the data and the two would have been indistinguishable.

v.84.45 (2026-08-02)

  • Highlight chosen tissues or subtypes. Color by... now has a Pick groups button: tick the tissues or subtypes you care about and only those are colored, with everything else folded into one gray Other series. By subtype is available without first choosing a tissue, since picking a handful out of 70+ is now practical. Works in the single and three-panel views, and the choice is kept in exports and new tabs.
  • The hotspot three-panel view is usable as it comes. The panels are square by construction instead of taking their height from the single-plot size box, which made each panel a third as wide as it was tall and had to be shrunk by hand every time.
  • Fix: the axis labels were wrong. The y axis used a shortened form (“TP53 Effect”) and the x axis had no label at all, because its label was worked out and then never applied. Both now read the same as the single-panel view, e.g. TP53 Expression (log2 TPM+1) and MDM2 Gene Effect, shown once for the row rather than repeated on each panel.
  • Panel headings sit clear of the title and stay put if you move them. Dragging one used to be undone by the next redraw.

v.84.44 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: strong results reported "p = 0.0e+0". That was not a real number. The normal-distribution approximation behind every p-value was only accurate to about 1 in 10 million, so anything stronger than that rounded to certainty and the p-value collapsed to exactly zero. The CDKN1A / TP53 comparison that showed 0.0e+0 is in fact p = 2.3 × 10−26. Replaced with a method that stays accurate down to about 10−300.
  • p-values now read as numbers, not code. Above 0.001 they are plain decimals (p = 0.032); below that they use proper scientific notation (p = 2.3 × 10−26) instead of 2.3e-26. If a value is genuinely beyond what can be computed it says p < 10−300 rather than pretending to be zero.
  • Applied everywhere: the gene-effect and mutation charts, the by-tissue and by-genetic-change tables, the correlation-analysis and comparison views. CSV exports keep full machine-readable precision, and now carry real values where they previously wrote 0.

v.84.43 (2026-08-02)

  • One hover box on network genes. There were two: the gene-effect numbers appeared straight away in the browser's own box, then a second box with the gene description arrived a second later and overlapped it. Now a single box shows GE mean, GE SD, LFC and FDR with the gene name and summary underneath.
  • Fix: "Hold Shift for full text" is reliable. It only ever worked in the fraction of a second between the second box appearing and the pointer moving, which is why it seemed to work sometimes. The box now appears at once, so there is a real window, and holding Shift keeps the gene-effect numbers instead of dropping them.
  • Fix: the exported legend sat left of center. Its width was estimated from fixed column slots, counting empty space after the last column and using the wrong width for the node-color block. It is now measured from what is actually drawn, so the legend centers under the figure. The network itself still exports exactly as arranged on screen.
  • Every chart exports the same way. The leftover .svg / SVG / PNG buttons next to Export image... are gone from the correlation scatter, tissue chart, Gene Effect chart, expression-correlate scatter, correlation analysis, mutation table and the UMAP / PCA plot. One button everywhere, with format, print size, resolution and background in the dialog.

v.84.42 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: exporting from the UpSet plot did nothing visible. The export dialog opened behind the plot, because it only looked at the declared modals when deciding how high to stack, and the UpSet popup sits above all of them. It now stacks above whatever is actually on screen.
  • Fix: the print size chosen for an SVG was ignored. Width and height were set in cm and then overwritten in points by the step that cleans the file for drawing programs, so every SVG came out at the same size no matter what you asked for. This affected every chart in the app.
  • One export button everywhere. Separate SVG and PNG buttons are replaced by Export image..., which opens the usual dialog with format, print size, resolution and background. The oncoprint no longer saves straight to disk with no choices; its data export is now labeled Export data (CSV).
  • Fix: the Tissues heading floated over the list. A 4px strip at the top of the list sat above where the heading pins, so rows scrolled through it and the heading looked like it was hovering in mid-list. Also fixed the heading being see-through, which needed the table's borders separated to work at all.
  • The lineage list is no longer a native menu. With 31 tissues the browser's own menu opened taller than the screen and scrolled by growing upward with no way back down. It is now a panel that fits on screen, with a filter box for typing a tissue name.
  • The SVG option no longer names a particular drawing program.

v.84.41 (2026-08-02)

  • Fix: network coloring survived by "Show all input genes". Turning that on rebuilt the network with default colors and only restored Color by GE, so Color by stats silently reverted to green while its box stayed ticked. Both are restored now, and the newly shown genes are colored too.
  • Fix: input genes with no correlations now show LFC and FDR on hover. The lookup was simply missing on those nodes, so the genes added by "Show all input genes" had no statistics in their tooltip.
  • Fix: "Hold Shift for full text" now works. The tooltip appears a second after you start hovering and never saw a Shift key that was already held, so only pressing Shift after the box appeared did anything. Holding it works as the text says.
  • Loading stats no longer opens a dialog. "Loaded N genes with statistics" was an alert that appeared on load and again on every Run, since Run re-reads the box. It is now a quiet line under the text area.
  • Lists inside popups no longer drag the page with them. Reaching the end of a scrollable list passed the rest of the scroll to the page behind, which slid the page under panels anchored to a button, so they looked like they had jumped and could not be put back.
  • Fix: the Tissues table heading is opaque. Its background sat on the row rather than the cells, which browsers do not reliably paint on a pinned row, so rows could be seen through it.
  • Oncoprint and UpSet take genes beyond the top 25. Both have an add gene box; adding one in either place shows it in both.
  • Oncoprint SVG is about 15× smaller (1.8 MB to ~115 KB) with no loss of quality. Wild-type cells were one rectangle each, roughly 30,000 of them; they are identical, so they are now a single tiled pattern and only mutated cells are drawn individually.
  • Network: Show all input genes now sits above Show gene effect (GE) in label. The Test Genes button in the With Stats panel no longer overflows its column.

v.84.40 (2026-08-02)

  • Oncoprint shows every cell line. It used to cap at 200, which made the per-gene counts misleading: "RAC1 2" meant 2 of the first 200 cell lines, not 2 of the cohort. The counts are now true counts, the grid scrolls sideways, and the gene names and counts stay frozen in place while you scroll.
  • Oncoprint exports are publication quality. PNG is redrawn at up to 6× instead of being upscaled from the on-screen copy, so text and boxes are sharp rather than soft. SVG covers the whole cohort. The on-screen oncoprint is also drawn at your display's pixel density now.
  • UpSet asks what to compare. The unlabeled 3/5/7/10 dropdown is gone. UpSet... opens a picker where you choose which genes, not just how many, with a "Top N by mutation count" shortcut and the 5 most-mutated ticked by default.
  • The page no longer scrolls behind an open dialog. Scrolling while Reference Data, Gene Effect, the Cell Line Browser or any other full-screen dialog is open used to move the app underneath. Small popouts that sit beside the page while you work (oncoprint, UpSet, the "?" popouts) are unaffected on purpose.
  • Dialogs can be dragged by their title bar, so you can move one aside to read what's behind it.
  • A sources link next to the loaded-data line opens Reference Data without going to the nav bar.
  • Fix: hovering the oncoprint grid threw an error and never showed the cell-line tooltip. Hovering a cell now names the gene, the cell line and whether it's mutated.

v.84.39 (2026-08-01)

  • Reference Data moved to the nav bar. The sources are now behind a Reference Data link next to How it works, which opens them in full, no toggle needed. They were taking a card on the homepage for something you read once. The load state ("18,435 genes, 1,186 cell lines loaded") stays on the homepage as a line under the Options buttons, so it's still obvious when the app is ready.
  • Options now sits top-left, where Reference Data used to be, so the sidebar reads Options, then boxes 1 and 2. The button labels wrap to two lines, which makes them narrow enough to share one row in the sidebar at full size.
  • Reset moved to the Results tab row, at the far right beside Summary. It clears the workspace, so it no longer sits among the buttons you click to start work.
  • 3. Results is now the whole right column and starts at the top of the page.

v.84.38 (2026-08-01)

  • Options moved above Reference Data. The Options bar now spans the full width at the top of the page instead of sitting in the right column beside Reference Data. The right column is given over entirely to 3. Results, which gains the height the bar used to take. The five controls still sit on one row: the 415px sidebar was too narrow for that, which is why the bar spans the page rather than dropping into the column.
  • Reset separated from the tool buttons. It now sits at the far right of the Options bar, away from the buttons you click to start work, so it is harder to hit by accident.
  • Reference Data condensed. The three source lines are now two, with shorter labels and the details toggle inline on the second, and the card has tighter padding and a slimmer title bar. The full file and knowledge-base list is unchanged behind ▾ details.

v.84.37 (2026-08-01)

  • Fix: picking a tissue no longer empties the gene list. The minimum of 10 cell lines introduced in v.84.36 was counted against whatever cohort you had filtered to, and since every lineage is smaller than 200 cells, choosing for example Kidney cleared the list and silently dropped your gene. The minimum now scales with the cohort in view, from 10 on all cell lines down to 3 on a small lineage, and never below the 3 the analysis itself needs. If nothing qualifies, the list says so instead of appearing blank.
  • Each filter is now one row. The gene box and the mutated / WT box sit side by side rather than stacked, so a filter reads as one setting. Their labels are shortened (Mutated, WT, Altered, Fused) so nothing is cut off in the narrow column; counts still appear once you pick a gene.
  • The sub-type ? text now appears as a popout beside the question mark instead of a block pushed into the box.

v.84.36 (2026-08-01)

  • Deep deletion removed. Mutation analysis now has four sub-types: Hotspot mutation, Fusion, Functional loss, Amplification. Functional loss already treats deep deletion as one of its three mechanisms, on genes that have the cell lines to support it. Of the 14 genes Deep deletion offered, 4 had none at all and 8 more had under 10, and its one well-powered gene (CDKN2B) sits beside CDKN2A on 9p21 and is almost always co-deleted with it, which Functional loss covers better.
  • Genes with too few cell lines are no longer offered. A stratifier needs at least 10 carriers among the cell lines currently in scope, counted after your tissue and subtype filters, so the list shortens as you narrow the cohort. Amplification now lists MYC, CCND1, KRAS, MYCN, ERBB2, CDK4, MDM2, CCNE1, EGFR and MET. Fusions are exempt, since driver fusions are rare by nature and the rule would leave only two.

v.84.35 (2026-08-01)

  • Fix, affects results: cell lines with no copy-number data are no longer counted as unaltered. Copy number comes from whole-genome sequencing, which covers 830 of the 1,186 lines. The other 356 were being placed in the wild-type group, so every Amplification and Deep deletion comparison was diluted with cell lines that had never been measured. They are now excluded. Group sizes for these two sub-types now add up to 830, and p-values will differ from before.
  • The ? next to each sub-type is quieter and opens on hover, no click needed. Clicking still works on touch screens.

v.84.34 (2026-08-01)

  • Every mutation analysis sub-type now has a ? explaining what it is, which cell lines count as altered, the exact thresholds used and where the data comes from.
  • CN amplification and CN deep deletion renamed to Amplification and Deep deletion.
  • Correction: the old Deep deletion tooltip named CDKN2A/B, PTEN, SMAD4 and STK11 as examples. Only STK11 is actually in that panel. CDKN2A and PTEN are covered by Functional loss instead, and SMAD4 is not in it at all. The new help text lists the real 14 genes.
  • The gene dropdowns in the sub-type box no longer crop their text.
  • Enrichr in mutation analysis now asks which genes to send when you press it, instead of a separate unlabeled dropdown sitting next to the button. The link to the Enrichr site moved into the same menu.

v.84.33 (2026-08-01)

  • Mutation analysis: Compare by Hotspot and Compare by Fusion removed. Compare by Tissue stays.
  • The filter inputs in box 1 are another 15% smaller, so the section headings carry the eye.

v.84.32 (2026-08-01)

  • The two gene set alternatives are now separate boxed choices instead of two lines of running text, and the one in use is highlighted.
  • Lineage filter is now a bold section heading matching Genetic alterations, so box 1 reads as two clear groups of settings.
  • The filter inputs and dropdowns in box 1 are smaller and their labels lighter. They were competing with the headings for attention, which made the box look busier than it is.

v.84.31 (2026-08-01)

  • Gene set analysis and Mutation analysis are now separate buttons in Options, instead of one Analysis button plus a mode choice inside box 1. Options now reads: Gene set analysis, Mutation analysis, Cell Line Browser, Other, Reset.
  • Box 1 only shows the options for the mode you picked. In Gene set analysis you choose between correlating within your set or expanding it; in Mutation analysis you go straight to the alteration type and gene. The two sets of choices are no longer stacked on top of each other.
  • Gene set analysis stays the default on opening.

v.84.30 (2026-08-01)

  • Options simplified. The box is now a single row: Analysis, Cell Line Browser, Other and Reset. Gene Effect, Correlation and opening a saved figure moved into the Other menu, and the instruction line above the buttons is gone, so the box takes up much less room.
  • Analysis is now the default. Boxes 1, 2 and 3 are ready as soon as the app opens, so you can type a gene set straight away instead of first clicking a tool. The Analysis button is filled in to show it is the current mode, and now just jumps back to the gene box.

v.84.29 (2026-08-01)

  • New tab now works from a Mutation Inspect view. Opening a mutation analysis gene distribution (for example CDKN1A by TP53 mutation) in a new tab used to give a blank app, because that view is driven by the mutation results rather than the ordinary gene effect state. The new tab now rebuilds the analysis and reopens the same distribution, carrying the tissue / subtype / hotspot / fusion / CN filters with it.
  • New tab from a copy-number scatter. A scatter with a CN axis on one of the roughly 2,500 genes that only exist in the CN matrix opened a blank tab. It now restores correctly.
  • Sub-type filters now travel to the new tab. Opening a Gene Effect or Correlation view filtered to a sub-lineage (for example Lymphoid, Mature B-Cell Neoplasms) used to fall back to the whole parent tissue.

v.84.28 (2026-08-01)

  • The page no longer freezes while the copy-number and expression data are being unpacked. Both are now decoded in smaller pieces so the browser stays responsive, and expression decoding shows a percentage as it goes.

v.84.27 (2026-08-01)
