  • Correlation scatter redraws are faster. The chart is now updated in place instead of being torn down and rebuilt every time, so changing a filter or typing a gene name feels quicker.
  • Fixed chart click and drag handlers piling up. Each redraw added another copy without removing the old one, so a long session got progressively slower and a single click could end up handled several times over. Affects the correlation scatter, the gene effect plot and the cell line browser UMAP.

v.84.26 (2026-08-01)

  • The version badge in the top bar was stuck at v.84.22 and did not follow the last three releases. Exported figures read their version stamp from this badge, so anything exported since v.84.23 carried the wrong version in its metadata.
  • The badge also had a duplicate style attribute, which meant its monospace pill styling was silently dropped and it rendered as a plain link. Merged into one attribute so the intended styling applies.

v.84.25 (2026-06-18)

  • Find correlates: if the Expression panel is blank because expression data hasn't loaded, it now says so explicitly and how to fix it (reopen Find correlates once it finishes), instead of just showing an empty list. Empty lists from the |r| cutoff also get a short note.

v.84.24 (2026-06-18)

  • Find correlates: expression data now loads automatically when you run it, so the "Top Expression correlates" panel populates even when the X gene is a gene-effect gene (it was coming out empty / 0 outputs).
  • Network filter banner: the text-settings panel now reads and edits the live banner (#networkHeader) properly, the Font Size / Text / Color controls stay in sync, and a custom banner text now survives re-renders (zoom etc.) and is used in exports. (The panel previously read a removed element, so the banner text field never appeared and edits didn't stick.)

v.84.23 (2026-06-17)

  • Cell-line CSV exports: renamed the FocalCN column to CancerCN and clarified the key, so it's clear it's the curated cancer-driver focal call (only the ~30 driver genes get a value), distinct from the CN column which is the relative copy number for every gene (so a whole amplicon shows many neighbouring genes with high CN, with only the driver flagged in CancerCN).

v.84.22 (2026-06-17)

  • Cell-line CSV exports: the header is now a compact aligned 2-column (Field, Value) block instead of long single-cell comment lines, so it opens tidily with text-to-columns. Added per-gene Chr and Cytoband (GRCh38) columns to the full-profile export (and a gene-location listing in the per-gene export).

v.84.21 (2026-06-17)

  • Correlation scatter: opening the scatter directly (the Correlation button) now shows the Amp/Del and Fusion compare buttons and the CN filter from the start, instead of only after the first Update. The dot hover now spells out "Shift-click to open in Cell Line Browser".

v.84.20 (2026-06-17)

  • Gene Effect "by genetic change": new "CN amp, all genes" scan option (full DepMap CN matrix, not just the curated panel). It scans every recurrently-amplified gene for shifts in the target's dependency. The CN filter now also accepts any gene (matrix fallback), so clicking a row drills in. Loads the CN matrix on first use.

v.84.19 (2026-06-17)

  • Correlation scatter: added CN (relative copy number) as an X/Y axis type alongside GE and Expression, so you can plot copy number vs gene effect / expression / copy number for any gene. The CN matrix loads on demand the first time.

v.84.18 (2026-06-17)

  • Wiki: new "Major copy-number regions" block in the genome section. From the full DepMap gene CN matrix + gene cytoband locations, it surfaces focal amplifications and deep deletions per cell line, naming the driver cancer genes (e.g. THP-1 shows the 1p34 amplification with MYCL at >20 copies). Loads the CN matrix on demand.

v.84.17 (2026-06-17)

  • Cell-line CSV exports now include a relative copy-number column per gene from the full DepMap gene-level CN matrix (all genes, not just the curated focal amp/del panel). 1.0 = the line's modal baseline, >1 gain, <1 loss. Added to the full-profile, comprehensive and per-gene exports (the matrix loads on demand the first time).

v.84.16 (2026-06-17)

  • Text settings (Aa) on charts: the Gene Effect plots draw the stats line (n cells, means, p-value) as a separate subtitle annotation, which the panel couldn't see, so it looked like the app "forgot" the subtitle and title/subtitle scaling was off. The panel now reads and edits that subtitle directly, so you can change the stats text and size the title / subtitle independently.

v.84.15 (2026-06-17)

  • Gene-effect inspect opened from Mutational Analysis: the inspect-level subtype / hotspot / fusion filters now override the conserved analysis-level filters instead of stacking with them, so changing a filter in inspect mode no longer silently intersects with the analysis cohort and collapses to zero cells. (Reset Filters still clears all conserved analysis filters.)

v.84.14 (2026-06-17)

  • Network view controls now sync between screen and export: the filter-banner font/color/text settings were targeting an old element that no longer exists (so changes only showed in exports) and now style the live banner; the export legend font size was hardcoded (so legend size changes only showed live) and now follows the legend text setting.

v.84.13 (2026-06-17)

  • Network: zooming in then out could leave a "ghost" of the zoomed-in frame at the bottom of the graph (and in exported images, which copy the live canvas). The canvas now does a clean resize + full redraw after zooming and before export, clearing the residue.

v.84.12 (2026-06-17)

  • Network export (PNG / PDF / SVG): the edge-thickness legend now scales with the current zoom to match the actual edges. Previously the legend drew reference lines at full base width while the exported edges were drawn zoom-scaled, so a strong r=0.9 edge looked far thinner than the legend implied.

v.84.11 (2026-06-17)

  • Screenshot "Full content": tall popouts were producing a canvas past the browser's max size, so only the .json downloaded and the image silently failed. The capture scale is now clamped to a safe size so the image always exports (with a clear message if it's still too big to fit).
  • Export dialog now notes that a matching .correlate.json downloads alongside the image (reopen it later with Open).
  • HLA (and other polymorphic HLA/MIC/KIR loci) no longer appear as hotspot mutations in the Cell Line Browser hotspot filter, the scatter "compare by hotspot" table, the wiki hotspot list, or the cell-line report export, they're germline allelic divergence, not somatic hotspots.

v.84.10 (2026-06-17)

  • Find correlates: each gene now shows the n (cell lines with both genes valid) next to r, sortable, and flagged red when n < 10, so low-n / unreliable top hits are easy to spot.

v.84.9 (2026-06-16)

  • Set Parameters: added a subtle divider and a "Genetic alterations" heading above the hotspot / copy number / fusion filters, to group them apart from the lineage / tissue filters.

v.84.8 (2026-06-16)

  • Set Parameters: the Hotspot and Fusion filter dropdowns dropped the "All cells" option, so all three filters (hotspot / fusion / copy number) now consistently default to the altered side (clear the gene to turn a filter off).
  • Condensed the bias note to "Selecting for genetic alterations can introduce unintended bias in analysis" with a "?" you can click for the fuller explanation.

v.84.7 (2026-06-15)

  • Cell Line Browser filters: the hotspot / fusion / CN filters now have WT vs altered level selectors (default mutated 1+2 / fused / with-event), so you can list cells that are WT for a gene, not just carriers.
  • Results Correlations tab: the action button is now labeled Correlation (was "Scatter").
  • Results Clusters tab: the action column is now labeled Analyze (was mislabeled "Correlation"; it holds the Gene Effect button).

v.84.6 (2026-06-15)

  • Correlation Analysis popout: the hotspot / fusion / CN filters now have WT vs altered level selectors (default mutated 1+2 / fused / with-event), the active filters are listed under the plot title, and Reset no longer leaves a stale "All tissues (n=…)" count.
  • CN amp/del filter lists are now sorted purely by count (high to low), instead of all amplifications first then all deletions.
  • Network edge-thickness legend now tracks the real zoom when zoomed far out (it was clamped and drew ~2-3x too thick at low zoom).

v.84.5 (2026-06-15)

  • Cell line CSV exports (full profile / gene info): the comment header lines no longer contain commas, so they stay in one column and the gene table parses cleanly in Excel / text-to-columns instead of opening misaligned.
  • Cell Line Browser card: moved the Wiki button to just below the executive summary, above the Tissue row.

v.84.4 (2026-06-15)

  • Correlation scatter filters: picking a hotspot / fusion / CN event now defaults to the altered side (mutated 1+2 / fused / with-event); dropped the "All cells" option (clear the gene to turn a filter off); and the CN amp/del filter now has a with-event vs WT selector like the others.
  • Correlation scatter: the active hotspot / fusion / CN filters (with their level) are now all listed under the plot title, and Reset no longer leaves a stale "All tissues (n=…)" count.
  • Compare tables: clicking a row now applies that change as the matching filter (hotspot / fusion / amp-del), not a color overlay, and every row is clickable (previously CN and curated-fusion rows weren't).
  • Fusion overlay now lists only curated / validated fusion genes, matching the rest of the app.

v.84.3 (2026-06-15)

  • Wiki PDF export: hyperlinks (DepMap, Cellosaurus, references, etc.) are now clickable in the PDF.
  • Gene Effect toolbar: removed the duplicate separator next to Analyze.
  • By genetic change chart: fixed the clipped header (title now stays in view on tall charts), made the zero line a thin light gray instead of a heavy black bar, and narrowed the chart so the statistics table gets more width.

v.84.2 (2026-06-14)

  • Set Parameters (correlation): the Fusion filter is now the searchable, curated ★ clinical-driver-pair picker (matching Gene Effect), with WT vs with-fusion (defaults to with-fusion on pick). All cohort consumers (network, oncoprint, mutation-analysis additional filter) updated to the curated-pair model. Picking any hotspot / fusion / CN now defaults its level to "altered" every time.

v.84.1 (2026-06-14)

  • Set Parameters (correlation): the Hotspot filter is now a searchable, curated, context-aware picker like Gene Effect, keeping the WT / 1 / 2 / 1+2 level selector (defaults to 1+2 when you pick a gene). Added a new Copy Number filter (focal amp ▲ / deep deletion ▼) with "with event" vs WT, which restricts the correlation cohort. (Fusion picker and the other popouts follow in the next updates.)

v.84.0 (2026-06-14)

  • Results "Correlations" table: simplified the actions column to just the Scatter button and renamed the column to "Correlation" (By Tissue / By Hotspot are reachable from inside the scatter view).

v.83.99 (2026-06-14)

  • Running an analysis that takes longer than ~2s now shows a "Analyzing gene set..." spinner so it's clear the app is still working, not crashed. Fast runs finish before the spinner appears, so there's no flicker.

v.83.98 (2026-06-14)

  • Δ subset-compare table (by tissue / hotspot / fusion / amp / del) now defaults to hiding rows with fewer than 3 cells in either group (WT or altered), not just by total subset size, and the cutoff box has −/+ step buttons.

v.83.97 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect "by genetic change" now plots every cell line as an individual dot with a mean line (WT blue / Altered orange), instead of box plots. Hover a dot for the cell line's executive summary, click to label it, Shift-click to open its Wiki.

v.83.96 (2026-06-14)

  • Opening a popout screenshot's .correlate.json sidecar now restores the view (Gene Effect / Correlation / Correlation Analysis popout, or the cell line Wiki) instead of saying restore is unsupported.

v.83.95 (2026-06-14)

  • Fixed: the Gene Effect by-mutation plot was forced to full width (overriding the ~55% used elsewhere), which also pushed the y-axis label off-screen. It now matches the other views and the y-axis label shows.
  • Gene Effect dots: click a placed name label to remove it; Shift-click now opens the cell line's Wiki (instead of double-click), and the hover card spells out "Click to label · Shift-click to open its Wiki".

v.83.94 (2026-06-14)

  • Homepage: the Analysis button is no longer filled-green on load, it matches the other tool buttons at all times (the Options box is what is emphasised).
  • Gene Effect plots: interactive cell-line dots, hover a dot for that cell line's executive summary, single-click to toggle its name label, double-click to open its Wiki on top of the plot (closing the Wiki returns to the plot). Shift-click still opens the Cell Line Browser.

v.83.93 (2026-06-14)

  • By genetic change: the box plots now show every cell line as a dot plus a mean line, with the box faded right back, so you see the actual cell-line distribution rather than a box summary.

v.83.92 (2026-06-14)

  • By genetic change: defaults to the p < 0.05 filter on first open; fixed the legend overlapping the n=… line and the x-axis label sitting on the tick numbers; bigger axis-label and row-label fonts.

v.83.91 (2026-06-14)

  • Fixed: on the Gene Effect by-mutation plot the rotated y-axis label could be missing on screen (it showed in exports). Its position was measured before the chart was sized to its width, pushing it off-screen; the chart is now sized first.

v.83.90 (2026-06-14)

  • By genetic change: every row is now a clean binary comparison, WT vs Altered, for all types (hotspot mutations are no longer split into 1 / 2 hits here, which looked odd next to the binary fusion / CN rows). The 0/1/2 mutation dose detail is still in Mutation Inspect for a single gene. The table dropped the now-empty "2 hits" columns.

v.83.89 (2026-06-14)

  • Homepage: the Analysis button is no longer emphasised (now a normal outline button like the other tools), and the Options box itself gets a stronger green outline + glow on load to draw the eye.

v.83.88 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect by-mutation header rebuilt as two separate text blocks (title + stats), each with its own line spacing, so a two-row title no longer overlaps itself and the stats stay tight. The whole block is anchored above the plot and the top margin grows to fit it, so it never overlaps the graph, on screen or in exports.

v.83.87 (2026-06-14)

  • By genetic change: now defaults to hotspot mutations only. Fusions and amp/deep-del are offered in a highlighted "+ also scan" pill so it's clear you can add them.

v.83.86 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect: the Reset Filters button is kept and now shows in all views (By Tissue / By genetic change / Mutation Inspect), at the end of the filters row, and resets the current view.

v.83.85 (2026-06-14)

  • By genetic change: the Min cell lines field now has − / + stepper buttons.

v.83.84 (2026-06-14)

  • Export dialog: Width and Height each keep their cm input right next to their label (grouped), and the dialog is a bit wider so nothing wraps.
  • Fixed: PDF chart exports showed a stray quote instead of the minus sign on negative axis ticks (Plotly's Unicode minus is now written as a plain hyphen for the PDF font).
  • Gene Effect: the Reset Filters button moved to the far end of the filters row.
  • Gene Effect: pressing Enter after typing a gene now runs the analysis (the Analyze button still works too).

v.83.83 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect by-mutation header: reverted to the original look.
  • By genetic change: new "Min cell lines" filter (default 3) so only changes present in at least that many lines are shown. The table now puts the type chip on its own line above the full change name.
  • Gene Effect: the redundant blue summary banner is gone; active filters now show as chips on the Custom CLs row (like the Cell Line Browser).
  • Fixed: the Custom CLs filter now actually restricts the Gene Effect plots to the pasted cell lines, in every view.

v.83.82 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect by-mutation header: the title is now larger (closer to the axis-label size) while the stats lines stay tightly packed.
  • Tissue filters across the app now show the cell count per tissue and list the most abundant tissues first (the Gene Effect Mutation Inspect and Correlation Analysis ones were missing this).

v.83.81 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect popout: new Reset button that restarts the analysis (clears the gene, filters and view).

v.83.80 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect: "By Hotspot" is now By genetic change, the scan compares cells with vs without each genetic change. It now covers hotspot mutations, curated fusions (★) and focal amplifications / deep deletions (▲▼), not just hotspots. Checkboxes let you include/exclude each type. Clicking a row drills in (hotspot genes open Mutation Inspect; fusion / CN apply that filter).

v.83.79 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect by-mutation header: the title and stats lines are now close in size and packed tightly (small line-height) instead of being spread far apart down the y-axis.

v.83.78 (2026-06-14)

  • Gene Effect "By Hotspot" view: the plot is a bit narrower so the statistics table (Gene, N/GE WT, N/GE Mut, Δ, p) fits without horizontal scrolling.

  • Renamed the "Aa" buttons to "Settings" across the app.
  • Gene Effect by-mutation header: tighter line spacing and a smaller title so it no longer takes too much vertical space or looks too spread out (while still clearing the plot).

v.83.77 (2026-06-14)

v.83.75 (2026-06-14)

v.83.74 (2026-06-14)

v.83.73 (2026-06-14)

  • Phone: the x-axis label on the Gene Effect by-mutation plot was clipped off the bottom (the smaller phone bottom margin cut it off). It's now pulled closer to the plot with a bit more bottom room so it's visible.

v.83.72 (2026-06-13)

v.83.71 (2026-06-13)

v.83.70 (2026-06-13)

v.83.69 (2026-06-13)

v.83.68 (2026-06-13)

The Gene Effect and Correlation Analysis download rows (image / SVG / CSV / .json.gz), the scatter CSV / .json.gz / background-toggle exports, and the width / height / zero-line / size-hint chart settings are now hidden on phones. The phone app is for viewing details / gene effect / expression, not exporting or advanced analysis.

v.83.67 (2026-06-13)

v.83.65 (2026-06-13)

v.83.64 (2026-06-13)

  • Phone: in the cell line Wiki, the label column was too wide and squeezed the value column into many wrapped lines (e.g. Sample taken from). The label column is now narrower on phones so the value gets the room.

v.83.63 (2026-06-13)

  • Phone: the cell-line detail (executive summary) now has a Close button at the top, so you can dismiss it and get the list back instead of it taking over the screen.

v.83.61 (2026-06-13)

v.83.60 (2026-06-13)

v.83.59 (2026-06-13)

Hover still works, and the gate-draw and UMAP / cluster lasso-select tools are unaffected. Done globally via per-axis fixedrange, so it applies to all current and future charts.

v.83.56 (2026-06-13)

v.83.52 (2026-06-13)

v.83.50 (2026-06-13)

v.83.47 (2026-06-13)

v.83.43 (2026-06-13)

v.83.42 (2026-06-13)

Wiring it into the first-page parameters and the Gene Effect / scatter / Correlation Analysis popouts follows.

v.83.38 (2026-06-13)

  • Wiki drug response: added a short, prominent note that “standout sensitive” means selective, not strong, a line can be more sensitive than others (low z) yet still not very sensitive in absolute terms (high AUC). Read AUC and z-score together.

v.83.37 (2026-06-12)

  • Hotspot filters are now consistent everywhere. HLA / MIC / KIR polymorphic-locus calls (germline divergence, not somatic hotspots) are dropped from every hotspot picker / stratifier, the Gene Effect, scatter and Correlation Analysis popouts now match the Cell Line Browser.

v.83.36 (2026-06-12)

  • Fix: opening a GE-vs-expression scatter (or any mixed-axis pair) in a new tab now keeps both axis data types, instead of falling back to GE vs GE.
  • Fix: popout screenshots now always include the chart again, the crisp Plotly image is composited onto the capture (fixing the offset gray background) rather than swapped into the clone (which html2canvas didn't always render). Input/box text centring improved.

v.83.35 (2026-06-12)

  • Correlation chart spacing: the title block is lifted off the top of the plot and the rotated y-axis title is pushed clear of the tick numbers.
  • Cleaner popout screenshots: charts are flattened to a crisp image before capture (no more nudged gray plot background), and text inside input boxes (gene names, plot size, axis ranges) is now vertically centered.
  • Options box is outlined in black on load (until Analysis is clicked) so it's the obvious starting point.
  • Text settings travel with the view: font sizes are saved into the metadata and re-applied when you open a metadata file or open a view in a new tab.

v.83.34 (2026-06-12)

  • Removed Open Saved Inspect from the Cell Line Browser. Re-opening a view is now done from Open on the first page, mainly via the metadata (.correlate.json) file saved next to every image export.
  • Opening a metadata file now regenerates the exact graph. Image-export metadata now carries the full state, the underlying network (genes, mode, cutoff, filters, network settings) plus the popout and every filter / setting control, so Open rebuilds the network and the chart exactly as exported. (The same composite is used by Open-in-new-tab and the embedded PNG/SVG metadata.)

v.83.33 (2026-06-12)

  • Fix: clicking a network edge now reliably opens the correlation popout, including after applying a “best filter” and re-running. The lookup falls back to opening the pair directly if the edge isn't in the current correlation list.
  • Open in new tab now duplicates the whole app. The new tab rebuilds the underlying network (genes, mode, cutoff, filters, network settings) and then opens the popout on top, so closing the popout leaves you with the same network you came from, not a blank app.

v.83.32 (2026-06-12)

  • Wiki subtype / badge colors reworked to earthy tones: breast calls now read HR+ = moss green, HER2+ = ochre, TNBC = terracotta; the hotspot / damaging / fusion / tissue pills move off their bright amber / purple / blue onto the same earth-toned palette. Functional status colors (pathway traffic-lights, warnings, the histogram “this line” marker) are left as-is since they signal alerts, not categories.

v.83.31 (2026-06-12)

  • Removed the Inspect Correlations button from the Cell Line Browser toolbar.
  • The Cell Line Browser export buttons are now grouped under an explicit Export CSV: label (and the inspect buttons under Inspect:) so it's clear what they do.
  • Color cleanup: the export / screenshot / data-download buttons swap their off-palette purple for an earthy bronze that sits alongside the brand green. Semantic colors (subtype calls, mutation badges) are unchanged.

v.83.30 (2026-06-12)

  • Open in new tab now carries the full view. The new tab reproduces the same gene(s) plus the current filters and settings (data type, tissue / subtype / hotspot / fusion / mutation filters, stratification gene, min group size, axis ranges, colors, etc.), not just the gene and view.
  • The popout Figure button is renamed Screenshot.

v.83.29 (2026-06-12)

  • Options is now a normal card matching the rest of the app (same green title bar, same font) instead of the bright banner. Its header sits on the same row as the Reference Data header, with the action buttons on the row below.

v.83.28 (2026-06-12)

  • Open a popout in a new tab. The Gene Effect, Correlation and Correlation Analysis popouts now have a New tab ↗ button. It opens the same view in a fresh browser tab (the view's settings travel in the URL), so you can park e.g. TP53 gene effect by tissue in one tab and keep working on the network in the other.

v.83.27 (2026-06-12)

  • Homepage rearranged (experimental). The action buttons now sit in a green Options banner at the top, in the order Analysis · Gene Effect · Correlation · Cell Line Browser · Open · Reset. Boxes 1 / 2 / 3 start grayed out and are enabled by the new Analysis button; the other buttons still jump straight to their tool. Reference Data stays in the sidebar. (Opening a saved view or running an analysis also enables the boxes.)

v.83.26 (2026-06-12)

  • Screenshot a popout for a figure. A new 📷 Figure button on the Wiki, Gene Effect, Correlation and Correlation Analysis popouts captures the whole popout as a high-resolution image (PNG / TIFF / PDF), with a choice of full content or visible area only and a metadata sidecar. Pure charts keep their existing vector (SVG/PDF) export via the Export image button.

v.83.25 (2026-06-12)

  • Every image export now saves a companion metadata file (.correlate.json) alongside the image, holding the view's settings (filters, genes, mode, cohort). Open now accepts that file and recreates the figure from it. This metadata file is the main way to reopen a figure; the older embedded SVG/PNG settings still work too.

v.83.24 (2026-06-12)

  • Quick filters popout is now movable — drag it by its header. On small screens it's clamped into the viewport so the last filter rows are always reachable instead of disappearing below the fold.

v.83.23 (2026-06-12)

  • Wiki drug responses can be exported as a CSV (every PRISM compound with this line's AUC, the cohort mean / SD / z-score, and target / mechanism / indication) so you can make your own plot.
  • Wiki breast receptor expression can be exported as a CSV (ESR1 / PGR / ERBB2 for every breast line, this line flagged).
  • Wiki histograms refreshed: soft-filled bars with a thin border, a crisp solid red marker with a value pill for this cell line, cleaner axes and a touch more height. Receptor, drug-response and genome panels now share one look.

v.83.22 (2026-06-12)

  • Cell line browser exports renamed and expanded. Three clearer exports: Cell line: GE + expression (selected lines, every gene), Cell line: full profile (selected lines, every gene with GE + Expression + Hotspot + Damaging + Fusion + focal CN amplifications / deletions), and Genes: full profile (one or a few genes, all that info across the selected/visible lines). All include the DepMap version and citation.
  • Export gene info (.csv) button added to the cell line Wiki, next to Download PDF, exporting the full per-gene profile for that one cell line.

v.83.21 (2026-06-12)

  • Sort: Drug response — broadly cytotoxic compounds now sort to the top of the compound list (they kill the most lines) instead of being pushed to the bottom. They keep the “broadly cytotoxic %” badge so it stays clear they're broad killers, not targeted hits.
  • HLA / polymorphic loci no longer counted as hotspot mutations. Calls in HLA / MIC / KIR genes reflect germline allelic divergence from GRCh38, not somatic hotspots, so they're excluded from hotspot counts, the cell-line hotspot list, the oncoprint, the wiki, and the hotspot-gene pickers.
  • Sort menu trimmed in the cell line browser to the four that matter: Name (default), GE, Expression, Drug response.

v.83.20 (2026-06-09)

  • Wiki "Download PDF" now saves a real PDF file directly (no print dialog / PDF-printer needed). Multi-page, white background, charts embedded as images; a few MB.
  • The "not found" gene-suggestion box now checks the mouse to human ortholog table first, so it correctly suggests Trp53 to TP53 instead of unrelated fuzzy matches (ARPC3 / BRPF3 / LRP3). Real typos still fall back to nearest-match suggestions. Also fixed the "Find Synonyms" ortholog lookup to handle lower-case input.

v.83.19 (2026-06-09)

  • Wiki download is now a clean PDF (via the print view) instead of a raw HTML file. Each chart is embedded as a flat white image rather than the live Plotly layers, so it no longer looks broken.
  • Wiki chart PNG downloads (the per-panel camera button on the genome / receptor / drug histograms) now have a white background instead of a transparent / gray one.

v.83.18 (2026-06-08)

  • Wiki Genome signatures: when a line has only an MSI score and no PureCN structural call (ploidy / WGD / aneuploidy / CIN / LoH), it now says so explicitly instead of silently showing nothing, and WGD no longer reads "No" when the value is actually missing (missing data is not a negative result).

v.83.17 (2026-06-08)

  • Breast lines now show their receptor subtype by expression (HR+ / luminal, HER2+, or triple-negative) in the executive summary: the hover card, the Cell Line Browser detail card, and the wiki.
  • Gene-effect chart: the gene name is now a proper x-axis title (e.g. "RAN Gene Effect") under the scale, so it shows in the condensed popout and in exports instead of being clipped behind the button bar.
  • Hid the Expression Correlates button in the condensed gene-effect popout (it needs a mutation-analysis subgroup that the popout doesn't have); it stays available in the full gene-effect view.

v.83.16 (2026-06-08)

  • Fixed: "Export image" did nothing when the condensed gene-effect popout was open over the Cell Line Browser. The export dialog was opening behind the popout; it now stacks above whatever is on top, so export works from that popout.

v.83.15 (2026-06-08)

  • Renamed the leftover "Design mode" wording to match the current label "Expand my set": the < 20 genes warning, the stats-table note, and the "How it works" card.

v.83.14 (2026-06-08)

  • Export dialog format list now reads with " / " separators (e.g. "PDF / vector (scalable, selectable text)"), and the dialog title is "Export chart / FORMAT". The earlier "raster image inside" wording for PDF is gone, since PDF is true vector.
  • "How it works" updated: mutation analysis now lists copy-number amplification / deep deletion alongside hotspots, fusions and functional loss.
  • Writing pass across the app: removed em-dashes from labels, tooltips, the "How it works" panel, the Cell Line Browser help, and the cell-line wiki text, using "/" as a separator and commas/colons for clauses.

v.83.13 (2026-06-08)

  • Export dialog — corrected the format descriptions now that PDF is true vector: “PDF — vector (scalable, selectable text)” (it previously, wrongly, still said “raster image inside”).
  • PowerPoint export now places the figure on a standard 16:9 widescreen slide (13.33×7.5in), scaled to fit with a margin and centered, instead of sizing the slide to the figure — so it drops straight into a normal deck.

v.83.12 (2026-06-08)

  • Typography polish across the app: balanced wrapping for headings, labels and buttons (no more lopsided lines or a single word stranded on its own line), pretty wrapping for body text, crisper font rendering, and tabular figures so numbers in tables/badges keep a fixed width. Tidied the Analysis-mode sub-labels and stopped short button labels (e.g. “Test Genes”) from breaking across two lines.

v.83.11 (2026-06-08)

  • Image export — PDF and PowerPoint are now true vector for chart exports (previously the figure was embedded as a raster image). PDFs are written straight from the plot SVG (scalable paths + selectable text); PPTX embeds the SVG natively (PowerPoint 2016+) with a PNG fallback for older viewers. TIFF/PNG remain raster as before.
  • Mutation-analysis drill-down tables (inline compare, expression correlates) now use the correct axis wording for the CN sub-types (e.g. “Amp / Neutral”, “Del / Neutral”) instead of the generic “Mut / WT”.
  • “1. Set Parameters” — subtle dividers added below Min Cell Lines and the Lineage Filter to group the controls.

v.83.10 (2026-06-08)

  • Mutation analysis — two new stratification sub-types: CN amplification (focal ≥ 3× oncogene amp; MYC, ERBB2, MDM2, CDK4 …) and CN deep deletion (near-homozygous TSG loss; CDKN2A/B, PTEN, SMAD4, STK11 …), both drawn from the curated focal copy-number panel. Pick a gene and the whole analysis (split, plots, tissue breakdown, table) runs against amplified-vs-neutral or deep-deleted-vs-neutral lines.
  • Cell Line Wiki — breast lines now show a Receptor status block: ESR1 / PGR / ERBB2 expression as histograms across all breast lines (this line marked), with the expression-surrogate call (HR+ / HER2+ / triple-negative) shown alongside.

v.83.9 (2026-06-08)

  • Gene-link clicks now always open the correct data type: a gene clicked in a gene-effect context opens the GE popout, one clicked in an expression context opens expression — previously the popout could inherit the last-used type (e.g. clicking a gene-effect hit after viewing an expression gene wrongly showed expression).
  • Cell Line Browser — clicking any gene name in the detail card (hotspots, functional loss, focal CN, the depleted/enriched lists) now opens the gene-effect popout on top of the browser for a quick look (it was opening behind it / not at all).
  • Mutation analysis — results table now has an “only p < 0.05 (mutant vs WT)” filter, on by default, so genes that only reach significance on a secondary comparison (e.g. 2-vs-0) no longer clutter the list with poor primary p-values.
  • Analysis-mode labels rewritten to be clearer: Correlate genes within my set / Expand my set — find correlated genes / Genes affected by a mutation (mutant vs wild-type), each with a hover explanation.
  • Wiki — expression no longer described as “turned on/off” (now “highly expressed” / signatures “elevated / reduced”).

v.83.8 (2026-06-08)

  • Wiki — Key genetic alterations now also lists hotspot-mutated canonical drivers that lack a specific-variant call (e.g. STK11, KEAP1 in lung adeno), so they show as ✓ typical and are no longer wrongly listed under “not altered.” A POLE / POLD1 damaging mutation is now surfaced even without an elevated mutation burden (flagged as likely-not-a-functional-ultramutator). The driver tags read “typical / not a canonical hallmark” (no more confusing “atypical”).
  • Wiki — removed treatment / drug-recommendation language (these are cell lines, not patients): pathway-status no longer suggests inhibitors/therapies, the “targeted therapies matched” block and the executive-summary “model for … therapy” / “drug-target candidate” lines are gone. In-vitro PRISM drug-sensitivity data is kept (it characterises the line). Pathway status now states it covers only a few curated high-level pathways.
  • Wiki — the patient-origin row is relabeled “Sample taken from” and clarifies it’s the tumor site this cell line was established from (primary vs metastasis), not the patient’s overall disease stage.
  • Quick filters — breast receptor subtypes now consistently labeled “approximate” (expression surrogate); a “hover any filter for how it’s defined” hint added at the top; the “Pathway-activity expression signatures” group renamed Active expression programs.

v.83.7 (2026-06-08)

  • Analysis mode reorganized into two clearer choices: Gene set analysis (with a sub-choice of correlations within my gene set vs find new correlated genes across all genes, and the “also correlate the discovered genes with each other” option) and Mutation analysis. “2. Input Genes” renamed 2. Input Gene Set.
  • TIFF / PDF / PowerPoint now offered everywhere an image is exported — the network graph, the mutation-analysis table, and the gate-comparison report now use the same single-button / format-popup as the charts (in addition to the correlation scatter, tissue, gene-effect, expression-correlate and correlation-analysis charts).

v.83.6 (2026-06-08)

  • Color-by-subtype legend — entries are now sized to the full subtype name so they no longer overlap (long names get their own row), the whole legend stays visible below the plot and is included in exports, and the chip legend in the controls panel no longer widens the panel / breaks the layout.
  • Fusion filter in 1. Set Parameters is now a dropdown (matching the Hotspot filter) instead of a search box, and the “selecting for mutations/fusions may introduce bias” note sits below it.
  • Clicking a gene in the Wiki’s Expression profile section now opens the popout showing expression (not gene effect).

v.83.5 (2026-06-08)

  • Chart exports consolidated to a single Export image ▾ button (was separate PNG / SVG). Clicking it opens the format popup where you choose PNG / SVG / TIFF / PDF / PowerPoint plus size, DPI and background. Applied to the correlation scatter, the tissue chart, the Gene Effect chart, the expression-correlate scatter, and the correlation-analysis chart.

v.83.4 (2026-06-08)

  • Clicking a gene inside the Cell Line Wiki (or any overlay) now opens its gene-effect-by-cancer-type plot on top, in a condensed popout — just the graph and the export buttons, no filter bar or stats table — instead of opening behind the wiki where you couldn’t see it. A ⤢ Full view button expands it to the complete analysis if you want the table and filters.

v.83.3 (2026-06-08)

  • Removed the HeLa cell line from the app entirely. It was never in the CRISPR cohort, but it remained in the expression and copy-number matrices; its column has now been dropped from both (and their metadata), so no HeLa-derived data is present anywhere. (HeLa derives from Henrietta Lacks’ cells, taken without consent and not anonymized; its genomic data carries specific consent/governance constraints.)

v.83.2 (2026-06-07)

  • Chart export — in addition to PNG and SVG, you can now export TIFF, PDF and PowerPoint (.pptx). Pick the format in the export dialog (one selector, available from every chart’s export); size / DPI / background apply to all raster formats. TIFF is a journal-ready RGB image at your chosen DPI, PDF is a correctly-sized single page, PPTX drops the figure onto a slide sized to match.
  • Cell Line Wiki — the Expression profile now has the same “cancer family” view as CRISPR dependencies (uniquely-high genes vs same-lineage lines), and both sections now flag which whole-cohort hits are lineage-typical (✓ tag) — i.e. common for the cancer type rather than specific to this line — for both gene effect and expression.

v.83.1 (2026-06-07)

  • Cell Line Wiki — CRISPR dependencies now also shows a “cancer family” view: the same z-scored dependency ranking but computed against only the same-lineage cell lines, surfacing what this line needs beyond what its tissue siblings share (e.g. A549 tops its lung family on MDM4 — a p53 regulator it depends on more than other lung lines — which the all-lineages view buries). Shown alongside the whole-cohort list; needs ≥ 5 lines in the lineage.

v.83.0 (2026-06-07)

  • Cell Line Wiki — driver sections consolidated & clarified. The old Expected drivers for this subtype, Driver mutations and Functional loss sections (which overlapped a lot) are now one “Key genetic alterations” section: the alterations likely central to this line’s transformation — activating oncogene mutations, tumor-suppressor functional loss, validated driver fusions and focal CN gains/losses — each tagged ✓ typical or not a canonical hallmark for the cancer subtype, with the typical driver pattern shown for context and the genotype × CRISPR pathway read-out below.
  • Wiki wording clarified for scientists: Aneuploidy now explains it counts chromosome-arm gains/losses (not just “Ben-David score”); Fusion landscape defines what a validated fusion is vs the raw caller list; CRISPR dependencies and Expression profile now state explicitly that “unique / uniquely expressed” is vs the whole cohort across all lineages (not same-tissue lines); pathway-activity signatures ON/OFF are now properly explained.

v.82.6 (2026-06-07)

  • Scatter color-by legend now fully visible & exported — with many tissue/subtype categories the legend wraps into many rows below the plot; the canvas now grows to fit the whole legend (measured after render) so nothing is clipped on screen and the PNG / SVG / data exports include it.
  • Help text refreshed for recent changes — the Cell Line Browser “?” now covers the CN filter, the Ploidy / Aneuploidy / CIN / Copy-number / Drug-response sorts, the hotspot dropdown, the executive-summary card and the Show Selected toggle; the “How it works” mutation-analysis note now reads “validated driver fusions / functional loss”.

v.82.5 (2026-06-07)

  • Scatter “color by tissue/subtype” — expanded the palette from 20 to 40 distinct colors and made it cycle instead of dumping the overflow into gray, so far fewer categories collapse to the same look.
  • Cell Line Browser hotspot filter now uses the same multi-line dropdown (gene + live n= mutated count) as the Fusion and CN filters — the native list that Safari truncated is gone. The Oncoprint button stays.
  • When you pick a gene in a hotspot or fusion filter (1. Set Parameters), the level now defaults to Only mutated instead of All cells.
  • Cell Line Browser help (“?”) updated — now documents the CN filter and the Ploidy / Aneuploidy / CIN / Copy-number / Drug-response (PRISM AUC) sorts.

v.82.4 (2026-06-07)

  • Cell-line executive summary — a plain-language overview (what cancer it is, the patient it came from, and standout molecular features: driver fusions, hotspot variants, functional losses, MSI, ploidy) now appears as the cell-line hover popout on every plot, and at the top of the Cell Line Browser card by default.
  • Just-labeled scatter dots are now reliably hoverable — the draggable name label defaulted too close to its dot and was intercepting the hover; it now sits clear, and the marker is a touch larger.
  • Cell Line Browser card — the Immunology section now sits after Fusions (it’s one signal among many, not a headline).
  • Removed Synonym/Ortholog Lookup as a standalone analysis mode (kept in code). The synonym matching itself is unchanged — the “Find Synonyms” helper still recovers aliases for genes not found in the dataset.

v.82.3 (2026-06-07)

  • Fusion filter (1. Set Parameters) now uses the curated/validated driver fusions (high+medium tier, 23 named fusions like BCR-ABL1, EWSR1-FLI1, EML4-ALK) instead of the raw ~9,500-gene DepMap fusion matrix — matching the curated set used by the Fusion analysis axis and the Cell Line Browser. The level filter is now simply WT vs has-fusion (curated calls are present/absent).

v.82.2 (2026-06-07)

  • Stable homepage layout — the main two-column layout (Reference data / 1&2 on the left, 3. Results on the right) now stays put at every browser zoom level instead of stacking Results underneath when you zoom in. It shrinks gracefully rather than reflowing.
  • Network sliders — removed the redundant min/max numbers (e.g. the 10 and 40 on Font Size) above the −/+ buttons; the tick scale below already shows the range. The current-value badge stays.

v.82.1 (2026-06-07)

  • Deep link — the cell-line-browser URL hash now also accepts the plural / spelled-out forms (#cells, #cellbrowser, #cell-line-browser, #browser), not just #cell. Note it’s a URL hash (e.g. …/#cells), not a path (/cells) — a path won’t work on a static host.

v.82.0 (2026-06-07)

  • Cell Line Browser — new Show Selected button in the selection group. Toggles the list down to just the cell lines you’ve ticked (click again, now labeled Show All, to restore the full list). Turns itself off if you Deselect All or Reset.

v.81.99 (2026-06-07)

  • Cell-line hover — now a single popout. The plot’s built-in hover label (name / tissue / x·y) is suppressed so only the summary card shows, with no duplicated text. The card also appears faster, and a just-clicked / labeled (orange) dot is now hoverable too — both in the correlation scatter and the gene-effect graphs.
  • Cell Line Browser — the list now fills column by column: read straight down the first column (top→bottom) in sort order, then continue at the top of the next column, instead of left-to-right across rows.

v.81.98 (2026-06-07)

  • Network drag fix — once the hover info-box appeared, trying to drag a node would instead start selecting the legend text below the graph. The hover box now ignores the mouse (it’s purely informational), so a click-drag always grabs the node underneath. Pinned boxes (Shift) stay clickable for their links.
  • Network loading indicator — building a large graph (e.g. after a low correlation cutoff pulls in many genes) now shows a spinner with a progress percentage over the canvas, so it’s clear the layout is working rather than frozen.

v.81.97 (2026-06-07)

  • Cell-line hover summary — hovering a cell-line dot in the scatter / gene-effect plots now shows a small summary card (the same identity block from the top of that line’s Wiki: name, tissue · disease · subtype, age / sex / primary-vs-metastatic, and the ACH & RRID ids). Appears after a brief pause and doesn’t block clicking the dot underneath.

v.81.96 (2026-06-07)

  • Network hover — cleaned up the two boxes. The small box (gene + mean gene effect / SD) appears quickly as before; the extended gene-info box (name / description / links) is now delayed (~1s) and no longer repeats the gene-effect data — previously a condensed copy popped up immediately and duplicated the GE line. Shift still pins the info box for clicking links.

v.81.94 (2026-06-07)

  • Network hover — refined the two-stage tooltip. The compact gene-effect popout now appears almost immediately (~0.15s), and the extended gene-info box follows ~1s later and no longer repeats the gene-effect line (it only adds the name / description / links), so the two don’t overlap.

v.81.93 (2026-06-07)

  • Network — the Font / Node / Edge Width sliders now have − / + step buttons too.
  • Correlation Analysis — the plot now shows the same thing as the table (correlation), not gene effect. The By-Hotspot plot was drawing box plots of gene1’s gene effect (x-axis “… Gene Effect”) while the table reported the WT-vs-mutated correlation — two different metrics. It’s now a dumbbell plot of WT (blue) vs mutated (red) correlation per gene, and the By-Tissue plot is a lollipop of correlation per tissue, both on a “Correlation (r)” axis matching the table. The per-cell scatter for any one group is still available by clicking its table row. Also bumped the y-axis gene/tissue labels from ~8–9 px to 12–13 px so they’re legible.

v.81.92 (2026-06-07)

  • Network — hover tooltip is now two-stage so it stops getting in the way while you drag nodes: a compact mean gene-effect readout appears quickly (~0.25s), and the fuller gene info (name + description + links) only follows after ~1.2s. Queued tooltips are canceled the moment you start dragging.
  • Network — removed the Show Hidden button (redundant: removed nodes already appear in a “Removed” list where you can click any one to restore it, or use Restore All) and the Layout button (the alternative layouts weren’t useful).

v.81.91 (2026-06-07)

  • Network — new Reset button (next to Aa) that restores all the appearance controls above the network to defaults in one click: font / node / edge size sliders, the Aa text settings (font family, label & node color, legend & banner size/color), the node-border toggle, and the GE / stats label & color options. Re-renders the network with the restored settings.

v.81.90 (2026-06-07)

  • Set parameters — Correlation Cutoff and Min Slope sliders now have − / + step buttons on either side (matching the Min Cell Lines control), so you can nudge them by one step without dragging.

v.81.89 (2026-06-07)

  • “Test Genes w/ Stats” now writes the example data into the With-Stats input box (tab-separated Gene/LFC/FDR) instead of loading it silently — so you can see and edit it. It then loads it through the normal manual-stats parser.

v.81.88 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Browser — the selection count is now filter-aware. It still reports the full selection (which Inspect / Export act on), but when a filter hides some of the selected lines it shows how many are currently in view, e.g. “1186 selected · 126 in view”. Refreshes whenever the list re-renders.

v.81.87 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Browser — the list now shows a live count at the top (e.g. “126 cell lines of 1186”) that updates as you change tissue / quick filters / any other filter.

v.81.86 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Browser — the Quick filters list now scales to the other active filters. Each quick filter's count is computed against the cell lines passing the current tissue / subtype / sex / mutation / CN filters (and the other active quick filters), and filters that match zero lines in that context are hidden. So with a Lung tissue filter on, leukaemia/sarcoma fusions like BCR-ABL1 and EWSR1-FLI1 drop out of the list while KRAS- and EGFR-mutant stay (38 → 27 quick filters in that example). The filter you've already selected is never hidden.

v.81.85 (2026-06-06)

  • Mutational analysis — the Fusion and Functional loss gene pickers are now proper dropdown menus (like the Hotspot one) instead of search boxes, and their Tissues button now works — opening the linked tissue breakdown that ranks tissues by how many of the selected fusion/loss cell lines fall in each (the fusion button was previously broken because it checked the old gene-keyed data).
  • Clicking a cell-line dot from inside a chart modal (gene-effect, inspect, correlation-analysis) now opens the Cell Line Browser in front instead of behind it. Raised the browser (and its child wiki / info / quick-filters / selection modals) above the analysis modals in the z-order.

v.81.84 (2026-06-06)

  • Gene-effect distribution plot — cleaned up for the Functional-loss and Fusion axes (which are binary). (1) The stratifier control above the plot now reads “Functional loss (Y)” / “Fusion (Y)” instead of always “Hotspot mutation (Y)”, and its option counts say “lost” / “fused” instead of “mut”. (2) The y-axis now shows just two rows — Intact / Lost (or No fusion / Fusion+) — instead of an empty “2” level. (3) The header no longer repeats the lineage when the inspect tissue filter restates it, and the reference (WT/Intact) and mutant (Lost/Fused) stats are now on separate lines so it doesn’t crowd or wrap.

v.81.83 (2026-06-06)

  • Mutational analysis — the Fusion axis now picks a specific fusion, not a gene. The axis is relabeled simply “Fusion” and the selector lists the named driver fusions themselves (BCR-ABL1, EWSR1-FLI1, EML4-ALK, PAX3-FOXO1, … — 23 in total), splitting cell lines into carriers vs non-carriers of that exact fusion. Previously it listed the individual participating genes (ABL1, BCR, …).
  • Click a cell-line dot to open it in the Cell Line Browser. On the read-only plots (gene-effect distribution / by-tissue / by-hotspot, correlation-analysis tissue & hotspot, expression-correlate) a plain click on a point now opens that cell line — previously it required Shift-click, which wasn’t discoverable. The main correlation scatter keeps its existing behavior (plain click toggles the inspect selection; Shift-click opens the browser).

v.81.82 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Wiki — spot-checked the data against two more lines beyond A549: K562 (Myeloid / CML, BCR-ABL1+) and HCT116 (MSI-high colorectal). Both render correctly — K562 shows the BCR-ABL1 fusion, female/XIST sex call, and IMATINIB as top sensitive drug (−5.4σ); HCT116 shows MSI-high (score 89, mismatch-repair deficient, hypermutated), KRAS p.G13 + PIK3CA p.H1047 hotspots, male/Y-marker sex call. One small display fix from this pass: collection-site values stored with underscores (e.g. “large_intestine”) now render as “Large Intestine”.

v.81.81 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Wiki data audit — sections 1–4. Cancer classification, Sex (annotation vs expression) and Genome signatures verified correct (right source fields, thresholds consistent with the rest of the app). Fixed three issues in Patient & sample origin: patient age showed as a float (“58.0” → “58”); the row labeled “Tumor stage (at sampling)” was actually the primaryOrMetastasis field, so it’s relabeled “Primary vs metastatic”; and free-text fields stored lowercase (ancestry, collection site) are now capitalized for display.

v.81.80 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Wiki — visual refresh (step 1 of an ongoing pass). Each section is now a clean white card on a light-gray backdrop, with a slim header bar (green dot + uppercase title) and a muted source footer; the executive summary and label/value rows were aligned to match. Applied consistently across all 13 sections via the shared section()/row() helpers. Data-heavy sections (genome-signature histograms, drug-response plots) render correctly inside the cards. A field-by-field data-correctness pass follows.

v.81.79 (2026-06-06)

  • App-wide GE-vs-Expression wording sweep. Audited the rest of the app (correlation scatter, find-correlates, expression-correlate scatter, compare modals, Cell Line Browser) — almost everything already labels axes dynamically from each axis’s data type. Found and fixed one bug: the scatter CSV export hardcoded the column headers as Gene1_Effect,Gene2_Effect regardless of axis type, so a Gene-Effect-vs-Expression scatter exported both columns as “Effect”. The headers now reflect each axis (_Effect / _Expression / _GrowthRate / _GeneSetScore).

v.81.78 (2026-06-06)

  • Gene Effect modal — By-Hotspot view in Expression mode: verified the plot title (“… Expression by Hotspot Mutation”), x-axis label and results-table columns all read “Expression”/“Expr” via headless-browser screenshot. Also fixed the remaining caution banner, which still said “Observed differences in gene effect may reflect cancer type” — now neutral (“Observed differences may reflect cancer type”) so it reads correctly in both Gene Effect and Expression modes.

v.81.77 (2026-06-06)

  • Gene-effect distribution plot — y-axis label no longer overlaps the tick labels at narrow widths. Same root cause as the title fix: canvas.measureText underestimated the tick-label width, so too little left margin was reserved and the rotated “… Functional Loss” label sat on top of the row labels. Added the 1.25× safety factor to the tick measurement.
  • Correlation scatter — pairing Gene Effect with Expression now defaults to the same gene on both axes. When you switch one axis to Expression (or GE) so the two axes use different data types, the empty axis’s gene is auto-filled from the other axis — so “GENE gene-effect vs GENE expression” works in one step.
  • Gene Effect modal — correct wording in Expression mode. When the data-type toggle is set to Expression, the modal title, the “Mean” summary label, the By-Tissue and By-Hotspot plot titles/axis labels, the results-table headers, and the CSV export headers now say “Expression” instead of “Gene Effect”/“GE”. The hotspot-mutation-filter tooltip is now neutral (“Stratify the plotted values (gene effect or expression) …”). Verified via headless-browser screenshots.

v.81.76 (2026-06-06)

  • Gene-effect distribution plot — follow-up to the title/subtitle wrap fix. At narrower window widths the text still clipped because canvas.measureText (Arial fallback) underestimates the width Plotly actually renders (Open Sans), so a line measured as “fits” still overflowed. Added a 1.25× safety factor to the measurement so wrapping happens slightly early. Verified clean at both wide and narrow widths via headless-browser screenshot.

v.81.75 (2026-06-06)

  • Gene-effect distribution plot — fixed the title and stats subtitle being cropped on the left/right. The title/subtitle are centered on the plot area, which is offset to the right by the wide left margin reserved for the rotated y-axis label, so long text (e.g. “ZRSR2 Gene Effect by RB1 Functional Loss” and the “WT: n=… · Mut: n=…” stats line) overflowed the right edge and was clipped. The title now wraps to the actual drawable width, and the subtitle — which was previously never wrapped — now wraps too. Also fixed the functional-loss row label that still read “1 Damaging” (now “1 Lost”).

v.81.74 (2026-06-06)

  • Cell Line Browser — “Collections” renamed to “Quick filters” and trimmed from ~100 down to 54. The list had grown unwieldy and esoteric — ~33 single-gene copy-number amp/del filters (AR amp, BCL2 amp, MITF amp, BAP1 del, …), 9 pathway-expression signatures (E2F active, TGF-β active, …), rare-TSG losses (SMAD4/STK11/VHL), Lehmann TNBC sub-subtypes, and genetic-only MSI. We now surface only the quick filters that are genuinely useful to at least some users: driver mutations (KRAS/BRAF/EGFR/PIK3CA/IDH/CTNNB1), common tumor-suppressor functional losses (TP53/PTEN/RB1/CDKN2A/APC/NF1 + any/multi), MSI-high / HR-deficient / hypermutated / POLE / SLFN11-high, breast receptor subtypes, disease-defining fusions, oncogene-addiction sets, WGD / high-aneuploidy, NE / EMT, PD-L1-high / likely-immunogenic, the key focal CN events (MYC/ERBB2/MDM2/CDK amps; CDKN2A/RB1/PTEN deletions), and patient-age groups. The full definitions are preserved in the catalog, so any hidden filter can be re-enabled by adding its id to a single allow-list.

v.81.73 (2026-06-06)

  • Mutational analysis — the Fusion and Damaging axes now use validated data, cutting the noise. The old “Translocation/Fusion” axis counted every raw DepMap fusion call (mostly passengers/read-through artifacts); it is now “Fusion (validated)” — the curated driver fusions shown in the Cell Line Browser’s “Clinically relevant fusions” section (BCR-ABL1, EWSR1-FLI1, EML4-ALK, PAX3-FOXO1, …), validated per cell line by tissue match + partner expression + partner CRISPR dependency, kept at high+medium confidence (36 participating genes). The old “Damaging Mutation” axis (DepMap’s 8,926-gene predicted-LoF matrix, full of passengers like TTN/MUC19) is replaced by “Functional loss” — the 8 tumor suppressors from the Cell Line Browser’s “Functional loss” section (APC, CDKN2A, MTAP, NF1, PTEN, RB1, TP53, VHL), DepMap’s integrated CN+mutation+expression call that also catches deletion-driven losses the mutation matrix misses. Built by scripts/build_validated_fusions.py and scripts/build_functional_loss.py. The Cell Line Browser, Wiki, antigen-presentation and HR-deficiency views still use the full raw damaging/fusion data; the optional additional mutation/fusion sub-filters in the analysis also still use the raw sets.

v.81.72 (2026-06-06)

  • Scatter plots — Shift-click any cell-line dot to open it in the Cell Line Browser. Works across the main correlation scatter (including the 3-panel WT/mutant view), the expression-correlate scatter, the gene-effect distribution box plots (tissue, hotspot and tissue-comparison views), and the correlation-analysis tissue/hotspot scatters — the same destination you already get by clicking a point in the browser’s UMAP. A plain click keeps its existing behavior (e.g. toggling a line into the inspect panel on the main scatter); only Shift-click navigates.

v.81.71 (2026-05-17)

  • CN matrix — drop the WGS-vs-WES per-line provenance tag. The values themselves come uniformly from DepMap OmicsCNGene.csv (24Q4 release), which is already a per-line hybrid by DepMap’s own construction. The earlier “WGS” / “WES” pill was set by looking up each line in the newer OmicsCNGeneWGS 25Q3 file — one release ahead of the values — which created false precision (a line whose 24Q4 value was still WES-derived could be flagged as WGS because DepMap had WGS’d it since). Cleaner story: one source, one sentence. Affects both Correlate V2 (small italic “wes” tag on CN sort-value pills removed) and Green Listed (per-column WGS / WES badges in the CN results table removed).

v.81.70 (2026-05-17)

  • CN matrix — gene list now cross-referenced against the greenlisted human CRISPR libraries (Brunello, Gattinara, GeCKO v2, Jacquere, VBC, MinLibCas9, TKOv3, Yusa v1), expanded through the human synonym table so an alias hit counts. Anything not reachable by any sgRNA in any of those libraries is dropped — in practice this removes residual pseudogenes (MARK2P17, NPM1P28, ...), Ig/TR gene segments (IGHJ2, TRBC1), MTND* mitochondrial pseudogenes, RN7SL / RNA5SP / SNRPEP small-RNA pseudogenes, and obscure LINC entries with no library coverage. Real genes including all the previously-recovered ones (TP53, TP63, TP73, USP1, USP7, BMP1–BMP7, AKAP1–AKAP12, CASP3, MARK2 etc.) are kept. Gene count 32 174 → 20 794 (close to the realistic ~20 k protein-coding count), binary 92 → 59 MB.

v.81.69 (2026-05-17)

  • CN matrix — bug fix: TP53 was missing. Cause: an over-broad pseudogene regex (P\d+$) that was meant to drop ribosomal pseudogenes like RPL32P26 / RPS12P2 also matched any gene symbol ending with P + digits: TP53, TP63, TP73, USP1–USP54, BMP1–BMP15, AKAP1–AKAP14, GAPDHP* etc. Replaced with narrow patterns anchored to specific known pseudogene prefixes (RPL, RPS, HNRNP, HBA / HBB, EEF1, TUBB, GAPDH). Gene count 24 567 → 32 174 (recovered 7 607 real genes). Binary 70 → 92 MB.

v.81.68 (2026-05-17)

  • CN matrix — widened gene coverage. Filter relaxed from “WGS-set only” to “all parseable symbols minus noise patterns”. Drops obvious clutter (LOC IDs, RNU / SNORA / SNORD small nuclear RNAs, antisense / divergent-transcript suffixes, pseudogenes ending in P + digits) but keeps protein-coding + named lncRNAs + miRNA hosts + olfactory receptors + Ig/TCR segments. Gene count 18 660 → 24 567. Binary 53 → 70 MB.
  • New CN-based collections (20). Per-gene focal-amplification filters added for AR, BCL2, EGFR, KIT, KRAS, MITF, PDGFRA, SOX2. New “Focal deletions” category with per-gene filters for CDKN2A, CDKN2B, RB1, PTEN, BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, ARID1A, SMARCA4, STK11, KEAP1, BAP1 plus an “Any focal deletion” catch-all. Each collection filters lines with the gene at amp tier (CN ≥ 3) or deletion tier (CN ≤ 0.5) on the curated panel. Distinct from the integrated TSG functional-loss collections (which combine CN + mutation + expression); these are CN-only deep deletions.

v.81.67 (2026-05-17)

  • CN matrix upgraded to hybrid WGS-primary / WES-fallback. Source: DepMap OmicsCNGene.csv (24Q4) — DepMap’s own merged file that combines WGS and WES inferences. Cell-line coverage jumps from 1095 (WGS-only) to 1929 (WGS + WES). Lines that were never WGS’d — Jurkat, K562, many older hematopoietic lines — now appear in the CN sort. Per-line provenance preserved: lines also in OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv (25Q3) are tagged WGS; lines absent get a small wes caveat next to the CN tier pill, hover for the explanation. Binary blob grew from 32 → 55 MB to accommodate the extra ~834 cell lines.

v.81.66 (2026-05-16)

  • URL-hash deep link — loading the app with #cell (or #cellbrowser) in the URL opens the cell-line browser modal automatically. So correlate.cmm.se/#cell jumps straight to the browser, useful for linking from sibling apps (Greenlisted, MouseCLB, lab pages). Also responds to in-app hash changes via hashchange.

v.81.65 (2026-05-13)

  • CN values in the cell-line list now show a biological tier label instead of just a 2-decimal number. Tiers: deep del < 0.3, het loss 0.3–0.7, WT 0.7–1.3, low gain 1.3–2.0, gain 2.0–3.0, amp 3.0–5.0, strong amp ≥ 5.0. Each tier carries its own colored pill (red for losses, gray for WT, blue for gains, darker / saturated blue for amp / strong amp). The raw number is kept as a small de-emphasised suffix and in the tooltip for anyone who wants the underlying value. Previously the raw “1.48” / “1.77” type values read as sequencing noise rather than biology — this maps each line to a discrete biological category. Caption row updated to list the tier cutoffs.

v.81.64 (2026-05-13)

  • Fix — CLB list caption (“Values shown: ...”) now spans the full width of the row-major grid instead of occupying the first cell. Previously it consumed grid position 1, pushing the first cell line into position 2 of the top row. Caption updated to reflect matrix-vs-panel scope dynamically (full DepMap matrix when loaded, curated panel only otherwise).

v.81.63 (2026-05-13)

  • CN sort opened to any gene. The full DepMap OmicsCNGeneWGS matrix (19366 genes × 1095 cell lines) is now processed into web_data/cn.bin.gz (32 MB) with the same gene-major int16 + scaleFactor encoding as geneEffects.bin.gz. App lazy-loads the matrix on first CN-sort use; the curated-panel data still serves as the pre-load fallback so MYC / ERBB2 / CDKN2A / etc. work instantly while the matrix is downloading. Picker now lists the curated panel at the top (with event counts) and any matrix gene below by substring match — pick any gene for CRISPR-targeting reference (high CN often means more guides needed for biallelic knockout).

v.81.62 (2026-05-13)

  • Drug-response colors aligned between the cell-line list and the sort-drug dropdown. The list previously used AUC < 0.6 = green (anything that “kills many cells”), so a row with AUC = 0.5 showed green even though the dropdown counted it as “partly sensitive” (amber). Now both use the same thresholds: green = very-sensitive (AUC < 0.3), amber = partly-sensitive (0.3 – 0.6), light gray = modest, very light gray = little effect.
  • Broadly-cytotoxic flag in the drug-sort dropdown. Compounds where ≥ 40 % of the cohort scores very-sensitive get a broadly cytotoxic % badge. Romidepsin (HDAC1/2) is very-sensitive in 304 / 386 (79 %) lines, Gemcitabine (dNTP depletion) in 274 / 389 (70 %) — broadly toxic chemotherapy signatures, not targeted-therapy candidates. Sort order now puts targeted hits (Trametinib / Dasatinib / Dabrafenib etc.) above broadly-cytotoxic ones with the same raw v-count, so the top of the dropdown surfaces actually selective therapies first. Header copy updated to explain the threshold.

v.81.61 (2026-05-13)

  • Wiki drug-response section now shows a per-compound AUC histogram, mirroring the genome-section pattern. Each “Standout sensitive” and “Standout resistant” row gets a thin Plotly histogram of the AUC distribution across all PRISM-tested cell lines (gray bars), with a red dashed line at this cell line’s AUC. Lets you see at a glance whether a low AUC is part of a long tail (broad killer) or genuinely isolated (selective hit), the same way the Ploidy / Aneuploidy / CIN histograms work.

v.81.60 (2026-05-13)

  • New sort option: “Sort: Copy number of gene”. Pick a gene from the curated cancer-relevant CN panel (33 amp + 14 del genes from clinical_cn.json — MYC, ERBB2, CDK4, MDM2, EGFR, CDKN2A, BRCA1/2, etc.) and the cell-line list sorts by that gene’s copy number. Picker shows per-gene event counts (e.g. “MYC amp — 87 lines”) so you can see at a glance which genes have the most flagged lines. Per-row CN value is colored blue for amplification (CN ≥ 3) and red for deletion (CN ≤ 0.5). Lines without a significant CN event for the selected gene show “—” at the end of the list. Scope note: the curated panel covers ~47 clinically actionable cancer genes; sorting by arbitrary genes (any of the 25 k in the genome) would need processing the full DepMap OmicsCNGene matrix into a binary blob like geneEffects.bin.gz — queued as a future addition.

v.81.59 (2026-05-13)

  • CLB detail card — Immunology section restyle. The previous layout placed the badge (“MSI-high” / “Class-I lost”) and the explanation sentence in an inline flex row, squeezing the sentence into whatever horizontal space was left next to the badge — awkward in the 280 px detail pane. The two now stack vertically (badge above, sentence below), matching the layout of the other sections (Hotspot Mutations, Functional loss, Genome) and giving the caption full width to wrap naturally. Section header gained a flag count and a ? help icon explaining that these are cell-intrinsic inferences (what a CD8+ T cell could see if it got there), not tumor-microenvironment readouts — most human cancer cell lines can only be grown in immunocompromised hosts in vivo.

v.81.58 (2026-05-13)

  • Fix — hovering a functional-loss or focal-CN gene chip in the CLB detail card now shows a single combined tooltip instead of two overlapping popups. The chips previously had both a custom gene tooltip (NCBI summary) and a native browser title attribute (why the gene is highlighted); the browser tooltip overlay would partially cover the custom one. Now the “why this gene is flagged” line is rendered inside the custom tooltip as a red-bordered context block above the gene info.

v.81.57 (2026-05-13)

  • Wiki “Strong drug-target candidates” now requires PRISM corroboration before naming a drug class. Previously a collection-based call (e.g. A375 flagged as CDK4/6-dependent from CDKN2A loss + CRISPR signal) was added unconditionally, so the summary could claim “CDK4/6 inhibitors” while the drug-response section below showed no CDK4/6 inhibitor in the top-sensitive list. Now, for any drug class PRISM tested (CDK4/6, MEK, BRAF, EGFR, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, ABL), the claim is emitted only if at least one matching compound is sensitive (z < −1σ) in this cell line. Classes PRISM doesn’t test at all (e.g. KRAS-G12C inhibitors) are still emitted so legitimate biology isn’t suppressed.
  • “Useful as a model for” softened to “May be useful as a model for”. The inference is built from mutation + dependency layers without prospective validation; the modal verb is more honest about the claim.
  • “Context-aware cross-checks” renamed to “Targeted therapies matched to this cell line’s alterations” and given a one-line explanation: “For each driver alteration detected in this cell line, the PRISM compounds with a matching target are listed below, sorted by sensitivity in this line (most-sensitive first).” Previously the section header gave no hint of what cross-check meant.

v.81.56 (2026-05-13)

  • CLB list flow changed from CSS multi-column (column-major fill) to CSS grid (row-major fill). The list now reads left-to-right then wraps to the next row, so when sorted descending the highest value is in the upper-left and the actual lowest sits at the bottom-right end of the list. Previously the bottom of column 1 was a mid-range value, which made “the lowest is not at the end” a real visual gotcha.
  • Lines that don’t have a value for the current sort axis (GE / Expr / drug / hotspot count / etc.) now show a dim “—” in the value column instead of being blank, so the cluster of no-data lines at the end of the list is visually distinct from data-having lines that just happen to have small values.
  • Drug-response wiki cohort counts now use the GE-cohort intersection (same basis as the sort-drug dropdown), so the two parts of the app show matching numbers. Previously the wiki counted all PRISM keys (e.g. Romidepsin 370 V / 78 P of 461) while the dropdown counted GE-cohort overlap (304 V / 71 P of 386); both numbers were technically correct but the discrepancy was confusing.

v.81.55 (2026-05-12)

  • Drug-response dropdown now refreshes its per-compound very-/partly-sensitive counts when the visible cell-line subset changes. Previously, toggling a collection (e.g. excluding TP53 functional loss) updated the list of cell lines but the open dropdown kept showing counts from the previous subset — so the numbers next to each drug didn’t add up to what was actually shown. The dropdown was already scoring against _clbVisibleCellLines; it just wasn’t re-rendered on filter change. Now renderCellLineList() triggers a re-render of the open drug dropdown.

v.81.54 (2026-05-12)

  • Sort input now clears when the sort basis changes. Previously a gene name left in the box from “Sort: Expression” would carry over to “Sort: Drug response” (and vice versa), where it would either match nothing or be mistaken for the other kind of token. The suggestion dropdown is also closed on the switch.

v.81.53 (2026-05-12)

  • Fix — audit pass on the GE-vs-expression index mismatch from v.81.52. Same root cause was reaching three more places: (1) showGeneEffectByTissue — the main per-tissue expression boxplot was reading expressionData[gi * nCellLines_GE + i] and pairing the result with metadata.cellLines[i]; with GE = 1186 and Expr = 1699 lines in different orders, that often straddled into a neighbouring gene’s row. (2) CSV export — the Expr_GENE columns were resolved through the GE index map. (3) _computeCollectionMemberships — the NE, EMT, and expression-based TNBC / HR+ / HER2+ breast subtype calls were using the GE stride against expressionData, so the cohort scoring was reading the wrong lines’ values. All three now resolve each cell line through expressionMetadata.cellLines with nExprCL stride. Also fixed: mem.tnbc = new Set() in the breast block was wiping the v.81.46 Lehmann-annotated belt-and-braces adds — now preserved.

v.81.52 (2026-05-12)

  • Fix — inline Expr value next to a cell line in the list was reading from the wrong slot when sorting by expression. The GE matrix and the expression matrix have different cell-line orderings (and may have different cohort sizes), but renderCellLineList() was using the GE index map and GE nCellLines for the expressionData[gi * nCL + ci] lookup regardless of mode. Result: the value displayed for a given line was actually some other line’s expression. The PD-L1-high collection itself was correct (it already used the expression matrix indices), so the discrepancy showed up as SNU423 — correctly flagged as PD-L1-high — appearing with the inline value of a low-CD274 line. Now uses expressionMetadata.cellLines / nCellLines when sorting by expression.

v.81.51 (2026-05-12)

  • Fix — gene autocomplete suggestions flashed and disappeared in GE / Expression sort mode before the user could click them. updateSortControls() (debounced 200 ms after each keystroke) was hiding the suggestion dropdown for any non-drug mode, but the dropdown is now also used for the gene autocomplete from v.81.47. Now keeps the dropdown visible for any sort mode that uses it (drug, GE, expression).

v.81.50 (2026-05-12)

  • Fix — pressing Reset and then picking “Sort: Drug response” (or GE / Expression) didn’t show the input box. Cause: the reset handler still set display:none on the inner clbSortGene input from before v.81.35, but the input is now inside a clbSortGeneWrap wrapper. When the user later switched modes, the wrapper became visible but the input was still stuck on display:none and stayed invisible. Fix: reset now hides the wrapper, not the input; clears any stale inline display on the input itself; and dismisses the drug-picker dropdown for good measure.

v.81.49 (2026-05-12)

  • Collections — the “?” inclusion-criteria modal now matches the live panel. (1) Same order and category-note explainers as the panel (CATEGORY_ORDER and CATEGORY_NOTES factored in), so both surfaces read as one document. Previously the modal followed catalog insertion order which was arbitrary. (2) Section headers re-styled to the same green-accent banner (14 px, 2 px green underline) used by the panel and the Wiki, so visual hierarchy is consistent everywhere. (3) Inclusion-source badge on every entry — a small uppercase pill (MUTATION, EXPRESSION, CN AMP, FUSION, MSISENSOR2 SCORE, LEHMANN PUBLICATION, INTEGRATED LOF, etc.) tells the user at a glance which DepMap data layer or publication panel each collection was built from. Intro paragraph explains the badge. (4) TNBC dual-inclusion rule documented. The Triple-negative breast (approximate) description now explicitly states both inclusion paths: (a) expression-based receptor-status surrogate (ESR1 / PGR below breast median + ERBB2 not in top 20 %), OR (b) the line carries a Lehmann TNBC subtype annotation. The (a)+(b) union guarantees Lehmann ⊆ TNBC by construction — the earlier discrepancy where the sub-types appeared to contain more lines than their parent set is resolved and explained.

v.81.48 (2026-05-12)

  • Collections panel — category headlines made larger and clearer. Bumped from 10 px to 13 px, weight 600 → 700, and the bottom rule changed from a faint 1 px gray hairline to a 2 px green accent so the major sections of the collection panel separate visually at a glance. More top margin (16 px) and a touch of padding give each section room to breathe. Italic category-note line under each header bumped from 10 px to 11 px to match.

v.81.47 (2026-05-12)

  • Two fixes prompted by user inspection of the PD-L1 high collection. (1) PD-L1 (CD274) threshold corrected. Previous z > +1.0 cutoff picked up lines with absolute log2(TPM+1) of 0.4–4.4 because CD274 has a strongly-left-skewed cohort distribution (most cell lines barely express PD-L1 at all). A z above the mean caught lines that are still essentially silent in absolute terms. Now requires BOTH top-quintile absolute expression AND log2(TPM+1) ≥ 3 (≈ TPM > 7, the “clearly expressed” floor used elsewhere in the app for lineage markers). Description updated to spell out the dual-threshold rationale. (2) Gene-symbol autocomplete on the sort input. When the user picks Sort: GE for gene(s) or Sort: Expression of gene(s) and focuses the gene-name input, a suggestion dropdown now opens (same UX as the drug-response dropdown). Typing “CD27” surfaces CD27, CD274, CD276, etc.; cancer-pathway-panel genes float to the top of the suggestion list (marked with a green dot) so the relevant matches show first. Exact prefix matches outrank middle-substring matches. Click a suggestion to fill the input and trigger the sort; outside-click closes the dropdown.

v.81.46 (2026-05-12)

  • Two data-integrity fixes that the user flagged in the collections panel. (1) TNBC consistency. Every cell line with a Lehmann TNBC annotation IS TNBC by the source papers’ definition, but the existing Triple-negative breast collection used expression-based criteria (ESR1 below breast median + PGR below breast median + ERBB2 not in top 20 %) that sometimes missed Lehmann-annotated lines, producing the impossible situation where the Lehmann sub-types appeared to contain more lines than their parent TNBC collection. Now: any line with a Lehmann tnbcType4 / tnbcType6 annotation is also added to the tnbc set, so Lehmann ⊆ TNBC by construction. Runs unconditionally (not gated on expression load). (2) MMR-deficient vs MSI-high. The card’s “MSI-high” badge uses DepMap’s MSIsensor2 readout (functional MSI), while the existing MMR-deficient (likely MSI-high) collection used “any damaging mutation in MLH1 / MSH2 / MSH6 / PMS2 / EPCAM” (genetic signal). These overlap but aren’t identical — sporadic MMR-deficiency by MLH1 promoter hypermethylation is invisible to the mutation matrix, and heterozygous mutations don’t always abolish MMR. So the existing collection includes MSS lines and misses methylation-driven MSI-high lines. Fix: renamed the old collection to “MMR-mutated (Lynch-panel damaging mutation)” to make the signal honest, and added a separate “MSI-high (functional; MSIsensor2 ≥ 20)” collection that matches the card badge. Descriptions on both spell out the overlap-but-not-identical relationship.

v.81.45 (2026-05-12)

  • Collections — substantive reorganisation and expansion to match how cancer doctors and researchers actually talk. (1) Renamed and expanded “Oncogene hotspot mutations (mutation only)” → “Driver oncogene mutations”. The old name was opaque and the category had only 2 entries. Now contains KRAS-mut, BRAF-mut, EGFR-mut, PIK3CA-mut (the canonical four every oncologist asks about) plus the pre-existing CTNNB1 and IDH entries. Category note clarifies it’s mutation-only and points at the stricter “Oncogene addiction” for the CRISPR-confirmed subset. (2) Consolidated four singleton DNA-repair categories + Mutation burden into one “DNA repair / damage response” category containing MMR-deficient, HR-deficient/BRCAness, POLE/POLD1 ultramutated, ATM-deficient, and Hypermutated. Previously these were five separate categories with one entry each, which made the panel feel over-segmented.
