(3) Three new focal-amp collections: MET amp (NSCLC actionable; capmatinib / tepotinib), FGFR1 / FGFR2 / FGFR3 amp (urothelial, gastric, breast, lung-SCC; erdafitinib / pemigatinib / futibatinib), CCNE1 amp alone (pulled out from the G1/S bundle — CCNE1 is a CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance background and a CDK2 / WEE1 / PKMYT1-responder background). (4) Four new disease-defining fusions: SS18-SSX1/2+ (synovial sarcoma), PAX3-FOXO1+ (alveolar RMS), TMPRSS2-ERG+ (prostate), NPM1-ALK+ (ALCL). (5) New immunology collection: PD-L1 (CD274) high expression (z > +1 vs cohort) — canonical clinical checkpoint-immunotherapy biomarker. Description spells out the IHC-vs-mRNA caveat and the cell-intrinsic IFN-pathway cross-link.

v.81.44 (2026-05-12)

  • Drug list — clinical indication is now explicitly labeled wherever it appears. Previously the cancer-type list (CRC, SCLC, pancreatic, …) trailed the per-compound row as bare italic text after the σ block, with no label, so it read as a random out-of-context label instead of “the diseases this drug is used for”. Now every place a compound is rendered carries an explicit “Used in:” prefix on the indication string: (1) Standout-sensitive / -resistant lists in the Wiki Drug-response section. (2) Context-aware cross-checks block (the same section). (3) The drug-response autocomplete dropdown in the cell-line browser sort — the dropdown rows now split target/MoA on one subtitle line and the clinical indication on its own labeled line, instead of joining all three with middle dots. Drug-response intro paragraph also names every column explicitly so the user knows what to expect before reading any single compound.

v.81.43 (2026-05-12)

  • Collections panel — multi-column layout. Panel max-width bumped from 420 px to min(1100px, calc(100vw - 80px)) and max-height to min(640px, calc(100vh - 160px)), so on a wide monitor it spreads out instead of being a tall narrow scroll. Within each category, entries are laid out in a responsive CSS grid (repeat(auto-fill, minmax(300px, 1fr))) that auto-flows into 2 or 3 columns when there’s room, and collapses to a single column on narrow viewports. Category headers and their italic explainer lines stay full-width so the section structure is still clear. Long collection labels truncate with ellipsis rather than wrapping or pushing the n=count off-screen.

v.81.42 (2026-05-12)

  • Drug-response sort dropdown — compounds are now ranked by potency in the currently-visible cell-line subset, not alphabetically. Two upgrades: (1) Per-compound very-sensitive / partly-sensitive counts are computed against the visible subset (i.e. respecting all active filters — tissue / collection / hotspot / fusion / CN / oncoprint), not the full PRISM cohort. So when the user has filtered down to e.g. paediatric KRAS-mutant pancreatic lines, the counts and ranking reflect that cohort. (2) Sort order: descending very-sensitive count, then descending partly-sensitive count, then alphabetic by name. The most potent drugs for the current selection bubble to the top, instead of being hidden alphabetically among 89 compounds. Each row shows the in-subset summary inline: 17 v · 28 p / 84 means “17 of 84 lines in this selection are very-sensitive, 28 partly-sensitive.” Compounds with zero potency in the subset are dimmed but still clickable. Header strip restates the bucket thresholds and the selection size.

v.81.41 (2026-05-12)

  • New Patient age at diagnosis collection category with five clinical buckets, computed from the numeric age field in the DepMap Model table (not the coarse ageCategory which is just Adult / Pediatric / Unknown / Fetus). Infant (≤ 1 yr) — congenital and very-early-onset cancers (infant ALL, neuroblastoma stage MS). Paediatric (≤ 14 yr) — standard paediatric-oncology definition; enriched for driver fusions, chromatin / polycomb mutations, embryonal histologies. AYA (15–39 yr) — NCI Adolescent & Young Adult bucket; Ewing, osteosarcoma, testicular GCT, T-ALL, Hodgkin lymphoma. Adult (40–64 yr) — the canonical adult-onset solid-tumor bulk (CRC, breast, lung, pancreatic, prostate). Elderly (≥ 65 yr) — MDS / secondary AML / late prostate / GBM-in-elderly; often distinct mutational backgrounds. Sits in a new “Patient demographics” slot between Disease subtypes and Immunology in the collection ordering. Combine with other oncoprint-style filters for queries like “AYA AND EWSR1-FLI1+”, “Paediatric AND TP53-loss”, or “Elderly AND POLE-deficient”.

v.81.40 (2026-05-11)

  • CRISPR dependencies section — explicit fallback message for cell lines with no usable CRISPR data (e.g. 538MGBA). Previously the intro paragraph rendered and then nothing followed (because the z-scored dependency rows produced empty strings), so the user saw a silent void between intro and Source line. Now a red callout reads: “No usable CRISPR gene-effect data for this cell line. The cell line is indexed in the cohort but its CRISPR row contains no measurable values (NaN-only across the matrix), so the z-scored dependency view cannot be built. This happens for a handful of lines per DepMap release — usually those screened too recently to be in this quarter’s CRISPRGeneEffect file, or dropped during QC. Other Wiki sections still show available data for this line.”

v.81.39 (2026-05-11)

  • Drug-response section — each compound now shows cohort-wide sensitivity counts. Below the per-line viability / z-score row, a small gray line spells out: “PRISM cohort: N very-sensitive (AUC < 0.3) · M partly-sensitive (AUC 0.3–0.6) of K tested.” Lets the user tell apart a niche-hit compound that kills only a handful of lines from a broadly active drug that kills hundreds. The cohort counts also appear inline in the context-aware cross-checks section in a compact form. Computed once per compound at first Wiki open and cached on the drug-response object for the session.

v.81.38 (2026-05-11)

  • Executive-summary drug recommendations are now variant-aware. The previous “KRAS-G12C inhibitors (if G12C)” hedge is gone — we already have the specific codon in the inferred-hotspot data, so the summary now names the drug that actually applies. PANC0504 (KRAS G12D, typical pancreatic) will now show “KRAS-G12D-targeting strategies (MRTX1133 investigational; MEK-inhibitor combinations for p.G12D)” rather than a G12C hedge. Variant-aware mappings: KRAS G12C → sotorasib/adagrasib; KRAS G12D → MRTX1133/MEK combos; KRAS G12R → MEK combos only (no allele-specific inhibitor); other KRAS codons → named explicitly. BRAF V600 → vemurafenib/dabrafenib + trametinib; non-V600 BRAF → flagged as vemurafenib-resistant. EGFR T790M → osimertinib (T790M-specific); L858R / exon-19-del → osimertinib first-line + erlotinib/gefitinib alternatives. IDH1 R132 → ivosidenib / vorasidenib (glioma); IDH2 → enasidenib. Both the “Useful as a model for” and the “Strong drug-target candidates” sentences use the same logic.

v.81.37 (2026-05-11)

  • Collections panel categories reordered into a logical research-workflow flow rather than insertion order. New order: (1) Cancer drivers — Disease-defining fusions › Tumor-suppressor functional loss › Focal amplifications › Oncogene hotspot mutations (mutation only) › Oncogene addiction (mutation × CRISPR dependency). Drivers come first because they’re the most common starting point. (2) Disease subtypes — Breast — receptor subtype followed immediately by TNBC molecular subtypes (Lehmann), so the breast-cancer subtype groupings sit together. (3) Phenotype / immune state — Immunology. (4) DNA repair / mutation burden — mismatch repair › homologous recombination › polymerase proofreading › ATM/ATR axis › Mutation burden. (5) Genome state — ploidy / instability (WGD, aneuploidy, LoH). (6) Chromatin / oxidative / pathway — SWI/SNF › NRF2-mutation › Pathway-activity expression signatures › Expression signature (NE / EMT). Category notes (italic gray one-liners under each header) extended to Disease-defining fusions, Oncogene hotspot mutations, and TNBC molecular subtypes so jargon-heavy category names are self-explanatory.

v.81.36 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — POLE / POLD1 ultramutators (e.g. JHUEM7) now get their own flag and a passenger-noise caveat. (1) New flag pill when POLE or POLD1 is damaged AND damaging-mutation count > 200: “POLE / POLD1 proofreading-deficient (ultramutator)”. Tooltip explains: replication errors not corrected → > 100 mut/Mb point-mutation burden, but the genome stays structurally calm (low CIN / aneuploidy / LoH, no WGD, microsatellite stable). Distinct from MMR-deficiency, which is the other major hypermutator route. (2) Passenger-noise caveat on the existing “Very high mutation burden” flag (> 1000 damaging) and “High mutation burden” (> 500): at hypermutator burdens, single damaging mutations in any driver gene panel are statistically likely to be passenger events, so flags like HRD / TP53 should be cross-checked against the integrated functional-loss view rather than taken at face value. (3) Genome signatures intro now states explicitly that the displayed metrics are structural / chromosomal (WGD, aneuploidy, CIN, LoH, MSI) and not point-mutation burden — so a structurally-calm genome at very high TMB (the JHUEM7 picture) reads as a real biological state, not an annotation error.

v.81.35 (2026-05-11)

  • Drug-response sort — proper dropdown panel. The previous native <datalist> approach only revealed compound suggestions when the user typed or clicked the input’s tiny caret, which the user couldn’t see was even there. Replaced with a custom dropdown panel that opens on focus (just click into the input), shows all ~89 PRISM compounds with target / MoA / indication subtitles, and live-filters as the user types. Mirrors the existing CN / fusion-filter dropdown pattern. Clicking an option fills the input and triggers the sort. Outside-click closes the panel.

v.81.34 (2026-05-11)

  • Drug-response sort — PRISM compound autocomplete. The input field for the “Sort: Drug response (PRISM AUC)” mode is now wired to an HTML <datalist> populated from drugResponse.compounds — the user gets a typeahead dropdown of every PRISM compound name (sorted A–Z) with the target / MoA / indication shown as a secondary subtitle. Placeholder updated to “type a PRISM compound (autocomplete)” so the affordance is obvious.
  • Thirteen new collections targeting gaps in the catalog. (1) TNBC molecular subtypes (Lehmann) — four entries (BL1, BL2, M, LAR) for the ~22 TNBC overlap cell lines annotated in lehmannTnbc. Each entry summarizes the panel-defined phenotype (DDR for BL1, growth-factor signaling for BL2, EMT/stem for M, AR signaling for LAR) and predicted therapy. (2) Disease-defining fusions — four entries: BCR-ABL1+ (CML/Ph+ ALL), EWSR1-FLI1+ (Ewing sarcoma), EML4-ALK+ (ALK-rearranged NSCLC), PML-RARA+ (APL). Members are cell lines where the curated clinical-fusion panel calls that specific fusion. (3) Additional DNA-repair contexts. POLE / POLD1 proofreading-deficient (ultramutated; distinct from MMR — usually > 100 mut/Mb and ICB-responsive), ATM-deficient (HRD-adjacent, separate from the BRCA-centric set). (4) Oncogene hotspots not covered by addiction. CTNNB1 hotspot (β-catenin / Wnt activator; mutually exclusive with APC loss), IDH1 / IDH2 hotspot (oncometabolite 2-HG producers; mutant-IDH-inhibitor cohort). (5) Expression-based DDR predictor. SLFN11-high (z > +1) — the single strongest expression-based predictor of platinum / topo-I / PARPi / alkylator response.

v.81.33 (2026-05-11)

  • Executive summary — new “Strong drug-target candidates” sentence. Surfaces specific drug names where the evidence is robust: (a) any oncogene-addiction collection fires for this cell line (mutation + functional CRISPR dependency, the strongest combined signal) — KRAS-G12C inhibitors / BRAF+MEK / EGFR TKIs / ABL TKIs / PI3K-α / CDK4/6 inhibitors named directly; (b) PRISM-screen compounds with z < −1.5σ sensitivity — top 2 named with target and z. Capped at four entries. The earlier “Useful as a model for” sentence frames biology; this one names concrete therapies likely to work.
  • Collections panel — categories with jargon-heavy names get inline explainers. Under each affected category header, a small italic gray line spells out the gist. Examples: Oncogene addiction (mutation × CRISPR dependency) → “Cancer cells that have become functionally dependent on a driver gene — knocking it out (or blocking it with a drug) kills the cell. Stricter than the mutation-only collections above.” Pathway-activity expression signatures → “Each set marks lines where the pathway is transcriptionally active (mean z > +0.75 across a curated gene panel). Reflects what the cell is doing, not just what is mutated.” Tumor-suppressor functional loss and Focal amplifications also get one-line gists.

v.81.32 (2026-05-11)

  • Fifteen new collections lifting Wiki-only views into cohort-level filters. (a) Oncogene addiction — new category “Oncogene addiction (mutation × CRISPR dependency)”. Six entries combine the driver-mutation call with the actual CRISPR knock-out read-out (GE < −0.5): KRAS-addicted, BRAF-addicted, EGFR-dependent, CDK4/6-dependent (RB1-intact + CDK4/6 essential), BCR-ABL-addicted, PI3K-active and dependent. Stricter than the existing mutation-only collections — picks lines where losing the driver actually kills the cell, not just lines that carry the mutation. (b) Pathway-activity expression signatures — new category. Eight entries reuse the same curated panels the Wiki uses (MYC targets, E2F / S-phase, G2/M, IFN response, TGF-β, hypoxia / HIF, NRF2 signature, stem / lineage plasticity). Membership = mean z > +0.75 across the panel genes. Computed lazily after expression loads, mirroring the existing NE / EMT / breast-subtype collections. (c) High LoH (≥ 0.3) added to the existing Genome — ploidy / instability category for HRD-adjacent stratification.

v.81.31 (2026-05-11)

  • STR authentication block now links to the source data. New “Validate against the source” sub-block above the reference STR profile table with a direct Cellosaurus link for this cell line’s RRID (provenance, parent / derivative relationships, contamination flags, misidentification history are all there), plus ATCC search and DSMZ search links for buying commercial authentication services. The reference STR profile is also explicitly attributed to Cellosaurus (SIB / ExPASy) in a footnote line so the user knows where to validate.
  • Executive summary gets a “Useful as a model for” sentence. One additional synthesized sentence at the end of the summary banner mapping the cell line’s driver pattern to the biology / therapy questions it’s well-suited to study. Examples: BRAF V600E → “BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response (vemurafenib / dabrafenib / trametinib)”; BCR-ABL1 → “ABL TKI (imatinib / dasatinib / nilotinib) response”; EML4-ALK → “ALK-inhibitor (crizotinib / alectinib / lorlatinib) response”; CDKN2A loss → “CDK4/6-inhibitor (palbociclib) response”; BRCA1/2 loss → “PARP-inhibitor response”; MSI-high → “checkpoint-immunotherapy response background”; ERBB2 amp → “HER2-targeted-therapy response”; MDM2 amp with WT TP53 → “MDM2-inhibitor (nutlin) response”; Class-I lost / reduced → “cancer immune-escape via MHC-I loss”. Capped at three angles to keep the summary tight.

v.81.30 (2026-05-11)

  • Drug response — clearer σ / z-score explanation. The intro paragraph now defines σ explicitly (standard deviation of the AUC for that drug across all PRISM cell lines), explains what “−1.4σ below average” concretely means (this line kills 1.4 SDs harder than typical for this drug), and gives interpretation thresholds: |z| > 1σ = noteworthy, |z| > 2σ = strong outlier. AUC scale also restated at the top so the user doesn’t have to remember 0 = killed / 1 = no effect.
  • New “Sort: Drug response” in the cell line browser. Pick the option, type a compound name (or substring; multiple compounds averaged) in the input field — e.g. PALBOCICLIB, IRINOTECAN, PALBO, ABEMA. List sorts ascending by AUC by default (most-sensitive lines at top) with the AUC value shown inline on each row, color-coded by sensitivity (green < 0.6, amber 0.6–0.85, gray > 0.85). Lines not in the PRISM screen sink to the bottom regardless of direction.
  • Wiki palette sweep — calmer, fewer hues. The Wiki was previously using purple (druggable targets), teal (FACS markers), bright orange (pathway-activity signatures), sky blue (lineage markers), and several blue shades (typical-pattern, hallmark-checklist) on top of the existing green/red/gray base. All consolidated into four accent colors: green for active / dependencies / sensitivities / druggable / FACS, red for loss / resistance / immune escape, indigo for typical patterns / lineage / cross-checks, gray for neutral / other / off. Section headers keep their existing green strip styling; pathway-status synthesis colors (per-panel, dynamic) keep their amber/green/red since those convey the call.

v.81.29 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki Expression profile — new “Potential FACS markers” block. Intersects expression with a curated ~100-gene panel of well-known cell-surface antigens: CD molecules (CD3/4/8/14/19/20/22/24/27/33/44/45/56/68/127/133, …), receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR, HER2-4, FGFR1-4, MET, AXL, KIT, IGF1R, NTRK, ALK, …), immune checkpoints (PD-L1, PD-L2, PD-1, CTLA4, LAG3, TIM-3, TIGIT, B7-H3, VISTA), ADC / bispecific / clinical targets (TROP2, FOLR1, MSLN, NECTIN4, CEACAM5/6, MUC1/16, DLL3, LIV1, STEAP1/2, PSMA, NaPi2b, claudins), adhesion molecules (EPCAM, CDH1/2, ICAM1, integrins), death receptors (FAS, DR4, DR5), Notch family, and tumor-associated antigens (CA9, GPC3, …). Threshold TPM > 4 (a bit stricter than druggable targets, since FACS needs antibody-detectable protein); top 12 shown, sorted by uniqueness vs cohort (z-score). Each entry shows raw TPM and z, so the user can pick markers that are both bright AND distinctive to this line as wet-lab handles for FACS, antibody assays, or candidate targeting.

v.81.28 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki executive summary — new synthesized opening paragraph at the very top of every cell-line Wiki, so the headline biology is visible before scrolling. Driver hierarchy: clinical fusion › canonical oncogene hotspot › canonical TSG functional loss. Genomic flags (WGD, MSI, Class-I status, hypermutation) follow as a final sentence. Examples: “JR is a Rhabdomyosarcoma cell line. Driven by PAX3-FOXO1 driver fusion plus FGFR3 p.K650, with functional loss of TP53, RB1. Focal amplification of MYCN, MDM2. Genome / phenotype: whole-genome doubled; Class-I antigen presentation reduced.” Falls back to a gentle “no canonical driver detected” note when nothing in the integrated panels triggers.
  • HLA / polymorphic-locus hotspots demoted from the default view. Hotspot mutation calls in HLA-A/B/C / MIC / KIR genes are usually allelic divergence from the GRCh38 reference, not somatic events — surfacing them as “hotspot mutations” falsely implied they were cancer drivers. They’re now hidden behind the existing “show all” toggle in the cell-line detail card’s Hotspot Mutations list, and filtered out of the Wiki’s “Top hotspot hits” line. Still recoverable via the toggle for users who want to inspect them; the ⚠ polymorphic-locus marker still flags them when shown.

v.81.27 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki Expression profile section reworked from raw top-expression to uniquely-high vs cohort + pathway-activity signatures. The previous “Most-expressed genes” row was always dominated by mitochondrial and ribosomal genes (MT-ATP8, GAPDH, EEF1A1, MT-CO2 …) that are high in every cell line and tell you nothing about this specific one. (1) Top uniquely high expression — now z-ranked against the full cohort. Each gene shows both its raw TPM and its z-score, e.g. FGFR3 (TPM 6.4, z +2.8). Pan-housekeeping genes drop out naturally because they have low SD across the cohort. (2) Pathway-activity signatures — new block. Nine curated gene panels (MYC targets, E2F / S-phase replication, G2/M progression, IFN response, EMT, TGF-β response, hypoxia / HIF target, NRF2 / oxidative-stress, stem / lineage plasticity). For each panel we compute the mean z-score over the panel genes in this cell line; panels with mean z > +0.75 are surfaced as “turned ON” (with the pathway note in a tooltip) and mean z < −0.75 as “turned OFF”. (3) Lineage markers and druggable targets kept and now annotated with z-scores so you can see which are uniquely high here vs typical for the cohort, not just absolutely high.

v.81.26 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — bug fix: hovering a gene name in the Wiki body showed the help cursor but no actual MyGene.info tooltip popped up. Cause: openCellLineWiki rendered the body HTML but never called attachGeneTooltips on it, so the mouseenter handlers that fetch and display the gene-info tooltip were never bound. One-line fix: call this.attachGeneTooltips(body) after the Wiki body is composed and the modal is shown.

v.81.25 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki Genome signatures rows — every numeric value now carries a plain-English descriptor so the user doesn’t have to know what a “high” or “low” value looks like. Ploidy 3.43 now reads as “near-tetraploid”, Aneuploidy 23 / 39 as “medium”, CIN 0.14 as “low”, LoH 0.46 as “high”, MSI 2.9 as “microsatellite stable — well below the MSI-high cutoff of 20”. Each row also restates the relevant threshold inline (e.g. “high tier ≥ 25 of 39” for Aneuploidy, “high tier ≥ 0.3, often seen in WGD-positive or HRD lines” for LoH) so the cutoff is visible without scrolling to the cohort histogram below. Thresholds are the same ones already used elsewhere in the app for collections and the card view.

v.81.24 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — section headers (Cancer classification, Patient & sample origin, Genome signatures, Driver mutations, etc.) made much larger and visually distinct so the major sections separate cleanly. Header bumped 13 → 17 px, bold, set on a light-green tinted strip with a green left-border accent and a small right-curve, mirroring the “section” treatment in the live app. Outer section bottom margin nudged 18 → 24 px for extra breathing room. The downloadable standalone-HTML version of the Wiki picks up the same header styling (h3 rule added to its embedded CSS) so exported reports also read as cleanly-sectioned documents.

v.81.23 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — CRISPR dependencies section now ranks by z-score vs the full cohort instead of raw gene-effect, so the top entries are uniquely essential to this cell line (downstream of its driver mutations, lineage-specific factors, etc.) instead of the pan-essentials (RAN, PCNA, RPL17 …) that every cell line shares. Pan-essentials are additionally filtered out against the DepMap common-essentials list as a safety net. Each gene is now annotated with both its raw GE and its z-score, e.g. FOXA1 (GE −1.20, z −3.2). The matching “growth-promoting on knockout” row is also z-ranked. The 💊 pill meaning is now spelled out inline in the section header: approved or clinical-stage drug targets this gene. Druggable / pathway dependency interpretation panels also switched to the uniquely-essential set (z < −1.5). Computation: per-gene mean and SD across the full cohort, cached on first Wiki open. Section caption rewritten to make this framing explicit.

v.81.22 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — Driver mutations section condensed and corrected. (1) Self-contradiction fixed. For an RB1-lost / CDK4/6-dependent cell line (e.g. JMSU1), the pathway bullet previously said “CDK4/6 inhibitors likely active” while the synthesis underneath said “CDK4/6 inhibitors typically ineffective”. Bullet now appends the caveat “but RB1 is lost — RB1 sits downstream of CDK4/6, so clinical CDK4/6 inhibitors are typically not effective even when the cell is CDK4/6-dependent by gene-effect”. (2) “Essential” language calibrated. Gene-effect −0.33 is no longer described as “essential” — CRISPR thresholds across all pathway-status panels (RB/CDK4-6, p53, RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT, BCR-ABL, EGFR) are now: < −0.5 = “strongly reduces growth / essential”, −0.5 to −0.2 = “moderately reduces growth / partial dependency”, ≥ −0.2 = neutral. The dependency caption now notes the scale explicitly: 0 = no effect, −0.5 = selectively essential threshold, −1 ≈ typical strongly-essential gene. (3) Condensed. Dropped the “TP53 is mutated” and “G1/S cell-cycle brake lost” flag cards (covered better by the p53 and Cell cycle pathway-status panels); remaining flags (MMR / HRD / very-high TMB) are now compact inline pills with the narrative on hover instead of bordered title-plus-body cards. Three count rows (damaging, hotspot-mutated, top hits) combined into one line. Each pathway-scan entry collapsed from four rows (title, note, gene list, divider) to a single line. Pathway status now appears before Pathway scan so the interpretive view comes first.

v.81.21 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — remove WGD / MSI-high from the “Other alterations in this cell line” block under Expected drivers for this subtype. They are genome-wide phenotypes, not gene-specific driver alterations, and both are already prominent in the Genome signatures section directly above (full WGD row, MSI score row, plus the cohort histograms). Surfacing them twice in adjacent sections was duplicative and confusing. The drivers block now stays focused on what it’s for: gene-specific alterations — fusions, functional-loss calls, and hotspot mutations.

v.81.20 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki “Expected drivers for this subtype” section reorganized into three clearly-separated blocks so the expected-vs-found split is readable at a glance. (1) Typical alteration pattern — the curated KB description for the Oncotree subtype (blue panel). (2) Hallmark-gene checklist — one row per expected gene with a ✓ when present in this cell line (plus a short per-row hit summary: hotspot p.V600E, damaging, functional loss, fusion, etc.) or ✗ when absent. Header shows “N of M present”. (3) Other alterations in this cell line — driver fusions, functional-loss calls, and hotspot mutations on cancer-panel genes that are not in the hallmark list, plus genome-level flags (MSI-high, WGD). This makes the “hallmark expected but missing” vs “present but unexpected” structure visible without scanning a wall of text.

v.81.19 (2026-05-11)

  • Wiki — new “Where this line sits in the cohort” sub-block under the Genome signatures section. Four small Plotly panels rendered FACS-style: Ploidy, Aneuploidy, CIN as continuous histograms, WGD as a binary two-bar count. This cell line’s value is marked with a dashed red line (continuous) or a red bar (WGD), with its numeric value labeled above the line. Per-panel PNG / SVG export via Plotly’s built-in modebar (hover top-right of each plot). Cohort CSV export button next to the heading dumps ModelID, Name, Ploidy, WGD, Aneuploidy, CIN, plus an IsInspected flag for the currently-open cell line. Skipped silently for lines with no global-signatures entry.

v.81.18 (2026-05-11)

  • Cell-line list sex symbol — when the annotated sex and the expression-inferred sex directly conflict (e.g. TE6: annotation Male, expression Female), the line now shows “?” with a conflict tooltip instead of the annotated symbol. Neither signal is trustworthy on its own when they disagree, and silently picking the annotation hides the conflict from the user. The detail card still shows both Sex (annotation) and Sex (expression) on separate rows with the existing amber-disagreement style, so the raw signals stay available for users who want to dig in. The sex filter dropdown is unchanged — selecting “Male (annotation)” still includes TE6 since that is its annotation.

v.81.17 (2026-05-11)

  • New collections category Focal amplifications. Five entries covering the gain-of-function side of focal CN events (the loss side is already represented by the per-TSG functional-loss collections, since DepMap’s integrated LoF call already picks up deep deletions). MYC family amp (MYC / MYCN / MYCL — pathway active across lineages), ERBB2 amp (HER2-driven; lineage-agnostic, distinct from the breast-only expression-based HER2+ collection), MDM2 amp (p53 functionally suppressed without a TP53 mutation — nice contrast to the TP53-loss set), G1/S amp (CDK4 / CDK6 / CCND1 / CCNE1 — G1/S deregulation; contrast to RB1-loss / CDKN2A-loss), and Any focal amplification as a generic catch-all. Membership pulls from the curated clinical CN panel (clinicalCn.byCellLine.amplifications).

v.81.16 (2026-05-11)

  • New collections category Tumor-suppressor functional loss. One filter entry per gene in the standard 9-gene TSG panel — TP53, PTEN, RB1, CDKN2A, APC, NF1, SMAD4, STK11/LKB1, VHL — plus aggregates “Any TSG functional loss (≥ 1 of the 9)” and “Multiple TSG losses (≥ 2)”. Each gene-specific entry includes the pathway implication (e.g. “TP53 functional loss → p53 checkpoint lost”, “APC loss → WNT pathway active”). Membership pulls from DepMap’s integrated functional-loss call (low CN, damaging mutation at high allele frequency, or near-zero expression) so deep deletions and silenced loci that the damaging-mutation matrix misses are still captured. Combine with the existing include / exclude oncoprint-style controls to ask things like “TP53-loss AND not RB1-loss” in one shot.

v.81.15 (2026-05-11)

  • Collections panel — fixed strange-looking text in tooltips. HTML entities (&mdash;, &minus;, &ge;, &rsquo;, &ndash;) used in the catalog description strings were rendering literally in some tooltip contexts. Swapped them out for the Unicode characters directly (— − ≥ – etc.) so they show as glyphs everywhere, regardless of whether the text ends up inside a title="" attribute, a textContent assignment, or innerHTML body.
  • Immunogenicity prediction added as two new collections under Immunology, replacing the hot/cold framing. Likely immunogenic = ≥ 200 damaging coding mutations and class-I antigen presentation appears intact (no B2M damaging, HLA-A/B/C expression not strongly reduced, HLA CN not lost vs B2M). Likely non-immunogenic = either class-I reduced/lost (immune escape) or ≤ 50 damaging mutations with otherwise intact MHC-I (too few neoantigens). Lines that don't fit either profile are unlabeled. The catalog description spells out the inputs and the cell-intrinsic-proxy caveat (real-tumor immunogenicity also depends on the TME, which isn't observable in cell lines).

v.81.14 (2026-05-11)

  • Collections filter — oncoprint-style include/exclude. The single-collection dropdown is replaced with a “Collections [N]” button that opens a multi-select panel. Each collection has two toggle buttons: + = require (cell line must be IN this set), − = exclude (cell line must NOT be in this set). Multiple collections combine with AND, so e.g. you can ask for “MSI-high” AND not “WGD-positive” in one shot. Active states are rendered as removable chips in the active-filter strip; clicking × on a chip clears just that state. Button label and chips stay in sync with the panel, and Reset clears all of them.

v.81.13 (2026-05-11)

  • Cell-line browser — iterative cleanup step 3. (1) Tooltips rewritten in plain language with term definitions. The “?” tooltips next to Genome, Functional loss, Focal CN events and Clinically relevant fusions previously read like method-section snippets. They now define every term inline (Ploidy, WGD, Aneuploidy, CIN; the three-signal LoF / focal-CN / fusion criteria) before going into the caveats. (2) Three new collections. “Class-I antigen presentation reduced/lost” (Immunology) groups the immune-escape candidates surfaced by the per-cell-line flag. “WGD-positive” and “High aneuploidy” (Genome — ploidy / instability) let the user pick or contrast genomically unstable lines. (3) Three new sort options: Ploidy, Aneuploidy, CIN. The numeric value appears inline on each row alongside a short unit tag (pl 2.29, aneup 12, CIN 0.14). Lines missing the metric are pushed to the bottom regardless of sort direction. Caption line above the list spells out the unit so the numbers read unambiguously.

v.81.12 (2026-05-11)

  • Cell-line detail card — iterative cleanup step 2. Damaging mutations list now defaults to only the cancer-panel-relevant subset (genes that appear in any of the curated cancer pathway panels). The long passenger tail (ACTN1, ADGRG6, BZW2, etc. on most lines) sits behind a “show all N” toggle. When zero cancer-panel hits, the section shows “None in cancer-panel set” with the toggle still available. Hotspot and fusion lists unchanged (they’re already curated). The new flags section renamed “Phenotype flags” → “Immunology” since both MSI-high and Class-I reduced are immunology-relevant signals (checkpoint-inhibitor response prediction and immune evasion, respectively).

v.81.11 (2026-05-11)

  • Cell-line detail card — calmer, more readable. Step 1 of an iterative cleanup. The MSI and Class-I antigen-presentation badges no longer sit next to the cell-line ID where they read as the headline feature; they now live in a new “Phenotype flags” section with a one-line plain-English caption next to each chip so the user doesn’t need to hover to know what they mean. Genome row rewritten from a single cryptic line (“Ploidy 2.29 · Aneup. 4 · CIN 0.14”) into four indented rows with descriptors (“Ploidy 2.29 (near-diploid)”, “Aneuploidy 4 / 39 (low)”, “CIN 0.14 (low)”, “WGD yes” when positive). Focal-CN chips no longer use the ↑↓ glyphs (they read as “going up / down” rather than “amplified / deleted”); the gene name now sits next to a small “amp” / “del” / “strong amp” / “deep del” word. Palette muted across the card: amps use dark-blue text on a light-blue tint, deletions and LoF use dark-red text on a light-red tint; fusion tier pills (high/med/low) keep the semantic color but on neutral gray borders; the Lehmann TNBC chip is now gray instead of saturated purple. No data removed.

v.81.10 (2026-05-11)

  • Network legend zoom-sync — bug fix: clicking the vis-network home/reset button (above the “+” in the lower-right nav cluster) reset the view but the legend kept reading “at current zoom 2.44×”. Cause: vis-network only fires zoom on wheel/pinch input, not on the home button or programmatic fit(). Switched the listener to afterDrawing with a scale-change diff (cheap; only re-renders the legend HTML when getScale() actually changed) so the legend tracks every kind of view change — mousewheel, pinch, nav buttons, double-click fit, and stabilization-done autofit.

v.81.9 (2026-05-11)

  • Network — edge-thickness legend now scales with the canvas zoom, so the legend lines visually match the edges actually being drawn (avoids the misrepresentation where the legend stayed at base size while zoomed-in edges looked much thicker). A small “(at current zoom N.NN×)” hint appears next to the legend heading when zoom ≠ 1. Hint and scaled widths are screen-only — PNG/SVG exports continue to render the legend at the canonical base-scale mapping with no zoom annotation, so exported figures remain publication-ready. Line widths clamped to [0.5×, 3×] in the legend panel to avoid overflow at extreme zoom.

v.81.8 (2026-05-11)

  • Mutation analysis “Compare by Tissue / Additional Hotspot / Fusion” inline table redesigned to make subset counts obvious. New leading N (in subset) column shows how many cells share the row’s tissue / hotspot / fusion (e.g. how many cells carry GNAS mutation); a vertical separator divides it from the right-hand block, which now sits under a colspan header naming the main stratification gene (e.g. “TP53 stratification (within subset)”) so it’s clear that N(WT) / N(Mut) are the main-gene intersection within that subset. Added a “Hide rows with N < x” filter (default 5) so trivial subsets (e.g. 3-cell hotspots) are suppressed; the filter shows how many rows are hidden. Sort key map extended to 7 columns to match the new layout.

v.81.7 (2026-05-11)

  • Export-chart dialog layout fix — Width, Height and Lock-aspect were wrapping in three rows because the labels plus inputs didn't fit in the 420 px modal. Modal widened to 500 px and the three controls are now in a single flex-wrap:nowrap row, so Height number sits on the same row as the Height label.

v.81.6 (2026-04-27)

  • Curated focal CN events integrated end-to-end. New scripts/clinical_cn_anchor.json + scripts/process_clinical_cn.py extract clinically actionable amplifications and TSG deletions from OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv. Output web_data/clinical_cn.json (~125 KB; 527 cell lines with at least one focal CN event).
    • Amplification panel (~32 oncogenes): ERBB2, MYC, MYCN, MYCL, EGFR, MDM2, MDM4, CDK4, CDK6, CCND1/2/3, CCNE1, FGFR1/2/3, MET, KIT, PDGFRA, KRAS, AR, ESR1, MITF, SOX2, NKX2-1, BCL2, AURKA/B, NTRK1, NUTM1, TERT, IGF1R. Threshold: relative CN ≥ 3.0 (high-level amp), ≥ 5.0 (strong amp).
    • Extended-deletion panel (~14 TSGs): BAP1, SMARCA4, SMARCB1, ARID1A, STK11, BRCA1/2, SETD2, ATM, CDKN2B, KEAP1, FAT1, FBXW7, TET2. Deliberately excludes the 8 TSGs already in DepMap inferred-LoF (TP53, RB1, PTEN, NF1, CDKN2A, VHL, MTAP, APC) to avoid duplication.
    • Cell-line browser detail panel: new "Focal CN events" section with red ▲ chips (amplifications) and blue ▼ chips (deletions). Bold border for strong / deep tier; thin border for suggestive. Hover shows CN value plus context (e.g. "MYC amplification (CN = 8.4, strong). Pan-cancer driver. Burkitt lymphoma, neuroblastoma, breast, colon, etc.").
    • AI .json.gz export: per-cell-line cellLineMetadata.<cl>.cnEvents = { amplifications: [{gene, cn, tier}], deletions: [...] }. Schema bumped to 3.2 with documentation and threshold definitions.
    • New CLB toolbar CN filter — same multi-line dropdown pattern as the fusion filter. Lists every (gene, kind) tuple in the panel with live n= scaled to the active cohort filters. Selecting "▲ MYC amp (n=65)" filters the cell-line list to the 65 MYC-amplified lines; selecting "▼ BAP1 del" similarly. Sorted with amplifications first, deletions after.
    • Top amp counts (sanity check): MYC n=65, CCND1 n=61, KRAS n=27, MYCN n=27, ERBB2 n=25, CDK4 n=24, MDM2 n=23, CCNE1 n=15, EGFR n=15, MET n=11. Top extended-deletion counts: CDKN2B n=295 (chr9p21 co-deletion with CDKN2A; expected high), FAT1 n=50, STK11 n=22, BAP1 n=15, ATM n=14, SMARCB1 n=14.
  • Reference Data card on main page updated to list the new "Focal CN events" annotation alongside HLA CN.
  • Deferred (next pass): adding CN-state filtering to the main parameter panel (correlation analysis), so users can stratify "MYC-amplified vs not" cohorts. Bigger UI change touching multiple analysis paths; keep as a separate session.

v.81.5 (2026-04-27)

  • HLA copy-number ingested + class-I inference activated. Ran scripts/process_hla_cn.py against the downloaded OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv (~400 MB DepMap WGS CN matrix); output web_data/hla_cn.json (190 KB) covers 830 cell lines for HLA-A/B/C, B2M, and antigen-processing-machinery genes. Two corrections during ingestion:
    • The CSV format is DepMap's relative copy number (1.0 = diploid), not log2 ratio or absolute — format detection rewritten to recognize this from the B2M reference distribution.
    • Short-read WGS systematically under-maps HLA-C in the polymorphic region (cohort median ~0.22, not real loss). The class-I CN inference now uses HLA-A/B normalized to B2M per cell line (B2M sits on chr15, clean diploid reference). Ratio < 0.5 = strong loss, < 0.7 = suggestive loss. Catches HLA-specific copy loss while controlling for sample-level mappability and the HLA-C reference bias.
  • Lehmann TNBC subtype annotation. The Oncotree subtypes (Breast Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Triple-Negative Breast Cancer, etc.) don't capture the Lehmann TNBC molecular axis (BL1, BL2, IM, M, MSL, LAR) and our previous user-flagged: "the cell-line browser TNBC labels don't match Lehmann's classifications." Added curated subtype assignments from Lehmann JCI 2011 (PMID 21633166) plus the 2016 reclassification (PMID 27310713; collapsed to four classes — BL1, BL2, M, LAR — with IM and MSL re-attributed to immune / stromal infiltrate). New scripts/lehmann_tnbc_anchor.json + scripts/process_lehmann_tnbc.py; output web_data/lehmann_tnbc.json covers 22 of 29 panel cell lines (the other 7 aren't in DepMap 25Q3). Surfaced as a small purple chip next to the Subtype row in the cell-line browser detail panel (e.g. "Lehmann BL1" or "Lehmann MSL → M" when 2016 reclassified). Hover for full definitions of the six classes. Also embedded per cell line in the AI .json.gz export as cellLineMetadata.<cl>.lehmannTnbc.
  • Reference Data card on main page updated to list HLA CN and Lehmann TNBC under the curated-annotations bucket.
  • schemaVersion 3.0 → 3.1.

v.81.4 (2026-04-27)

  • Class-I antigen-presentation inference per cell line. Three integrated signals — none alone is conclusive, hence the integration:
    1. B2M damaging mutation — β2-microglobulin truncation knocks out the entire class-I antigen-presentation system regardless of HLA status. Strongest single signal.
    2. HLA-A/B/C expression — z-score vs the full cohort. Very low expression of all three implies functional loss (transcriptional silencing OR LOH; we can't distinguish without phased reads).
    3. HLA-A/B/C copy number — from web_data/hla_cn.json (extracted from DepMap's WGS CN matrix). log2-ratio < −0.4 in all three suggests one-copy loss.
    Status tier: likely_lost (B2M damaging hit, OR strong reduction in two independent signals), reduced (one signal), intact (data available, no signals), unknown (data missing). Surfaces as a small red / amber chip next to the cell-line ID in the browser detail panel, with a hover tooltip listing the specific evidence. Also embedded in the AI .json.gz export per cell line as cellLineMetadata.<cl>.class1AntigenPresentation (only emitted when status is non-trivial). Schema bumped to 3.0.
  • Important caveat: this is a functional inference, not allele-specific HLA-LOH detection. Real LOH calls would need phased reads (LOHHLA) on raw BAMs, which DepMap doesn't redistribute. The integration here catches the same class of immune-escape-candidate cell lines for biology purposes — tooltip and AI-export field both spell that out.
  • New scripts/process_hla_cn.py — takes a downloaded OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv (~400 MB), extracts copy number for HLA-A/B/C, B2M, antigen-processing-machinery genes (TAP1/2, TAPBP, ERAP1/2, NLRC5), and class-II HLA. Output: web_data/hla_cn.json (~50 KB). The CN file isn't bundled (gitignored); download it once from DepMap, run the script, commit the resulting JSON.

v.81.3 (2026-04-27)

  • HLA / polymorphic-locus caveat. The HLA region (chr 6p21) is the most polymorphic in the human genome — HLA-A alone has >7,000 known alleles — and gnomAD-based germline filtering leaks here. So "hotspot" calls in HLA / MIC / KIR genes typically reflect allelic divergence from the GRCh38 reference, not somatic events. Real cancer-relevant HLA loss exists (immune escape via class-I LoF + LOH, especially in MSI-high tumors) but should be inferred from expression loss + LOH, not the raw hotspot matrix.

    New _POLYMORPHIC_LOCI set covers the classical class-I HLA (A/B/C), non-classical (E/F/G), class-II (DPA/DPB/DQA/DQB/DRA/DRB1-5/DM/DO), MIC (A/B), and the KIR family. Wherever a hotspot or damaging mutation is rendered, polymorphic-locus genes now get a small ⚠ marker with a hover tooltip explaining the caveat:

    • Cell-line browser detail panel — hotspot / damaging / fusion gene lists. Polymorphic genes also sorted to the end of those lists so they don't crowd the always-visible top-10 (still surfaced when "Show all" is expanded).
    • Mutation analysis results table — gene name now carries a ⚠ when polymorphic.
    • AI .json.gz export — cellLineMetadata.<cl>.mutations.<gene>.caveat: "polymorphic_locus" per-cell-line flag, with the schema description telling the LLM to treat such calls as suspect unless paired with expression loss + LOH.

v.81.2 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — precomputed extras for the remaining view types that were lagging behind gene_effect / scatter (Priority 5 of the recent brief). Schema bumped to 2.8.
    • Correlation view: new extras.tissueStratifiedCorrelations — top 20 correlation pairs by |r|, each broken out into per-tissue r values for tissues with n ≥ 10 cell lines. Catches the most common artifact in cross-cohort correlation analysis: a cohort-wide r that's actually lineage segregation rather than biology. If a pair's overall r is 0.5 but the per-tissue r is near zero in every tissue, the LLM can flag it as lineage-driven before reading anything into the relationship.
    • Cluster view: new extras.clusterAnnotations — per-cluster pathway overlap with the wiki cancer pathway KB (pathway must share ≥2 genes with the cluster) plus a CORUM co-member count. Tells the LLM whether a cluster is biologically coherent (e.g. "cluster 3 has 5/8 members in PI3K/AKT/mTOR") or a grab-bag without obvious functional unity.
    • Gate-comparison view already shipped most of the relevant precomputed extras (differentialGeneEffect, differentialExpression, tissueEnrichment, subtissueEnrichment, mutationEnrichment) via _gateCompareResults; left unchanged.

v.81.1 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — three additions from a Claude Code brief targeting the scatter view (Priorities 1–2 of the brief). Schema bumped to 2.7.
    • New topExpressionCorrelates field — top 30 expression-vs-expression Pearson correlates of the focal gene. Parallel to topCoessentials (GE-vs-GE) and topCorrelates (GE-vs-expression), but answers a different axis: which other genes' expression covaries with the focal gene's expression in this cohort? Most useful for scatter / expression-correlate views where the focal axis is expression. Polarity description in dataStructure: positive r = co-regulated (often shared transcriptional program / phenotype state / lineage marker); negative r = anti-correlated. Same n-gate as the other correlate blocks (n ≥ max(50, 0.6 × cohortSize)). Suppressed when focal-gene expression SD < 0.05.
    • Variance warning extended to expression axis. Was previously gated only on the GE axis (|mean| < 0.3, SD < 0.15, frac essential < 5%). Now also fires when focal-gene expression has SD < 0.5 OR mean < 0.5 (log2-TPM+1, gene silent or stably expressed everywhere). Warning structure became { geneEffect: ..., expression: ... } so both can fire independently. Catches the case where a "what explains the variability in expression of X" question is asked about a silent / housekeeping gene.
    • New extras.pairCorrelation for scatter views — Pearson + Spearman + n + two-sided p between the two scatter axes, computed over the filtered cohort. Reviewer flagged that context.correlation was null in scatter exports; the most basic precomputed thing for a scatter view, missing entirely. Now precomputed at export time over whichever combination of GE / expression / dual-gene the user picked.
  • Deferred from this round: applying the same precomputed-extras discipline to mutation_analysis / gate_comparison / correlation / cluster / expression_correlate view types (Priority 5 of the brief). Bigger scope; ship after the scatter improvements are tested.

v.81.0 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — the precomputed-summary discipline (topCoessentials / topCorrelates / focalGeneTissueSummary / focalGeneMutationSummary / pathway-partner whitelist) was silently scoped to the gene-effect view because the focal-gene resolver only checked context.gene. Scatter / mutation / expression-correlate exports were quietly emitting empty extras while the _analysisInstructions still told the LLM to use those fields. Fixed: the resolver now falls back through context.gene → context.hotspotGene → context.targetGene → context.gene1, so every view that has a single focal gene now produces all the same precomputed summaries (caught when an Opus 4.7 review of a FAM167A scatter export found none of the extras present).
  • New extras.focalGeneVarianceWarning — emitted when the focal gene sits in screen noise (|mean GE| < 0.3, SD < 0.15, fewer than 5% of cohort lines essential). Stops the LLM from confidently inventing biology from noise-driven correlations — FAM167A in 74 Skin lines (mean=−0.05, SD=0.11, 0/74 essential) is the canonical case where this warning fires. Step 0 of _analysisInstructions now tells the LLM to read this warning first and recommend stratification before pattern-hunting.
  • Scatter view description rewritten. Was producing tautological text like "Scatter of FAM167A vs FAM167A filtered by Skin" when both axes were the same gene with different types (GE vs expression). Now: "Scatter of FAM167A gene effect (x) vs FAM167A expression (y), filtered by Skin." — explicit about which axis carries which data type.
  • _analysisInstructions revised: Step 1 now says the precomputed scans are present "when the export includes them (gene-effect / scatter / mutation / expression-correlate views with a single focal gene)" rather than asserting they're always there. Multi-gene views (correlation / cluster / gate-comparison) are explicitly told to recompute. Eliminates the silent failure where an LLM following the instructions for an unsupported view kept hitting empty fields.
  • schemaVersion 2.5 → 2.6.

v.80.9 (2026-04-27)

  • "Reference Data" card — was eating the entire upper-left of the homepage after v.80.8 added all the new sources to the visible bullet lists. Collapsed back down to three named-source one-liners (DepMap 25Q3 · CORUM + Reactome · in-app curated KBs) with a "▾ show files & details" toggle that expands the full per-bucket file / KB list when needed. The Cell Lines / Gene Effect / Correlation / Open / Reset buttons are now visible without scrolling again.

v.80.8 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — Reactome integration. Layered as a fourth tier in the focal-gene partner lookup, after CORUM. Catches pathway / signaling-cascade relationships CORUM doesn't cover — e.g. for IL4R, CORUM gives the receptor complex (IL13, IL13RA1, IL2RG, IL4) while Reactome adds the JAK/STAT cascade (STAT1, STAT5A, STAT5B, STAT6, plus PIK3CA and SOCS members from the broader signaling neighbourhood). New scripts/process_reactome.py fetches the GMT (~290 KB) directly from reactome.org via its public download URL (no auth, no manual intervention), filters to specific pathways (size 5–100 genes — drops broad parents like "Signal Transduction" with 2,600+ members), caps per-gene partners at 120 most-co-occurring. Output: web_data/reactome_partners.json (~6 MB; covers ~10,000 human genes — about half the protein-coding genome). Schema bumped to 2.5.
  • "Reference Data" card on the main page restructured to show all data sources in three buckets: Cell-line data (DepMap files, expanded to include the new CSVs we ingest — OmicsInferredMolecularSubtypes, OmicsGlobalSignatures, OmicsFusionFilteredSupplementary, PRISM Repurposing), Pathway / complex memberships (CORUM + Reactome + in-app curated KBs), Curated annotations (clinical fusions, subtype hallmarks, STR profiles). Clearer attribution for CORUM and Reactome alongside the existing DepMap acknowledgement note.

v.80.7 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — CORUM integration. The pathway-partner expression carve-out is no longer hand-curated for ~9 complexes; it now layers three sources so any focal gene gets meaningful partners:
    1. Hand-curated complexes (NEDD8/CRL, Proteasome, Hippo, MYC, TP53, BRCA, mTOR, BCL2, splicing) — tight, biologist-vetted high-value sets.
    2. CORUM (manually curated mammalian protein complexes, ~3,000 human genes covered) — auto-populates partners for arbitrary focal genes (SMARCA4 → BAF subunits, MCM4 → MCM2-7 helicase, RUVBL1 → INO80/SRCAP, etc.).
    3. Wiki cancer pathways — signaling-cascade groupings CORUM doesn't cover (RAS/MAPK, RTK family, p53-MDM2-CDKN2A axis).
    New scripts/process_corum.py reads a downloaded CORUM TSV (mips.helmholtz-muenchen.de/corum/, "Human" complexes) and writes web_data/corum_partners.json. Schema bumped to 2.4; dataStructure.expression documents the layered lookup. CORUM data file is optional — if not present, the export falls back to the hand-curated + wiki-pathway layers and still works.

v.80.6 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — bug fixes after a third Opus 4.7 review of v.80.5. Two precomputed summaries had real bugs that were actively misleading the LLM (worse than not having the summaries at all per the reviewer). Schema bumped to 2.3.
    • topCoessentials n-gate. The list was entirely noise — every entry computed on n=23 or 24 cell lines because ~65 GE genes have screen-batch-only partial coverage and there was no minimum-n filter. Now gated at n >= max(50, 0.6 × cohortSize). The real biology (POMP, UBE2M, UBA3, SKP1 for NEDD8) should now surface as the actual top hits.
    • topCoessentials partner genes added back to the geneEffect matrix if they were dropped by the variance filter, so the LLM can verify the correlation by recomputing from the file (in v.80.5 the partner genes weren't in the matrix at all, making the values unreproducible).
    • Same n-gate applied to topCorrelates for consistency.
    • Both correlate sets suppressed when focal-gene SD < 0.05 — near-zero focal variance produces only noise correlations, so emit empty rather than 30 spurious entries.
    • focalGeneMutationSummary rewritten. Was ranking by |Δ| which floated meaningless n=3 entries (BCL6 with n_mut=3, p=0) above canonical drivers. Now split into two:
      • coreDrivers: TP53, KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, EGFR, PIK3CA, PTEN, APC, RB1, CDKN2A, NF1, NF2, STK11, SMAD4, MYC, IDH1, ARID1A, SMARCA4, KMT2D — always shown (n_mut ≥ 5) so "did TP53 status matter?" answers itself even when Δ is small.
      • topByEffect: top 20 from the extended panel (n_mut ≥ 10), ranked by |t| not |Δ| so small-n large-effect noise no longer outranks well-powered drivers.
      Each row now has a callType field (hotspot / damaging / hotspot+damaging). p-value approximation fixed — using Abramowitz & Stegun 26.2.17 normal-CDF (was a worse approximation that returned p=0 for |t|>~7, the literal printable bug the reviewer caught).
    • extras._method block added with concrete formulas for every precomputed summary (mirrored at dataStructure._method for cases where extras is omitted). Reviewer wanted it next to the values it documents.

Deferred: generalising the pathway-partner whitelist away from hand-curated complexes to CORUM / Reactome / STRING (separate task with its own data file).

v.80.5 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — second round after another Opus 4.7 review of the v.80.4 NEDD8 export. The reviewer's ranked five all done. Schema bumped to 2.2.
    • New topCoessentials field — top 30 GE-vs-GE Pearson correlates of the focal gene, parallel to the existing topCorrelates (which is GE-vs-expression). Positive r means co-essentiality buffering (lines that depend more on partner depend less on focal); negative r means same-pathway co-essentiality. Reviewer flagged this as the more biologically central question for many gene-effect views (the NEDD8 example: the proteasome / cullin / Hippo co-essentiality story was the most informative finding and required a hand-rolled GE-vs-GE scan).
    • Pathway-partner whitelist for the focal gene's expression. Curated complex / machinery memberships for common analysis targets bypass the variance filter so housekeeping-ish pathway components are present in the expression matrix. Initial coverage: Neddylation/CRL (NEDD8 + UBA3, NAE1, UBE2M, UBE2F, RBX1/2, SKP1, CUL1-5, CAND1, COPS5/6, DCUN1D1/5), Proteasome (PSMA/B/C/D/POMP/ADRM1/USP14), Hippo/YAP-TAZ, MYC network, TP53/MDM2, BRCA/HR, mTOR/PI3K, BCL2 family, mRNA splicing core. Easy to extend in _FOCAL_GENE_COMPLEX_PARTNERS. Plus the existing wiki cancer pathways still feed into the always-include set when the focal gene is in one.
    • New extras.focalGeneMutationSummary — per common driver gene (~70 curated), Welch's t comparing focal-gene GE in mutated vs WT cell lines. Top 30 by |delta|. Saves the LLM from running per-gene t-tests by hand (the reviewer had to do TP53/KRAS/BRAF/etc. manually for the NEDD8 question).
    • bySubtype gated at n ≥ 5 (was 3). At n=3 the SD/z is noise and tempts the LLM to over-interpret. Tissue-level (byTissue) stays at n ≥ 3 since tissue groups are typically larger.
    • topCorrelates polarity guidance now in _analysisInstructions step 1. Was only in dataStructure before, so an LLM following only the analysis steps could misread sign. Step 1 now explicitly says: "topCoessentials (GE-vs-GE) … positive r = co-essentiality buffering within a complex, negative r = same-pathway co-essentiality. topCorrelates (GE-vs-expression) … positive r = high partner expression covaries with WEAKER focal-gene essentiality. Read both fields before running your own correlations." Step 3 also nudges the LLM to use extras before scanning the matrix.
    • Top-level nTotal field added (= length of cellLineOrder) so the LLM knows the cohort denominator without having to count.
    • dataStructure._method block added documenting the z-score formula, the topCorrelates / topCoessentials Pearson method, and the focalGeneMutationSummary Welch's t methodology — reviewer flagged that without provenance, citing numbers required guesswork.

v.80.4 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — round of fixes after a real Opus 4.7 review of a NEDD8 export. The reviewer caught real gaps: NEDD8's own expression had been dropped by the variance filter, the neddylation machinery (UBA3, NAE1, UBE2M) wasn't in the expression matrix despite being the most informative genes for the question, and the AI had to hand-roll tissue rollups to discover that the Bone signal was entirely Ewing sarcoma. Schema bumped to 2.1.
    • Focal gene always included in both matrices regardless of variance threshold. For a NEDD8 GE export, the NEDD8 row of geneEffect and expression are guaranteed present.
    • Genes surfaced in topCorrelates are always included in the expression matrix. The expression-correlate scan runs before the expression matrix is filtered, and any gene that turns up in the top 30 is added to the always-include set. So the neddylation E1/E2/CRL components that drive co-essentiality with NEDD8 are now present in expression even if they're stable housekeeping-ish genes that the variance filter would otherwise drop.
    • New extras.focalGeneTissueSummary — precomputed per-tissue and per-subtype mean / sd / n / z-vs-overall for the focal gene's GE, sorted by mean. The reviewer had to discover by hand that "Bone = Ewing sarcoma", "Eye includes 5 RPE1 non-cancerous lines", "PNS = neuroblastoma"; this surfaces all of that automatically.
    • Schema docs updated — topCorrelates now has an explicit description (Pearson, focal-gene GE vs partner expression, with a note that n can vary per gene because expression coverage isn't uniform). The reviewer was confused enough by the missing description to recompute everything from scratch.
    • Step 2 confirmation gate softened: the analysis instructions now explicitly tell the LLM to skip the "ask the user to confirm" step when the question is specific and self-contained, only triggering it for open-ended questions like "explain the variability". Prevents the friction the reviewer flagged.

v.80.3 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — fixes after a real export from the Gene Effect browser on all 1186 cell lines came out at 64 MB. Variance threshold alone wasn't tight enough at large n: ~9000 genes still passed |GE|>0.5 in 1186 cells, dominating file size. Added a per-matrix gene cap on top of the variance filter — after the threshold, genes are sorted by relevance (max-abs for GE, sd for expression) and the top N kept:
    • ≤100 cells: no cap
    • 100–500: cap 12 000
    • 500–1000: cap 6 000
    • 1000–1500: cap 3 500 (your case — should now be ~20–25 MB)
    • >1500: cap 2 500
  • AI export file shape unified across all sources. v.80.1 had results-only sources (correlations / clusters / expression correlates) skip the matrices entirely, which produced very different files between e.g. the Gene Effect browser (64 MB with full matrices) and the Correlation browser (~2 MB metadata-only). With the gene cap, every source now ships the same shape — capped GE matrix + capped expression matrix + cell-line metadata + source-specific extras. Comparing files between sources should feel consistent now.
  • AI dialog tier description updated to reflect the new "variance filter + cap" rules.

v.80.2 (2026-04-27)

  • AI export dialog unified across all 8 source views (gene effect / scatter / mutation analysis / gate compare / correlation / cluster / expression correlate / GE-modal). The four sources that previously used a bare browser prompt() for the question (mutation, scatter, plus the four "Export for AI" menu items in correlation / cluster / gate / expression correlate panels) now open the same fixed-position modal as the GE-modal export. Every export path now shows: source name, cell-line cohort size, exactly what's getting written into the file (matrices vs results-only, with the active tier filters spelled out), the question textarea, and an "After download" suggestion pointing at claude.ai for the actual analysis (the embedded aiInstructions are tuned for it; ChatGPT / Gemini also accept .json.gz). Dialog dismisses on close button, outside click, or after a successful export.

v.80.1 (2026-04-27)

  • AI .json.gz export — size fixes after a real export from the correlation analysis on all 1186 cell lines came out at 74 MB (claude.ai's attachment limit is ~30 MB).
    • Results-only sources skip the matrices. For Correlation / Cluster / Expression correlate exports, the analytical result is the result table itself (correlation pairs / cluster genes / per-gene r-values), which is already shipped in extras. Including the full GE matrix on top was dead weight — the AI doesn't need to re-derive correlations to interpret them. With matrices skipped, a 1186-cell correlation export should now be a few MB rather than 74 MB. Cell-line metadata, mutations, clinical fusions, inferred subtypes and global signatures are still included so the AI can reason about the cohort.
    • Tighter matrix tiers for the data-heavy sources (gene effect / scatter / mutation analysis / gates). Split the old 500–1500 band into 500–1000 (unchanged: GE>0.3, expr mean>2.0 OR sd>0.5) and 1000–1500 (new: GE>0.5, expr mean>2.5 OR sd>0.8). Top tier (>1500) tightened to expr mean>3.0 OR sd>1.0. Mutations / fusions / LoF / signatures still always full at every tier.
    • Tier-info text in the AI dialog updated to show which path applies (results-only vs matrix-bearing) and the new bands.

v.80.0 (2026-04-27)

  • AI JSON export — major refactor (Phases 1+2+3 from the colleague-Claude review brief). All eight "Analyze with AI" buttons (gene-effect, scatter, mutation analysis, gate compare, correlation, cluster, expression correlate, plus the existing GE-modal export) now produce the same gzipped schema. Source-specific result tables (gate enrichment, correlation pairs, cluster genes, expression correlate r values, differential GE for mutation analysis) live under a single extras field; the context field tells the AI which view it came from.
  • Phase 1 — size + tiering: the 400-cell-line hard cap is gone. New tier table: ≤100 full / 100–500 GE>0.2 + expr mean>1.0 OR sd>0.5 / 500–1500 GE>0.3 + expr mean>2.0 OR sd>0.5 / >1500 GE>0.5 + expr mean>2.0 OR sd>1.0. Mutations, clinical fusions, inferred subtypes, and global signatures are always full (they're tiny relative to the matrices and most useful at large n where stratification power matters). Expression filter switched from AND to OR so tissue-restricted markers (low overall mean, high SD — e.g. AFP in liver lines, MITF in melanoma) survive instead of being silently dropped. GE values now rounded to 3 decimals (was 4) — ~25% gzipped-size reduction with no analytical loss. Snapshot PNG dropped from gzipped exports (the AI was told to ignore it anyway, it inflated parse cost ~30% for a typical scatter, and the context field already gives the model everything it needs to restate the view).
  • Phase 2 — schema cleanup: per-cell-line mutations unified from hotspotMutations: {gene:level} + damagingMutations: {gene:level} into a single mutations: {gene: {hotspot: 0|1|2, damaging: bool}}. New per-cell-line layers: clinicalFusions (curated driver fusion calls with tier), inferred (DepMap inferred subtypes — specificVariants like KRAS p.G12D, namedFusions, functionalLoss covering CDKN2A/RB1/PTEN/etc., msi binary), signatures (ploidy, wgd, cin, lohFraction, msiScore, aneuploidy from PureCN + MSIsensor2 + Ben-David). Added top-level schemaVersion: "2.0". Null fields (topCorrelates, cellLineGroups, extras, question) are now omitted when not applicable rather than emitted as null with documentation that an LLM had to disambiguate "not applicable" from "computation failed".
  • Phase 3 — unified export paths: the five _buildXxxAIExport builders (mutation / gates / correlations / clusters / exprCorrelates) and the separate uncompressed JSON output are gone. exportForAI() is now a thin shim that prompts for an optional question, stashes it in the shared aiQuestion textarea, and routes through exportFullAIAnalysis. _getAICellLines extended to handle all eight sources: GE / scatter / mutation use existing logic; gates returns gateA ∪ gateB with stratification under cellLineGroups; correlations / clusters re-derive the main-panel filtered cohort via getFilteredCellLineIndices; exprCorrelates uses _exprCorrelateContext.subgroupIndices. Source-specific context blocks added per source so the AI can describe what the user was looking at regardless of view.

v.79.2 (2026-04-27)

  • Cache-bust the app.js script tag (was ?v=20260224v1 from a February release; bumped to ?v=v79_1). Without this, browsers happily kept the cached old app.js while loading the fresh index.html, producing weird state where some buttons worked (their handlers hadn't changed) but the cell-line browser didn't open (the cached old JS referenced DOM IDs that no longer exist in the new HTML). Will re-bump on every JS release going forward.

v.79.1 (2026-04-27)

  • CLB fusion filter dropdown rebuilt as a custom multi-line component — Safari truncates native datalist options to the input width, which was hiding the n= and clipping fusion names mid-word ("★ KMT2A-", "★ EWSR1-", and rendering several option rows visibly empty). The new dropdown shows two lines per entry: bold name with n=, then disease context for clinical fusions ("Ewing sarcoma", "CML / Ph+ B-ALL", …) or "any fusion involving this gene" for the gene-based long tail. Auto-completes as you type, capped at 200 visible items, click to commit a clean canonical name to the input.
  • CLB toolbar buttons grouped with vertical separators: selection (Select Visible · Deselect All · Copy Names) | inspect (Inspect Gene Effects · Inspect Correlations · Open Saved Inspect — all green-tinted, run analyzes on the selected cell lines) | export (Export Genes CSV · GE matrix CSV · All matrices CSV — now purple-tinted, raw-data exports). The three exports remain because they have non-overlapping scopes (typed gene panel vs genome-wide GE only vs all matrices); the wiki download (per-cell-line HTML) is a different artifact entirely.
  • Cell-line wiki "Expected drivers" section reworked for clarity. Was confusing when the Oncotree subtype label itself contained a fusion name — users were reading "Chronic Myeloid Leukemia, BCR-ABL1+" as a positive call about the cell line rather than the disease classification. Now two clearly separated blocks:
    • Observed in this cell line (green) — pulls from every integrated layer: specific driver variants (KRAS p.G12D), driver fusions with tier badges, functional-loss tumor suppressors, top hotspot-mutated genes, MSI-high flag, WGD flag.
    • Typical for this disease subtype (blue, was the old block) — the curated knowledge-base description, plus the intersection with what's actually mutated in the line.
    Section header explains that the subtype label is a disease classification, not a per-cell-line call. When no curated KB entry exists for the subtype, the observed block still gives actionable info instead of just an "uncovered" message.
  • Subtype knowledge base extended with 9 new entries: Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (BCR-ABL1+), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (BCR-ABL1+), Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia with PML-RARA, Diffuse Glioma, Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Esophageal Adenocarcinoma, Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Stomach Adenocarcinoma, Endometrial Carcinoma.

v.79.0 (2026-04-27)

  • Cell line Wiki restructured for clarity. Sections regrouped into four buckets: Identity (Cancer classification · Patient & sample origin · Sex), Genome state (NEW — Genome signatures), Driver landscape (Expected drivers for this subtype · Driver mutations · Functional loss NEW · Fusion landscape), Functional behavior (CRISPR dependencies · Expression profile · Drug response), and Lab use (STR authentication · External resources). Headers shortened, each section opens with one short sentence saying what it contains, then the data, then a small gray "Source:" footer.
  • Genome signatures section — Ploidy, WGD (in red when positive), Aneuploidy score (Ben-David 0–39), CIN, LoH fraction, and MSI score (MSI-high lines flagged red). One-liner per metric explaining what it means. WGD-positive lines (~58% of the panel) and MSI-high lines (~6%) are systematically different in many comparisons, so this is interpretive context that affects how every section below should be read.
  • Functional loss section — new red-bordered chips for tumor suppressors that are functionally inactivated by integrated CN + mutation + expression evidence (RB1, TP53, PTEN, NF1, CDKN2A, VHL, MTAP, APC). Catches deletion-driven losses (CDKN2A homo-del in 445 lines panel-wide, RB1 deep deletion) that the damaging-mutation matrix alone is blind to.
  • Driver mutations — the top-hotspots line now shows the specific variant in green next to the gene symbol (e.g. KRAS (p.G12D)) when DepMap's inferred-subtype pipeline calls a specific codon (KRAS p.G12D/G12C, BRAF V600E, EGFR L858R, JAK2 V617F, EGFR exon-19 del, plus generic group-level calls).
  • Fusion landscape — clinically relevant fusions (BCR-ABL1 high, EWSR1-FLI1 high, …) now appear at the top of the section with green/amber/red tier chips and the ⚠ atypical badge where applicable, before the noisy raw partner list. Source footer points at the curated list provenance and the per-cell-line orthogonal validation.

v.78.1 (2026-04-27)

  • CLB fusion filter dropdown — the n= count was getting truncated by Safari's narrow datalist subtitle row (showed "★ EWSR1-" rather than "★ EWSR1-FLI1 (n=14)"). Moved the full label (★ marker, fusion / gene name, n= count) into the option's value attribute so it renders as the only line. Filter lookup gained a small helper that strips the ★ prefix and the (n=N) suffix to recover the underlying name, applied everywhere the value is used (cell-line filter, GE-modal forwarding, active-filter badges, CSV export labels). Free-typing a canonical name like "BCR-ABL1" still works, with or without the (n=11) suffix.
  • Inline ? tooltips next to the new section headers in the cell line detail panel: Clinically relevant fusions (recaps the orthogonal-evidence tier rules), Functional loss (explains the integrated CN/mutation/expression call and why it catches deletion-driven losses the damaging-mutation matrix misses), and Genome signatures (defines Ploidy / WGD / Aneuploidy / CIN). Hover the ? for the explanation without leaving the detail panel.
  • DepMap genome-wide signatures integrated. New scripts/process_global_signatures.py + web_data/global_signatures.json (~80 KB) processes OmicsGlobalSignatures.csv — Ploidy (PureCN), WGD (whole-genome doubling, 692/1186 lines ≈58%), CIN, LoH fraction, MSI score (continuous), and Aneuploidy (Ben-David 2021 score). Each cell line now shows a one-line "Genome" row in the detail panel with the most useful four (Ploidy / WGD / Aneuploidy / CIN), each with a hover tooltip. WGD displayed in red when positive.

v.78.0 (2026-04-27)

  • DepMap inferred molecular subtypes integrated. New scripts/process_inferred_subtypes.py + web_data/inferred_subtypes.json (~140 KB) processes OmicsInferredMolecularSubtypes.csv — per-cell-line specific hotspot variants (KRAS p.G12D, BRAF p.V600E, etc.), 11 named driver fusions, integrated LoF for 8 tumor suppressors (RB1, TP53, PTEN, NF1, CDKN2A, VHL, MTAP, APC), and MSI status. Cross-validation against our own clinical_fusions.json shows perfect agreement on BCR-ABL1 (12/12), EWSR1-FLI1 (14/14), EWSR1-ERG (3/3), ETV6-RUNX1, TCF3-PBX1, PAX-FOXO1.
  • Cell-line browser detail panel surfaces three new things:
    • Specific hotspot variants in green next to the gene symbol — e.g. "KRAS (p.G12D)" instead of just "KRAS". Most-specific call wins (p.G12D > generic p.G12).
    • New Functional loss section showing integrated LoF calls as red-bordered chips. Most importantly catches deletion-driven losses (CDKN2A homo-del in 445 lines, RB1 deep deletion, etc.) that the damaging-mutation matrix alone is blind to — LoF combines CN < 0.3, likely-LoF mutation with AF > 0.5, or expression < 0.1 log-TPM.
    • Small red MSI badge next to the cell-line ID when MSIsensor2 score ≥ 20 (74 lines).
  • CLB ? help modal updated with sections explaining the new hotspot-variant suffixes, Functional loss tier and what data sources feed it, and the MSI badge threshold.

v.77.1 (2026-04-27)

  • Clinically relevant fusions — renamed (was "Clinical Fusions" which sounded off). Tier rules refined to add soft-pass logic: a strong signal in one channel + a directionally supportive signal in the other (in correct direction at half-magnitude) now reaches high, not just both-strong. This fixes the canonical EWSR1-FLI1 lines like A-673 (exprZ=1.9 strong, depZ=−0.42 supportive) which previously landed at medium only because FLI1 is broadly used in many lineages so absolute dependency z-scores stay small even when the call is genuinely fusion-driven. Atypical-with-no-support cases (e.g. BCR-ABL1 in an Ovary line, depZ=−0.08) still land at low because the supportive threshold is not crossed. Run now: 57 high / 23 medium / 4 low (was 51 / 29 / 4).
  • Cell-line browser fusion filter dropdown now lists the clinically relevant fusion pairs first (★ BCR-ABL1 (n=11), ★ EWSR1-FLI1 (n=14), …) with live n= scaled to the active cohort filters (tissue / subtype / hotspot / etc.), followed by a separator and the existing gene-based long tail. Selecting a pair filters the cell-line list to the exact curated validated set; selecting a gene keeps the original behavior (any line with any fusion of that gene). Filter and dropdown both honour the dual lookup so the n= counts and the resulting cell-line list always agree.
  • CLB ? help modal — new section explaining what clinically relevant fusions mean, what the high/medium/low tiers are based on, why the ⚠ atypical badge appears, and what data source the calls come from.

v.77.0 (2026-04-27)

  • Clinical Fusions — new curated driver-fusion classifier. Built from a 51-fusion anchor list (BCR-ABL1, EWSR1-FLI1, EML4-ALK, PML-RARA, TMPRSS2-ERG, etc. plus 7 KMT2A partners), each entry validated per cell line with three orthogonal signals: lineage match, partner expression z-score vs lineage-matched negatives, and partner dependency (CRISPR gene effect) z-score. Tier rules consider only the signals the curator marked as informative (e.g. BCR-ABL1 doesn't elevate ABL1 mRNA, so expression isn't checked — the call rests on the strong ABL1 dependency). Lineage is a modifier not a gate: a solid call in an atypical tissue (e.g. EML4-ALK in a Bowel line with ALK exprZ=51) keeps its tier and gets an "atypical" badge instead of being hidden. Cell-line browser detail panel now shows a Clinical Fusions block with green/amber/red tier chips, and the long noisy raw fusion list (formerly the only source) is collapsed under "Show all fusions" so it doesn't dominate. New scripts/clinical_fusions_anchor.json + scripts/process_clinical_fusions.py — pipeline reads the higher-quality OmicsFusionFilteredSupplementary.csv (Arriba-annotated), filters to confidence: high and drops read-through transcripts. Output: web_data/clinical_fusions.json. First run produced 84 calls across 24 fusions: 51 high, 29 medium, 4 low; 8 atypical-lineage calls (e.g. EWSR1-FLI1 in a CNS/Brain line, EML4-ALK in a Bowel line) preserved with their tier and a flag.

v.76.6 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB cell-line list — when sorted by GE / Expression / mutation count, the inline number is now prefixed with a small gray unit tag (GE 0.45, Expr 4.12, hs 2), carries a tooltip that spells out the metric + gene(s) + direction ("negative = essential" / "higher = more expressed"), and GE values are tinted red when essential (< −0.5) or amber (< −0.2). A one-line caption above the list repeats what the numbers represent and which gene(s) they average.

v.76.5 (2026-04-24)

  • p-value added to the plot heading for the remaining two gate-comparison views — the scatter/inspect gate compare (showGateGenePlot) and the GE-inspect gate compare (showGEGateGenePlot). v.76.1 only covered the UMAP/PCA variant; the other two still showed Δ without p, which is what the latest screenshot pointed out. Mutation uses the chi² approximation already used in the gate tables; GE and expression use Welch's t-test.

v.76.4 (2026-04-24)

  • AI JSON export — rewrote aiInstructions so the assistant produces a concise one-line chart description followed by the question, instead of trying to render the embedded base64 snapshot. The previous wording encouraged pasting a Markdown image tag with the full data URI; some assistants took that literally and spewed a screen of base64 gibberish. The new instructions explicitly say the snapshot is metadata, not something to display, and give a filled-in sentence template derived from context.

v.76.3 (2026-04-24)

  • AI JSON export — the embedded aiInstructions now tells the assistant to open its reply with two explicit paragraphs: (1) "You were looking at this chart:" + the image + a plain-English sentence describing what the chart shows (derived from context: analysis type, cohort size, applied filters); (2) "You asked:" + the verbatim question, skipped if empty. Analysis only starts after those two paragraphs. Previously the instructions just said to show the image and restate the question inline, without guaranteeing the AI would describe what the figure contained.

v.76.2 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB gate-comparison Tissue / Subtissue tables now include a p-value column (2×2 χ² test of tissue presence vs gate assignment, same approximation the Mutations tab uses). The header is clickable to sort by significance and values below 0.05 are bold-weighted. Previously only mutations / diff-GE / expression tabs exposed a p-value.

v.76.1 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB UMAP / PCA gate comparison — clicking a gene in the Mutations / Diff GE / Expression tabs now shows the Welch t-test (or chi² for mutations) p-value in the plot heading alongside the Δ already there, so significance is visible without switching back to the table.
  • Fixed a silent crash in the gate-comparison GE plot (gateA.length / gateB.length were referenced but never defined in scope, throwing a ReferenceError before the title was rendered). Now reads this._umapGateA / this._umapGateB.

v.76.0 (2026-04-24)
