  • Inspect modal Genes (X/Y) row — the controls now wrap inside the box instead of pushing Find correlates outside it. Button widths reduced, the swap button sits between the X and Y fields, and the row uses flex-wrap so narrow modals stack cleanly.

v.75.9 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB PCA loadings now appear in gene-color mode too, not only when coloring by tissue / subtype. The loadings sidecar describes the PCA axes (which don't change when you recolor), so it stays useful alongside any color scheme.
  • Long gene symbols in the loadings sidecar are no longer cropped. The SVG widens based on the longest label (measured with canvas.measureText), the 182×182 axis square stays centered, and both anchor positions (start on the right, end on the left) have room to spell out the full symbol.

v.75.8 (2026-04-24)

  • Inspect / correlation browser — Update is now the primary (filled) button, the same size as Find correlates, so the main action is visually obvious.
  • New ⇄ swap button next to the gene inputs exchanges the X and Y axes (both gene symbols and the GE / Expression types) and re-renders in one click.

v.75.7 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB PCA / UMAP — the data area of the plot (not just the outer canvas) is now square. Canvas height is derived from the width minus the fixed margins, so the scatter box you see between the axes is a true square at any size. The H input is auto-synced to the computed value.

v.75.6 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB PCA / UMAP — plot area is now the same across tissue / subtype / gene-color / cluster-highlight views. The right margin is fixed at 170 px and the legend (or colorbar) is pinned at x=1.02, so toggling the coloring mode no longer resizes the main plot.
  • Gene-color colorbar title is placed above the bar (horizontal) instead of rotated on the right, and the tick font size is reduced, so long GENE_SYMBOL / Gene Effect titles no longer clip at the right edge of the figure.
  • The Color by dropdown (tissue / subtype) is now live: changing it drops any active gene-color overlay or cluster highlight and re-renders with the new grouping. Previously you had to press Clear on the gene-color row first.
  • Click-to-label and the label layer now work in gene-color mode too; previously clicking a point in gene-color view opened the cell-line detail but didn't place a label on the plot.

v.75.5 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB PCA / UMAP — clicking a point now labels that cell line on the plot (same behavior as the correlation scatter). Click again to remove the label, or use the Clear labels button that appears once at least one label is placed.
  • New Cluster stats button opens a floating panel ranking tissues (or subtypes, via the Group by selector) by mean silhouette score in the current 2D projection. Higher = tighter cluster; the bar visualizes the score on a −1 … +1 scale with the zero mark. Click any row to highlight its cells in green and render everyone else in gray; click the same row (or Clear highlight) to return to the tissue coloring.

v.75.4 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB PCA / UMAP with a custom gene list now z-scores each gene (unit variance) before the projection. Without this, a single gene with a larger dynamic range (e.g. a strong dependency at ±3 alongside a partner at ±0.5) dominated PC1/PC2 and the plot showed a perfect gradient along that gene with the rest contributing noise. Top-variance (default, no list) keeps the old unscaled behavior since those genes already have comparable magnitudes.

v.75.3 (2026-04-24)

  • CLB Dimensionality Reduction now defaults to PCA instead of UMAP.
  • New Genes input next to the method selector. If you enter a list (comma / semicolon / whitespace separated), the projection is computed from those genes only; leave it empty to keep the previous top-variance behavior. Unknown symbols are skipped silently.
  • When a custom gene list is used, a Highlight gene dropdown appears next to the Color by gene row. Pick any gene from your list to color points by that gene's GE (or Expression, when the analysis is run on expression data), without having to type the symbol back into the color-by box.

v.75.2 (2026-04-23)

  • Find correlates — r now matches the scatter r for the same pair. Two bugs were feeding the discrepancy: (1) the X-mean and X-variance were fixed over the whole filtered set, but correlation with a candidate Y was computed on the cells where that Y was valid — a classical mismatch when Y had NaNs that X didn't. Fixed by recomputing Pearson pair-completely for each candidate. (2) The starting cell-line set was _inspectFilteredCellLineIds, which also excludes cells where the previously displayed Y gene was NaN. After clicking a suggestion the scatter rebuilt with a different cell set. Fixed by taking the filter set directly from DOM with no gene-validity pre-filter.

v.75.1 (2026-04-23)

  • Correlation browser — tissue / mutation / fusion filter dropdowns are now populated and visible as soon as the modal opens (previously you had to enter genes and click Update first). Any selection you make is preserved when the plot is built.
  • Find correlates — now refreshes the filtered cell-line set at click time and falls back to computing it straight from the DOM filters when the plot hasn't been built yet. Previously it could operate on all cell lines even though you had a tissue filter selected.

v.75.0 (2026-04-23)

  • Scatter / inspect .json.gz (AI export) finally honours the inspect-modal filters. The cell-line set is pulled from _inspectFilteredCellLineIds (tissue, subtype, mutation, fusion, custom CL list all applied). The context block records each of those filters so the AI can see the cohort definition.
  • Mutation .json.gz context now also records excluded tissues, additional hotspot, oncoprint gates, and the custom cell-line list count.
  • Scatter and mutation .json.gz buttons now prompt for an optional question; previously only the gene-effect view exposed a textarea.
  • Every AI export embeds a PNG snapshot of the current chart (inspect scatter / GE) and an aiInstructions field telling the assistant to open its reply with "You were looking at this chart:" and render the image back before answering.

v.74.9 (2026-04-23)

  • Find correlates — Search field filters both lists by gene-symbol substring.
  • Find correlates — column headers are now clickable to sort. Gene toggles alphabetical asc/desc; r toggles signed desc/asc. Default sort is still |r| descending.

v.74.8 (2026-04-23)

  • Find correlates — clicking a result now preserves the inspect modal's filters (tissue / subtype / mutation / fusion / custom-CL list). Previously, selecting a suggested gene rebuilt the scatter from the main parameter filters and dropped the inspect-local ones, so the r shown on the new plot was computed on a different cell-line set and didn't match the value in the correlate list. The r now matches.

v.74.7 (2026-04-23)

  • Find correlates modal now has an |r| ≥ threshold (default 0.3) that filters both the GE and Expression lists live. Each list shows its own count (and "showing top 500" when the full set exceeds the display cap).
  • An Enrichr button next to each list sends the currently-thresholded correlates to Enrichr for pathway enrichment (GO:BP / MF / CC, KEGG, Reactome).

v.74.6 (2026-04-23)

  • CLB Export Genes CSV: dropped the Sex_expression column. The CSV now carries a single Sex column (annotated sex) alongside Tissue and Subtype.

v.74.5 (2026-04-23)

  • Correlation / cluster Export for AI now captures the filter state applied when the analysis ran — lineage, sub-lineage, excluded tissues, hotspot, fusion, oncoprint gates, selection label, and custom cell-line list — so the AI can see the cohort definition, not just the results.
  • Every Export for AI button now prompts for an optional question; the text is written into the JSON as question.
  • Every Export for AI export embeds a PNG snapshot of the current view as a data URI under snapshot, plus an aiInstructions field telling the assistant to open its reply with "You were looking at this chart:" and render the image back, then restate the question, then answer from the data.

v.74.4 (2026-04-23)

  • CLB ? help text updated with the new sort options: GE for gene(s) and Expression of gene(s). Explains that multiple gene symbols are averaged per cell line (comma / semicolon / newline / whitespace separators).
  • New Export Genes CSV button in the CLB toolbar. Prompts for one or more gene symbols and exports a tidy CSV with one row per selected cell line (or per visible cell line if nothing is selected). Columns: CellLineID, CellLineName, Tissue, Subtype, Sex_annotation, Sex_expression, GE_<gene>, Expr_<gene> — two data columns per gene.
  • New Find correlates button in the correlation / inspect scatter modal. Takes the X-axis gene (GE or Expression, as selected), applies the current inspect filters (tissue / hotspot / fusion / custom-CL), and returns two lists side-by-side: top GE correlates and top Expression correlates (|r|-sorted, n=100 each). Click any gene to set it as the Y axis with the matching data type and redraw the scatter.

v.74.3 (2026-04-23)

  • Gene Effect analysis modal can now plot expression instead of gene effect. New GE / Expression toggle next to the gene input; switching re-analyzes the current gene against the expression matrix (log2-TPM+1) and redraws the By Tissue box plot. The label, axis title, and hover read Expression in expression mode. Switching from the mutation-inspect layout to Expression falls back to the standalone view (0/1/2 stratification is tied to GE).

v.74.2 (2026-04-23)

  • Cell Line Browser sort gains two features:
    • Sort by Expression (in addition to Gene Effect). New option in the Sort dropdown; defaults to descending so highest-expressing lines surface first. Falls back to a name sort until expression data is loaded.
    • Multi-gene input — the Gene box now accepts one or more symbols (comma, semicolon, newline, or whitespace separated). Multiple genes are averaged per cell line, so you can rank cells by combined expression / dependency of a set. Useful for finding cell lines with the strongest signature across a pathway or marker panel.

v.74.1 (2026-04-23)

  • Network PNG / SVG exports now match the on-screen layout: the filter banner sits in its own header strip above the network rather than being drawn over the upper nodes. Both formats reserve a header area sized to the banner font, paint a light-gray strip with a thin separator (matching the on-screen header), center the filter text in it, and shift the network and legend down by the strip’s height so nothing overlaps. Transparent-background mode keeps just the centered banner text without the gray strip.

v.74.0 (2026-04-23)

  • Network filter banner moved out of the canvas overlay and into a dedicated header strip above the network plot. The earlier overlay kept landing on top of nodes whatever pan was applied because vis.js’s physics + fit re-centered the layout. With a strip outside the canvas, the network has the full plot area and the banner is unambiguously above it. PNG / SVG exports still draw the filter text inline at the top of the figure (no change to the export look).

v.73.9 (2026-04-23)

  • Correlation scatter highlights are no longer an unreadable blob when many cell lines are selected. Two-tier behavior: when up to 12 cells are highlighted, each is labeled with just its name (lineage dropped from the label, since it’s already in the hover); when more than 12, the per-point labels are dropped entirely — the orange markers stay, hover still shows each name, and a small caption pinned in the upper-left says “● N cell lines highlighted (hover to see names)”.

v.73.8 (2026-04-23)

  • Curated-collection descriptions rewritten to be honest about what each set captures and what it doesn’t. Each entry now has a structured Inclusion / Mechanism / Caveat block with the explicit gene panel, the biology, and the limitations (e.g. SWI/SNF-deficient now scoped specifically to the BAF/PBAF complex subunits, with a caveat that the broader chromatin machinery — histone writers/readers/erasers, DNMTs, etc. — is not captured). Categories also tightened: “Chromatin” → “Chromatin remodelling — SWI/SNF complex”; “DNA repair” split into “mismatch repair” and “homologous recombination”; “Breast subtype” → “Breast — receptor subtype” with explicit “approximate” tags reminding the reader that transcript-based receptor calls are not clinical IHC/FISH.

v.73.7 (2026-04-23)

  • Network filter banner pan: the previous offset was being reset by a fit() call inside the stabilization callback. Moved the pan into the same callback, after the fit, so the top nodes really do drop below the banner now.
  • Clicking a correlation row from the CLB inspect-correlations modal now also pre-populates the scatter’s highlight list with the selected cell-line names — so the cells driving the result show up labeled in red on the correlation scatter, set against the rest of the dataset.

v.73.6 (2026-04-23)

  • Network filter banner cleaned up. When the analysis was launched from a CLB selection, the trailing “n=1186” (the full dataset size) used to appear after the “Selection (58 cell lines)” tag, contradicting it. Suppressed when a selection label is present, since the count is already in the label.
  • Banner now sits a bit lower with an opaque white background and a subtle shadow so it doesn’t blend into the network. The network view also pans down ~40 px after the initial physics settle, giving the top nodes breathing room below the banner.

v.73.5 (2026-04-23)

  • Selection-Inspect (GE / Correlations) results can now be saved to a JSON file and re-opened later — no more losing a 5–10 minute correlation run if you wanted to look at a different pair afterwards. Save button appears in the modal header once results are computed; Open Saved Inspect button next to the Inspect Correlations button on the CLB toolbar pops a file picker, restores the result table, and re-wires all interactivity (sort, cutoff, Network, Enrichr).
  • Clicking a correlation row in Inspect Correlations used to close the inspect modal AND open the correlation popup behind the Cell Line Browser, leaving it invisible. Two fixes: the inspect modal now stays open (it's still useful), and the correlation popup z-index was raised above the CLB so it surfaces on top.

v.73.4 (2026-04-23)

  • Curated collections dropdown moved to its own row below the main CLB toolbar with a ? info button that opens a reference modal listing each collection’s inclusion criteria + current dataset count. Adding / editing collections in the catalog automatically updates both the dropdown and the reference modal.
  • Sex filter split into By annotation (Male / Female / Unknown) and By expression (Male / Female / Unknown) option groups. Each gets a live count under the current filter intersection. Previously “Unknown” collapsed the two axes together, hiding that many cell lines are annotation-called but expression-unconfirmed (or vice versa).
  • Inspect Gene Effects overhauled:
    • Row count now configurable (default 200, up to 2000 per side) via a Top N input.
    • Sortable columns — click any header to sort ascending / descending. Headers and numeric columns are centered; Gene column stays left-aligned.
    • Per-side |Δ| cutoff input filters the table instantly. Right side defaults to |Δ| ≥ 0.1.
    • Per-side Network button — prompts for r cutoff, then builds a correlation network from the currently-displayed genes restricted to the selected cell lines. Same flow as the Inspect Correlations network button.

v.73.3 (2026-04-23)

  • Inspect Correlations: refactored the inner loop. The previous implementation did a full first pass to build the top-r-in-selected list, then a second pass that recomputed the same values while also computing r-in-rest. Now it’s a single pass that emits both top lists in one go. Baseline changed from selected vs rest to selected vs all cells; the all-cells centered-vector matrix is cached on the instance so subsequent inspect runs skip that setup entirely. Warning updated to be honest about cost: up to 5–10 minutes on a typical laptop.
  • Clicking a gene pair in the inspect-correlations results used to require an analysis to have been run already (the old path tried to find the pair in this.results.correlations and silently failed when it wasn’t there). Now it opens the correlation inspect directly with a synthetic correlation stub — always works.
  • Clicking a gene in Inspect Gene Effects now highlights the selected cell lines in the By-Tissue box plot in red with a larger marker and a dark outline, so you can see where the selected lines fall within each tissue. The subtitle picks up a small “● N selected cell lines highlighted” note. Highlight clears when you close the GE modal.

v.73.2 (2026-04-23)

  • CLB dropdowns now show n=X per option with live scaling to all active filters — the Sex dropdown and Curated collections dropdown are now joined to the tissue / subtype / hotspot / fusion / custom-CL filter state (previously only tissue / subtype / hotspot / fusion had live counts). Counts exclude the dropdown’s own selection when computing its labels so switching is predictable.
  • Inspect Correlations: each column gets an |r| ≥ / |Δ| ≥ cutoff input and a Network button. Typing in the cutoff filters the table instantly (no recompute). Clicking Network prompts for a cutoff, pulls the genes from pairs above the cutoff, populates the main gene list + the current selection as a custom cell-line filter, and runs the analysis — yielding a correlation network of those gene pairs restricted to the selected cell lines.
  • Removed the now-redundant Transparent background checkbox from the Network export sidebar. The publication-quality export dialog asks about background when you click Export, so the separate checkbox was duplicative.

v.73.1 (2026-04-23)

  • Two new buttons in the Cell Line Browser toolbar: Inspect Gene Effects and Inspect Correlations, operating on the currently-selected cell lines.
    • Inspect Gene Effects — fast (< 1 s for typical selections). Two panels: most depleted in selection (lowest mean GE) and largest Δ vs the rest (most differentially essential). Click a row to open Gene Effect inspect for that gene.
    • Inspect Correlations — unbiased all-vs-all Pearson correlation across the selection. Shows a size estimate + confirmation first; during compute a progress bar with ETA and a Cancel button. Two panels: strongest pair correlations in the selection and largest Δr (selection r − rest r). Click a row to open the correlation inspect for that gene pair.
    Helpers _showProgress / _hideProgress wrap a generic cancellable progress overlay that’s ready for future long-running analyzes.

v.73.0 (2026-04-23)

  • Cell Line Browser gains a Curated collections dropdown next to Tissue / Subtype. Multi-gene / phenotype groups that aren’t well served by a single-gene filter:
    • DNA repair: MMR-deficient (MSI-high), HR-deficient (BRCAness)
    • Mutation burden: Hypermutated (top decile)
    • Chromatin: SWI/SNF-deficient
    • Oxidative-stress: NRF2-activated
    • Expression signature: Neuroendocrine phenotype, EMT-high
    • Breast subtype: Triple-negative (TNBC), HR+ (luminal), HER2+ — calls are relative to breast-only thresholds
    Memberships computed at load (mutation-based ones) and on expression-data load (signature / breast-subtype ones). Dropdown shows live count per collection and is grouped by category. (Inspect correlations / gene effects buttons for selected cell lines coming next.)

v.72.5 (2026-04-23)

  • Export dialog gains three size presets — Small (5 cm), Medium (10 cm), Large (15 cm) — that set the width and auto-scale the height from the on-screen plot aspect. New Lock aspect checkbox (default on): when enabled, using +/− on Width or Height rescales the other dimension to preserve the plot aspect, so the figure doesn’t stretch accidentally.

v.72.4 (2026-04-22)

  • Default export DPI raised from 300 to 600; max raised to 2400. Step is now 100 (with the −/+ buttons). The hint reads “300 = screen / draft; 600 = print; 1200+ = high-quality print”. Existing exports were noticeably soft because the network is rasterised from a DOM canvas at screen density.
  • Network legend frame is now opt-in. The faint gray box around the bottom legend is gone by default; the dialog gains a checkbox Draw a thin frame around the legend for users who want it back. Same toggle works for both PNG and SVG network exports.

v.72.3 (2026-04-22)

  • Number boxes throughout the UI now have − / + step buttons on either side (matching the Plot Size / Axis Ranges pattern in the inspect modal). Wired up to: Min Cell Lines on the main page, Highlight / Color font size in the inspect modal, Min n in the Gene Effect modal, the export-options Width / Height / DPI fields, and the UMAP/PCA Width / Height. Backed by a new app.adjustNumber(id, delta) helper that respects each input’s min/max/step and fires change events so re-renders run as expected.
  • Default Highlight / Color font size in the inspect modal raised from 3 to 5 for better readability.
  • Inspect (correlation) modal no longer closes on backdrop click or on Escape — same exit-safety policy as the Cell Line Browser. The X in the upper-right is the only exit; otherwise typed input or a stray click could lose all filter / gate / highlight state.

v.72.2 (2026-04-22)

  • Publication-quality export dialog now appears for every chart export, not just the Plotly-based ones. Added to the inspect scatter (was missing), the network PNG, the network SVG, and the UMAP/PCA export. Each respects the chosen size, DPI, and background; PNG outputs include the pHYs chunk so Word / Office / LaTeX honour the physical size, and SVG outputs use cm units on the outer tag.
  • Removed the “Solid white is recommended for PowerPoint / PDF…” line from the export dialog — the app is for general use and shouldn’t recommend specific downstream tools.

v.72.1 (2026-04-22)

  • “Adjust graph size with Width/Height sliders…” hint under the Gene Effect chart is now hidden whenever the sliders themselves are hidden (By Tissue overview + By Hotspot scan). It only appears in the detailed tissue view and Hotspot Mutation Inspect where the sliders actually exist.

v.72.0 (2026-04-22)

  • Clicking any chart PNG / SVG Export button now opens a publication-quality export dialog. Defaults: width 5 cm, height auto-scaled to preserve the on-screen aspect ratio, 300 DPI for PNG, and solid white background. Width / height / DPI / background are editable per export; the last chosen values are remembered for the session.
  • PNG export now honours the chosen DPI: the canvas is sized to widthCm × dpi / 2.54 px, and a pHYs chunk is written into the PNG so Word / PowerPoint / LaTeX place the image at its real physical size instead of the default 96-DPI guess.
  • SVG export sets absolute cm units on the outer <svg> tag so downstream tools (Illustrator, Inkscape) open at the intended print size.
  • Transparent backgrounds are opt-in — default is solid white. This fixes the faint edge lines that appeared when transparent PNGs were pasted into PowerPoint and then exported to PDF (alpha-edge compositing artifact).

v.71.3 (2026-04-22)

  • Caution banners in Hotspot Mutation Inspect, the By Hotspot scan, and the correlation-analysis mutation view now add a concrete recommendation: For meaningful analysis, narrow down using the All tissues and subtype filters above so WT and mutated cell lines come from the same cancer context. (Previously only warned about the confound, without telling the user what to do.)

v.71.2 (2026-04-22)

  • “Draw rectangles on plot to define gates” status text now lives inside the Gates group span, so it hides together with the gate buttons in By Tissue and By Hotspot views (where gates aren’t available) and only shows in Hotspot Mutation Inspect.

v.71.1 (2026-04-21)

  • Swept all chart exports in V2 through a single helper (_exportPlotly → _expandSvgToContent) so every PNG/SVG download now matches the on-screen plot and never crops content. Previously 6 separate export functions each had their own “Plotly.toImage → blob → canvas” pipeline (upset plot direct-PNG from Plotly, correlation analysis by tissue/hotspot, tissue by-gene chart, expression-correlate scatter, gene-effect chart, mutation-inspect chart) — some missed viewBox expansion and the upset-PNG path skipped SVG entirely. All now: match _fullLayout dimensions, get SVG from Plotly, measure true content bbox, expand viewBox, then either serialize (SVG) or rasterise at 2× (PNG). Removes hundreds of duplicated lines.

v.71.0 (2026-04-21)

  • Gene Effect chart PNG / SVG export now matches the on-screen plot exactly. Previous code forced a minimum height of 650 / 550 + 40 “for safety” which stretched the exported plot taller than it appears on screen, and still cropped the stats annotations below the box plot (the Skin p-value line was cut off in the last report). The new path uses _fullLayout.width / height as rendered (which already includes Plotly’s reserved bottom margin for annotations), then runs a post-pass _expandSvgToContent helper that measures the true content bounding box and enlarges the viewBox so nothing outside the nominal figure gets cropped. Applies to both formats.

v.70.9 (2026-04-21)

  • Gates are now Mutation-Inspect only. The root problem: when a gate rectangle was drawn on the By Tissue box plot, the filtering code silently ignored the Y axis (_geGatePlotData is only populated for the mutation-inspect scatter) and matched cells across all tissues at the same gene-effect level — so a rectangle around 10 cells in one tissue returned hundreds of cells across all of them. The Gates UI now only appears in Mutation Inspect view, where the 2D rectangle is meaningful (gene effect × 0/1/2 mutation level). Switching to By Tissue or By Hotspot hides the group and clears any active gates.

v.70.8 (2026-04-21)

  • GE gate buttons: the Compare button sometimes stayed hidden after both gates were drawn. Cause: the show-handler set style.display = '' which clears the inline style but lets the stylesheet default take over, and in some render paths that default was resolving to none before the inline-flex parent recomputed. Set display: inline-block explicitly for both the Compare and Clear buttons on gate creation so they always show.

v.70.7 (2026-04-21)

  • By Hotspot scan: clicking a hotspot-gene row now hands off directly to Hotspot Mutation Inspect with that gene pre-selected (0/1/2 plot in the full mutation-analysis inspect layout), instead of rendering the old separate detailed graph. Same data, more useful chrome (compare buttons, custom exports, filter context).
  • Hotspot Mutation Inspect now shows the same caution banner that the By Hotspot scan has: hotspot mutations are often enriched in specific cancer types, so GE differences can reflect lineage rather than the mutation itself.
  • Δ Tissue / Δ Hotspot / Δ Fusion compare buttons moved from row 2 (Filters) to row 3 (View + Gates), appearing after the Gates group. They’re compare actions that only show in Mutation Inspect mode, so grouping them with the view / gate actions fits better than living in the filter row.

v.70.6 (2026-04-21)

  • In Gene Effect → By Tissue, clicking the pinned All row at the top of the stats table now returns to the all-tissues overview when a specific tissue is currently focused (previously the “All” row was inert). The hover title reads “Click to return to the all-tissues overview.” Any active filters stay applied.

v.70.5 (2026-04-21)

  • Gene-Effect modal toolbar reorganized. Row 2 is now a dedicated “Filters:” row (mirroring the “Gene Effect:” legend on row 1), ending at the compare buttons. Row 3 is a dedicated “View:” row with the three mode buttons + “Gates:” group — so view buttons and gate buttons always sit together regardless of window width (no more wrapping apart).
  • Third view button renamed from “Mutation Inspect” to Hotspot Mutation Inspect to make clear it’s specifically the hotspot-mutation 0/1/2 stratification (not any mutation type).
  • Hotspot-gene selector (the one next to Analyze, which sets the Y-axis stratification gene) now shows the mutation count per gene under the currently-active filters — e.g. TP53 (88 mut). Options are also sorted descending by count so the most-informative genes surface first. Label changed to Hotspot mutation (Y):.

v.70.4 (2026-04-21)

  • Mutation Inspect refined. Only the mutation-analysis inspect’s existing hotspot-gene selector (the one next to Analyze) is shown now — the extra dropdown next to the View toggle was redundant. Clicking Mutation Inspect defaults the hotspot gene to TP53 (or the first available one) and hands off to the full mutational-analysis layout; change the stratifying gene in the selector next to the plot. The View toggle (By Tissue / By Hotspot / Mutation Inspect) now stays visible in all three states so the user can switch back to the standalone views from Mutation Inspect without closing the modal.

v.70.3 (2026-04-20)

  • Third Gene-Effect view renamed to Mutation Inspect and reworked to reuse the existing mutational-analysis inspect layout instead of a separate simplified plot. Clicking Mutation Inspect surfaces a hotspot-gene picker; picking a gene bootstraps a minimal mutation-analysis context on the fly and hands off to showGeneEffectDistribution — the resulting view is identical to the Inspect opened from a mutation-analysis results table (full-width chart, hotspot / fusion filters, Δ Tissue / Δ Hotspot / Δ Fusion compare buttons, custom export). Clicking By Tissue or By Hotspot from that state cleanly restores the standalone GE layout. By Hotspot (scan) label reverted to By Hotspot now that the three views are clearly distinct. Removed the v.70.2 stand-alone “By Mutation” box plot (duplicated what mutation-analysis inspect already does better).

v.70.2 (2026-04-20)

  • Gene Effect inspect gains a third view: By Mutation. Pick a hotspot-mutated gene from the dropdown and the plot stratifies the current gene’s effect by 0 / 1 / 2 mutation levels of that gene — the same view you get from “Inspect” in a mutation-analysis result table, now reachable from the standalone GE inspect. Rolled back v.70.1’s attempt to share the toggle with the mutation-analysis inspect (“By Hotspot” means subtly different things there, which was more confusing than helpful). “By Hotspot” renamed to “By Hotspot (scan)” in the standalone inspect to make its scan-table semantics explicit. Mutation-analysis inspect is back to its original chromeless look.

v.70.1 (2026-04-20)

  • Mutational-analysis inspect and gene-effect inspect are now the same modal with a stratify toggle. Previously they were two separate entry points (“Inspect” in the mutation-analysis results vs. clicking a gene name elsewhere) that looked similar but showed subtly different views — a recurring source of confusion. Now the mutation-analysis inspect keeps the existing By Hotspot look and feel (0/1/2 level plot, compare buttons, exports) but exposes the existing By Tissue | By Hotspot toggle, so the user can flip the stratification axis without leaving the mutation-analysis context. Switching to By Tissue re-plots the same gene grouped by lineage while keeping the mutation-analysis filters (lineage filter, excluded tissues, subLineage filter) in effect. Switching back to By Hotspot returns to the mutation-stratified plot exactly as before.

v.70.0 (2026-04-20)

  • Cell Line Browser is now exit-safe. Previously a stray click on the dark backdrop or an Esc keystroke (e.g. while dismissing a gene tooltip) closed the whole browser, taking all filters, selections, and the current inspect state with it. The X in the upper-right corner is now the only exit path. Other dialogs that are cheap to reopen (Aa text settings, help popovers, etc.) still dismiss on outside click / Esc as before. Same change applied to V1 and CoExpress.

v.69.9 (2026-04-20)

  • Escape on a pinned gene tooltip was bubbling up and closing the Cell Line Browser (and any other modal that listens for Esc). The tooltip now intercepts Escape in the capture phase, stops propagation, and only dismisses itself — the underlying modal stays open. Ported to V1 and CoExpress as well.

v.69.8 (2026-04-20)

  • Gene hover tooltip now carries links and supports Shift-to-pin. Every tooltip has a small footer with a direct NCBI Gene ↗ link (and HGNC when available) so the source of the summary is always one click away. Shift-hover (or press Shift while a quick tooltip is showing) pins the tooltip: it widens, shows the full untruncated summary, gets a close button and a green border, and stays open until you press Esc or click outside. Non-pinned tooltips still fade on mouseleave as before.

v.69.7 (2026-04-20)

  • UMAP/PCA hover tooltip: &middot; HTML entities were leaking through as literal text because Plotly’s hover renderer doesn’t parse named entities. Replaced with the actual Unicode middle-dot (·). The “click to inspect” hint was also a washed-out gray that didn’t read against the tooltip background — now shown in italic at the default tooltip text color so it’s clearly visible.

v.69.6 (2026-04-20)

  • PCA loadings sidecar now top-aligns with the plot. The “Loadings (top 8)” header sits at the same vertical position as the Plotly plot title, so the two axes boxes share a common top border.
  • PNG and SVG export now include the loadings graph when it’s visible. The plot SVG and the loadings SVG are composed into a single outer SVG (plot on the left, title + loadings on the right), then downloaded as SVG or rasterised to PNG at 2x. Previously the loadings were on screen only.
  • New button under the plot: Select in list above. After lassoing a cluster, press it to tick those cell lines in the browser list — they then flow into Export GE and Full Data Export. Pairs naturally with the existing Copy selected.
  • PNG, SVG and Aa buttons moved from the “Display” row (row 2) to the main Run/Reset row (row 1), with a small divider between them and the colored action buttons. They’re less buried now.

v.69.5 (2026-04-20)

  • UMAP/PCA point hover tooltip rebalanced. Instead of just “Hotspot mutations: N” (which on its own said little about genetic complexity), hover now shows Hotspot N · Damaging N · Fusions N side-by-side, so one glance compares the three mutation axes. A small “click to inspect” hint is also added.
  • Clicking a point in the plot now opens the inspect panel for that cell line (same as clicking its row in the list above). The matching list entry is scrolled into view and highlighted, so you can jump straight into the Wiki, gene lists, etc. for any cell line you spot on the plot.

v.69.4 (2026-04-20)

  • Short explainer added above the Lasso select / Copy selected buttons under the UMAP/PCA plot: draw a lasso on the plot to pick a cluster of cell lines, then copy their names for downstream use (paste into Custom CLs above, a new session, or a spreadsheet). Both buttons also gained descriptive tooltips.

v.69.3 (2026-04-20)

  • Dimensionality-reduction tissue dropdown gains a new top option: “Visible in list above (n=X)”. Pick it to project only the cell lines currently rendered in the Cell Line Browser list — so whatever you’ve filtered upstairs (search, custom CLs, mutation state, subtype, …) drives the UMAP/PCA directly. The count stays in sync with the list above, and selecting it hides the subtype dropdown (it would be meaningless against an arbitrary cell-line set). Default selection on open.

v.69.2 (2026-04-20)

  • UMAP/PCA plot defaults to 500 × 500 (square) instead of 580 × 480, so the scaleanchor-constrained axes don’t leave awkward dead space.
  • PCA loadings moved from a floating inset to a proper sidecar next to the main plot, labeled “Loadings (top 8)”. Size bumped 30% (140 px → 182 px) with correspondingly bigger gene labels and axis tags. No more accidental cover-up of the PCA scatter.

v.69.1 (2026-04-20)

  • Dimensionality-reduction control panel reorganized from six ragged rows into three aligned ones. Row 1 is the compute inputs (method, data, tissue, subtype, color-by, Run, Reset); row 2 is display (axes, dot size, width/height, PNG/SVG/Aa/Top-Genes/Loadings); row 3 is overlays (Color-by-gene, Split, Gate-Compare). All controls share a common 24 px height with a consistent 11 px font, group dividers between related button clusters, and a flex-spacer that pushes Run/Reset to the right so the eye can find them in a fixed place
  • Default UMAP/PCA dot size bumped from 6 to 9 so cell lines are visible without reaching for the size slider
  • Fixed: splitting by mutation and then pressing Clear left the right-hand WT and Mutated panels on screen as ghosts. _renderUmapPlot now purges the child Plotly instances and wipes the plot container before re-rendering the single-panel view

v.69.0 (2026-04-20)

  • Cell-line inspect panel reorganized for readability. Subtype and other long values no longer run flush against their labels on wrap (fixed with proper right-alignment and a label gap). Wiki deep-dive button moved to the top of the panel so it’s visible before scrolling. Hotspot, Damaging and Fusion gene lists now show the first 10 cancer-panel genes (bold) with a Show all toggle for the rest — Jurkat’s 658 damaging mutations and 48 fusions no longer dominate the panel. Gene Effect section separated from the mutation block by a thin divider and relabeled (“Gene Effects” with Genes scored / Mean / Range), which keeps Most Depleted and Most Enriched as clear sub-sections underneath. Removed the redundant “Cell Line Detail Report” CSV button (the Wiki already covers this and now has a Download button that saves a standalone, styled HTML file per cell line).
  • Version scheme switched to single-decimal (v.69.0, v.69.1 … v.69.9, v.70.0). Small changes bump the tenths digit, large changes bump the integer.

v.68.02 (2026-04-19)

  • Pathway-scan section in the Mutation profile clarified. The intro now states explicitly that the scan is based on mutation calls only (copy-number, fusions and expression are excluded); drops the inaccurate "hotspot = oncogenic / damaging = tumor suppressor" shorthand; and explains the asterisk (gene carries both a hotspot and a damaging mutation). Pathway rows restructured so the name, plain-English description, and gene list each sit on their own line, with a clear "Mutated genes in panel:" label before the tags so the genes no longer run on directly after the description. Cryptic shorthand like "RTK (receptor tyr kinase) — receptor TKI targets — check amplification / fusion" is replaced with full sentences, e.g. a note on receptor tyrosine kinases explaining that the mutation panel misses amplifications and fusions — common driver mechanisms for this pathway — so a clean panel does not rule it out

v.67.92 (2026-04-19)

  • New Pathway status (genotype + dependency) sub-section in the Mutation profile. For 5 clinically-important pathways (p53, RB / cell cycle, RAS-MAPK, PI3K/AKT, EGFR + BCR-ABL when relevant) it combines mutation status with CRISPR knockout gene-effect to infer whether the pathway is functionally active. Catches the common mismatch where a TP53-wild-type cell line shows neutral TP53 knockout (pathway dormant despite WT genotype), or where TP53-WT cells with positive TP53 gene-effect are actively restraining growth and become MDM2-inhibitor candidates. Each card shows genotype, the relevant gene-effect read-outs, and a one-line interpretation

v.67.82 (2026-04-19)

  • Mutation-profile flags turned into titled cards instead of a running block of colored pills. Each flag now has a short clear title ("Mismatch repair is broken", "Very high mutation burden", "TP53 is mutated", "G1/S cell-cycle brake lost", etc.) with a one-line plain-English explanation of what it means and why it matters. Much easier to scan

v.67.72 (2026-04-19)

  • Mutation-section intro corrected: hotspots aren’t exclusively oncogenic-driver positions — they include recurrent tumor-suppressor mutations too (TP53 R175H, R248Q are classic hotspots but inactivate a tumor suppressor). New wording covers both cases

v.67.62 (2026-04-19)

  • Subtype-hallmarks phrasing tightened: "Altered hallmark genes (N of M)" / "Hallmark genes without detected alterations: ...". Previous phrasing was ambiguous ("not detected") or over-explained

v.67.52 (2026-04-19)

  • First pass at clarifying hallmark phrasing

v.67.42 (2026-04-19)

  • Sex section rephrased: "annotation" / "annotated male" instead of "patient records say" (we never access patient records directly — we use the sex annotation supplied with the cell line)

v.67.32 (2026-04-19)

  • Drug bullets now show a plain-English viability score ("kills most cells / kills many / modest killing / little effect") alongside the AUC number. Hover on the AUC value shows a tooltip explaining what AUC is
  • Oncotree code in Classification is now a clickable link that opens Oncotree's page for the specific code, so users can see where this disease sits in the hierarchy

v.67.31 (2026-04-19)

  • Wiki rewrite: plainer English, acronyms spelled out (MMR → mismatch repair, HR → homologous recombination, TSG → tumor suppressor gene, ICB → checkpoint immunotherapy, MSI → microsatellite instability). Generic phrasing throughout (no brand-name references). Each section gets a one-line intro in plain language explaining what it shows
  • Authentication section now embeds the actual STR reference profile for the cell line (parsed from Cellosaurus for 1105/1186 cell lines). Table shows expected alleles at each marker — the core ANSI/ATCC 9-marker panel plus extended markers. Users can compare lab-report numbers directly against this table
  • Offline pipeline: new scripts/extract_str_profiles.py parses the Cellosaurus flat-file dump and merges STR profiles into cellLineMetadata.json

v.67.30 (2026-04-19)

  • Cell Line Wiki: new Drug response section (DepMap PRISM Repurposing Secondary, 25Q2). Curated panel of 89 clinically or mechanistically relevant compounds with editorial target / MOA / indication annotations. For each cell line shows: Standout sensitive compounds (z < −1 vs the panel mean), Standout resistant (z > +1), and Context-aware cross-checks that cross-reference mutations/fusions/lineage already detected in the wiki (BRAF-mut → BRAFi/MEKi, EGFR-mut → EGFR TKI, ALK fusion → ALK inhibitors, BCR-ABL → ABL TKI, HR-deficient → PARP, TP53-WT → MDM2, CDKN2A loss → CDK4/6, Lymphoid → BCR/BCL2 axis). Offline pipeline: new scripts/process_drug_response.py + web_data/drug_response.json (1.1 MB)

v.67.29 (2026-04-19)

  • Cell Line Wiki: added a Subtype hallmarks section. Curated knowledge base of ~30 Oncotree subtypes (CLL, Burkitt Lymphoma, DLBCL GCB/ABC, MCL, FL, Hairy-Cell Leukaemia, Plasma Cell Myeloma, B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, Hodgkin Lymphoma, Plasmablastic Lymphoma, Melanoma, Lung Adeno/Squamous, Colon, Breast, HGSOC, PDAC, GBM, Prostate, Bladder, HCC, Ewing, Osteosarcoma, ccRCC) with expected mutations/fusions per subtype. Green box shows hallmarks observed in the cell line, blue box shows what's typical, red box flags when zero canonical hallmarks are seen (possible atypical driver or misidentified cell line)
  • Cell Line Wiki: added Pathway scan in the Mutation profile. 14 cancer pathways × ~90 curated genes (p53/apoptosis, cell cycle/RB, RAS-MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, RTK, WNT, MYC/MAX, SWI-SNF, epigenetic writers, HR/FA, MMR, NOTCH, hematopoietic TFs, telomere). Each pathway shows which genes are hit (hotspot in red, damaging in amber)
  • Cell Line Wiki: new flags — HR-deficient (PARP-inhibitor candidate), TP53 mutant, cell-cycle checkpoint loss (RB1 or CDKN2A)
  • GE signature turned interpretive: druggable dependencies (top-essential genes that have approved/clinical inhibitors, ~60-gene curated panel, highlighted purple with 💊 marker), pathway dependencies (top-essential genes grouped by cancer pathway), tumor-suppressor-positive-on-KO flag (canonical TSGs scoring positive on knockout indicates they're still functional)
  • Expression signature turned interpretive: per-lineage marker panels (e.g. Lymphoid: CD19/MS4A1/CD79A/PAX5/CD3D/CD8A…; Breast: ESR1/PGR/ERBB2/FOXA1/GATA3…), highly-expressed druggable targets flagged

v.67.28 (2026-04-19)

  • New Cell line Wiki modal (button in the CLB detail panel). Sections: Classification (Oncotree subtype/code + PatientSubtypeFeatures — exposes CLL/Burkitt/DLBCL/MCL etc. under Lymphoid), Patient/tumor origin (age, race, primary/metastasis, collection site, grade, growth pattern, engineered model), Sex deep-dive with Y-loss / XIST-silencing reasoning, Mutation profile with MMR-deficiency and hypermutation flags, Fusion profile with caveat for counts >30 (hypermutated / chromothripsis artifacts), GE signature (top essential / enriched), Expression signature (top expressed, XIST, Y-mean), STR authentication explainer (ANSI/ATCC 9-marker + Promega PowerPlex 16 panel, Cellosaurus reference profiles), and outbound links to DepMap Portal, Cellosaurus, COSMIC, PubMed, ATCC
  • Every section carries a Source citation line. No live scraping — outbound links only
  • web_data/cellLineMetadata.json enriched via new scripts/enrich_cellline_metadata.py with 14 new per-cell-line fields from Model 25Q3 (age, ageCategory, patientRace, primaryOrMetastasis, sampleCollectionSite, growthPattern, patientTumorGrade, depmapModelType, oncotreeSubtype, oncotreeCode, patientSubtypeFeatures, rrid, engineeredModel, culturedResistanceDrug)

v.67.11 (2026-04-18)

  • Gene Effect mutation-inspect view: title no longer clips at narrow widths or with long gene names. Canvas measureText checks whether the title fits at 25 px bold; if not, wraps greedily at word boundaries; if still too wide, steps font size down to a minimum of 12 px. Preserves user drag positions via _geUserTitlePos

v.67.10 (2026-04-18)

  • Gene Effect mutation-inspect view: y-axis label no longer overlaps tick labels. Left margin and label x-position are now computed from Canvas measureText of the widest tick label (e.g. "0/WT (n=1059)"), so the label always sits just left of the ticks regardless of width-slider value or tick-content length. User drag positions still respected via _geUserYLabelPos

v.67.5 (2026-04-18)

  • Sex-by-expression classifier now uses independent Y-marker and XIST thresholds (Y>1.0 → male; XIST>1.0 with Y low → female). Earlier score-based threshold required XIST to be extremely high, causing many XIST-silenced female cancers (esp. breast) to fall into Unknown
  • Breast cancer cell lines called female by expression: 26/53 (was 15/53)
  • DepMap-female cell lines correctly identified: 54% (was 34%)
  • Note: XIST-silenced breast cancers (27/53) still land in Unknown — this is a biological limitation of expression-based sex inference

Loading data...

Cell-line data: DepMap 26Q1

  • CRISPRGeneEffect.csv (gene effects)
  • OmicsExpressionTPMLogp1HumanProteinCodingGenes.csv (expression)
  • OmicsSomaticMutationsMatrixHotspot.csv / Damaging.csv (mutations)
  • OmicsFusionFiltered{Supplementary}.csv (fusions, Arriba)
  • OmicsInferredMolecularSubtypes.csv (specific variants, integrated LoF, MSI)
  • OmicsGlobalSignatures.csv (WGD, ploidy, CIN, aneuploidy)
  • Model.csv (cell-line metadata)
  • PRISM Repurposing Secondary (drug response, curated panel of ~90 compounds)
  • OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv / OmicsCNGene.csv (full gene-level copy number, all genes; WGS-derived calls first, with the 24Q4 gene matrix filling in lines never WGS'd)

Pathway / complex memberships

  • CORUM (manually curated mammalian protein complexes; ~5,000 human genes)
  • Reactome (curated human pathways & signaling cascades; pathways of size 5–100)
  • Curated cancer-pathway and complex KBs (in-app)

Annotations curated for Correlate

Data layers we assembled while building the app, by combining and re-analysing the sources named on each line. They are not taken ready-made from any one database.

  • Clinically relevant fusions (51 driver fusions + 7 KMT2A partners, drawn from COSMIC; each call validated per cell line)
  • Subtype hallmarks KB (expected driver alterations per cancer type, compiled from the WHO Classification of Tumours 5th ed. 2022, COSMIC, OncoKB and NCCN guidelines; ~40 Oncotree subtypes)
  • Lehmann TNBC subtypes (Lehmann JCI 2011 + 2016 update; BL1/BL2/IM/M/MSL/LAR for ~22 TNBC lines)
  • Focal CN events (curated panel of ~32 amps + ~14 extended TSG deletions; from OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv)
  • HLA copy number (extracted from OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv; B2M-normalized to control for HLA-C mapping bias)
  • Retroelement signal (how much LINE-1, HERV-K and SVA RNA each cell line makes. We downloaded the raw RNA sequencing of these cell lines from the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE, the Broad project behind DepMap), took the reads that map uniquely to one of 750 full-length retroelement copies lying outside genes, and counted them per line, scaled to reads per million. 669 of the 1,208 lines have public sequencing to do this with)
  • Interferon score (computed in-app: mean z-score of 34 interferon-stimulated genes from the expression matrix)
  • STR profiles (Cellosaurus reference panels)
  • Published fusion calls (Cellosaurus; fills in cell lines with no RNA-seq, and recurrent driver fusions the caller did not report)
  • Problematic cell lines (Cellosaurus; contaminated / misidentified / misclassified flags, 56 lines in this panel)
  • Viral transformation (Cellosaurus Transformant records; 53 lines in this panel are confirmed transformed by EBV, HPV16/18, HBV, KSHV or HTLV-1. A line without a record has not been recorded, which is not the same as being free of the virus)

If you publish results from Correlate, please acknowledge DepMap, which the screening, sequencing and molecular data come from. The annotation layers have their own sources: if your figures lean on one, also cite the resource behind it: CORUM or Reactome for complex and pathway memberships, COSMIC for fusion and hallmark curation, and Cellosaurus (Bairoch A. J Biomol Tech 2018) for cell-line identity, fusion and provenance records.

How Correlate Works

Multi-omics analysis of human cancer cell lines, built around CRISPR screens

What is Correlate?

Correlate is an analysis platform built around CRISPR knockout screens of more than 1,100 human cancer cell lines (DepMap), and it integrates multi-omics data for the same lines, mRNA expression, hotspot mutations, driver fusions and copy number. Two tools cover the main uses: Gene set analysis to discover and present the connections within a gene set and extend it into wider networks, and the Cell Line Browser to identify cell lines with the features a project needs. Outside tools are integrated for further analysis: any gene list can be sent to Enrichr for pathway enrichment, and every view has an Export for AI that packages its data and settings into one file an AI assistant can analyse. Every view also carries a Methods button beside its export buttons: it writes out how the picture on screen was made, as one paragraph ready for a materials and methods section and as a longer plain-language walk-through, both read from the view exactly as it stands.

Two Tools

🕸 Gene set analysis

Paste a gene set (screen hits, a pathway, a complex) and see how its members connect: pairwise correlations of knockout fitness drawn as an interactive network, with clusters, statistics and per-pair scatter plots. Expand my set reaches beyond the input to discover new correlated partners, extending the set into a wider network.

📊 Cell Line Browser

Find human cell lines with the features that matter for a project: filter by tissue, disease, sex, mutations, fusions, copy number, expression or dependency, then read each line's Wiki page for a curated overview before choosing a model.

More under Options → Other: Mutation analysis splits the cell lines by a chosen alteration (hotspot mutation, driver fusion, functional loss or amplification) and ranks the genes carriers depend on more, or express differently.

Inside gene set analysis: gene-gene correlation

Each gene pair is compared by their gene effect scores across all cell lines. The Pearson correlation (r) measures how similarly two gene knockouts affect cell fitness:

↗
Positive (r > 0)

Knockout of the two genes shifts fitness in a similar way across the cell lines, suggesting shared pathway or complex membership.

⟷
No correlation (r ≈ 0)

Gene knockouts have unrelated fitness effects across cell lines.

↘
Negative (r < 0)

Gene knockouts have opposite effects across cell lines: when one is essential, the other is dispensable, suggesting compensatory or antagonistic roles.

Fig 1: TSC1 vs TSC2 gene effect across 1,208 cell lines (r = 0.90). Knockout of either gene produces nearly identical fitness effects, yet the impact is highly context-dependent: some cell lines thrive while others are depleted.

Fig 2: The strong correlation reveals that TSC1 and TSC2 work as one complex, discovered directly from the data without any prior knowledge of the pathway.

Pathway adapted from Huang & Manning, Cell Res (2008) 18:62–69

The Correlation Network

All pairwise correlations between your genes are combined into an interactive network graph. Each node is a gene; edges connect correlated pairs. Edge color and thickness encode the correlation:

Fig 3: Genes cluster by functional relationships. TSC1–TSC2 (thick blue edge) share a complex; TP53–MDM2 (red edge) show opposing fitness effects.
Double-click a node to see its gene effect profile, or an edge to view the scatter plot.

Quick start: Click Test Genes, then Run ▶ to see an example analysis.
Lower the correlation cutoff and re-run to reveal weaker interactions.

Cell Line Wiki

Cell Line Browser / Help

Filters: stack with AND. Click Reset to clear.

  • Tissue / Subtype: DepMap OncotreeLineage and primary disease subtype.
  • Sex: annotation and expression are two independent axes (see below).
  • Hotspot filter: only show cell lines mutated in this gene at a hotspot position. The dropdown lists genes with live n= mutated counts (matching the Fusion / CN filter style).
  • Fusion filter: the dropdown lists clinically relevant fusion pairs first (★ BCR-ABL1, ★ EWSR1-FLI1, …) followed by the gene-based long tail. Selecting a pair filters to the curated set; selecting a gene returns any line with any fusion involving that gene.
  • CN amp/del filter: the dropdown lists curated focal amplifications (▲) and tumor-suppressor deletions (▼) with live n=; selecting one filters to lines carrying that focal copy-number event.
  • Disease: searchable, and scoped by whatever else is filtered, so choosing Skin leaves only the skin diseases. Abbreviations work: type CLL, AML, GBM, PDAC.
  • Alteration grids (▦ beside each alteration box): a grid of the cell lines currently shown, one for hotspot mutations, one for curated driver fusions, one for copy number. Click a gene in the grid to require it altered or wild-type.
  • Quick filters: curated cell-line collections to include or exclude, among them the two provenance sets below.
  • Interferon score (Sort: Interferon score, and the interferon-high / interferon-low quick filters): the average of 34 interferon-stimulated genes, each expressed as how far the line sits from the panel average for that gene. 0 is typical, above +0.5 is called interferon-high here and below −0.5 interferon-low. It measures the cell's own interferon signalling, which shapes how visible a line is to the immune system, and is the readout for viral mimicry. A cell line has no immune infiltrate, so it says nothing about the interferon environment of a tumor. Lines with no expression data are unscored and sort to the end. The score also appears on each cell line's own card.
  • Retroelement signal (Sort: Retroelement signal, and the retroelement-high quick filter): RNA output of 750 full-length LINE-1, HERV-K and SVA elements outside genes, in counts per million, measured from the public CCLE sequencing files. The panel median is about 40 CPM; the top tenth, about 80 CPM and up, counts as retroelement-high. Lines with a higher signal depend measurably more on ADAR1, beyond what the interferon score predicts. 669 of 1,208 lines have public data; the rest are unscored and sort to the end. The score also appears on each cell line's card and wiki.
  • Heatmap: draws a gene set across the cell lines the filters leave showing. Open it from the Heatmap button in this header, or from Options / Other / Gene set heatmap. Pick a preset or paste your own genes, and choose mRNA or gene effect. The column order is carried by the annotation rows under the grid: mark one row as the blocks and the colour strip, legend and Min n follow it, turn on other rows' sort arrows to order the lines within each block, and the score (the mean of the shown genes) settles ties. Rows can show hotspot mutations, fusions, copy number, lineage, subtype, disease, one gene's expression or gene effect, cell-line clustering, or the gates. Saves as an image, to the clipboard, as a .csv or as a reopenable view file, and its Methods button writes out exactly how the picture was made.

⚠ Warning marks: a triangle beside a cell line's name means Cellosaurus records a problem with it. 56 of the 1,208 lines are flagged. Hover the mark for the full explanation, or open the line to see it with a link to the source.

🦠 Virus marks: a virus beside a cell line's name means Cellosaurus records which virus the line was transformed by. 53 of the 1,208 lines carry one, most often EBV, HPV16/18 or HBV. It matters because viral oncoproteins override host pathways: an HPV-transformed line behaves as p53- and RB-deficient whatever its TP53 and RB1 sequence says, and an EBV-immortalised lymphoblastoid line is not a tumour line at all. A line without the mark simply has no such record, which is not the same as being free of the virus. The matching quick filters are named “Confirmed …-transformed” for that reason.

  • Identity disputed (36 lines): the line is contaminated, misidentified, or a derivative of another line, so a result attributed to it may belong to something else. MKN28 is a MKN74 derivative; KP-1N is a PANC-1 derivative.
  • Cancer type disputed (4 lines): the line is itself, but its recorded disease or tissue is genuinely unresolved, so any tissue-grouped analysis may place it incorrectly.
  • Earlier classification corrected (16 lines): the type shown here is already the corrected one, so this is background rather than a warning and carries no marker in the list. SK-N-MC was called a neuroblastoma for years and is an Ewing-family tumor; KE-97 was filed as gastric and is a B-lymphoblastoid line.
  • Both sets are available as quick filters, to exclude or to inspect. Nothing is hidden: a flagged line can still be a good experimental model, it just cannot be evidence about the tumor type on its label. Calls that Cellosaurus states as possible rather than settled say so.

Selecting cell lines: tick lines (or Select Visible) to build a set for Inspect / Export. Show only my N collapses the list to just your ticked lines and carries the count; it is greyed out until something is ticked, and turns off on Deselect All / Reset. The list fills column by column (down the first column in sort order, then the next).

Inspect selected vs rest: compares your selection with the cell lines it is measured against, CRISPR gene effect on the left, mRNA expression on the right. Both columns rank by the size of the difference in either direction, so genes higher and lower in your selection appear together. Each gene carries a Welch's t-test adjusted across all genes tested (Benjamini-Hochberg), shown as q and filterable. The comparison group is yours to choose: all other cell lines, only those sharing a lineage with your selection (taking tissue of origin out of the comparison), a group picked from the tissue table, or a pasted list of names. The two measures cover different cell lines, so each states its own group sizes. Either ranked gene list can be opened in the heatmap (top 10 to 100, or any number), carried over with the inspected cell lines.

Send to another view: carries the listed cell lines, or just the ticked ones, into the correlation scatter, the gene effect charts or the heatmap, either marking them there or narrowing the view to them, and can set them as the cohort for the mutation and gene set analyses. Each target row explains itself in the popout.

Detail card: clicking a line opens a card that now leads with a plain-language executive summary (cancer type, patient origin, and standout molecular features), the same overview shown when you hover a cell-line dot on any plot.

Hotspot variants: when DepMap's inferred-subtype pipeline calls a specific codon (KRAS p.G12D, BRAF p.V600E, EGFR p.L858R, JAK2 p.V617F, EGFR exon-19 del), the variant is appended in green next to the gene name in the Hotspot Mutations list. Generic group calls like KRAS p.G12 (any G12 not specifically D or C) are also shown when no specific call is available. Source: OmicsInferredMolecularSubtypes.csv.

Functional loss: integrated tumor-suppressor inactivation calls (RB1, TP53, PTEN, NF1, CDKN2A, VHL, MTAP, APC) shown as red-bordered chips in the detail panel. A gene is "lost" if any of: WGS-based relative CN < 0.3, likely-LoF mutation with AF > 0.5, or expression < 0.1 log-TPM. This catches deletion-driven losses that the damaging-mutation matrix alone misses: e.g. CDKN2A homozygous deletion in 445 lines (~37% of the panel), most of which look mutation-clean. Source: OmicsInferredMolecularSubtypes.csv.

MSI badge: small red MSI chip next to the cell-line ID when MSIsensor2 score ≥ 20 (DepMap's threshold for microsatellite instability).

Genome signatures (small row near the top of the detail panel): Ploidy (PureCN avg chromosome dosage), WGD (whole-genome doubling, shown in red when positive, ~58% of the panel), Aneuploidy (Ben-David 2021 score, 0–39), CIN (chromosomal instability). These shape interpretation when comparing gene effect across cell lines: WGD-positive lines are systematically different. Source: OmicsGlobalSignatures.csv.

Each new section in the detail panel has an inline ? with a hover tooltip recapping the key explanation, so you don't need to come back to this modal to remember what a tier or column means.

Clinically relevant fusions: shown as green/amber/red chips in the cell line detail panel.

  • Curated list of ~50 well-validated driver fusions (BCR-ABL1, EWSR1-FLI1, EML4-ALK, PML-RARA, TMPRSS2-ERG, …) sourced from COSMIC fusion gene census.
  • Each call is validated per cell line on three orthogonal signals: lineage match, partner expression z-score vs lineage-matched negatives, and partner dependency (CRISPR gene effect) z-score. Only the signals the curator marked as informative for that fusion are scored: e.g. BCR-ABL1 doesn't elevate ABL1 mRNA, so expression isn't checked and the call rests on the strong ABL1 dependency.
  • high: both informative signals support the call (or one strong + the other directionally supportive).
  • med: partial orthogonal support, or curated + lineage match without orthogonal validation.
  • low: neither signal supports and lineage doesn't match the canonical disease (suspect, often artifact).
  • ⚠ atypical: the cell line's tissue isn't the canonical context for this fusion (e.g. EML4-ALK in a Bowel line). Lineage is a modifier, not a gate: when orthogonal evidence is strong the call is kept and flagged, not hidden (could be a misclassified line or a genuine rare event worth investigating).
  • Source: Arriba-annotated fusion calls from OmicsFusionFilteredSupplementary.csv, filtered to confidence=high with read-through transcripts dropped.

Fusion calls, and what “not fused” means: a fusion is called from RNA-seq, so a cell line that was never sequenced is unknown, not fusion-negative. Those lines are held out of both groups rather than counted as wild-type, and the count is reported wherever a fusion comparison is made. Where the answer is published it is filled in from Cellosaurus instead: for EWSR1-FLI1 in Ewing sarcoma that returns nine cell lines, taking the fused group from 13 to 22.

Published calls also add recurrent driver fusions the caller did not report, among them EML4-ALK in NCI-H3122, TPM3-NTRK1 in KM12 and KMT2A-AFF1 in RS4;11. Private one-off fusions and ordinary immunoglobulin rearrangements are deliberately left out. Note that a line without the fusion you filtered on may carry a different one of the same gene: every EWSR1-FLI1-negative Ewing line carries EWSR1-ERG or EWSR1-FEV.

Sex: two independent axes:

  • Sex (annotation): from DepMap's Model table (patient-reported). Values: Male, Female, Unknown.
  • Sex (expression): computed from Y-chromosome markers (RPS4Y1, DDX3Y, EIF1AY, KDM5D, UTY, USP9Y) and XIST expression. Rules: Y-mean > 1.0 log-TPM → male; XIST > 1.0 with Y low → female; otherwise unknown. Validated on DepMap-labeled cells: ~3% false-positive on males, ~0.14% on females.

When expression is “Unknown”:

  • Annotation Male → “Unknown (likely Y-chromosome loss)”: Y loss is common in cancer, esp. older male patients and advanced tumors.
  • Annotation Female → “Unknown (likely XIST silencing)”: XIST silencing is documented in breast and other cancers.

Sex symbols in the list

  • ♂ blue, upright: Male by annotation.
  • ♀ pink, upright: Female by annotation.
  • ♂ blue, italic: Male by expression only (annotation unknown).
  • ♀ pink, italic: Female by expression only (annotation unknown).
  • ? gray: Unknown in both axes.

Sort options, six in all. The arrow beside the picker reverses the order; for a gene or compound sort it waits until you have entered one.

  • Name: alphabetical.
  • GE for gene(s): type one or more genes; lines are ordered by CRISPR gene effect (Chronos), most essential first. Several genes are averaged, which ranks lines by combined essentiality.
  • Expression of gene(s): type one or more genes; lines are ordered by log₂(TPM+1), highest first. Several genes are averaged, so a panel like ASCL1, NEUROD1, CHGA, SYP finds the strongest combined signature.
  • Drug response (PRISM AUC): type a compound; the picker lists PRISM Repurposing compounds ranked by how many of the visible lines they kill. Ordered by area under the curve, most sensitive first, so a lower AUC means more killing.
  • Interferon score and Retroelement signal: the two scores described above, highest first; the retroelement sort adds a picker for which measurement to use (total signal, LINE-1, HERV-K, SVA, or active elements). Unscored lines sort to the end.

Gene-sort input: comma, semicolon, newline or whitespace can separate multiple symbols.

Data sources: DepMap 26Q1 for every measurement. Cell-line identity warnings and the published fusion calls come from Cellosaurus; the curated fusion and subtype panels draw on COSMIC, OncoKB, WHO and NCCN. All filters and sorts use the data currently loaded in the browser; changing tissue / subtype filters narrows the visible set that subsequent sorts operate on.

After download:
Upload the file to any language model that accepts file attachments. The embedded aiInstructions were written and tested against Claude, so that is where the wording fits best, but the file is JSON (plain or gzipped, your choice below) and works with other assistants too. The model will open with a one-line description of what you exported, restate your question, then run the analysis.
File format
Plain is the safer upload: an assistant reads it directly, while a .gz has to be unpacked first, which needs a code / data-analysis tool switched on. Pick compressed if you know yours has one, or if the file is large. Exports over 8 MB switch to compressed on their own. The exact sizes appear beside each choice once you have exported.
Instruction for your AI assistant: This file is JSON (if the name ends in .gz, it is gzip-compressed, decompress it first; if your assistant will not accept a .gz at all, export again with the plain .json option above). Start by reading the readMe fields; every section explains itself, and matrixCoverage says how much of the release the matrices carry before you read anything into a gene you cannot find.
